text_entry: The man, I do assure you, is not here;

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: For I myself at this time have employd him.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: And, sheriff, I will engage my word to thee

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: That I will, by to-morrow dinner-time,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Send him to answer thee, or any man,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: For any thing he shall be charged withal:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: And so let me entreat you leave the house.

speaker: Sheriff
text_entry: I will, my lord. There are two gentlemen

speaker: Sheriff
text_entry: Have in this robbery lost three hundred marks.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: It may be so: if he have robbd these men,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: He shall be answerable; and so farewell.

speaker: Sheriff
text_entry: Good night, my noble lord.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I think it is good morrow, is it not?

speaker: Sheriff
text_entry: Indeed, my lord, I think it be two oclock.

speaker: Sheriff
text_entry: Exeunt Sheriff and Carrier

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: This oily rascal is known as well as Pauls. Go,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: call him forth.

speaker: PETO
text_entry: Falstaff!--Fast asleep behind the arras, and

speaker: PETO
text_entry: snorting like a horse.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Hark, how hard he fetches breath. Search his pockets.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: He searcheth his pockets, and findeth certain papers

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: What hast thou found?

speaker: PETO
text_entry: Nothing but papers, my lord.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Lets see what they be: read them.

speaker: PETO
text_entry: [Reads]  Item, A capon,. . 2s. 2d.

speaker: PETO
text_entry: Item, Sauce,. . . 4d.

speaker: PETO
text_entry: Item, Sack, two gallons, 5s. 8d.

speaker: PETO
text_entry: Item, Anchovies and sack after supper, 2s. 6d.

speaker: PETO
text_entry: Item, Bread,        ob.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: O monstrous! but one half-penny-worth of bread to

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: this intolerable deal of sack! What there is else,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: keep close; well read it at more advantage: there

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: let him sleep till day. Ill to the court in the

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: morning. We must all to the wars, and thy place

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: shall be honourable. Ill procure this fat rogue a

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: charge of foot; and I know his death will be a

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: march of twelve-score. The money shall be paid

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: back again with advantage. Be with me betimes in

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: the morning; and so, good morrow, Peto.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: PETO
text_entry: Good morrow, good my lord.

speaker: PETO
text_entry: ACT III

speaker: PETO
text_entry: SCENE I. Bangor. The Archdeacons house.

speaker: PETO
text_entry: Enter HOTSPUR, WORCESTER, MORTIMER, and GLENDOWER

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: These promises are fair, the parties sure,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: And our induction full of prosperous hope.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Lord Mortimer, and cousin Glendower,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Will you sit down?

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And uncle Worcester: a plague upon it!

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I have forgot the map.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: No, here it is.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Sit, cousin Percy; sit, good cousin Hotspur,

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: For by that name as oft as Lancaster

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Doth speak of you, his cheek looks pale and with

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: A rising sigh he wisheth you in heaven.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And you in hell, as oft as he hears Owen Glendower spoke of.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: I cannot blame him: at my nativity

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: The front of heaven was full of fiery shapes,

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Of burning cressets; and at my birth

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: The frame and huge foundation of the earth

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Shaked like a coward.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Why, so it would have done at the same season, if

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: your mothers cat had but kittened, though yourself

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: had never been born.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: I say the earth did shake when I was born.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And I say the earth was not of my mind,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: If you suppose as fearing you it shook.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: The heavens were all on fire, the earth did tremble.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: O, then the earth shook to see the heavens on fire,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And not in fear of your nativity.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Diseased nature oftentimes breaks forth

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: In strange eruptions; oft the teeming earth

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Is with a kind of colic pinchd and vexd

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: By the imprisoning of unruly wind

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Within her womb; which, for enlargement striving,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Shakes the old beldam earth and topples down

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Steeples and moss-grown towers. At your birth

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Our grandam earth, having this distemperature,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: In passion shook.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Cousin, of many men

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: I do not bear these crossings. Give me leave

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: To tell you once again that at my birth

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: The front of heaven was full of fiery shapes,

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: The goats ran from the mountains, and the herds

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Were strangely clamorous to the frighted fields.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: These signs have markd me extraordinary;

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: And all the courses of my life do show

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: I am not in the roll of common men.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Where is he living, clippd in with the sea

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: That chides the banks of England, Scotland, Wales,

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Which calls me pupil, or hath read to me?

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: And bring him out that is but womans son

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Can trace me in the tedious ways of art

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: And hold me pace in deep experiments.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I think theres no man speaks better Welsh.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Ill to dinner.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Peace, cousin Percy; you will make him mad.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: I can call spirits from the vasty deep.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Why, so can I, or so can any man;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: But will they come when you do call for them?

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Why, I can teach you, cousin, to command

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: The devil.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And I can teach thee, coz, to shame the devil

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: By telling truth: tell truth and shame the devil.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: If thou have power to raise him, bring him hither,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And Ill be sworn I have power to shame him hence.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: O, while you live, tell truth and shame the devil!

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Come, come, no more of this unprofitable chat.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Three times hath Henry Bolingbroke made head

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Against my power; thrice from the banks of Wye

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: And sandy-bottomd Severn have I sent him

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Bootless home and weather-beaten back.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Home without boots, and in foul weather too!

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: How scapes he agues, in the devils name?

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Come, heres the map: shall we divide our right

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: According to our threefold order taen?

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: The archdeacon hath divided it

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Into three limits very equally:

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: England, from Trent and Severn hitherto,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: By south and east is to my part assignd:

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: All westward, Wales beyond the Severn shore,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: And all the fertile land within that bound,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: To Owen Glendower: and, dear coz, to you

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: The remnant northward, lying off from Trent.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: And our indentures tripartite are drawn;

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Which being sealed interchangeably,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: A business that this night may execute,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: To-morrow, cousin Percy, you and I

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: And my good Lord of Worcester will set forth

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: To meet your father and the Scottish power,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: As is appointed us, at Shrewsbury.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: My father Glendower is not ready yet,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Not shall we need his help these fourteen days.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Within that space you may have drawn together

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Your tenants, friends and neighbouring gentlemen.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: A shorter time shall send me to you, lords:

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: And in my conduct shall your ladies come;

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: From whom you now must steal and take no leave,

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: For there will be a world of water shed

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Upon the parting of your wives and you.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Methinks my moiety, north from Burton here,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: In quantity equals not one of yours:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: See how this river comes me cranking in,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And cuts me from the best of all my land

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: A huge half-moon, a monstrous cantle out.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Ill have the current in this place dammd up;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And here the smug and silver Trent shall run

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: In a new channel, fair and evenly;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: It shall not wind with such a deep indent,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: To rob me of so rich a bottom here.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Not wind? it shall, it must; you see it doth.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Yea, but

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Mark how he bears his course, and runs me up

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: With like advantage on the other side;

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Gelding the opposed continent as much

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: As on the other side it takes from you.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Yea, but a little charge will trench him here

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: And on this north side win this cape of land;

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: And then he runs straight and even.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Ill have it so: a little charge will do it.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Ill not have it alterd.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Will not you?

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: No, nor you shall not.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Who shall say me nay?

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Why, that will I.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Let me not understand you, then; speak it in Welsh.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: I can speak English, lord, as well as you;

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: For I was traind up in the English court;

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Where, being but young, I framed to the harp

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Many an English ditty lovely well

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: And gave the tongue a helpful ornament,

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: A virtue that was never seen in you.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Marry,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And I am glad of it with all my heart:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I had rather be a kitten and cry mew

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Than one of these same metre ballad-mongers;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I had rather hear a brazen canstick turnd,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Or a dry wheel grate on the axle-tree;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And that would set my teeth nothing on edge,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Nothing so much as mincing poetry:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Tis like the forced gait of a shuffling nag.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Come, you shall have Trent turnd.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I do not care: Ill give thrice so much land

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: To any well-deserving friend;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: But in the way of bargain, mark ye me,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Ill cavil on the ninth part of a hair.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Are the indentures drawn? shall we be gone?

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: The moon shines fair; you may away by night:

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Ill haste the writer and withal

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Break with your wives of your departure hence:

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: I am afraid my daughter will run mad,

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: So much she doteth on her Mortimer.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Exit GLENDOWER

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Fie, cousin Percy! how you cross my father!

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I cannot choose: sometime he angers me

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: With telling me of the mouldwarp and the ant,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Of the dreamer Merlin and his prophecies,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And of a dragon and a finless fish,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: A clip-wingd griffin and a moulten raven,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: A couching lion and a ramping cat,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And such a deal of skimble-skamble stuff

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: As puts me from my faith. I tell you what;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: He held me last night at least nine hours

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: In reckoning up the several devils names

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: That were his lackeys: I cried hum, and well, go to,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: But markd him not a word. O, he is as tedious

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: As a tired horse, a railing wife;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Worse than a smoky house: I had rather live

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: With cheese and garlic in a windmill, far,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Than feed on cates and have him talk to me

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: In any summer-house in Christendom.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: In faith, he is a worthy gentleman,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Exceedingly well read, and profited

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: In strange concealments, valiant as a lion

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: And as wondrous affable and as bountiful

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: As mines of India. Shall I tell you, cousin?

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: He holds your temper in a high respect

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: And curbs himself even of his natural scope

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: When you come cross his humour; faith, he does:

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: I warrant you, that man is not alive

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Might so have tempted him as you have done,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Without the taste of danger and reproof:

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: But do not use it oft, let me entreat you.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: In faith, my lord, you are too wilful-blame;

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: And since your coming hither have done enough

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: To put him quite beside his patience.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: You must needs learn, lord, to amend this fault:

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Though sometimes it show greatness, courage, blood,--

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: And thats the dearest grace it renders you,--

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Yet oftentimes it doth present harsh rage,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Defect of manners, want of government,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Pride, haughtiness, opinion and disdain:

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: The least of which haunting a nobleman

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Loseth mens hearts and leaves behind a stain

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Upon the beauty of all parts besides,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Beguiling them of commendation.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Well, I am schoold: good manners be your speed!

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Here come our wives, and let us take our leave.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Re-enter GLENDOWER with the ladies

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: This is the deadly spite that angers me;

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: My wife can speak no English, I no Welsh.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: My daughter weeps: she will not part with you;

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Shell be a soldier too, shell to the wars.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Good father, tell her that she and my aunt Percy

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Shall follow in your conduct speedily.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Glendower speaks to her in Welsh, and she answers him in the same

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: She is desperate here; a peevish self-wind harlotry,

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: one that no persuasion can do good upon.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: The lady speaks in Welsh

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: I understand thy looks: that pretty Welsh

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Which thou pourst down from these swelling heavens

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: I am too perfect in; and, but for shame,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: In such a parley should I answer thee.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: The lady speaks again in Welsh

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: I understand thy kisses and thou mine,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: And thats a feeling disputation:

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: But I will never be a truant, love,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Till I have learned thy language; for thy tongue

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Makes Welsh as sweet as ditties highly pennd,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Sung by a fair queen in a summers bower,

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: With ravishing division, to her lute.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Nay, if you melt, then will she run mad.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: The lady speaks again in Welsh

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: O, I am ignorance itself in this!

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: She bids you on the wanton rushes lay you down

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: And rest your gentle head upon her lap,

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: And she will sing the song that pleaseth you

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: And on your eyelids crown the god of sleep.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Charming your blood with pleasing heaviness,

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Making such difference twixt wake and sleep

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: As is the difference betwixt day and night

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: The hour before the heavenly-harnessd team

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Begins his golden progress in the east.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: With all my heart Ill sit and hear her sing:

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: By that time will our book, I think, be drawn

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Do so;

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: And those musicians that shall play to you

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Hang in the air a thousand leagues from hence,

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: And straight they shall be here: sit, and attend.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Come, Kate, thou art perfect in lying down: come,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: quick, quick, that I may lay my head in thy lap.

speaker: LADY PERCY
text_entry: Go, ye giddy goose.

speaker: LADY PERCY
text_entry: The music plays

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Now I perceive the devil understands Welsh;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And tis no marvel he is so humorous.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Byr lady, he is a good musician.

speaker: LADY PERCY
text_entry: Then should you be nothing but musical for you are

speaker: LADY PERCY
text_entry: altogether governed by humours. Lie still, ye thief,

speaker: LADY PERCY
text_entry: and hear the lady sing in Welsh.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I had rather hear Lady, my brach, howl in Irish.

speaker: LADY PERCY
text_entry: Wouldst thou have thy head broken?

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: No.

speaker: LADY PERCY
text_entry: Then be still.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Neither;tis a womans fault.

speaker: LADY PERCY
text_entry: Now God help thee!

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: To the Welsh ladys bed.

speaker: LADY PERCY
text_entry: Whats that?

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Peace! she sings.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Here the lady sings a Welsh song

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Come, Kate, Ill have your song too.

speaker: LADY PERCY
text_entry: Not mine, in good sooth.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Not yours, in good sooth! Heart! you swear like a

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: comfit-makers wife. Not you, in good sooth, and

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: as true as I live, and as God shall mend me, and

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: as sure as day,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And givest such sarcenet surety for thy oaths,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: As if thou never walkst further than Finsbury.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Swear me, Kate, like a lady as thou art,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: A good mouth-filling oath, and leave in sooth,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And such protest of pepper-gingerbread,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: To velvet-guards and Sunday-citizens.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Come, sing.

speaker: LADY PERCY
text_entry: I will not sing.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Tis the next way to turn tailor, or be red-breast

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: teacher. An the indentures be drawn, Ill away

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: within these two hours; and so, come in when ye will.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Exit

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: Come, come, Lord Mortimer; you are as slow

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: As hot Lord Percy is on fire to go.

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: By this our book is drawn; well but seal,

speaker: GLENDOWER
text_entry: And then to horse immediately.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: With all my heart.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: SCENE II. London. The palace.

speaker: MORTIMER
text_entry: Enter KING HENRY IV, PRINCE HENRY, and others

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Lords, give us leave; the Prince of Wales and I

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Must have some private conference; but be near at hand,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: For we shall presently have need of you.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Exeunt Lords

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: I know not whether God will have it so,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: For some displeasing service I have done,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: That, in his secret doom, out of my blood

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Hell breed revengement and a scourge for me;

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: But thou dost in thy passages of life

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Make me believe that thou art only markd

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: For the hot vengeance and the rod of heaven

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: To punish my mistreadings. Tell me else,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Could such inordinate and low desires,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Such poor, such bare, such lewd, such mean attempts,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Such barren pleasures, rude society,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: As thou art matchd withal and grafted to,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Accompany the greatness of thy blood

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: And hold their level with thy princely heart?

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: So please your majesty, I would I could

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Quit all offences with as clear excuse

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: As well as I am doubtless I can purge

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Myself of many I am charged withal:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Yet such extenuation let me beg,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: As, in reproof of many tales devised,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: which oft the ear of greatness needs must hear,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: By smiling pick-thanks and base news-mongers,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I may, for some things true, wherein my youth

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Hath faulty wanderd and irregular,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Find pardon on my true submission.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: God pardon thee! yet let me wonder, Harry,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: At thy affections, which do hold a wing

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Quite from the flight of all thy ancestors.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Thy place in council thou hast rudely lost.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Which by thy younger brother is supplied,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: And art almost an alien to the hearts

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Of all the court and princes of my blood:

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: The hope and expectation of thy time

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Is ruind, and the soul of every man

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Prophetically doth forethink thy fall.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Had I so lavish of my presence been,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: So common-hackneyd in the eyes of men,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: So stale and cheap to vulgar company,

speaker: KING HENRY IV

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: not pocket up wrong: art thou not ashamed?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Dost thou hear, Hal? thou knowest in the state of

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: innocency Adam fell; and what should poor Jack

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Falstaff do in the days of villany? Thou seest I

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: have more flesh than another man, and therefore more

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: frailty. You confess then, you picked my pocket?

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: It appears so by the story.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Hostess, I forgive thee: go, make ready breakfast;

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: love thy husband, look to thy servants, cherish thy

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: guests: thou shalt find me tractable to any honest

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: reason: thou seest I am pacified still. Nay,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: prithee, be gone.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Exit Hostess

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Now Hal, to the news at court: for the robbery,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: lad, how is that answered?

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: O, my sweet beef, I must still be good angel to

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: thee: the money is paid back again.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: O, I do not like that paying back; tis a double labour.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I am good friends with my father and may do any thing.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Rob me the exchequer the first thing thou doest, and

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: do it with unwashed hands too.

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: Do, my lord.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I have procured thee, Jack, a charge of foot.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: I would it had been of horse. Where shall I find

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: one that can steal well? O for a fine thief, of the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: age of two and twenty or thereabouts! I am

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: heinously unprovided. Well, God be thanked for

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: these rebels, they offend none but the virtuous: I

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: laud them, I praise them.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Bardolph!

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: My lord?

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Go bear this letter to Lord John of Lancaster, to my

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: brother John; this to my Lord of Westmoreland.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Exit Bardolph

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Go, Peto, to horse, to horse; for thou and I have

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: thirty miles to ride yet ere dinner time.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Exit Peto

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Jack, meet me to-morrow in the temple hall at two

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: oclock in the afternoon.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: There shalt thou know thy charge; and there receive

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Money and order for their furniture.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: The land is burning; Percy stands on high;

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: And either we or they must lower lie.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Exit PRINCE HENRY

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Rare words! brave world! Hostess, my breakfast, come!

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: O, I could wish this tavern were my drum!

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Exit

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: ACT IV

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: SCENE I. The rebel camp near Shrewsbury.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter HOTSPUR, WORCESTER, and DOUGLAS

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Well said, my noble Scot: if speaking truth

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: In this fine age were not thought flattery,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Such attribution should the Douglas have,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: As not a soldier of this seasons stamp

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Should go so general current through the world.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: By God, I cannot flatter; I do defy

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: The tongues of soothers; but a braver place

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: In my hearts love hath no man than yourself:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Nay, task me to my word; approve me, lord.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Thou art the king of honour:

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: No man so potent breathes upon the ground

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: But I will beard him.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Do so, and tis well.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Enter a Messenger with letters

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: What letters hast thou there?--I can but thank you.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: These letters come from your father.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Letters from him! why comes he not himself?

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: He cannot come, my lord; he is grievous sick.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Zounds! how has he the leisure to be sick

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: In such a rustling time? Who leads his power?

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Under whose government come they along?

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: His letters bear his mind, not I, my lord.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: I prithee, tell me, doth he keep his bed?

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: He did, my lord, four days ere I set forth;

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: And at the time of my departure thence

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: He was much feard by his physicians.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: I would the state of time had first been whole

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Ere he by sickness had been visited:

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: His health was never better worth than now.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Sick now! droop now! this sickness doth infect

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: The very life-blood of our enterprise;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Tis catching hither, even to our camp.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: He writes me here, that inward sickness--

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And that his friends by deputation could not

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: So soon be drawn, nor did he think it meet

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: To lay so dangerous and dear a trust

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: On any soul removed but on his own.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Yet doth he give us bold advertisement,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: That with our small conjunction we should on,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: To see how fortune is disposed to us;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: For, as he writes, there is no quailing now.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Because the king is certainly possessd

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Of all our purposes. What say you to it?

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Your fathers sickness is a maim to us.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: A perilous gash, a very limb loppd off:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And yet, in faith, it is not; his present want

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Seems more than we shall find it: were it good

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: To set the exact wealth of all our states

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: All at one cast? to set so rich a main

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: On the nice hazard of one doubtful hour?

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: It were not good; for therein should we read

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: The very bottom and the soul of hope,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: The very list, the very utmost bound

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Of all our fortunes.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Faith, and so we should;

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Where now remains a sweet reversion:

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: We may boldly spend upon the hope of what

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Is to come in:

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: A comfort of retirement lives in this.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: A rendezvous, a home to fly unto.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: If that the devil and mischance look big

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Upon the maidenhead of our affairs.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: But yet I would your father had been here.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: The quality and hair of our attempt

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Brooks no division: it will be thought

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: By some, that know not why he is away,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: That wisdom, loyalty and mere dislike

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Of our proceedings kept the earl from hence:

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: And think how such an apprehension

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: May turn the tide of fearful faction

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: And breed a kind of question in our cause;

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: For well you know we of the offering side

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Must keep aloof from strict arbitrement,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: And stop all sight-holes, every loop from whence

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: The eye of reason may pry in upon us:

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: This absence of your fathers draws a curtain,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: That shows the ignorant a kind of fear

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Before not dreamt of.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: You strain too far.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I rather of his absence make this use:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: It lends a lustre and more great opinion,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: A larger dare to our great enterprise,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Than if the earl were here; for men must think,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: If we without his help can make a head

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: To push against a kingdom, with his help

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: We shall oerturn it topsy-turvy down.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Yet all goes well, yet all our joints are whole.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: As heart can think: there is not such a word

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Spoke of in Scotland as this term of fear.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Enter SIR RICHARD VERNON

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: My cousin Vernon, welcome, by my soul.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Pray God my news be worth a welcome, lord.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: The Earl of Westmoreland, seven thousand strong,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Is marching hitherwards; with him Prince John.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: No harm: what more?

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: And further, I have learnd,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: The king himself in person is set forth,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Or hitherwards intended speedily,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: With strong and mighty preparation.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: He shall be welcome too. Where is his son,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: The nimble-footed madcap Prince of Wales,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And his comrades, that daffd the world aside,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And bid it pass?

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: All furnishd, all in arms;

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: All plumed like estridges that with the wind

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Baited like eagles having lately bathed;

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Glittering in golden coats, like images;

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: As full of spirit as the month of May,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: And gorgeous as the sun at midsummer;

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Wanton as youthful goats, wild as young bulls.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: I saw young Harry, with his beaver on,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: His cuisses on his thighs, gallantly armd

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Rise from the ground like featherd Mercury,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: And vaulted with such ease into his seat,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: As if an angel droppd down from the clouds,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: To turn and wind a fiery Pegasus

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: And witch the world with noble horsemanship.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: No more, no more: worse than the sun in March,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: This praise doth nourish agues. Let them come:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: They come like sacrifices in their trim,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And to the fire-eyed maid of smoky war

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: All hot and bleeding will we offer them:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: The mailed Mars shall on his altar sit

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Up to the ears in blood. I am on fire

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: To hear this rich reprisal is so nigh

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And yet not ours. Come, let me taste my horse,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Who is to bear me like a thunderbolt

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Against the bosom of the Prince of Wales:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Harry to Harry shall, hot horse to horse,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Meet and neer part till one drop down a corse.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: O that Glendower were come!

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: There is more news:

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: I learnd in Worcester, as I rode along,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: He cannot draw his power this fourteen days.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Thats the worst tidings that I hear of yet.

speaker: WORCESTER
text_entry: Ay, by my faith, that bears a frosty sound.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: What may the kings whole battle reach unto?

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: To thirty thousand.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Forty let it be:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: My father and Glendower being both away,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: The powers of us may serve so great a day

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Come, let us take a muster speedily:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Doomsday is near; die all, die merrily.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Talk not of dying: I am out of fear

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Of death or deaths hand for this one-half year.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: SCENE II. A public road near Coventry.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Enter FALSTAFF and BARDOLPH

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Bardolph, get thee before to Coventry; fill me a

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: bottle of sack: our soldiers shall march through;

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: well to Sutton Cofil tonight.

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: Will you give me money, captain?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Lay out, lay out.

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: This bottle makes an angel.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: An if it do, take it for thy labour; and if it make

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: twenty, take them all; Ill answer the coinage. Bid

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: my lieutenant Peto meet me at towns end.

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: I will, captain: farewell.

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: Exit

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: If I be not ashamed of my soldiers, I am a soused

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: gurnet. I have misused the kings press damnably.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: I have got, in exchange of a hundred and fifty

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: soldiers, three hundred and odd pounds. I press me

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: none but good house-holders, yeomans sons; inquire

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: me out contracted bachelors, such as had been asked

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: twice on the banns; such a commodity of warm slaves,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: as had as lieve hear the devil as a drum; such as

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: fear the report of a caliver worse than a struck

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: fowl or a hurt wild-duck. I pressed me none but such

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: toasts-and-butter, with hearts in their bellies no

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: bigger than pins heads, and they have bought out

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: their services; and now my whole charge consists of

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: ancients, corporals, lieutenants, gentlemen of

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: companies, slaves as ragged as Lazarus in the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: painted cloth, where the gluttons dogs licked his

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: sores; and such as indeed were never soldiers, but

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: discarded unjust serving-men, younger sons to

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: younger brothers, revolted tapsters and ostlers

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: trade-fallen, the cankers of a calm world and a

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: long peace, ten times more dishonourable ragged than

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: an old faced ancient: and such have I, to fill up

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: the rooms of them that have bought out their

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: services, that you would think that I had a hundred

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: and fifty tattered prodigals lately come from

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: swine-keeping, from eating draff and husks. A mad

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: fellow met me on the way and told me I had unloaded

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: all the gibbets and pressed the dead bodies. No eye

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: hath seen such scarecrows. Ill not march through

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Coventry with them, thats flat: nay, and the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: villains march wide betwixt the legs, as if they had

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: gyves on; for indeed I had the most of them out of

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: prison. Theres but a shirt and a half in all my

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: company; and the half shirt is two napkins tacked

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: together and thrown over the shoulders like an

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: heralds coat without sleeves; and the shirt, to say

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: the truth, stolen from my host at Saint Albans, or

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: the red-nose innkeeper of Daventry. But thats all

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: one; theyll find linen enough on every hedge.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter the PRINCE and WESTMORELAND

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: How now, blown Jack! how now, quilt!

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: What, Hal! how now, mad wag! what a devil dost thou

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: in Warwickshire? My good Lord of Westmoreland, I

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: cry you mercy: I thought your honour had already been

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: at Shrewsbury.

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: Faith, Sir John,tis more than time that I were

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: there, and you too; but my powers are there already.

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: The king, I can tell you, looks for us all: we must

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: away all night.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Tut, never fear me: I am as vigilant as a cat to

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: steal cream.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I think, to steal cream indeed, for thy theft hath

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: already made thee butter. But tell me, Jack, whose

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: fellows are these that come after?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Mine, Hal, mine.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I did never see such pitiful rascals.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Tut, tut; good enough to toss; food for powder, food

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: for powder; theyll fill a pit as well as better:

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: tush, man, mortal men, mortal men.

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: Ay, but, Sir John, methinks they are exceeding poor

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: and bare, too beggarly.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Faith, for their poverty, I know not where they had

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: that; and for their bareness, I am sure they never

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: learned that of me.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: No Ill be sworn; unless you call three fingers on

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: the ribs bare. But, sirrah, make haste: Percy is

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: already in the field.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: What, is the king encamped?

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: He is, Sir John: I fear we shall stay too long.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Well,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: To the latter end of a fray and the beginning of a feast

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Fits a dull fighter and a keen guest.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: SCENE III. The rebel camp near Shrewsbury.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter HOTSPUR, WORCESTER, DOUGLAS, and VERNON

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Well fight with him to-night.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: It may not be.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: You give him then the advantage.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Not a whit.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Why say you so? looks he not for supply?

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: So do we.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: His is certain, ours is doubtful.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Good cousin, be advised; stir not tonight.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Do not, my lord.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: You do not counsel well:

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: You speak it out of fear and cold heart.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Do me no slander, Douglas: by my life,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: And I dare well maintain it with my life,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: If well-respected honour bid me on,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: I hold as little counsel with weak fear

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: As you, my lord, or any Scot that this day lives:

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Let it be seen to-morrow in the battle

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Which of us fears.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Yea, or to-night.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Content.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: To-night, say I.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Come, come it nay not be. I wonder much,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Being men of such great leading as you are,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: That you foresee not what impediments

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Drag back our expedition: certain horse

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Of my cousin Vernons are not yet come up:

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Your uncle Worcesters horse came but today;

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: And now their pride and mettle is asleep,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Their courage with hard labour tame and dull,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: That not a horse is half the half of himself.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: So are the horses of the enemy

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: In general, journey-bated and brought low:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: The better part of ours are full of rest.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: The number of the king exceedeth ours:

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: For Gods sake. cousin, stay till all come in.

text_entry: My nephews trespass may be well forgot;

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: it hath the excuse of youth and heat of blood,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: And an adopted name of privilege,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: A hair-braind Hotspur, governd by a spleen:

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: All his offences live upon my head

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: And on his fathers; we did train him on,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: And, his corruption being taen from us,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: We, as the spring of all, shall pay for all.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Therefore, good cousin, let not Harry know,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: In any case, the offer of the king.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Deliver what you will; Ill say tis so.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Here comes your cousin.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Enter HOTSPUR and DOUGLAS

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: My uncle is returnd:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Deliver up my Lord of Westmoreland.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Uncle, what news?

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: The king will bid you battle presently.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Defy him by the Lord of Westmoreland.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Lord Douglas, go you and tell him so.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Marry, and shall, and very willingly.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: There is no seeming mercy in the king.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Did you beg any? God forbid!

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: I told him gently of our grievances,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Of his oath-breaking; which he mended thus,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: By now forswearing that he is forsworn:

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: He calls us rebels, traitors; and will scourge

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: With haughty arms this hateful name in us.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Re-enter the EARL OF DOUGLAS

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Arm, gentlemen; to arms! for I have thrown

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: A brave defiance in King Henrys teeth,

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: And Westmoreland, that was engaged, did bear it;

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Which cannot choose but bring him quickly on.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: The Prince of Wales steppd forth before the king,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: And, nephew, challenged you to single fight.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: O, would the quarrel lay upon our heads,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And that no man might draw short breath today

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: But I and Harry Monmouth! Tell me, tell me,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: How showd his tasking? seemd it in contempt?

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: No, by my soul; I never in my life

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Did hear a challenge urged more modestly,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Unless a brother should a brother dare

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: To gentle exercise and proof of arms.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: He gave you all the duties of a man;

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Trimmd up your praises with a princely tongue,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Spoke to your deservings like a chronicle,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Making you ever better than his praise

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: By still dispraising praise valued in you;

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: And, which became him like a prince indeed,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: He made a blushing cital of himself;

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: And chid his truant youth with such a grace

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: As if he masterd there a double spirit.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Of teaching and of learning instantly.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: There did he pause: but let me tell the world,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: If he outlive the envy of this day,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: England did never owe so sweet a hope,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: So much misconstrued in his wantonness.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Cousin, I think thou art enamoured

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: On his follies: never did I hear

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Of any prince so wild a libertine.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: But be he as he will, yet once ere night

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I will embrace him with a soldiers arm,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: That he shall shrink under my courtesy.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Arm, arm with speed: and, fellows, soldiers, friends,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Better consider what you have to do

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Than I, that have not well the gift of tongue,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Can lift your blood up with persuasion.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Enter a Messenger

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: My lord, here are letters for you.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I cannot read them now.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: O gentlemen, the time of life is short!

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: To spend that shortness basely were too long,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: If life did ride upon a dials point,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Still ending at the arrival of an hour.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: An if we live, we live to tread on kings;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: If die, brave death, when princes die with us!

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Now, for our consciences, the arms are fair,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: When the intent of bearing them is just.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Enter another Messenger

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: My lord, prepare; the king comes on apace.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I thank him, that he cuts me from my tale,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: For I profess not talking; only this--

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Let each man do his best: and here draw I

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: A sword, whose temper I intend to stain

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: With the best blood that I can meet withal

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: In the adventure of this perilous day.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Now, Esperance! Percy! and set on.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Sound all the lofty instruments of war,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And by that music let us all embrace;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: For, heaven to earth, some of us never shall

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: A second time do such a courtesy.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: The trumpets sound. They embrace, and exeunt

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: SCENE III. Plain between the camps.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: KING HENRY enters with his power. Alarum to the battle. Then enter DOUGLAS and SIR WALTER BLUNT

speaker: SIR WALTER BLUNT
text_entry: What is thy name, that in the battle thus

speaker: SIR WALTER BLUNT
text_entry: Thou crossest me? what honour dost thou seek

speaker: SIR WALTER BLUNT
text_entry: Upon my head?

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Know then, my name is Douglas;

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: And I do haunt thee in the battle thus

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Because some tell me that thou art a king.

speaker: SIR WALTER BLUNT
text_entry: They tell thee true.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: The Lord of Stafford dear to-day hath bought

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Thy likeness, for instead of thee, King Harry,

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: This sword hath ended him: so shall it thee,

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Unless thou yield thee as my prisoner.

speaker: SIR WALTER BLUNT
text_entry: I was not born a yielder, thou proud Scot;

speaker: SIR WALTER BLUNT
text_entry: And thou shalt find a king that will revenge

speaker: SIR WALTER BLUNT
text_entry: Lord Staffords death.

speaker: SIR WALTER BLUNT
text_entry: They fight. DOUGLAS kills SIR WALTER BLUNT. Enter HOTSPUR

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: O Douglas, hadst thou fought at Holmedon thus,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: never had triumphd upon a Scot.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Alls done, alls won; here breathless lies the king.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Where?

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Here.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: This, Douglas? no: I know this face full well:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: A gallant knight he was, his name was Blunt;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Semblably furnishd like the king himself.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: A fool go with thy soul, whither it goes!

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: A borrowd title hast thou bought too dear:

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Why didst thou tell me that thou wert a king?

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: The king hath many marching in his coats.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Now, by my sword, I will kill all his coats;

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Ill murder all his wardrobe, piece by piece,

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Until I meet the king.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Up, and away!

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Our soldiers stand full fairly for the day.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Alarum. Enter FALSTAFF, solus

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Though I could scape shot-free at London, I fear

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: the shot here; heres no scoring but upon the pate.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Soft! who are you? Sir Walter Blunt: theres honour

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: for you! heres no vanity! I am as hot as moulten

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: lead, and as heavy too: God keep lead out of me! I

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: need no more weight than mine own bowels. I have

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: led my ragamuffins where they are peppered: theres

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: not three of my hundred and fifty left alive; and

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: they are for the towns end, to beg during life.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: But who comes here?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter PRINCE HENRY

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: What, standst thou idle here? lend me thy sword:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Many a nobleman lies stark and stiff

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Under the hoofs of vaunting enemies,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Whose deaths are yet unrevenged: I prithee,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: lend me thy sword.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: O Hal, I prithee, give me leave to breathe awhile.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Turk Gregory never did such deeds in arms as I have

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: done this day. I have paid Percy, I have made him sure.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: He is, indeed; and living to kill thee. I prithee,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: lend me thy sword.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Nay, before God, Hal, if Percy be alive, thou getst

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: not my sword; but take my pistol, if thou wilt.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Give it to me: what, is it in the case?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Ay, Hal; tis hot, tis hot; theres that will sack a city.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: PRINCE HENRY draws it out, and finds it to be a bottle of sack

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: What, is it a time to jest and dally now?

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: He throws the bottle at him. Exit

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Well, if Percy be alive, Ill pierce him. If he do

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: come in my way, so: if he do not, if I come in his

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: willingly, let him make a carbonado of me. I like

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: not such grinning honour as Sir Walter hath: give me

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: life: which if I can save, so; if not, honour comes

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: unlooked for, and theres an end.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Exit FALSTAFF

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: SCENE IV. Another part of the field.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Alarum. Excursions. Enter PRINCE HENRY, LORD JOHN OF LANCASTER, and EARL OF WESTMORELAND

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: I prithee,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Harry, withdraw thyself; thou bleedst too much.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Lord John of Lancaster, go you with him.

speaker: LANCASTER
text_entry: Not I, my lord, unless I did bleed too.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I beseech your majesty, make up,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Lest your retirement do amaze your friends.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: I will do so.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: My Lord of Westmoreland, lead him to his tent.

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: Come, my lord, Ill lead you to your tent.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Lead me, my lord? I do not need your help:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: And God forbid a shallow scratch should drive

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: The Prince of Wales from such a field as this,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Where staind nobility lies trodden on,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: and rebels arms triumph in massacres!

speaker: LANCASTER
text_entry: We breathe too long: come, cousin Westmoreland,

speaker: LANCASTER
text_entry: Our duty this way lies; for Gods sake come.

speaker: LANCASTER
text_entry: Exeunt LANCASTER and WESTMORELAND

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: By God, thou hast deceived me, Lancaster;

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I did not think thee lord of such a spirit:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Before, I loved thee as a brother, John;

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: But now, I do respect thee as my soul.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: I saw him hold Lord Percy at the point

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: With lustier maintenance than I did look for

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Of such an ungrown warrior.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: O, this boy

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Lends mettle to us all!

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Exit

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Enter DOUGLAS

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: Another king! they grow like Hydras heads:

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: I am the Douglas, fatal to all those

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: That wear those colours on them: what art thou,

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: That counterfeitst the person of a king?

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: The king himself; who, Douglas, grieves at heart

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: So many of his shadows thou hast met

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: And not the very king. I have two boys

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Seek Percy and thyself about the field:

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: But, seeing thou fallst on me so luckily,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: I will assay thee: so, defend thyself.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: I fear thou art another counterfeit;

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: And yet, in faith, thou bearst thee like a king:

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: But mine I am sure thou art, whoeer thou be,

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: And thus I win thee.

speaker: EARL OF DOUGLAS
text_entry: They fight. KING HENRY being in danger, PRINCE HENRY enters

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Hold up thy head, vile Scot, or thou art like

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Never to hold it up again! the spirits

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Of valiant Shirley, Stafford, Blunt, are in my arms:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: It is the Prince of Wales that threatens thee;

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Who never promiseth but he means to pay.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: They fight: DOUGLAS flies

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Cheerly, my lordhow fares your grace?

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Sir Nicholas Gawsey hath for succor sent,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: And so hath Clifton: Ill to Clifton straight.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Stay, and breathe awhile:

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Thou hast redeemd thy lost opinion,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: And showd thou makest some tender of my life,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: In this fair rescue thou hast brought to me.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: O God! they did me too much injury

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: That ever said I hearkend for your death.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: If it were so, I might have let alone

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: The insulting hand of Douglas over you,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Which would have been as speedy in your end

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: As all the poisonous potions in the world

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: And saved the treacherous labour of your son.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Make up to Clifton: Ill to Sir Nicholas Gawsey.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Exit

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Enter HOTSPUR

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: If I mistake not, thou art Harry Monmouth.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Thou speakst as if I would deny my name.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: My name is Harry Percy.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Why, then I see

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: A very valiant rebel of the name.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I am the Prince of Wales; and think not, Percy,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: To share with me in glory any more:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Two stars keep not their motion in one sphere;

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Nor can one England brook a double reign,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Of Harry Percy and the Prince of Wales.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Nor shall it, Harry; for the hour is come

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: To end the one of us; and would to God

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Thy name in arms were now as great as mine!

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Ill make it greater ere I part from thee;

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: And all the budding honours on thy crest

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Ill crop, to make a garland for my head.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I can no longer brook thy vanities.

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: They fight

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Enter FALSTAFF

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Well said, Hal! to it Hal! Nay, you shall find no

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: boys play here, I can tell you.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Re-enter DOUGLAS; he fights with FALSTAFF,  who falls down as if he were dead, and exit DOUGLAS. HOTSPUR is wounded, and falls

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: O, Harry, thou hast robbd me of my youth!

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: I better brook the loss of brittle life

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Than those proud titles thou hast won of me;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: They wound my thoughts worse than sword my flesh:

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: But thoughts the slave of life, and life times fool;

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And time, that takes survey of all the world,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Must have a stop. O, I could prophesy,

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: But that the earthy and cold hand of death

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Lies on my tongue: no, Percy, thou art dust

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: And food for--

speaker: HOTSPUR
text_entry: Dies

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: For worms, brave Percy: fare thee well, great heart!

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Ill-weaved ambition, how much art thou shrunk!

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: When that this body did contain a spirit,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: A kingdom for it was too small a bound;

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: But now two paces of the vilest earth

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Is room enough: this earth that bears thee dead

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Bears not alive so stout a gentleman.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: If thou wert sensible of courtesy,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I should not make so dear a show of zeal:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: But let my favours hide thy mangled face;

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: And, even in thy behalf, Ill thank myself

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: For doing these fair rites of tenderness.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Adieu, and take thy praise with thee to heaven!

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Thy ignominy sleep with thee in the grave,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: But not rememberd in thy epitaph!

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: He spieth FALSTAFF on the ground

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: What, old acquaintance! could not all this flesh

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Keep in a little life? Poor Jack, farewell!

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I could have better spared a better man:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: O, I should have a heavy miss of thee,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: If I were much in love with vanity!

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Death hath not struck so fat a deer to-day,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Though many dearer, in this bloody fray.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Embowelld will I see thee by and by:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Till then in blood by noble Percy lie.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Exit PRINCE HENRY

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: [Rising up]  Embowelled! if thou embowel me to-day,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Ill give you leave to powder me and eat me too

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: to-morrow. Sblood,twas time to counterfeit, or

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: that hot termagant Scot had paid me scot and lot too.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Counterfeit? I lie, I am no counterfeit: to die,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: is to be a counterfeit; for he is but the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: counterfeit of a man who hath not the life of a man:

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: but to counterfeit dying, when a man thereby

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: liveth, is to be no counterfeit, but the true and

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: perfect image of life indeed. The better part of

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: valour is discretion; in the which better part I

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: have saved my life.Zounds, I am afraid of this

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: gunpowder Percy, though he be dead: how, if he

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: should counterfeit too and rise? by my faith, I am

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: afraid he would prove the better counterfeit.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Therefore Ill make him sure; yea, and Ill swear I

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: killed him. Why may not he rise as well as I?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Nothing confutes me but eyes, and nobody sees me.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Therefore, sirrah,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Stabbing him

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: with a new wound in your thigh, come you along with me.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Takes up HOTSPUR on his back

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Re-enter PRINCE HENRY and LORD JOHN OF LANCASTER

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Come, brother John; full bravely hast thou fleshd

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Thy maiden sword.

speaker: LANCASTER
text_entry: But, soft! whom have we here?

speaker: LANCASTER
text_entry: Did you not tell me this fat man was dead?

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I did; I saw him dead,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Breathless and bleeding on the ground. Art

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: thou alive?

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Or is it fantasy that plays upon our eyesight?

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I prithee, speak; we will not trust our eyes

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Without our ears: thou art not what thou seemst.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: No, thats certain; I am not a double man: but if I

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: be not Jack Falstaff, then am I a Jack. There is Percy:

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Throwing the body down

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: if your father will do me any honour, so; if not, let

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: him kill the next Percy himself. I look to be either

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: earl or duke, I can assure you.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Why, Percy I killed myself and saw thee dead.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Didst thou? Lord, Lord, how this world is given to

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: lying! I grant you I was down and out of breath;

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: and so was he: but we rose both at an instant and

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: fought a long hour by Shrewsbury clock. If I may be

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: believed, so; if not, let them that should reward

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: valour bear the sin upon their own heads. Ill take

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: it upon my death, I gave him this wound in the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: thigh: if the man were alive and would deny it,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: zounds, I would make him eat a piece of my sword.

speaker: LANCASTER
text_entry: This is the strangest tale that ever I heard.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: This is the strangest fellow, brother John.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Come, bring your luggage nobly on your back:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: For my part, if a lie may do thee grace,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Ill gild it with the happiest terms I have.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: A retreat is sounded

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: The trumpet sounds retreat; the day is ours.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Come, brother, let us to the highest of the field,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: To see what friends are living, who are dead.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Exeunt PRINCE HENRY and LANCASTER

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Ill follow, as they say, for reward. He that

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: rewards me, God reward him! If I do grow great,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Ill grow less; for Ill purge, and leave sack, and

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: live cleanly as a nobleman should do.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Exit

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: SCENE V. Another part of the field.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: The trumpets sound. Enter KING HENRY IV, PRINCE  HENRY, LORD JOHN LANCASTER, EARL OF WESTMORELAND, with WORCESTER and VERNON prisoners

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Thus ever did rebellion find rebuke.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Ill-spirited Worcester! did not we send grace,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Pardon and terms of love to all of you?

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: And wouldst thou turn our offers contrary?

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Misuse the tenor of thy kinsmans trust?

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Three knights upon our party slain to-day,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: A noble earl and many a creature else

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Had been alive this hour,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: If like a Christian thou hadst truly borne

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Betwixt our armies true intelligence.

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: What I have done my safety urged me to;

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: And I embrace this fortune patiently,

speaker: EARL OF WORCESTER
text_entry: Since not to be avoided it falls on me.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Bear Worcester to the death and Vernon too:

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Other offenders we will pause upon.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Exeunt WORCESTER and VERNON, guarded

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: How goes the field?

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: The noble Scot, Lord Douglas, when he saw

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: The fortune of the day quite turnd from him,

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: The noble Percy slain, and all his men

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Upon the foot of fear, fled with the rest;

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: And falling from a hill, he was so bruised

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: That the pursuers took him. At my tent

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: The Douglas is; and I beseech your grace

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: I may dispose of him.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: With all my heart.

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Then, brother John of Lancaster, to you

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: This honourable bounty shall belong:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Go to the Douglas, and deliver him

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Up to his pleasure, ransomless and free:

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: His valour shown upon our crests to-day

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Hath taught us how to cherish such high deeds

speaker: PRINCE HENRY
text_entry: Even in the bosom of our adversaries.

speaker: LANCASTER
text_entry: I thank your grace for this high courtesy,

speaker: LANCASTER
text_entry: Which I shall give away immediately.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Then this remains, that we divide our power.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: You, son John, and my cousin Westmoreland

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Towards York shall bend you with your dearest speed,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: To meet Northumberland and the prelate Scroop,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Who, as we hear, are busily in arms:

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Myself and you, son Harry, will towards Wales,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: To fight with Glendower and the Earl of March.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Rebellion in this land shall lose his sway,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Meeting the cheque of such another day:

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: And since this business so fair is done,

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Let us not leave till all our own be won.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: ACT I

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: SCENE I. Westminster Abbey.

speaker: KING HENRY IV
text_entry: Dead March. Enter the Funeral of KING HENRY the  Fifth, attended on by Dukes of BEDFORD, Regent of  France; GLOUCESTER, Protector; and EXETER, Earl of WARWICK, the BISHOP OF WINCHESTER, Heralds,  and c

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: Hung be the heavens with black, yield day to night!

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: Comets, importing change of times and states,

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: Brandish your crystal tresses in the sky,

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: And with them scourge the bad revolting stars

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: That have consented unto Henrys death!

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: King Henry the Fifth, too famous to live long!

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: England neer lost a king of so much worth.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: England neer had a king until his time.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Virtue he had, deserving to command:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: His brandishd sword did blind men with his beams:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: His arms spread wider than a dragons wings;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
