speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: I trust ere long to choke thee with thine own

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: And make thee curse the harvest of that corn.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: Your grace may starve perhaps before that time.

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: O, let no words, but deeds, revenge this treason!

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: What will you do, good grey-beard? break a lance,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: And run a tilt at death within a chair?

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Foul fiend of France, and hag of all despite,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Encompassd with thy lustful paramours!

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Becomes it thee to taunt his valiant age

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And twit with cowardice a man half dead?

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Damsel, Ill have a bout with you again,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Or else let Talbot perish with this shame.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Are ye so hot, sir? yet, Pucelle, hold thy peace;

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: If Talbot do but thunder, rain will follow.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: The English whisper together in council

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: God speed the parliament! who shall be the speaker?

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Dare ye come forth and meet us in the field?

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Belike your lordship takes us then for fools,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: To try if that our own be ours or no.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: I speak not to that railing Hecate,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: But unto thee, Alencon, and the rest;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Will ye, like soldiers, come and fight it out?

speaker: ALENCON
text_entry: Signior, no.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Signior, hang! base muleters of France!

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Like peasant foot-boys do they keep the walls

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And dare not take up arms like gentlemen.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Away, captains! lets get us from the walls;

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: For Talbot means no goodness by his looks.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: God be wi you, my lord! we came but to tell you

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: That we are here.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Exeunt from the walls

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And there will we be too, ere it be long,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Or else reproach be Talbots greatest fame!

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Vow, Burgundy, by honour of thy house,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Prickd on by public wrongs sustaind in France,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Either to get the town again or die:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And I, as sure as English Henry lives

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And as his father here was conqueror,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: As sure as in this late-betrayed town

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Great Coeur-de-lions heart was buried,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: So sure I swear to get the town or die.

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: My vows are equal partners with thy vows.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: But, ere we go, regard this dying prince,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: The valiant Duke of Bedford. Come, my lord,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: We will bestow you in some better place,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Fitter for sickness and for crazy age.

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: Lord Talbot, do not so dishonour me:

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: Here will I sit before the walls of Rouen

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: And will be partner of your weal or woe.

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: Courageous Bedford, let us now persuade you.

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: Not to be gone from hence; for once I read

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: That stout Pendragon in his litter sick

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: Came to the field and vanquished his foes:

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: Methinks I should revive the soldiers hearts,

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: Because I ever found them as myself.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Undaunted spirit in a dying breast!

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Then be it so: heavens keep old Bedford safe!

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And now no more ado, brave Burgundy,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: But gather we our forces out of hand

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And set upon our boasting enemy.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Exeunt all but BEDFORD and Attendants

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: An alarum: excursions. Enter FASTOLFE and a Captain

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Whither away, Sir John Fastolfe, in such haste?

speaker: FASTOLFE
text_entry: Whither away! to save myself by flight:

speaker: FASTOLFE
text_entry: We are like to have the overthrow again.

speaker: Captain
text_entry: What! will you fly, and leave Lord Talbot?

speaker: FASTOLFE
text_entry: Ay,

speaker: FASTOLFE
text_entry: All the Talbots in the world, to save my life!

speaker: FASTOLFE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Cowardly knight! ill fortune follow thee!

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Exit

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Retreat: excursions. JOAN LA PUCELLE, ALENCON, and CHARLES fly

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: Now, quiet soul, depart when heaven please,

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: For I have seen our enemies overthrow.

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: What is the trust or strength of foolish man?

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: They that of late were daring with their scoffs

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: Are glad and fain by flight to save themselves.

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: BEDFORD dies, and is carried in by two in his chair

speaker: BEDFORD
text_entry: An alarum. Re-enter TALBOT, BURGUNDY, and the rest

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Lost, and recoverd in a day again!

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: This is a double honour, Burgundy:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Yet heavens have glory for this victory!

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: Warlike and martial Talbot, Burgundy

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: Enshrines thee in his heart and there erects

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: Thy noble deeds as valours monuments.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Thanks, gentle duke. But where is Pucelle now?

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: I think her old familiar is asleep:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Now wheres the Bastards braves, and Charles his gleeks?

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: What, all amort? Rouen hangs her head for grief

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: That such a valiant company are fled.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Now will we take some order in the town,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Placing therein some expert officers,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And then depart to Paris to the king,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: For there young Henry with his nobles lie.

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: What wills Lord Talbot pleaseth Burgundy.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: But yet, before we go, lets not forget

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: The noble Duke of Bedford late deceased,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: But see his exequies fulfilld in Rouen:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: A braver soldier never couched lance,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: A gentler heart did never sway in court;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: But kings and mightiest potentates must die,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: For thats the end of human misery.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: SCENE III. The plains near Rouen.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Enter CHARLES, the BASTARD OF ORLEANS, ALENCON, JOAN LA PUCELLE, and forces

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Dismay not, princes, at this accident,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Nor grieve that Rouen is so recovered:

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Care is no cure, but rather corrosive,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: For things that are not to be remedied.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Let frantic Talbot triumph for a while

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: And like a peacock sweep along his tail;

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Well pull his plumes and take away his train,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: If Dauphin and the rest will be but ruled.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: We have been guided by thee hitherto,

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: And of thy cunning had no diffidence:

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: One sudden foil shall never breed distrust.

speaker: BASTARD OF ORLEANS
text_entry: Search out thy wit for secret policies,

speaker: BASTARD OF ORLEANS
text_entry: And we will make thee famous through the world.

speaker: ALENCON
text_entry: Well set thy statue in some holy place,

speaker: ALENCON
text_entry: And have thee reverenced like a blessed saint:

speaker: ALENCON
text_entry: Employ thee then, sweet virgin, for our good.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Then thus it must be; this doth Joan devise:

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: By fair persuasions mixd with sugard words

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: We will entice the Duke of Burgundy

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: To leave the Talbot and to follow us.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: Ay, marry, sweeting, if we could do that,

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: France were no place for Henrys warriors;

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: Nor should that nation boast it so with us,

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: But be extirped from our provinces.

speaker: ALENCON
text_entry: For ever should they be expulsed from France

speaker: ALENCON
text_entry: And not have title of an earldom here.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Your honours shall perceive how I will work

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: To bring this matter to the wished end.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Drum sounds afar off

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Hark! by the sound of drum you may perceive

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Their powers are marching unto Paris-ward.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Here sound an English march. Enter, and pass over at a distance, TALBOT and his forces

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: There goes the Talbot, with his colours spread,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: And all the troops of English after him.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: French march. Enter BURGUNDY and forces

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Now in the rearward comes the duke and his:

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Fortune in favour makes him lag behind.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Summon a parley; we will talk with him.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Trumpets sound a parley

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: A parley with the Duke of Burgundy!

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: Who craves a parley with the Burgundy?

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: The princely Charles of France, thy countryman.

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: What sayst thou, Charles? for I am marching hence.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: Speak, Pucelle, and enchant him with thy words.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Brave Burgundy, undoubted hope of France!

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Stay, let thy humble handmaid speak to thee.

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: Speak on; but be not over-tedious.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Look on thy country, look on fertile France,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: And see the cities and the towns defaced

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: By wasting ruin of the cruel foe.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: As looks the mother on her lowly babe

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: When death doth close his tender dying eyes,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: See, see the pining malady of France;

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Behold the wounds, the most unnatural wounds,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Which thou thyself hast given her woful breast.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: O, turn thy edged sword another way;

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Strike those that hurt, and hurt not those that help.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: One drop of blood drawn from thy countrys bosom

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Should grieve thee more than streams of foreign gore:

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Return thee therefore with a flood of tears,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: And wash away thy countrys stained spots.

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: Either she hath bewitchd me with her words,

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: Or nature makes me suddenly relent.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Besides, all French and France exclaims on thee,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Doubting thy birth and lawful progeny.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Who jointst thou with but with a lordly nation

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: That will not trust thee but for profits sake?

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: When Talbot hath set footing once in France

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: And fashiond thee that instrument of ill,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Who then but English Henry will be lord

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: And thou be thrust out like a fugitive?

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Call we to mind, and mark but this for proof,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Was not the Duke of Orleans thy foe?

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: And was he not in England prisoner?

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: But when they heard he was thine enemy,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: They set him free without his ransom paid,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: In spite of Burgundy and all his friends.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: See, then, thou fightst against thy countrymen

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: And jointst with them will be thy slaughtermen.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Come, come, return; return, thou wandering lord:

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Charles and the rest will take thee in their arms.

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: I am vanquished; these haughty words of hers

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: Have batterd me like roaring cannon-shot,

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: And made me almost yield upon my knees.

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: Forgive me, country, and sweet countrymen,

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: And, lords, accept this hearty kind embrace:

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: My forces and my power of men are yours:

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: So farewell, Talbot; Ill no longer trust thee.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: [Aside]  Done like a Frenchman: turn, and turn again!

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: Welcome, brave duke! thy friendship makes us fresh.

speaker: BASTARD OF ORLEANS
text_entry: And doth beget new courage in our breasts.

speaker: ALENCON
text_entry: Pucelle hath bravely playd her part in this,

speaker: ALENCON
text_entry: And doth deserve a coronet of gold.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: Now let us on, my lords, and join our powers,

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: And seek how we may prejudice the foe.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: SCENE IV. Paris. The palace.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: Enter KING HENRY VI, GLOUCESTER, BISHOP OF  WINCHESTER, YORK, SUFFOLK, SOMERSET, WARWICK,  EXETER, VERNONBASSET, and others. To them with his Soldiers, TALBOT

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: My gracious prince, and honourable peers,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Hearing of your arrival in this realm,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: I have awhile given truce unto my wars,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: To do my duty to my sovereign:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: In sign, whereof, this arm, that hath reclaimd

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: To your obedience fifty fortresses,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Twelve cities and seven walled towns of strength,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Beside five hundred prisoners of esteem,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Lets fall his sword before your highness feet,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And with submissive loyalty of heart

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Ascribes the glory of his conquest got

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: First to my God and next unto your grace.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Kneels

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Is this the Lord Talbot, uncle Gloucester,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: That hath so long been resident in France?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Yes, if it please your majesty, my liege.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Welcome, brave captain and victorious lord!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: When I was young, as yet I am not old,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: I do remember how my father said

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: A stouter champion never handled sword.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Long since we were resolved of your truth,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Your faithful service and your toil in war;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Yet never have you tasted our reward,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Or been reguerdond with so much as thanks,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Because till now we never saw your face:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Therefore, stand up; and, for these good deserts,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: We here create you Earl of Shrewsbury;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And in our coronation take your place.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Sennet. Flourish. Exeunt all but VERNON and BASSET

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Now, sir, to you, that were so hot at sea,

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Disgracing of these colours that I wear

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: In honour of my noble Lord of York:

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Darest thou maintain the former words thou spakest?

speaker: BASSET
text_entry: Yes, sir; as well as you dare patronage

speaker: BASSET
text_entry: The envious barking of your saucy tongue

speaker: BASSET
text_entry: Against my lord the Duke of Somerset.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Sirrah, thy lord I honour as he is.

speaker: BASSET
text_entry: Why, what is he? as good a man as York.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Hark ye; not so: in witness, take ye that.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Strikes him

speaker: BASSET
text_entry: Villain, thou knowst the law of arms is such

speaker: BASSET
text_entry: That whoso draws a sword, tis present death,

speaker: BASSET
text_entry: Or else this blow should broach thy dearest blood.

speaker: BASSET
text_entry: But Ill unto his majesty, and crave

speaker: BASSET
text_entry: I may have liberty to venge this wrong;

speaker: BASSET
text_entry: When thou shalt see Ill meet thee to thy cost.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Well, miscreant, Ill be there as soon as you;

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: And, after, meet you sooner than you would.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: ACT IV

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: SCENE I. Paris. A hall of state.

speaker: VERNON
text_entry: Enter KING HENRY VI, GLOUCESTER, BISHOP OF  WINCHESTER, YORK, SUFFOLK, SOMERSET, WARWICK, TALBOT, EXETER, the Governor, of Paris, and others

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Lord bishop, set the crown upon his head.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: BISHOP

speaker: OF WINCHESTER
text_entry: God save King Henry, of that name the sixth!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Now, governor of Paris, take your oath,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: That you elect no other king but him;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Esteem none friends but such as are his friends,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And none your foes but such as shall pretend

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Malicious practises against his state:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: This shall ye do, so help you righteous God!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Enter FASTOLFE

speaker: FASTOLFE
text_entry: My gracious sovereign, as I rode from Calais,

speaker: FASTOLFE
text_entry: To haste unto your coronation,

speaker: FASTOLFE
text_entry: A letter was deliverd to my hands,

speaker: FASTOLFE
text_entry: Writ to your grace from the Duke of Burgundy.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Shame to the Duke of Burgundy and thee!

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: I vowd, base knight, when I did meet thee next,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: To tear the garter from thy cravens leg,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Plucking it off

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Which I have done, because unworthily

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Thou wast installed in that high degree.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Pardon me, princely Henry, and the rest

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: This dastard, at the battle of Patay,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: When but in all I was six thousand strong

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And that the French were almost ten to one,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Before we met or that a stroke was given,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Like to a trusty squire did run away:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: In which assault we lost twelve hundred men;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Myself and divers gentlemen beside

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Were there surprised and taken prisoners.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Then judge, great lords, if I have done amiss;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Or whether that such cowards ought to wear

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: This ornament of knighthood, yea or no.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To say the truth, this fact was infamous

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And ill beseeming any common man,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Much more a knight, a captain and a leader.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: When first this order was ordaind, my lords,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Knights of the garter were of noble birth,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Valiant and virtuous, full of haughty courage,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Such as were grown to credit by the wars;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Not fearing death, nor shrinking for distress,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: But always resolute in most extremes.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: He then that is not furnishd in this sort

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Doth but usurp the sacred name of knight,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Profaning this most honourable order,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And should, if I were worthy to be judge,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Be quite degraded, like a hedge-born swain

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: That doth presume to boast of gentle blood.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Stain to thy countrymen, thou hearst thy doom!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Be packing, therefore, thou that wast a knight:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Henceforth we banish thee, on pain of death.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Exit FASTOLFE

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And now, my lord protector, view the letter

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Sent from our uncle Duke of Burgundy.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: What means his grace, that he hath changed his style?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: No more but, plain and bluntly, To the king!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Hath he forgot he is his sovereign?

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And Ill direct thee how thou shalt escape

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: By sudden flight: come, dally not, be gone.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Is my name Talbot? and am I your son?

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: And shall I fly? O if you love my mother,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Dishonour not her honourable name,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: To make a bastard and a slave of me!

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: The world will say, he is not Talbots blood,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: That basely fled when noble Talbot stood.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Fly, to revenge my death, if I be slain.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: He that flies so will neer return again.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: If we both stay, we both are sure to die.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Then let me stay; and, father, do you fly:

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Your loss is great, so your regard should be;

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: My worth unknown, no loss is known in me.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Upon my death the French can little boast;

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: In yours they will, in you all hopes are lost.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Flight cannot stain the honour you have won;

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: But mine it will, that no exploit have done:

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: You fled for vantage, everyone will swear;

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: But, if I bow, theyll say it was for fear.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: There is no hope that ever I will stay,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: If the first hour I shrink and run away.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Here on my knee I beg mortality,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Rather than life preserved with infamy.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Shall all thy mothers hopes lie in one tomb?

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Ay, rather than Ill shame my mothers womb.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Upon my blessing, I command thee go.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: To fight I will, but not to fly the foe.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Part of thy father may be saved in thee.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: No part of him but will be shame in me.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Thou never hadst renown, nor canst not lose it.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Yes, your renowned name: shall flight abuse it?

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Thy fathers charge shall clear thee from that stain.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: You cannot witness for me, being slain.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: If death be so apparent, then both fly.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And leave my followers here to fight and die?

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: My age was never tainted with such shame.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: And shall my youth be guilty of such blame?

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: No more can I be severd from your side,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Than can yourself yourself in twain divide:

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Stay, go, do what you will, the like do I;

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: For live I will not, if my father die.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Then here I take my leave of thee, fair son,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Born to eclipse thy life this afternoon.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Come, side by side together live and die.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And soul with soul from France to heaven fly.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: SCENE VI. A field of battle.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Alarum: excursions, wherein JOHN TALBOT is hemmed about, and TALBOT rescues him

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Saint George and victory! fight, soldiers, fight.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: The regent hath with Talbot broke his word

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And left us to the rage of France his sword.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Where is John Talbot? Pause, and take thy breath;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: I gave thee life and rescued thee from death.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: O, twice my father, twice am I thy son!

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: The life thou gavest me first was lost and done,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Till with thy warlike sword, despite of late,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: To my determined time thou gavest new date.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: When from the Dauphins crest thy sword struck fire,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: It warmd thy fathers heart with proud desire

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Of bold-faced victory. Then leaden age,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Quickend with youthful spleen and warlike rage,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Beat down Alencon, Orleans, Burgundy,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And from the pride of Gallia rescued thee.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: The ireful bastard Orleans, that drew blood

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: From thee, my boy, and had the maidenhood

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Of thy first fight, I soon encountered,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And interchanging blows I quickly shed

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Some of his bastard blood; and in disgrace

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Bespoke him thus; Contaminated, base

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And misbegotten blood I spill of thine,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Mean and right poor, for that pure blood of mine

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Which thou didst force from Talbot, my brave boy:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Here, purposing the Bastard to destroy,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Came in strong rescue. Speak, thy fathers care,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Art thou not weary, John? how dost thou fare?

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Wilt thou yet leave the battle, boy, and fly,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Now thou art seald the son of chivalry?

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Fly, to revenge my death when I am dead:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: The help of one stands me in little stead.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: O, too much folly is it, well I wot,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: To hazard all our lives in one small boat!

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: If I to-day die not with Frenchmens rage,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: To-morrow I shall die with mickle age:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: By me they nothing gain an if I stay;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Tis but the shortening of my life one day:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: In thee thy mother dies, our households name,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: My deaths revenge, thy youth, and Englands fame:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: All these and more we hazard by thy stay;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: All these are saved if thou wilt fly away.

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: The sword of Orleans hath not made me smart;

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: These words of yours draw life-blood from my heart:

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: On that advantage, bought with such a shame,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: To save a paltry life and slay bright fame,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Before young Talbot from old Talbot fly,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: The coward horse that bears me fail and die!

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: And like me to the peasant boys of France,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: To be shames scorn and subject of mischance!

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Surely, by all the glory you have won,

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: An if I fly, I am not Talbots son:

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: Then talk no more of flight, it is no boot;

speaker: JOHN TALBOT
text_entry: If son to Talbot, die at Talbots foot.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Then follow thou thy desperate sire of Crete,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Thou Icarus; thy life to me is sweet:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: If thou wilt fight, fight by thy fathers side;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And, commendable proved, lets die in pride.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: SCENE VII. Another part of the field.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Alarum: excursions. Enter TALBOT led by a Servant

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Where is my other life? mine own is gone;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: O, wheres young Talbot? where is valiant John?

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Triumphant death, smeard with captivity,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Young Talbots valour makes me smile at thee:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: When he perceived me shrink and on my knee,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: His bloody sword he brandishd over me,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And, like a hungry lion, did commence

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Rough deeds of rage and stern impatience;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: But when my angry guardant stood alone,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Tendering my ruin and assaild of none,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Dizzy-eyed fury and great rage of heart

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Suddenly made him from my side to start

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Into the clustering battle of the French;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: And in that sea of blood my boy did drench

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: His over-mounting spirit, and there died,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: My Icarus, my blossom, in his pride.

speaker: Servant
text_entry: O, my dear lord, lo, where your son is borne!

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Enter Soldiers, with the body of JOHN TALBOT

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Thou antic death, which laughst us here to scorn,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Anon, from thy insulting tyranny,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Coupled in bonds of perpetuity,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Two Talbots, winged through the lither sky,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: In thy despite shall scape mortality.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: O, thou, whose wounds become hard-favourd death,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Speak to thy father ere thou yield thy breath!

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Brave death by speaking, whether he will or no;

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Imagine him a Frenchman and thy foe.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Poor boy! he smiles, methinks, as who should say,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Had death been French, then death had died to-day.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Come, come and lay him in his fathers arms:

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: My spirit can no longer bear these harms.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Soldiers, adieu! I have what I would have,

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Now my old arms are young John Talbots grave.

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Dies

speaker: TALBOT
text_entry: Enter CHARLES, ALENCON, BURGUNDY, BASTARD OF ORLEANS, JOAN LA PUCELLE, and forces

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: Had York and Somerset brought rescue in,

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: We should have found a bloody day of this.

speaker: BASTARD OF ORLEANS
text_entry: How the young whelp of Talbots, raging-wood,

speaker: BASTARD OF ORLEANS
text_entry: Did flesh his puny sword in Frenchmens blood!

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Once I encounterd him, and thus I said:

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Thou maiden youth, be vanquishd by a maid:

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: But, with a proud majestical high scorn,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: He answerd thus: Young Talbot was not born

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: To be the pillage of a giglot wench:

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: So, rushing in the bowels of the French,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: He left me proudly, as unworthy fight.

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: Doubtless he would have made a noble knight;

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: See, where he lies inhearsed in the arms

speaker: BURGUNDY
text_entry: Of the most bloody nurser of his harms!

speaker: BASTARD OF ORLEANS
text_entry: Hew them to pieces, hack their bones asunder

speaker: BASTARD OF ORLEANS
text_entry: Whose life was Englands glory, Gallias wonder.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: O, no, forbear! for that which we have fled

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: During the life, let us not wrong it dead.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: Enter Sir William LUCY, attended; Herald of the French preceding

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Herald, conduct me to the Dauphins tent,

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: To know who hath obtained the glory of the day.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: On what submissive message art thou sent?

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Submission, Dauphin! tis a mere French word;

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: We English warriors wot not what it means.

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: I come to know what prisoners thou hast taen

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: And to survey the bodies of the dead.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: For prisoners askst thou? hell our prison is.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: But tell me whom thou seekst.

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: But wheres the great Alcides of the field,

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Valiant Lord Talbot, Earl of Shrewsbury,

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Created, for his rare success in arms,

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Great Earl of Washford, Waterford and Valence;

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Lord Talbot of Goodrig and Urchinfield,

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Lord Strange of Blackmere, Lord Verdun of Alton,

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Lord Cromwell of Wingfield, Lord Furnival of Sheffield,

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: The thrice-victorious Lord of Falconbridge;

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Knight of the noble order of Saint George,

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Worthy Saint Michael and the Golden Fleece;

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Great marshal to Henry the Sixth

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Of all his wars within the realm of France?

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Here is a silly stately style indeed!

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: The Turk, that two and fifty kingdoms hath,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Writes not so tedious a style as this.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Him that thou magnifiest with all these titles

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: Stinking and fly-blown lies here at our feet.

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Is Talbot slain, the Frenchmens only scourge,

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Your kingdoms terror and black Nemesis?

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: O, were mine eyeballs into bullets turnd,

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: That I in rage might shoot them at your faces!

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: O, that I could but call these dead to life!

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: It were enough to fright the realm of France:

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Were but his picture left amongst you here,

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: It would amaze the proudest of you all.

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Give me their bodies, that I may bear them hence

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: And give them burial as beseems their worth.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: I think this upstart is old Talbots ghost,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: He speaks with such a proud commanding spirit.

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: For Gods sake let him have em; to keep them here,

speaker: JOAN LA PUCELLE
text_entry: They would but stink, and putrefy the air.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: Go, take their bodies hence.

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: Ill bear them hence; but from their ashes shall be reard

speaker: LUCY
text_entry: A phoenix that shall make all France afeard.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: So we be rid of them, do with em what thou wilt.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: And now to Paris, in this conquering vein:

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: All will be ours, now bloody Talbots slain.

speaker: CHARLES
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: OF WINCHESTER

text_entry: in France, Before--

text_entry: My Lord of Gloucester, now ye grow too hot:

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: It was the pleasure of my lord the King.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: My Lord of Winchester, I know your mind;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Tis not my speeches that you do mislike,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But tis my presence that doth trouble ye.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Rancour will out: proud prelate, in thy face

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I see thy fury: if I longer stay,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: We shall begin our ancient bickerings.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Lordings, farewell; and say, when I am gone,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I prophesied France will be lost ere long.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Exit

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: So, there goes our protector in a rage.

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Tis known to you he is mine enemy,

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Nay, more, an enemy unto you all,

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: And no great friend, I fear me, to the king.

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Consider, lords, he is the next of blood,

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: And heir apparent to the English crown:

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Had Henry got an empire by his marriage,

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: And all the wealthy kingdoms of the west,

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Theres reason he should be displeased at it.

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Look to it, lords! let not his smoothing words

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Bewitch your hearts; be wise and circumspect.

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: What though the common people favour him,

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Calling him Humphrey, the good Duke of

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Gloucester,

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Clapping their hands, and crying with loud voice,

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Jesu maintain your royal excellence!

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: With God preserve the good Duke Humphrey!

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: I fear me, lords, for all this flattering gloss,

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: He will be found a dangerous protector.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Why should he, then, protect our sovereign,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: He being of age to govern of himself?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Cousin of Somerset, join you with me,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And all together, with the Duke of Suffolk,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Well quickly hoise Duke Humphrey from his seat.

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: This weighty business will not brook delay:

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Ill to the Duke of Suffolk presently.

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Exit

speaker: SOMERSET
text_entry: Cousin of Buckingham, though Humphreys pride

speaker: SOMERSET
text_entry: And greatness of his place be grief to us,

speaker: SOMERSET
text_entry: Yet let us watch the haughty cardinal:

speaker: SOMERSET
text_entry: His insolence is more intolerable

speaker: SOMERSET
text_entry: Than all the princes in the land beside:

speaker: SOMERSET
text_entry: If Gloucester be displaced, hell be protector.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Or thou or I, Somerset, will be protector,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Despite Duke Humphrey or the cardinal.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Exeunt BUCKINGHAM and SOMERSET

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Pride went before, ambition follows him.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: While these do labour for their own preferment,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Behoves it us to labour for the realm.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: I never saw but Humphrey Duke of Gloucester

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Did bear him like a noble gentleman.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Oft have I seen the haughty cardinal,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: More like a soldier than a man o the church,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: As stout and proud as he were lord of all,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Swear like a ruffian and demean himself

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Unlike the ruler of a commonweal.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Warwick, my son, the comfort of my age,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Thy deeds, thy plainness and thy housekeeping,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Hath won the greatest favour of the commons,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Excepting none but good Duke Humphrey:

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: And, brother York, thy acts in Ireland,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: In bringing them to civil discipline,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Thy late exploits done in the heart of France,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: When thou wert regent for our sovereign,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Have made thee feard and honourd of the people:

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Join we together, for the public good,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: In what we can, to bridle and suppress

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: The pride of Suffolk and the cardinal,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: With Somersets and Buckinghams ambition;

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: And, as we may, cherish Duke Humphreys deeds,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: While they do tend the profit of the land.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: So God help Warwick, as he loves the land,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And common profit of his country!

speaker: YORK
text_entry: [Aside]  And so says York, for he hath greatest cause.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Then lets make haste away, and look unto the main.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Unto the main! O father, Maine is lost;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: That Maine which by main force Warwick did win,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And would have kept so long as breath did last!

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Main chance, father, you meant; but I meant Maine,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Which I will win from France, or else be slain,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Exeunt WARWICK and SALISBURY

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Anjou and Maine are given to the French;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Paris is lost; the state of Normandy

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Stands on a tickle point, now they are gone:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Suffolk concluded on the articles,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The peers agreed, and Henry was well pleased

speaker: YORK
text_entry: To change two dukedoms for a dukes fair daughter.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: I cannot blame them all: what ist to them?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Tis thine they give away, and not their own.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Pirates may make cheap pennyworths of their pillage

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And purchase friends and give to courtezans,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Still revelling like lords till all be gone;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: While as the silly owner of the goods

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Weeps over them and wrings his hapless hands

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And shakes his head and trembling stands aloof,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: While all is shared and all is borne away,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Ready to starve and dare not touch his own:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: So York must sit and fret and bite his tongue,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: While his own lands are bargaind for and sold.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Methinks the realms of England, France and Ireland

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Bear that proportion to my flesh and blood

speaker: YORK
text_entry: As did the fatal brand Althaea burnd

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Unto the princes heart of Calydon.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Anjou and Maine both given unto the French!

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Cold news for me, for I had hope of France,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Even as I have of fertile Englands soil.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: A day will come when York shall claim his own;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And therefore I will take the Nevils parts

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And make a show of love to proud Duke Humphrey,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And, when I spy advantage, claim the crown,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: For thats the golden mark I seek to hit:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Nor shall proud Lancaster usurp my right,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Nor hold the sceptre in his childish fist,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Nor wear the diadem upon his head,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Whose church-like humours fits not for a crown.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Then, York, be still awhile, till time do serve:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Watch thou and wake when others be asleep,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: To pry into the secrets of the state;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Till Henry, surfeiting in joys of love,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: With his new bride and Englands dear-bought queen,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And Humphrey with the peers be falln at jars:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Then will I raise aloft the milk-white rose,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: With whose sweet smell the air shall be perfumed;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And in my standard bear the arms of York

speaker: YORK
text_entry: To grapple with the house of Lancaster;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And, force perforce, Ill make him yield the crown,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Whose bookish rule hath pulld fair England down.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Exit

speaker: YORK
text_entry: SCENE II. GLOUCESTERS house.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Enter GLOUCESTER and his DUCHESS

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Why droops my lord, like over-ripend corn,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Hanging the head at Ceres plenteous load?

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Why doth the great Duke Humphrey knit his brows,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: As frowning at the favours of the world?

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Why are thine eyes fixed to the sullen earth,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Gazing on that which seems to dim thy sight?

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: What seest thou there? King Henrys diadem,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Enchased with all the honours of the world?

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: If so, gaze on, and grovel on thy face,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Until thy head be circled with the same.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Put forth thy hand, reach at the glorious gold.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: What, ist too short? Ill lengthen it with mine:

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And, having both together heaved it up,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Well both together lift our heads to heaven,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And never more abase our sight so low

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: As to vouchsafe one glance unto the ground.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: O Nell, sweet Nell, if thou dost love thy lord,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Banish the canker of ambitious thoughts.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And may that thought, when I imagine ill

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Against my king and nephew, virtuous Henry,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Be my last breathing in this mortal world!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: My troublous dream this night doth make me sad.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: What dreamd my lord? tell me, and Ill requite it

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: With sweet rehearsal of my mornings dream.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Methought this staff, mine office-badge in court,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Was broke in twain; by whom I have forgot,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But, as I think, it was by the cardinal;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And on the pieces of the broken wand

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Were placed the heads of Edmund Duke of Somerset,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And William de la Pole, first duke of Suffolk.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: This was my dream: what it doth bode, God knows.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Tut, this was nothing but an argument

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: That he that breaks a stick of Gloucesters grove

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Shall lose his head for his presumption.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: But list to me, my Humphrey, my sweet duke:

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Methought I sat in seat of majesty

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: In the cathedral church of Westminster,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And in that chair where kings and queens are crownd;

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Where Henry and dame Margaret kneeld to me

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And on my head did set the diadem.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Nay, Eleanor, then must I chide outright:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Presumptuous dame, ill-nurtured Eleanor,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Art thou not second woman in the realm,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And the protectors wife, beloved of him?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Hast thou not worldly pleasure at command,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Above the reach or compass of thy thought?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And wilt thou still be hammering treachery,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To tumble down thy husband and thyself

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: From top of honour to disgraces feet?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Away from me, and let me hear no more!

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: What, what, my lord! are you so choleric

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: With Eleanor, for telling but her dream?

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Next time Ill keep my dreams unto myself,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And not be chequed.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Nay, be not angry; I am pleased again.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Enter Messenger

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: My lord protector, tis his highness pleasure

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: You do prepare to ride unto Saint Albans,

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Where as the king and queen do mean to hawk.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I go. Come, Nell, thou wilt ride with us?

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Yes, my good lord, Ill follow presently.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Exeunt GLOUCESTER and Messenger

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Follow I must; I cannot go before,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: While Gloucester bears this base and humble mind.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Were I a man, a duke, and next of blood,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: I would remove these tedious stumbling-blocks

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And smooth my way upon their headless necks;

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And, being a woman, I will not be slack

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: To play my part in Fortunes pageant.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Where are you there? Sir John! nay, fear not, man,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: We are alone; heres none but thee and I.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Enter HUME

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Jesus preserve your royal majesty!

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: What sayst thou? majesty! I am but grace.

speaker: HUME
text_entry: But, by the grace of God, and Humes advice,

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Your graces title shall be multiplied.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: What sayst thou, man? hast thou as yet conferrd

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: With Margery Jourdain, the cunning witch,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: With Roger Bolingbroke, the conjurer?

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And will they undertake to do me good?

speaker: HUME
text_entry: This they have promised, to show your highness

speaker: HUME
text_entry: A spirit raised from depth of under-ground,

speaker: HUME
text_entry: That shall make answer to such questions

speaker: HUME
text_entry: As by your grace shall be propounded him.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: It is enough; Ill think upon the questions:

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: When from St. Albans we do make return,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Well see these things effected to the full.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Here, Hume, take this reward; make merry, man,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: With thy confederates in this weighty cause.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Hume must make merry with the duchess gold;

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Marry, and shall. But how now, Sir John Hume!

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Seal up your lips, and give no words but mum:

speaker: HUME
text_entry: The business asketh silent secrecy.

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Dame Eleanor gives gold to bring the witch:

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Gold cannot come amiss, were she a devil.

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Yet have I gold flies from another coast;

speaker: HUME
text_entry: I dare not say, from the rich cardinal

speaker: HUME
text_entry: And from the great and new-made Duke of Suffolk,

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Yet I do find it so; for to be plain,

speaker: HUME
text_entry: They, knowing Dame Eleanors aspiring humour,

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Have hired me to undermine the duchess

speaker: HUME
text_entry: And buz these conjurations in her brain.

speaker: HUME
text_entry: They say A crafty knave does need no broker;

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Yet am I Suffolk and the cardinals broker.

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Hume, if you take not heed, you shall go near

speaker: HUME
text_entry: To call them both a pair of crafty knaves.

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Well, so it stands; and thus, I fear, at last

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Humes knavery will be the duchess wreck,

speaker: HUME
text_entry: And her attainture will be Humphreys fall:

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Sort how it will, I shall have gold for all.

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Exit

speaker: HUME
text_entry: SCENE III. The palace.

speaker: HUME
text_entry: Enter three or four Petitioners, PETER, the Armourers man, being one

speaker: First Petitioner
text_entry: My masters, lets stand close: my lord protector

speaker: First Petitioner
text_entry: will come this way by and by, and then we may deliver

speaker: First Petitioner
text_entry: our supplications in the quill.

speaker: Second Petitioner
text_entry: Marry, the Lord protect him, for hes a good man!

speaker: Second Petitioner
text_entry: Jesu bless him!

speaker: Second Petitioner
text_entry: Enter SUFFOLK and QUEEN MARGARET

speaker: PETER
text_entry: Here a comes, methinks, and the queen with him.

speaker: PETER
text_entry: Ill be the first, sure.

speaker: Second Petitioner
text_entry: Come back, fool; this is the Duke of Suffolk, and

speaker: Second Petitioner
text_entry: not my lord protector.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: How now, fellow! wouldst anything with me?

speaker: First Petitioner
text_entry: I pray, my lord, pardon me; I took ye for my lord

speaker: First Petitioner
text_entry: protector.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: [Reading]  To my Lord Protector! Are your

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: supplications to his lordship? Let me see them:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: what is thine?

speaker: First Petitioner
text_entry: Mine is, ant please your grace, against John

speaker: First Petitioner
text_entry: Goodman, my lord cardinals man, for keeping my

speaker: First Petitioner
text_entry: house, and lands, and wife and all, from me.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Thy wife, too! thats some wrong, indeed. Whats

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: yours? Whats here!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Reads

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Against the Duke of Suffolk, for enclosing the

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: commons of Melford. How now, sir knave!

speaker: Second Petitioner
text_entry: Alas, sir, I am but a poor petitioner of our whole township.

speaker: PETER
text_entry: [Giving his petition]  Against my master, Thomas

speaker: PETER
text_entry: Horner, for saying that the Duke of York was rightful

speaker: PETER
text_entry: heir to the crown.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: What sayst thou? did the Duke of York say he was

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: rightful heir to the crown?

speaker: PETER
text_entry: That my master was? no, forsooth: my master said

speaker: PETER
text_entry: that he was, and that the king was an usurper.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Who is there?

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Enter Servant

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Take this fellow in, and send for

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: his master with a pursuivant presently: well hear

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: more of your matter before the King.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Exit Servant with PETER

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And as for you, that love to be protected

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Under the wings of our protectors grace,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Begin your suits anew, and sue to him.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Tears the supplication

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Away, base cullions! Suffolk, let them go.

speaker: ALL
text_entry: Come, lets be gone.

speaker: ALL
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: My Lord of Suffolk, say, is this the guise,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Is this the fashion in the court of England?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Is this the government of Britains isle,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And this the royalty of Albions king?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: What shall King Henry be a pupil still

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Under the surly Gloucesters governance?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Am I a queen in title and in style,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And must be made a subject to a duke?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: I tell thee, Pole, when in the city Tours

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thou ranst a tilt in honour of my love

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And stolest away the ladies hearts of France,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: I thought King Henry had resembled thee

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: In courage, courtship and proportion:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: But all his mind is bent to holiness,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: To number Ave-Maries on his beads;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: His champions are the prophets and apostles,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: His weapons holy saws of sacred writ,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: His study is his tilt-yard, and his loves

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Are brazen images of canonized saints.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: I would the college of the cardinals

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Would choose him pope, and carry him to Rome,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And set the triple crown upon his head:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: That were a state fit for his holiness.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Madam, be patient: as I was cause

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Your highness came to England, so will I

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: In England work your graces full content.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Beside the haughty protector, have we Beaufort,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: The imperious churchman, Somerset, Buckingham,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And grumbling York: and not the least of these

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: But can do more in England than the king.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: And he of these that can do most of all

text_entry: Cannot do more in England than the Nevils:

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Salisbury and Warwick are no simple peers.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Not all these lords do vex me half so much

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: As that proud dame, the lord protectors wife.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: She sweeps it through the court with troops of ladies,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: More like an empress than Duke Humphreys wife:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Strangers in court do take her for the queen:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: She bears a dukes revenues on her back,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And in her heart she scorns our poverty:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Shall I not live to be avenged on her?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
