text_entry: Forsooth, a blind man at Saint Albans shrine,

speaker: Townsman
text_entry: Within this half-hour, hath received his sight;

speaker: Townsman
text_entry: A man that neer saw in his life before.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Now, God be praised, that to believing souls

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Gives light in darkness, comfort in despair!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Enter the Mayor of Saint Albans and his  brethren, bearing SIMPCOX, between two in a chair, SIMPCOXs Wife following

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Here comes the townsmen on procession,

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: To present your highness with the man.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Great is his comfort in this earthly vale,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Although by his sight his sin be multiplied.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Stand by, my masters: bring him near the king;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: His highness pleasure is to talk with him.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Good fellow, tell us here the circumstance,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: That we for thee may glorify the Lord.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: What, hast thou been long blind and now restored?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Born blind, ant please your grace.

speaker: Wife
text_entry: Ay, indeed, was he.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: What woman is this?

speaker: Wife
text_entry: His wife, ant like your worship.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Hadst thou been his mother, thou couldst have

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: better told.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Where wert thou born?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: At Berwick in the north, ant like your grace.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Poor soul, Gods goodness hath been great to thee:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Let never day nor night unhallowd pass,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: But still remember what the Lord hath done.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Tell me, good fellow, camest thou here by chance,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Or of devotion, to this holy shrine?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: God knows, of pure devotion; being calld

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: A hundred times and oftener, in my sleep,

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: By good Saint Alban; who said, Simpcox, come,

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Come, offer at my shrine, and I will help thee.

speaker: Wife
text_entry: Most true, forsooth; and many time and oft

speaker: Wife
text_entry: Myself have heard a voice to call him so.

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: What, art thou lame?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Ay, God Almighty help me!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: How camest thou so?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: A fall off of a tree.

speaker: Wife
text_entry: A plum-tree, master.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: How long hast thou been blind?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Born so, master.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: What, and wouldst climb a tree?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: But that in all my life, when I was a youth.

speaker: Wife
text_entry: Too true; and bought his climbing very dear.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Mass, thou lovedst plums well, that wouldst

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: venture so.

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Alas,  good master, my wife desired some damsons,

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: And made me climb, with danger of my life.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: A subtle knave! but yet it shall not serve.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Let me see thine eyes: wink now: now open them:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: In my opinion yet thou seest not well.

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Yes, master, clear as day, I thank God and

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Saint Alban.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Sayst thou me so? What colour is this cloak of?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Red, master; red as blood.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Why, thats well said. What colour is my gown of?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Black, forsooth: coal-black as jet.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Why, then, thou knowst what colour jet is of?

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: And yet, I think, jet did he never see.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But cloaks and gowns, before this day, a many.

speaker: Wife
text_entry: Never, before this day, in all his life.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Tell me, sirrah, whats my name?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Alas, master, I know not.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Whats his name?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: I know not.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Nor his?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: No, indeed, master.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Whats thine own name?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Saunder Simpcox, an if it please you, master.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Then, Saunder, sit there, the lyingest knave in

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Christendom. If thou hadst been born blind, thou

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: mightest as well have known all our names as thus to

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: name the several colours we do wear. Sight may

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: distinguish of colours, but suddenly to nominate them

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: all, it is impossible. My lords, Saint Alban here

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: hath done a miracle; and would ye not think his

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: cunning to be great, that could restore this cripple

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: to his legs again?

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: O master, that you could!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: My masters of Saint Albans, have you not beadles in

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: your town, and things called whips?

speaker: Mayor
text_entry: Yes, my lord, if it please your grace.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Then send for one presently.

speaker: Mayor
text_entry: Sirrah, go fetch the beadle hither straight.

speaker: Mayor
text_entry: Exit an Attendant

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Now fetch me a stool hither by and by. Now, sirrah,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: if you mean to save yourself from whipping, leap me

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: over this stool and run away.

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Alas, master, I am not able to stand alone:

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: You go about to torture me in vain.

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Enter a Beadle with whips

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Well, sir, we must have you find your legs. Sirrah

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: beadle, whip him till he leap over that same stool.

speaker: Beadle
text_entry: I will, my lord. Come on, sirrah; off with your

speaker: Beadle
text_entry: doublet quickly.

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: Alas, master, what shall I do? I am not able to stand.

speaker: SIMPCOX
text_entry: After the Beadle hath hit him once, he leaps over the stool and runs away; and they follow and cry, A miracle!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: O God, seest Thou this, and bearest so long?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: It made me laugh to see the villain run.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Follow the knave; and take this drab away.

speaker: Wife
text_entry: Alas, sir, we did it for pure need.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Let them be whipped through every market-town, till

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: they come to Berwick, from whence they came.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Exeunt Wife, Beadle, Mayor,  and c

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Duke Humphrey has done a miracle to-day.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: True; made the lame to leap and fly away.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But you have done more miracles than I;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: You made in a day, my lord, whole towns to fly.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Enter BUCKINGHAM

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: What tidings with our cousin Buckingham?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Such as my heart doth tremble to unfold.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: A sort of naughty persons, lewdly bent,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Under the countenance and confederacy

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Of Lady Eleanor, the protectors wife,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The ringleader and head of all this rout,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Have practised dangerously against your state,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Dealing with witches and with conjurers:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Whom we have apprehended in the fact;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Raising up wicked spirits from under ground,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Demanding of King Henrys life and death,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And other of your highness privy-council;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: As more at large your grace shall understand.

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: [Aside to GLOUCESTER]  And so, my lord protector,

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: by this means

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Your lady is forthcoming yet at London.

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: This news, I think, hath turnd your weapons edge;

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Tis like, my lord, you will not keep your hour.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Ambitious churchman, leave to afflict my heart:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Sorrow and grief have vanquishd all my powers;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And, vanquishd as I am, I yield to thee,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Or to the meanest groom.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: O God, what mischiefs work the wicked ones,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Heaping confusion on their own heads thereby!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Gloucester, see here the tainture of thy nest.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And look thyself be faultless, thou wert best.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Madam, for myself, to heaven I do appeal,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: How I have loved my king and commonweal:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And, for my wife, I know not how it stands;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Sorry I am to hear what I have heard:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Noble she is, but if she have forgot

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Honour and virtue and conversed with such

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: As, like to pitch, defile nobility,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I banish her my bed and company

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And give her as a prey to law and shame,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: That hath dishonourd Gloucesters honest name.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Well, for this night we will repose us here:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: To-morrow toward London back again,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: To look into this business thoroughly

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And call these foul offenders to their answers

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And poise the cause in justice equal scales,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Whose beam stands sure, whose rightful cause prevails.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Flourish. Exeunt

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: SCENE II. London. YORKS garden.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Enter YORK, SALISBURY, and WARWICK

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Now, my good Lords of Salisbury and Warwick,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Our simple supper ended, give me leave

speaker: YORK
text_entry: In this close walk to satisfy myself,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: In craving your opinion of my title,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Which is infallible, to Englands crown.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: My lord, I long to hear it at full.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Sweet York, begin: and if thy claim be good,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: The Nevils are thy subjects to command.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Then thus:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Edward the Third, my lords, had seven sons:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The first, Edward the Black Prince, Prince of Wales;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The second, William of Hatfield, and the third,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Lionel Duke of Clarence: next to whom

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Was John of Gaunt, the Duke of Lancaster;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The fifth was Edmund Langley, Duke of York;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The sixth was Thomas of Woodstock, Duke of Gloucester;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: William of Windsor was the seventh and last.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Edward the Black Prince died before his father

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And left behind him Richard, his only son,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Who after Edward the Thirds death reignd as king;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Till Henry Bolingbroke, Duke of Lancaster,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The eldest son and heir of John of Gaunt,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Crownd by the name of Henry the Fourth,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Seized on the realm, deposed the rightful king,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Sent his poor queen to France, from whence she came,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And him to Pomfret; where, as all you know,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Harmless Richard was murderd traitorously.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Father, the duke hath told the truth:

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Thus got the house of Lancaster the crown.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Which now they hold by force and not by right;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: For Richard, the first sons heir, being dead,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The issue of the next son should have reignd.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: But William of Hatfield died without an heir.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The third son, Duke of Clarence, from whose line

speaker: YORK
text_entry: I claimed the crown, had issue, Philippe, a daughter,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Who married Edmund Mortimer, Earl of March:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Edmund had issue, Roger Earl of March;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Roger had issue, Edmund, Anne and Eleanor.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: This Edmund, in the reign of Bolingbroke,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: As I have read, laid claim unto the crown;

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: And, but for Owen Glendower, had been king,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Who kept him in captivity till he died.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: But to the rest.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: His eldest sister, Anne,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: My mother, being heir unto the crown

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Married Richard Earl of Cambridge; who was son

speaker: YORK
text_entry: To Edmund Langley, Edward the Thirds fifth son.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: By her I claim the kingdom: she was heir

speaker: YORK
text_entry: To Roger Earl of March, who was the son

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Of Edmund Mortimer, who married Philippe,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Sole daughter unto Lionel Duke of Clarence:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: So, if the issue of the elder son

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Succeed before the younger, I am king.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: What plain proceeding is more plain than this?

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Henry doth claim the crown from John of Gaunt,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: The fourth son; York claims it from the third.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Till Lionels issue fails, his should not reign:

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: It fails not yet, but flourishes in thee

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And in thy sons, fair slips of such a stock.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Then, father Salisbury, kneel we together;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And in this private plot be we the first

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: That shall salute our rightful sovereign

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: With honour of his birthright to the crown.

speaker: BOTH
text_entry: Long live our sovereign Richard, Englands king!

speaker: YORK
text_entry: We thank you, lords. But I am not your king

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Till I be crownd and that my sword be staind

speaker: YORK
text_entry: With heart-blood of the house of Lancaster;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And thats not suddenly to be performd,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: But with advice and silent secrecy.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Do you as I do in these dangerous days:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Wink at the Duke of Suffolks insolence,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: At Beauforts pride, at Somersets ambition,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: At Buckingham and all the crew of them,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Till they have snared the shepherd of the flock,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: That virtuous prince, the good Duke Humphrey:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Tis that they seek, and they in seeking that

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Shall find their deaths, if York can prophesy.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: My lord, break we off; we know your mind at full.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: My heart assures me that the Earl of Warwick

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Shall one day make the Duke of York a king.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And, Nevil, this I do assure myself:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Richard shall live to make the Earl of Warwick

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The greatest man in England but the king.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: YORK
text_entry: SCENE III. A hall of justice.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Sound trumpets. Enter KING HENRY VI, QUEEN  MARGARET, GLOUCESTER, YORK, SUFFOLK, and SALISBURY;  the DUCHESS, MARGARET JOURDAIN, SOUTHWELL, HUME, and BOLINGBROKE, under guard

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Stand forth, Dame Eleanor Cobham, Gloucesters wife:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: In sight of God and us, your guilt is great:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Receive the sentence of the law for sins

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Such as by Gods book are adjudged to death.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: You four, from hence to prison back again;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: From thence unto the place of execution:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: The witch in Smithfield shall be burnd to ashes,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And you three shall be strangled on the gallows.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: You, madam, for you are more nobly born,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Despoiled of your honour in your life,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Shall, after three days open penance done,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Live in your country here in banishment,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: With Sir John Stanley, in the Isle of Man.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Welcome is banishment; welcome were my death.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Eleanor, the law, thou seest, hath judged thee:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I cannot justify whom the law condemns.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Exeunt DUCHESS and other prisoners, guarded

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Mine eyes are full of tears, my heart of grief.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Ah, Humphrey, this dishonour in thine age

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Will bring thy head with sorrow to the ground!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I beseech your majesty, give me leave to go;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Sorrow would solace and mine age would ease.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Stay, Humphrey Duke of Gloucester: ere thou go,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Give up thy staff: Henry will to himself

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Protector be; and God shall be my hope,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: My stay, my guide and lantern to my feet:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And go in peace, Humphrey, no less beloved

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Than when thou wert protector to thy King.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: I see no reason why a king of years

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Should be to be protected like a child.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: God and King Henry govern Englands realm.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Give up your staff, sir, and the king his realm.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: My staff? here, noble Henry, is my staff:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: As willingly do I the same resign

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: As eer thy father Henry made it mine;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And even as willingly at thy feet I leave it

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: As others would ambitiously receive it.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Farewell, good king: when I am dead and gone,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: May honourable peace attend thy throne!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Exit

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Why, now is Henry king, and Margaret queen;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And Humphrey Duke of Gloucester scarce himself,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: That bears so shrewd a maim; two pulls at once;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: His lady banishd, and a limb loppd off.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: This staff of honour raught, there let it stand

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Where it best fits to be, in Henrys hand.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Thus droops this lofty pine and hangs his sprays;

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Thus Eleanors pride dies in her youngest days.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Lords, let him go. Please it your majesty,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: This is the day appointed for the combat;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And ready are the appellant and defendant,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The armourer and his man, to enter the lists,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: So please your highness to behold the fight.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Ay, good my lord; for purposely therefore

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Left I the court, to see this quarrel tried.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: O Gods name, see the lists and all things fit:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Here let them end it; and God defend the right!

speaker: YORK
text_entry: I never saw a fellow worse bested,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Or more afraid to fight, than is the appellant,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The servant of this armourer, my lords.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Enter at one door, HORNER, the Armourer, and his  Neighbours, drinking to him so much that he is drunk;  and he enters with a drum before him and his staff  with a sand-bag fastened to it; and at the other  door PETER, his man, with a drum and sand-bag, and Prentices drinking to him

speaker: First Neighbour
text_entry: Here, neighbour Horner, I drink to you in a cup of

speaker: First Neighbour
text_entry: sack: and fear not, neighbour, you shall do well enough.

speaker: Second Neighbour
text_entry: And here, neighbour, heres a cup of charneco.

speaker: Third Neighbour
text_entry: And heres a pot of good double beer, neighbour:

speaker: Third Neighbour
text_entry: drink, and fear not your man.

speaker: HORNER
text_entry: Let it come, i faith, and Ill pledge you all; and

speaker: HORNER
text_entry: a fig for Peter!

speaker: HORNER
text_entry: First PrenticeHere, Peter, I drink to thee: and be not afraid.

speaker: HORNER
text_entry: Second PrenticeBe merry, Peter, and fear not thy master: fight

speaker: HORNER
text_entry: for credit of the prentices.

speaker: PETER
text_entry: I thank you all: drink, and pray for me, I pray

speaker: PETER
text_entry: you; for I think I have taken my last draught in

speaker: PETER
text_entry: this world. Here, Robin, an if I die, I give thee

speaker: PETER
text_entry: my apron: and, Will, thou shalt have my hammer:

speaker: PETER
text_entry: and here, Tom, take all the money that I have. O

speaker: PETER
text_entry: Lord bless me! I pray God! for I am never able to

speaker: PETER
text_entry: deal with my master, he hath learnt me so much fence already.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Come, leave your drinking, and fall to blows.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Sirrah, whats thy name?

text_entry: Dies

text_entry: Take away his weapon. Fellow, thank God, and the

text_entry: O Peter, thou hast prevailed in right!

text_entry: Go, take hence that traitor from our sight;

text_entry: For his death we do perceive his guilt:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And God in justice hath revealed to us

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: The truth and innocence of this poor fellow,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Which he had thought to have murderd wrongfully.

text_entry: SCENE IV. A street.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Enter GLOUCESTER and his Servingmen, in mourning cloaks

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Thus sometimes hath the brightest day a cloud;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And after summer evermore succeeds

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Barren winter, with his wrathful nipping cold:

text_entry: So cares and joys abound, as seasons fleet.

text_entry: Sirs, whats oclock?

text_entry: Ten, my lord.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Ten is the hour that was appointed me

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To watch the coming of my punishd duchess:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Uneath may she endure the flinty streets,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To tread them with her tender-feeling feet.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Sweet Nell, ill can thy noble mind abrook

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: The abject people gazing on thy face,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: With envious looks, laughing at thy shame,

text_entry: That erst did follow thy proud chariot-wheels

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: When thou didst ride in triumph through the streets.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But, soft! I think she comes; and Ill prepare

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: My tear-staind eyes to see her miseries.

text_entry: So please your grace, well take her from the sheriff.

text_entry: No, stir not, for your lives; let her pass by.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Now thou dost penance too. Look how they gaze!

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: See how the giddy multitude do point,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And nod their heads, and throw their eyes on thee!

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Ah, Gloucester, hide thee from their hateful looks,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And, in thy closet pent up, rue my shame,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And ban thine enemies, both mine and thine!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Be patient, gentle Nell; forget this grief.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Ah, Gloucester, teach me to forget myself!

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: For whilst I think I am thy married wife

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And thou a prince, protector of this land,

text_entry: Methinks I should not thus be led along,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Maild up in shame, with papers on my back,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And followed with a rabble that rejoice

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: To see my tears and hear my deep-fet groans.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: The ruthless flint doth cut my tender feet,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And when I start, the envious people laugh

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And bid me be advised how I tread.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Ah, Humphrey, can I bear this shameful yoke?

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Trowst thou that eer Ill look upon the world,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Or count them happy that enjoy the sun?

text_entry: No; dark shall be my light and night my day;

text_entry: To think upon my pomp shall be my hell.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Sometime Ill say, I am Duke Humphreys wife,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And he a prince and ruler of the land:

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Yet so he ruled and such a prince he was

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: As he stood by whilst I, his forlorn duchess,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Was made a wonder and a pointing-stock

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: To every idle rascal follower.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: But be thou mild and blush not at my shame,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Nor stir at nothing till the axe of death

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Hang over thee, as, sure, it shortly will;

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: For Suffolk, he that can do all in all

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: With her that hateth thee and hates us all,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And York and impious Beaufort, that false priest,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Have all limed bushes to betray thy wings,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And, fly thou how thou canst, theyll tangle thee:

text_entry: But fear not thou, until thy foot be snared,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Ah, Nell, forbear! thou aimest all awry;

text_entry: I must offend before I be attainted;

text_entry: And had I twenty times so many foes,

text_entry: And each of them had twenty times their power,

text_entry: All these could not procure me any scathe,

text_entry: So long as I am loyal, true and crimeless.

text_entry: Wouldst have me rescue thee from this reproach?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Why, yet thy scandal were not wiped away

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But I in danger for the breach of law.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Thy greatest help is quiet, gentle Nell:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I pray thee, sort thy heart to patience;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: These few days wonder will be quickly worn.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Enter a Herald

text_entry: Holden at Bury the first of this next month.

text_entry: And my consent neer askd herein before!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Exit Herald

speaker: GLOUCESTER

speaker: GLOUCESTER

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Death, at whose name I oft have been afeard,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Because I wishd this worlds eternity.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Stanley, I prithee, go, and take me hence;

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: I care not whither, for I beg no favour,

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Only convey me where thou art commanded.

speaker: STANLEY
text_entry: There to be used according to your state.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And shall I then be used reproachfully?

speaker: STANLEY

speaker: STANLEY
text_entry: According to that state you shall be used.

speaker: DUCHESS

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Although thou hast been conduct of my shame.

speaker: Sheriff
text_entry: It is my office; and, madam, pardon me.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Ay, ay, farewell; thy office is discharged.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Come, Stanley, shall we go?

speaker: STANLEY
text_entry: Madam, your penance done, throw off this sheet,

speaker: STANLEY
text_entry: And go we to attire you for our journey.

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: My shame will not be shifted with my sheet:

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: No, it will hang upon my richest robes

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: And show itself, attire me how I can.

speaker: DUCHESS

speaker: DUCHESS
text_entry: Exeunt

text_entry: But left that hateful office unto thee:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: The pretty-vaulting sea refused to drown me,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Knowing that thou wouldst have me drownd on shore,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: With tears as salt as sea, through thy unkindness:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: The splitting rocks cowerd in the sinking sands

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And would not dash me with their ragged sides,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Because thy flinty heart, more hard than they,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Might in thy palace perish Margaret.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: As far as I could ken thy chalky cliffs,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: When from thy shore the tempest beat us back,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: I stood upon the hatches in the storm,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And when the dusky sky began to rob

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: My earnest-gaping sight of thy lands view,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: I took a costly jewel from my neck,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: A heart it was, bound in with diamonds,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And threw it towards thy land: the sea received it,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And so I wishd thy body might my heart:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And even with this I lost fair Englands view

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And bid mine eyes be packing with my heart

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And calld them blind and dusky spectacles,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: For losing ken of Albions wished coast.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: How often have I tempted Suffolks tongue,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: The agent of thy foul inconstancy,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: To sit and witch me, as Ascanius did

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: When he to madding Dido would unfold

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: His fathers acts commenced in burning Troy!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Am I not witchd like her? or thou not false like him?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Ay me, I can no more! die, Margaret!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: For Henry weeps that thou dost live so long.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Noise within. Enter WARWICK, SALISBURY, and many Commons

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: It is reported, mighty sovereign,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: That good Duke Humphrey traitorously is murderd

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: By Suffolk and the Cardinal Beauforts means.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: The commons, like an angry hive of bees

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: That want their leader, scatter up and down

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And care not who they sting in his revenge.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Myself have calmd their spleenful mutiny,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Until they hear the order of his death.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: That he is dead, good Warwick, tis too true;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: But how he died God knows, not Henry:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Enter his chamber, view his breathless corpse,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And comment then upon his sudden death.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: That shall I do, my liege. Stay, Salisbury,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: With the rude multitude till I return.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Exit

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: O Thou that judgest all things, stay my thoughts,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: My thoughts, that labour to persuade my soul

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Some violent hands were laid on Humphreys life!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: If my suspect be false, forgive me, God,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: For judgment only doth belong to thee.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Fain would I go to chafe his paly lips

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: With twenty thousand kisses, and to drain

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Upon his face an ocean of salt tears,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: To tell my love unto his dumb deaf trunk,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And with my fingers feel his hand unfeeling:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: But all in vain are these mean obsequies;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And to survey his dead and earthly image,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: What were it but to make my sorrow greater?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Re-enter WARWICK and others, bearing GLOUCESTERS body on a bed

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Come hither, gracious sovereign, view this body.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: That is to see how deep my grave is made;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: For with his soul fled all my worldly solace,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: For seeing him I see my life in death.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: As surely as my soul intends to live

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: With that dread King that took our state upon him

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: To free us from his fathers wrathful curse,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: I do believe that violent hands were laid

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Upon the life of this thrice-famed duke.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: A dreadful oath, sworn with a solemn tongue!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: What instance gives Lord Warwick for his vow?

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: See how the blood is settled in his face.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Oft have I seen a timely-parted ghost,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Of ashy semblance, meagre, pale and bloodless,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Being all descended to the labouring heart;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Who, in the conflict that it holds with death,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Attracts the same for aidance gainst the enemy;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Which with the heart there cools and neer returneth

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: To blush and beautify the cheek again.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: But see, his face is black and full of blood,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: His eye-balls further out than when he lived,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Staring full ghastly like a strangled man;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: His hair upreard, his nostrils stretched with struggling;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: His hands abroad displayd, as one that graspd

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And tuggd for life and was by strength subdued:

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Look, on the sheets his hair you see, is sticking;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: His well-proportiond beard made rough and rugged,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Like to the summers corn by tempest lodged.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: It cannot be but he was murderd here;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: The least of all these signs were probable.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Why, Warwick, who should do the duke to death?

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Myself and Beaufort had him in protection;

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: And we, I hope, sir, are no murderers.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: But both of you were vowd Duke Humphreys foes,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And you, forsooth, had the good duke to keep:

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Tis like you would not feast him like a friend;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And tis well seen he found an enemy.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Then you, belike, suspect these noblemen

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: As guilty of Duke Humphreys timeless death.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Who finds the heifer dead and bleeding fresh

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And sees fast by a butcher with an axe,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: But will suspect twas he that made the slaughter?

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Who finds the partridge in the puttocks nest,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: But may imagine how the bird was dead,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Although the kite soar with unbloodied beak?

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Even so suspicious is this tragedy.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Are you the butcher, Suffolk? Wheres your knife?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Is Beaufort termd a kite? Where are his talons?

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: I wear no knife to slaughter sleeping men;

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: But heres a vengeful sword, rusted with ease,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: That shall be scoured in his rancorous heart

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: That slanders me with murders crimson badge.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Say, if thou darest, proud Lord of Warwick-shire,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: That I am faulty in Duke Humphreys death.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Exeunt CARDINAL, SOMERSET, and others

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: What dares not Warwick, if false Suffolk dare him?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: He dares not calm his contumelious spirit

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Nor cease to be an arrogant controller,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Though Suffolk dare him twenty thousand times.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Madam, be still; with reverence may I say;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: For every word you speak in his behalf

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Is slander to your royal dignity.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Blunt-witted lord, ignoble in demeanor!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: If ever lady wrongd her lord so much,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Thy mother took into her blameful bed

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Some stern untutord churl, and noble stock

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Was graft with crab-tree slip; whose fruit thou art,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: And never of the Nevils noble race.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: But that the guilt of murder bucklers thee

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And I should rob the deathsman of his fee,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Quitting thee thereby of ten thousand shames,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And that my sovereigns presence makes me mild,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: I would, false murderous coward, on thy knee

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Make thee beg pardon for thy passed speech,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And say it was thy mother that thou meantst

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: That thou thyself was born in bastardy;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And after all this fearful homage done,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Give thee thy hire and send thy soul to hell,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Pernicious blood-sucker of sleeping men!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Thou shall be waking well I shed thy blood,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: If from this presence thou darest go with me.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Away even now, or I will drag thee hence:

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Unworthy though thou art, Ill cope with thee

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And do some service to Duke Humphreys ghost.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Exeunt SUFFOLK and WARWICK

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: What stronger breastplate than a heart untainted!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Thrice is he armed that hath his quarrel just,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And he but naked, though lockd up in steel

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Whose conscience with injustice is corrupted.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: A noise within

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: What noise is this?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Re-enter SUFFOLK and WARWICK, with their weapons drawn

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Why, how now, lords! your wrathful weapons drawn

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Here in our presence! dare you be so bold?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Why, what tumultuous clamour have we here?

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: The traitorous Warwick with the men of Bury

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Set all upon me, mighty sovereign.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: [To the Commons, entering]  Sirs, stand apart;

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: the king shall know your mind.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Dread lord, the commons send you word by me,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Unless Lord Suffolk straight be done to death,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Or banished fair Englands territories,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: They will by violence tear him from your palace

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: And torture him with grievous lingering death.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: They say, by him the good Duke Humphrey died;

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: They say, in him they fear your highness death;

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: And mere instinct of love and loyalty,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Free from a stubborn opposite intent,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: As being thought to contradict your liking,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Makes them thus forward in his banishment.

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: They say, in care of your most royal person,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: That if your highness should intend to sleep

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: And charge that no man should disturb your rest

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: In pain of your dislike or pain of death,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Yet, notwithstanding such a strait edict,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Were there a serpent seen, with forked tongue,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: That slily glided towards your majesty,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: It were but necessary you were waked,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Lest, being sufferd in that harmful slumber,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: The mortal worm might make the sleep eternal;

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: And therefore do they cry, though you forbid,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: That they will guard you, whether you will or no,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: From such fell serpents as false Suffolk is,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: With whose envenomed and fatal sting,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: Your loving uncle, twenty times his worth,

speaker: SALISBURY
text_entry: They say, is shamefully bereft of life.

speaker: Commons
text_entry: [Within]  An answer from the king, my

speaker: Commons
text_entry: Lord of Salisbury!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Tis like the commons, rude unpolishd hinds,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Could send such message to their sovereign:

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: But you, my lord, were glad to be employd,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: To show how quaint an orator you are:

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: But all the honour Salisbury hath won

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Is, that he was the lord ambassador

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Sent from a sort of tinkers to the king.

speaker: Commons
text_entry: [Within]  An answer from the king, or we will all break in!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Go, Salisbury, and tell them all from me.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: I thank them for their tender loving care;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And had I not been cited so by them,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Yet did I purpose as they do entreat;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: For, sure, my thoughts do hourly prophesy

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Mischance unto my state by Suffolks means:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And therefore, by His majesty I swear,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Whose far unworthy deputy I am,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: He shall not breathe infection in this air

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: But three days longer, on the pain of death.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Exit SALISBURY

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O Henry, let me plead for gentle Suffolk!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Ungentle queen, to call him gentle Suffolk!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: No more, I say: if thou dost plead for him,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Thou wilt but add increase unto my wrath.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Had I but said, I would have kept my word,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: But when I swear, it is irrevocable.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: If, after three days space, thou here best found

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: On any ground that I am ruler of,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: The world shall not be ransom for thy life.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Come, Warwick, come, good Warwick, go with me;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: I have great matters to impart to thee.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Exeunt all but QUEEN MARGARET and SUFFOLK

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Mischance and sorrow go along with you!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Hearts discontent and sour affliction

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Be playfellows to keep you company!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Theres two of you; the devil make a third!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And threefold vengeance tend upon your steps!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Cease, gentle queen, these execrations,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: And let thy Suffolk take his heavy leave.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Fie, coward woman and soft-hearted wretch!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Hast thou not spirit to curse thine enemy?

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: A plague upon them! wherefore should I curse them?

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Would curses kill, as doth the mandrakes groan,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: I would invent as bitter-searching terms,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: As curst, as harsh and horrible to hear,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Deliverd strongly through my fixed teeth,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: With full as many signs of deadly hate,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: As lean-faced Envy in her loathsome cave:

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: My tongue should stumble in mine earnest words;

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Mine eyes should sparkle like the beaten flint;

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Mine hair be fixed on end, as one distract;

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Ay, every joint should seem to curse and ban:

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: And even now my burthend heart would break,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Should I not curse them. Poison be their drink!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Gall, worse than gall, the daintiest that they taste!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Their sweetest shade a grove of cypress trees!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Their chiefest prospect murdering basilisks!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Their softest touch as smart as lizards sting!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Their music frightful as the serpents hiss,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: And boding screech-owls make the concert full!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: All the foul terrors in dark-seated hell--

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Enough, sweet Suffolk; thou tormentst thyself;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And these dread curses, like the sun gainst glass,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Or like an overcharged gun, recoil,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And turn the force of them upon thyself.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: You bade me ban, and will you bid me leave?

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Now, by the ground that I am banishd from,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Well could I curse away a winters night,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Though standing naked on a mountain top,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Where biting cold would never let grass grow,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: And think it but a minute spent in sport.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O, let me entreat thee cease. Give me thy hand,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: That I may dew it with my mournful tears;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Nor let the rain of heaven wet this place,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: To wash away my woful monuments.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O, could this kiss be printed in thy hand,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: That thou mightst think upon these by the seal,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Through whom a thousand sighs are breathed for thee!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: So, get thee gone, that I may know my grief;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Tis but surmised whiles thou art standing by,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: As one that surfeits thinking on a want.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: I will repeal thee, or, be well assured,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Adventure to be banished myself:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And banished I am, if but from thee.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Go; speak not to me; even now be gone.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O, go not yet! Even thus two friends condemnd

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Embrace and kiss and take ten thousand leaves,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Loather a hundred times to part than die.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Yet now farewell; and farewell life with thee!

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Thus is poor Suffolk ten times banished;

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Once by the king, and three times thrice by thee.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Tis not the land I care for, wert thou thence;

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: A wilderness is populous enough,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: So Suffolk had thy heavenly company:

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: For where thou art, there is the world itself,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: With every several pleasure in the world,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: And where thou art not, desolation.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: I can no more: live thou to joy thy life;

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Myself no joy in nought but that thou livest.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Enter VAUX

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Wither goes Vaux so fast? what news, I prithee?

speaker: VAUX
text_entry: To signify unto his majesty

speaker: VAUX
text_entry: That Cardinal Beaufort is at point of death;

speaker: VAUX
text_entry: For suddenly a grievous sickness took him,

speaker: VAUX
text_entry: That makes him gasp and stare and catch the air,

speaker: VAUX
text_entry: Blaspheming God and cursing men on earth.

speaker: VAUX
text_entry: Sometimes he talks as if Duke Humphreys ghost

speaker: VAUX
text_entry: Were by his side; sometime he calls the king,

speaker: VAUX
text_entry: And whispers to his pillow, as to him,

speaker: VAUX
text_entry: The secrets of his overcharged soul;

speaker: VAUX
text_entry: And I am sent to tell his majesty

speaker: VAUX
text_entry: That even now he cries aloud for him.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Go tell this heavy message to the king.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Exit VAUX

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Ay me! what is this world! what news are these!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: But wherefore grieve I at an hours poor loss,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Omitting Suffolks exile, my souls treasure?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Why only, Suffolk, mourn I not for thee,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And with the southern clouds contend in tears,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Theirs for the earths increase, mine for my sorrows?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Now get thee hence: the king, thou knowst, is coming;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: If thou be found by me, thou art but dead.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: If I depart from thee, I cannot live;

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: And in thy sight to die, what were it else

text_entry: But like a pleasant slumber in thy lap?

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Here could I breathe my soul into the air,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: As mild and gentle as the cradle-babe

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Dying with mothers dug between its lips:

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Where, from thy sight, I should be raging mad,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: And cry out for thee to close up mine eyes,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: To have thee with thy lips to stop my mouth;

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: So shouldst thou either turn my flying soul,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Or I should breathe it so into thy body,

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: And then it lived in sweet Elysium.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: To die by thee were but to die in jest;

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: From thee to die were torture more than death:

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: O, let me stay, befall what may befall!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Away! though parting be a fretful corrosive,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: It is applied to a deathful wound.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: To France, sweet Suffolk: let me hear from thee;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: For wheresoeer thou art in this worlds globe,

text_entry: And take my heart with thee.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: A jewel, lockd into the wofullst cask

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: That ever did contain a thing of worth.

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Even as a splitted bark, so sunder we

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: This way fall I to death.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: This way for me.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET

text_entry: If thou best death, Ill give thee Englands treasure,

text_entry: Ah, what a sign it is of evil life,

speaker: KING HENRY VI

text_entry: Ill give a thousand pound to look upon him.

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Comb down his hair; look, look! it stands upright,

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Like lime-twigs set to catch my winged soul.

text_entry: Give me some drink; and bid the apothecary

speaker: CARDINAL
text_entry: Bring the strong poison that I bought of him.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: O thou eternal Mover of the heavens.

text_entry: Look with a gentle eye upon this wretch!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: O, beat away the busy meddling fiend

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: That lays strong siege unto this wretchs soul.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And from his bosom purge this black despair!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Lord cardinal, if thou thinkst on heavens bliss,

text_entry: Hold up thy hand, make signal of thy hope.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: He dies, and makes no sign. O God, forgive him!

speaker: KING HENRY VI

speaker: KING HENRY VI

text_entry: I lost mine eye in laying the prize aboard,

text_entry: To SUFFOLK

speaker: WHITMORE
text_entry: How now! why startst thou? what, doth

speaker: WHITMORE
text_entry: death affright?

text_entry: Never yet did base dishonour blur our name,

speaker: WHITMORE
text_entry: But with our sword we wiped away the blot;

text_entry: Therefore, when merchant-like I sell revenge,

text_entry: Broke be my sword, my arms torn and defaced,

text_entry: Obscure and lowly swain, King Henrys blood,

text_entry: When I have feasted with Queen Margaret?

speaker: SUFFOLK

speaker: SUFFOLK

text_entry: How in our voiding lobby hast thou stood

speaker: SUFFOLK

text_entry: This hand of mine hath writ in thy behalf,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Convey him hence and on our longboats side

speaker: Captain

text_entry: Thou darest not, for thy own.

speaker: Captain

speaker: SUFFOLK
text_entry: Pole!

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Pool! Sir Pool! lord!

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Ay, kennel, puddle, sink; whose filth and dirt

speaker: Captain
text_entry: For daring to affy a mighty lord

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Unto the daughter of a worthless king,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Having neither subject, wealth, nor diadem.

speaker: Captain
text_entry: By devilish policy art thou grown great,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: And, like ambitious Sylla, overgorged

speaker: Captain
text_entry: With gobbets of thy mothers bleeding heart.

speaker: Captain

text_entry: The princely Warwick, and the Nevils all,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: And lofty proud encroaching tyranny,

text_entry: Under the which is writ Invitis nubibus.

speaker: Captain

text_entry: Is crept into the palace of our king.

speaker: Captain
