text_entry: Stand, villain, stand, or Ill fell thee down. He

speaker: CADE
text_entry: shall be encountered with a man as good as himself:

speaker: CADE
text_entry: he is but a knight, is a?

speaker: MICHAEL
text_entry: No.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: To equal him, I will make myself a knight presently.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Kneels

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Rise up Sir John Mortimer.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Rises

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Now have at him!

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Enter SIR HUMPHREY and WILLIAM STAFFORD, with drum and soldiers

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: Rebellious hinds, the filth and scum of Kent,

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: Markd for the gallows, lay your weapons down;

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: Home to your cottages, forsake this groom:

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: The king is merciful, if you revolt.

speaker: WILLIAM STAFFORD
text_entry: But angry, wrathful, and inclined to blood,

speaker: WILLIAM STAFFORD
text_entry: If you go forward; therefore yield, or die.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: As for these silken-coated slaves, I pass not:

speaker: CADE
text_entry: It is to you, good people, that I speak,

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Over whom, in time to come, I hope to reign;

speaker: CADE
text_entry: For I am rightful heir unto the crown.

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: Villain, thy father was a plasterer;

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: And thou thyself a shearman, art thou not?

speaker: CADE
text_entry: And Adam was a gardener.

speaker: WILLIAM STAFFORD
text_entry: And what of that?

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Marry, this: Edmund Mortimer, Earl of March.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Married the Duke of Clarence daughter, did he not?

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: Ay, sir.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: By her he had two children at one birth.

speaker: WILLIAM STAFFORD
text_entry: Thats false.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Ay, theres the question; but I say, tis true:

speaker: CADE
text_entry: The elder of them, being put to nurse,

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Was by a beggar-woman stolen away;

speaker: CADE
text_entry: And, ignorant of his birth and parentage,

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Became a bricklayer when he came to age:

speaker: CADE
text_entry: His son am I; deny it, if you can.

speaker: DICK
text_entry: Nay, tis too true; therefore he shall be king.

speaker: SMITH
text_entry: Sir, he made a chimney in my fathers house, and

speaker: SMITH
text_entry: the bricks are alive at this day to testify it;

speaker: SMITH
text_entry: therefore deny it not.

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: And will you credit this base drudges words,

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: That speaks he knows not what?

speaker: ALL
text_entry: Ay, marry, will we; therefore get ye gone.

speaker: WILLIAM STAFFORD
text_entry: Jack Cade, the Duke of York hath taught you this.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: [Aside]  He lies, for I invented it myself.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Go to, sirrah, tell the king from me, that, for his

speaker: CADE
text_entry: fathers sake, Henry the Fifth, in whose time boys

speaker: CADE
text_entry: went to span-counter for French crowns, I am content

speaker: CADE
text_entry: he shall reign; but Ill be protector over him.

speaker: DICK
text_entry: And furthermore, well have the Lord Says head for

speaker: DICK
text_entry: selling the dukedom of Maine.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: And good reason; for thereby is England mained, and

speaker: CADE
text_entry: fain to go with a staff, but that my puissance holds

speaker: CADE
text_entry: it up. Fellow kings, I tell you that that Lord Say

speaker: CADE
text_entry: hath gelded the commonwealth, and made it an eunuch:

speaker: CADE
text_entry: and more than that, he can speak French; and

speaker: CADE
text_entry: therefore he is a traitor.

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: O gross and miserable ignorance!

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Nay, answer, if you can: the Frenchmen are our

speaker: CADE
text_entry: enemies; go to, then, I ask but this: can he that

speaker: CADE
text_entry: speaks with the tongue of an enemy be a good

speaker: CADE
text_entry: counsellor, or no?

speaker: ALL
text_entry: No, no; and therefore well have his head.

speaker: WILLIAM STAFFORD
text_entry: Well, seeing gentle words will not prevail,

speaker: WILLIAM STAFFORD
text_entry: Assail them with the army of the king.

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: Herald, away; and throughout every town

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: Proclaim them traitors that are up with Cade;

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: That those which fly before the battle ends

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: May, even in their wives and childrens sight,

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: Be hangd up for example at their doors:

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: And you that be the kings friends, follow me.

speaker: SIR HUMPHREY
text_entry: Exeunt WILLIAM STAFFORD and SIR HUMPHREY, and soldiers

speaker: CADE
text_entry: And you that love the commons, follow me.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Now show yourselves men; tis for liberty.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: We will not leave one lord, one gentleman:

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Spare none but such as go in clouted shoon;

speaker: CADE
text_entry: For they are thrifty honest men, and such

speaker: CADE
text_entry: As would, but that they dare not, take our parts.

speaker: DICK
text_entry: They are all in order and march toward us.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: But then are we in order when we are most

speaker: CADE
text_entry: out of order. Come, march forward.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: CADE
text_entry: SCENE III. Another part of Blackheath.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Alarums to the fight, wherein SIR HUMPHREY and WILLIAM STAFFORD are slain. Enter CADE and the rest

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Wheres Dick, the butcher of Ashford?

speaker: DICK
text_entry: Here, sir.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: They fell before thee like sheep and oxen, and thou

speaker: CADE
text_entry: behavedst thyself as if thou hadst been in thine own

speaker: CADE
text_entry: slaughter-house: therefore thus will I reward thee,

speaker: CADE
text_entry: the Lent shall be as long again as it is; and thou

speaker: CADE
text_entry: shalt have a licence to kill for a hundred lacking

speaker: CADE
text_entry: one.

speaker: DICK
text_entry: I desire no more.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: And, to speak truth, thou deservest no less. This

speaker: CADE
text_entry: monument of the victory will I bear;

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Putting on SIR HUMPHREYS brigandine

speaker: CADE
text_entry: and the bodies shall be dragged at my horse heels

speaker: CADE
text_entry: till I do come to London, where we will have the

speaker: CADE
text_entry: mayors sword borne before us.

speaker: DICK
text_entry: If we mean to thrive and do good, break open the

speaker: DICK
text_entry: gaols and let out the prisoners.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Fear not that, I warrant thee. Come, lets march

speaker: CADE
text_entry: towards London.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: CADE
text_entry: SCENE IV. London. The palace.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Enter KING HENRY VI with a supplication, and the QUEEN with SUFFOLKS head, BUCKINGHAM and Lord SAY

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Oft have I heard that grief softens the mind,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And makes it fearful and degenerate;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Think therefore on revenge and cease to weep.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: But who can cease to weep and look on this?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Here may his head lie on my throbbing breast:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: But wheres the body that I should embrace?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: What answer makes your grace to the rebels

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: supplication?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Ill send some holy bishop to entreat;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: For God forbid so many simple souls

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Should perish by the sword! And I myself,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Rather than bloody war shall cut them short,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Will parley with Jack Cade their general:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: But stay, Ill read it over once again.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Ah, barbarous villains! hath this lovely face

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Ruled, like a wandering planet, over me,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And could it not enforce them to relent,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: That were unworthy to behold the same?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Lord Say, Jack Cade hath sworn to have thy head.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Ay, but I hope your highness shall have his.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: How now, madam!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Still lamenting and mourning for Suffolks death?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: I fear me, love, if that I had been dead,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Thou wouldst not have mournd so much for me.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: No, my love, I should not mourn, but die for thee.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Enter a Messenger

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: How now! what news? why comest thou in such haste?

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: The rebels are in Southwark; fly, my lord!

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Jack Cade proclaims himself Lord Mortimer,

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Descended from the Duke of Clarence house,

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: And calls your grace usurper openly

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: And vows to crown himself in Westminster.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: His army is a ragged multitude

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Of hinds and peasants, rude and merciless:

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Sir Humphrey Stafford and h is brothers death

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Hath given them heart and courage to proceed:

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: All scholars, lawyers, courtiers, gentlemen,

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: They call false caterpillars, and intend their death.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: O graceless men! they know not what they do.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: My gracious lord, return to Killingworth,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Until a power be raised to put them down.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Ah, were the Duke of Suffolk now alive,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: These Kentish rebels would be soon appeased!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Lord Say, the traitors hate thee;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Therefore away with us to Killingworth.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: So might your graces person be in danger.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: The sight of me is odious in their eyes;

speaker: SAY
text_entry: And therefore in this city will I stay

speaker: SAY
text_entry: And live alone as secret as I may.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Enter another Messenger

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Jack Cade hath gotten London bridge:

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: The citizens fly and forsake their houses:

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: The rascal people, thirsting after prey,

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Join with the traitor, and they jointly swear

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: To spoil the city and your royal court.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Then linger not, my lord, away, take horse.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Come, Margaret; God, our hope, will succor us.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: My hope is gone, now Suffolk is deceased.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Farewell, my lord: trust not the Kentish rebels.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Trust nobody, for fear you be betrayd.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: The trust I have is in mine innocence,

speaker: SAY
text_entry: And therefore am I bold and resolute.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: SAY
text_entry: SCENE V. London. The Tower.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Enter SCALES upon the Tower, walking. Then enter two or three Citizens below

speaker: SCALES
text_entry: How now! is Jack Cade slain?

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: No, my lord, nor likely to be slain; for they have

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: won the bridge, killing all those that withstand

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: them: the lord mayor craves aid of your honour from

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: the Tower, to defend the city from the rebels.

speaker: SCALES
text_entry: Such aid as I can spare you shall command;

speaker: SCALES
text_entry: But I am troubled here with them myself;

speaker: SCALES
text_entry: The rebels have assayd to win the Tower.

speaker: SCALES
text_entry: But get you to Smithfield, and gather head,

speaker: SCALES
text_entry: And thither I will send you Matthew Goffe;

speaker: SCALES
text_entry: Fight for your king, your country and your lives;

speaker: SCALES
text_entry: And so, farewell, for I must hence again.

speaker: SCALES
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: SCALES
text_entry: SCENE VI. London. Cannon Street.

speaker: SCALES
text_entry: Enter CADE and the rest, and strikes his staff on London-stone

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Now is Mortimer lord of this city. And here, sitting

speaker: CADE
text_entry: upon London-stone, I charge and command that, of the

speaker: CADE
text_entry: citys cost, the pissing-conduit run nothing but

speaker: CADE
text_entry: claret wine this first year of our reign. And now

speaker: CADE
text_entry: henceforward it shall be treason for any that calls

speaker: CADE
text_entry: me other than Lord Mortimer.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Enter a Soldier, running

speaker: Soldier
text_entry: Jack Cade! Jack Cade!

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Knock him down there.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: They kill him

speaker: SMITH
text_entry: If this fellow be wise, hell never call ye Jack

speaker: SMITH
text_entry: Cade more: I think he hath a very fair warning.

speaker: DICK
text_entry: My lord, theres an army gathered together in

speaker: DICK
text_entry: Smithfield.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Come, then, lets go fight with them; but first, go

speaker: CADE
text_entry: and set London bridge on fire; and, if you can, burn

speaker: CADE
text_entry: down the Tower too. Come, lets away.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: CADE
text_entry: SCENE VII. London. Smithfield.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Alarums. MATTHEW GOFFE is slain, and all the rest. Then enter CADE, with his company.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: So, sirs: now go some and pull down the Savoy;

speaker: CADE
text_entry: others to the inns of court; down with them all.

speaker: DICK
text_entry: I have a suit unto your lordship.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Be it a lordship, thou shalt have it for that word.

speaker: DICK
text_entry: Only that the laws of England may come out of your mouth.

speaker: HOLLAND
text_entry: [Aside]  Mass, twill be sore law, then; for he was

speaker: HOLLAND
text_entry: thrust in the mouth with a spear, and tis not whole

speaker: HOLLAND
text_entry: yet.

speaker: SMITH
text_entry: [Aside]  Nay, John, it will be stinking law for his

speaker: SMITH
text_entry: breath stinks with eating toasted cheese.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: I have thought upon it, it shall be so. Away, burn

speaker: CADE
text_entry: all the records of the realm: my mouth shall be

speaker: CADE
text_entry: the parliament of England.

speaker: HOLLAND
text_entry: [Aside]  Then we are like to have biting statutes,

speaker: HOLLAND
text_entry: unless his teeth be pulled out.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: And henceforward all things shall be in common.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Enter a Messenger

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: My lord, a prize, a prize! heres the Lord Say,

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: which sold the towns in France; he that made us pay

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: one and twenty fifteens, and one shilling to the

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: pound, the last subsidy.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Enter BEVIS, with Lord SAY

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Well, he shall be beheaded for it ten times. Ah,

speaker: CADE
text_entry: thou say, thou serge, nay, thou buckram lord! now

speaker: CADE
text_entry: art thou within point-blank of our jurisdiction

speaker: CADE
text_entry: regal. What canst thou answer to my majesty for

speaker: CADE
text_entry: giving up of Normandy unto Mounsieur Basimecu, the

speaker: CADE
text_entry: dauphin of France? Be it known unto thee by these

speaker: CADE
text_entry: presence, even the presence of Lord Mortimer, that I

speaker: CADE
text_entry: am the besom that must sweep the court clean of such

speaker: CADE
text_entry: filth as thou art. Thou hast most traitorously

speaker: CADE
text_entry: corrupted the youth of the realm in erecting a

speaker: CADE
text_entry: grammar school; and whereas, before, our forefathers

speaker: CADE
text_entry: had no other books but the score and the tally, thou

speaker: CADE
text_entry: hast caused printing to be used, and, contrary to

speaker: CADE
text_entry: the king, his crown and dignity, thou hast built a

speaker: CADE
text_entry: paper-mill. It will be proved to thy face that thou

speaker: CADE
text_entry: hast men about thee that usually talk of a noun and

speaker: CADE
text_entry: a verb, and such abominable words as no Christian

speaker: CADE
text_entry: ear can endure to hear. Thou hast appointed

speaker: CADE
text_entry: justices of peace, to call poor men before them

speaker: CADE
text_entry: about matters they were not able to answer.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Moreover, thou hast put them in prison; and because

speaker: CADE
text_entry: they could not read, thou hast hanged them; when,

speaker: CADE
text_entry: indeed, only for that cause they have been most

speaker: CADE
text_entry: worthy to live. Thou dost ride in a foot-cloth, dost thou not?

speaker: SAY
text_entry: What of that?

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Marry, thou oughtest not to let thy horse wear a

speaker: CADE
text_entry: cloak, when honester men than thou go in their hose

speaker: CADE
text_entry: and doublets.

speaker: DICK
text_entry: And work in their shirt too; as myself, for example,

speaker: DICK
text_entry: that am a butcher.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: You men of Kent,--

speaker: DICK
text_entry: What say you of Kent?

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Nothing but this; tis bona terra, mala gens.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Away with him, away with him! he speaks Latin.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Hear me but speak, and bear me where you will.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Kent, in the Commentaries Caesar writ,

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Is termd the civilst place of this isle:

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Sweet is the country, because full of riches;

speaker: SAY
text_entry: The people liberal, valiant, active, wealthy;

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Which makes me hope you are not void of pity.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: I sold not Maine, I lost not Normandy,

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Yet, to recover them, would lose my life.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Justice with favour have I always done;

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Prayers and tears have moved me, gifts could never.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: When have I aught exacted at your hands,

speaker: SAY
text_entry: But to maintain the king, the realm and you?

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Large gifts have I bestowd on learned clerks,

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Because my book preferrd me to the king,

speaker: SAY
text_entry: And seeing ignorance is the curse of God,

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Knowledge the wing wherewith we fly to heaven,

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Unless you be possessd with devilish spirits,

speaker: SAY
text_entry: You cannot but forbear to murder me:

speaker: SAY
text_entry: This tongue hath parleyd unto foreign kings

speaker: SAY
text_entry: For your behoof,--

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Tut, when struckst thou one blow in the field?

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Great men have reaching hands: oft have I struck

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Those that I never saw and struck them dead.

speaker: BEVIS
text_entry: O monstrous coward! what, to come behind folks?

speaker: SAY
text_entry: These cheeks are pale for watching for your good.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Give him a box o the ear and that will make em red again.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Long sitting to determine poor mens causes

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Hath made me full of sickness and diseases.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Ye shall have a hempen caudle, then, and the help of hatchet.

speaker: DICK
text_entry: Why dost thou quiver, man?

speaker: SAY
text_entry: The palsy, and not fear, provokes me.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Nay, he nods at us, as who should say, Ill be even

speaker: CADE
text_entry: with you: Ill see if his head will stand steadier

speaker: CADE
text_entry: on a pole, or no. Take him away, and behead him.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Tell me wherein have I offended most?

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Have I affected wealth or honour? speak.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Are my chests filld up with extorted gold?

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Is my apparel sumptuous to behold?

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Whom have I injured, that ye seek my death?

speaker: SAY
text_entry: These hands are free from guiltless bloodshedding,

speaker: SAY
text_entry: This breast from harbouring foul deceitful thoughts.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: O, let me live!

speaker: CADE
text_entry: [Aside]  I feel remorse in myself with his words;

speaker: CADE
text_entry: but Ill bridle it: he shall die, an it be but for

speaker: CADE
text_entry: pleading so well for his life. Away with him! he

speaker: CADE
text_entry: has a familiar under his tongue; he speaks not o

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Gods name. Go, take him away, I say, and strike

speaker: CADE
text_entry: off his head presently; and then break into his

speaker: CADE
text_entry: son-in-laws house, Sir James Cromer, and strike off

speaker: CADE
text_entry: his head, and bring them both upon two poles hither.

speaker: ALL
text_entry: It shall be done.

speaker: SAY
text_entry: Ah, countrymen! if when you make your prayers,

speaker: SAY
text_entry: God should be so obdurate as yourselves,

speaker: SAY
text_entry: How would it fare with your departed souls?

speaker: SAY
text_entry: And therefore yet relent, and save my life.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Away with him! and do as I command ye.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Exeunt some with Lord SAY

speaker: CADE
text_entry: The proudest peer in the realm shall not wear a head

speaker: CADE
text_entry: on his shoulders, unless he pay me tribute; there

speaker: CADE
text_entry: shall not a maid be married, but she shall pay to me

speaker: CADE
text_entry: her maidenhead ere they have it: men shall hold of

speaker: CADE
text_entry: me in capite; and we charge and command that their

speaker: CADE
text_entry: wives be as free as heart can wish or tongue can tell.

speaker: DICK
text_entry: My lord, when shall we go to Cheapside and take up

speaker: DICK
text_entry: commodities upon our bills?

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Marry, presently.

speaker: ALL
text_entry: O, brave!

speaker: ALL
text_entry: Re-enter one with the heads

speaker: CADE
text_entry: But is not this braver? Let them kiss one another,

speaker: CADE
text_entry: for they loved well when they were alive. Now part

speaker: CADE
text_entry: them again, lest they consult about the giving up of

speaker: CADE
text_entry: some more towns in France. Soldiers, defer the

speaker: CADE
text_entry: spoil of the city until night: for with these borne

speaker: CADE
text_entry: before us, instead of maces, will we ride through

speaker: CADE
text_entry: the streets, and at every corner have them kiss. Away!

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: CADE
text_entry: SCENE VIII. Southwark.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Alarum and retreat. Enter CADE and all his rabblement

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Up Fish Street! down Saint Magnus Corner! Kill

speaker: CADE
text_entry: and knock down! throw them into Thames!

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Sound a parley

speaker: CADE
text_entry: What noise is this I hear? Dare any be so bold to

speaker: CADE
text_entry: sound retreat or parley, when I command them kill?

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Enter BUCKINGHAM and CLIFFORD, attended

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Ay, here they be that dare and will disturb thee:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Know, Cade, we come ambassadors from the king

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Unto the commons whom thou hast misled;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And here pronounce free pardon to them all

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: That will forsake thee and go home in peace.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: What say ye, countrymen? will ye relent,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: And yield to mercy whilst tis offerd you;

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Or let a rebel lead you to your deaths?

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Who loves the king and will embrace his pardon,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Fling up his cap, and say God save his majesty!

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Who hateth him and honours not his father,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Henry the Fifth, that made all France to quake,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Shake he his weapon at us and pass by.

speaker: ALL
text_entry: God save the king! God save the king!

speaker: CADE
text_entry: What, Buckingham and Clifford, are ye so brave? And

speaker: CADE
text_entry: you, base peasants, do ye believe him? will you

speaker: CADE
text_entry: needs be hanged with your pardons about your necks?

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Hath my sword therefore broke through London gates,

speaker: CADE
text_entry: that you should leave me at the White Hart in

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Southwark? I thought ye would never have given out

speaker: CADE
text_entry: these arms till you had recovered your ancient

speaker: CADE
text_entry: freedom: but you are all recreants and dastards,

speaker: CADE
text_entry: and delight to live in slavery to the nobility. Let

speaker: CADE
text_entry: them break your backs with burthens, take your

speaker: CADE
text_entry: houses over your heads, ravish your wives and

speaker: CADE
text_entry: daughters before your faces: for me, I will make

speaker: CADE
text_entry: shift for one; and so, Gods curse light upon you

speaker: CADE
text_entry: all!

speaker: ALL
text_entry: Well follow Cade, well follow Cade!

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Is Cade the son of Henry the Fifth,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: That thus you do exclaim youll go with him?

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Will he conduct you through the heart of France,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: And make the meanest of you earls and dukes?

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Alas, he hath no home, no place to fly to;

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Nor knows he how to live but by the spoil,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Unless by robbing of your friends and us.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Weret not a shame, that whilst you live at jar,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: The fearful French, whom you late vanquished,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Should make a start oer seas and vanquish you?

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Methinks already in this civil broil

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: I see them lording it in London streets,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Crying Villiago! unto all they meet.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Better ten thousand base-born Cades miscarry

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Than you should stoop unto a Frenchmans mercy.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: To France, to France, and get what you have lost;

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Spare England, for it is your native coast;

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Henry hath money, you are strong and manly;

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: God on our side, doubt not of victory.

speaker: ALL
text_entry: A Clifford! a Clifford! well follow the king and Clifford.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Was ever feather so lightly blown to and fro as this

speaker: CADE
text_entry: multitude? The name of Henry the Fifth hales them

speaker: CADE
text_entry: to an hundred mischiefs, and makes them leave me

speaker: CADE
text_entry: desolate. I see them lay their heads together to

speaker: CADE
text_entry: surprise me. My sword make way for me, for here is

speaker: CADE
text_entry: no staying. In despite of the devils and hell, have

speaker: CADE
text_entry: through the very middest of you? and heavens and

speaker: CADE
text_entry: honour be witness, that no want of resolution in me.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: but only my followers base and ignominious

speaker: CADE
text_entry: treasons, makes me betake me to my heels.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: What, is he fled? Go some, and follow him;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And he that brings his head unto the king

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Shall have a thousand crowns for his reward.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Exeunt some of them

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Follow me, soldiers: well devise a mean

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: To reconcile you all unto the king.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: SCENE IX. Kenilworth Castle.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Sound Trumpets. Enter KING HENRY VI, QUEEN MARGARET, and SOMERSET, on the terrace

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Was ever king that joyd an earthly throne,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And could command no more content than I?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: No sooner was I crept out of my cradle

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: But I was made a king, at nine months old.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Was never subject longd to be a king

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: As I do long and wish to be a subject.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Enter BUCKINGHAM and CLIFFORD

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Health and glad tidings to your majesty!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Why, Buckingham, is the traitor Cade surprised?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Or is he but retired to make him strong?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Enter below, multitudes, with halters about their necks

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: He is fled, my lord, and all his powers do yield;

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: And humbly thus, with halters on their necks,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Expect your highness doom of life or death.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Then, heaven, set ope thy everlasting gates,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: To entertain my vows of thanks and praise!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Soldiers, this day have you redeemed your lives,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And showd how well you love your prince and country:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Continue still in this so good a mind,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And Henry, though he be infortunate,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Assure yourselves, will never be unkind:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And so, with thanks and pardon to you all,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: I do dismiss you to your several countries.

speaker: ALL
text_entry: God save the king! God save the king!

speaker: ALL
text_entry: Enter a Messenger

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Please it your grace to be advertised

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: The Duke of York is newly come from Ireland,

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: And with a puissant and a mighty power

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Of gallowglasses and stout kerns

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Is marching hitherward in proud array,

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: And still proclaimeth, as he comes along,

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: His arms are only to remove from thee

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: The Duke of Somerset, whom he terms traitor.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Thus stands my state, twixt Cade and York distressd.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Like to a ship that, having scaped a tempest,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Is straightway calmd and boarded with a pirate:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: But now is Cade driven back, his men dispersed;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And now is York in arms to second him.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: I pray thee, Buckingham, go and meet him,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And ask him whats the reason of these arms.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Tell him Ill send Duke Edmund to the Tower;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And, Somerset, well commit thee thither,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Until his army be dismissd from him.

speaker: SOMERSET
text_entry: My lord,

speaker: SOMERSET
text_entry: Ill yield myself to prison willingly,

speaker: SOMERSET
text_entry: Or unto death, to do my country good.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: In any case, be not too rough in terms;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: For he is fierce and cannot brook hard language.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: I will, my lord; and doubt not so to deal

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: As all things shall redound unto your good.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Come, wife, lets in, and learn to govern better;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: For yet may England curse my wretched reign.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Flourish. Exeunt

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: SCENE X. Kent. IDENs garden.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Enter CADE

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Fie on ambition! fie on myself, that have a sword,

speaker: CADE
text_entry: and yet am ready to famish! These five days have I

speaker: CADE
text_entry: hid me in these woods and durst not peep out, for

speaker: CADE
text_entry: all the country is laid for me; but now am I so

speaker: CADE
text_entry: hungry that if I might have a lease of my life for a

speaker: CADE
text_entry: thousand years I could stay no longer. Wherefore,

speaker: CADE
text_entry: on a brick wall have I climbed into this garden, to

speaker: CADE
text_entry: see if I can eat grass, or pick a sallet another

speaker: CADE
text_entry: while, which is not amiss to cool a mans stomach

speaker: CADE
text_entry: this hot weather. And I think this word sallet

speaker: CADE
text_entry: was born to do me good: for many a time, but for a

speaker: CADE
text_entry: sallet, my brainpan had been cleft with a brown

speaker: CADE
text_entry: bill; and many a time, when I have been dry and

speaker: CADE
text_entry: bravely marching, it hath served me instead of a

speaker: CADE
text_entry: quart pot to drink in; and now the word sallet

speaker: CADE
text_entry: must serve me to feed on.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Enter IDEN

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Lord, who would live turmoiled in the court,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: And may enjoy such quiet walks as these?

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: This small inheritance my father left me

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Contenteth me, and worth a monarchy.

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: I seek not to wax great by others waning,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Or gather wealth, I care not, with what envy:

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Sufficeth that I have maintains my state

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: And sends the poor well pleased from my gate.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Heres the lord of the soil come to seize me for a

speaker: CADE
text_entry: stray, for entering his fee-simple without leave.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Ah, villain, thou wilt betray me, and get a thousand

speaker: CADE
text_entry: crowns of the king carrying my head to him: but

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Ill make thee eat iron like an ostrich, and swallow

speaker: CADE
text_entry: my sword like a great pin, ere thou and I part.

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Why, rude companion, whatsoeer thou be,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: I know thee not; why, then, should I betray thee?

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Ist not enough to break into my garden,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: And, like a thief, to come to rob my grounds,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Climbing my walls in spite of me the owner,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: But thou wilt brave me with these saucy terms?

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Brave thee! ay, by the best blood that ever was

speaker: CADE
text_entry: broached, and beard thee too. Look on me well: I

speaker: CADE
text_entry: have eat no meat these five days; yet, come thou and

speaker: CADE
text_entry: thy five men, and if I do not leave you all as dead

speaker: CADE
text_entry: as a doornail, I pray God I may never eat grass more.

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Nay, it shall neer be said, while England stands,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: That Alexander Iden, an esquire of Kent,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Took odds to combat a poor famishd man.

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Oppose thy steadfast-gazing eyes to mine,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: See if thou canst outface me with thy looks:

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Set limb to limb, and thou art far the lesser;

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Thy hand is but a finger to my fist,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Thy leg a stick compared with this truncheon;

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: My foot shall fight with all the strength thou hast;

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: And if mine arm be heaved in the air,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Thy grave is diggd already in the earth.

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: As for words, whose greatness answers words,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Let this my sword report what speech forbears.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: By my valour, the most complete champion that ever I

speaker: CADE
text_entry: heard! Steel, if thou turn the edge, or cut not out

speaker: CADE
text_entry: the burly-boned clown in chines of beef ere thou

speaker: CADE
text_entry: sleep in thy sheath, I beseech God on my knees thou

speaker: CADE
text_entry: mayst be turned to hobnails.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Here they fight. CADE falls

speaker: CADE
text_entry: O, I am slain! famine and no other hath slain me:

speaker: CADE
text_entry: let ten thousand devils come against me, and give me

speaker: CADE
text_entry: but the ten meals I have lost, and Ill defy them

speaker: CADE
text_entry: all. Wither, garden; and be henceforth a

speaker: CADE
text_entry: burying-place to all that do dwell in this house,

speaker: CADE
text_entry: because the unconquered soul of Cade is fled.

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Ist Cade that I have slain, that monstrous traitor?

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Sword, I will hollow thee for this thy deed,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: And hang thee oer my tomb when I am dead:

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Neer shall this blood be wiped from thy point;

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: But thou shalt wear it as a heralds coat,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: To emblaze the honour that thy master got.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Iden, farewell, and be proud of thy victory. Tell

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Kent from me, she hath lost her best man, and exhort

speaker: CADE
text_entry: all the world to be cowards; for I, that never

speaker: CADE
text_entry: feared any, am vanquished by famine, not by valour.

speaker: CADE
text_entry: Dies

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: How much thou wrongst me, heaven be my judge.

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Die, damned wretch, the curse of her that bare thee;

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: And as I thrust thy body in with my sword,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: So wish I, I might thrust thy soul to hell.

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Hence will I drag thee headlong by the heels

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Unto a dunghill which shall be thy grave,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: And there cut off thy most ungracious head;

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Which I will bear in triumph to the king,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Leaving thy trunk for crows to feed upon.

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Exit

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: ACT V

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: SCENE I. Fields between Dartford and Blackheath.

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Enter YORK, and his army of Irish, with drum and colours

speaker: YORK
text_entry: From Ireland thus comes York to claim his right,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And pluck the crown from feeble Henrys head:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Ring, bells, aloud; burn, bonfires, clear and bright,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: To entertain great Englands lawful king.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Ah! sancta majestas, who would not buy thee dear?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Let them obey that know not how to rule;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: This hand was made to handle naught but gold.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: I cannot give due action to my words,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Except a sword or sceptre balance it:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: A sceptre shall it have, have I a soul,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: On which Ill toss the flower-de-luce of France.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Enter BUCKINGHAM

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Whom have we here? Buckingham, to disturb me?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The king hath sent him, sure: I must dissemble.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: York, if thou meanest well, I greet thee well.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Humphrey of Buckingham, I accept thy greeting.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Art thou a messenger, or come of pleasure?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: A messenger from Henry, our dread liege,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: To know the reason of these arms in peace;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Or why thou, being a subject as I am,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Against thy oath and true allegiance sworn,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Should raise so great a power without his leave,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Or dare to bring thy force so near the court.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: [Aside]  Scarce can I speak, my choler is so great:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: O, I could hew up rocks and fight with flint,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: I am so angry at these abject terms;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And now, like Ajax Telamonius,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: On sheep or oxen could I spend my fury.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: I am far better born than is the king,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: More like a king, more kingly in my thoughts:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: But I must make fair weather yet a while,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Till Henry be more weak and I more strong,--

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Buckingham, I prithee, pardon me,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: That I have given no answer all this while;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: My mind was troubled with deep melancholy.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: The cause why I have brought this army hither

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Is to remove proud Somerset from the king,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Seditious to his grace and to the state.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: That is too much presumption on thy part:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: But if thy arms be to no other end,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The king hath yielded unto thy demand:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The Duke of Somerset is in the Tower.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Upon thine honour, is he prisoner?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Upon mine honour, he is prisoner.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Then, Buckingham, I do dismiss my powers.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Soldiers, I thank you all; disperse yourselves;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Meet me to-morrow in St. Georges field,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: You shall have pay and every thing you wish.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And let my sovereign, virtuous Henry,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Command my eldest son, nay, all my sons,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: As pledges of my fealty and love;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Ill send them all as willing as I live:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Lands, goods, horse, armour, any thing I have,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Is his to use, so Somerset may die.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: York, I commend this kind submission:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: We twain will go into his highness tent.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Enter KING HENRY VI and Attendants

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Buckingham, doth York intend no harm to us,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: That thus he marcheth with thee arm in arm?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: In all submission and humility

speaker: YORK
text_entry: York doth present himself unto your highness.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Then what intends these forces thou dost bring?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: To heave the traitor Somerset from hence,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And fight against that monstrous rebel Cade,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Who since I heard to be discomfited.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Enter IDEN, with CADES head

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: If one so rude and of so mean condition

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: May pass into the presence of a king,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Lo, I present your grace a traitors head,

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: The head of Cade, whom I in combat slew.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: The head of Cade! Great God, how just art Thou!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: O, let me view his visage, being dead,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: That living wrought me such exceeding trouble.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Tell me, my friend, art thou the man that slew him?

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: I was, ant like your majesty.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: How art thou calld? and what is thy degree?

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Alexander Iden, thats my name;

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: A poor esquire of Kent, that loves his king.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: So please it you, my lord, twere not amiss

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: He were created knight for his good service.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Iden, kneel down.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: He kneels

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Rise up a knight.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: We give thee for reward a thousand marks,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And will that thou henceforth attend on us.

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: May Iden live to merit such a bounty.

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: And never live but true unto his liege!

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Rises

speaker: IDEN
text_entry: Enter QUEEN MARGARET and SOMERSET

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: See, Buckingham, Somerset comes with the queen:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Go, bid her hide him quickly from the duke.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: For thousand Yorks he shall not hide his head,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: But boldly stand and front him to his face.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: How now! is Somerset at liberty?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Then, York, unloose thy long-imprisond thoughts,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And let thy tongue be equal with thy heart.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Shall I endure the sight of Somerset?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: False king! why hast thou broken faith with me,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Knowing how hardly I can brook abuse?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: King did I call thee? no, thou art not king,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Not fit to govern and rule multitudes,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Which darest not, no, nor canst not rule a traitor.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: That head of thine doth not become a crown;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Thy hand is made to grasp a palmers staff,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And not to grace an awful princely sceptre.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: That gold must round engirt these brows of mine,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Whose smile and frown, like to Achilles spear,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Is able with the change to kill and cure.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Here is a hand to hold a sceptre up

speaker: YORK

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And thine, Lord Clifford; and you both have vowd revenge

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: On him, his sons, his favourites and his friends.

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: If I be not, heavens be revenged on me!

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: The hope thereof makes Clifford mourn in steel.

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: What, shall we suffer this? lets pluck him down:

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: My heart for anger burns; I cannot brook it.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Be patient, gentle Earl of Westmoreland.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Patience is for poltroons, such as he:

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: He durst not sit there, had your father lived.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: My gracious lord, here in the parliament

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Let us assail the family of York.

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Well hast thou spoken, cousin: be it so.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Ah, know you not the city favours them,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And they have troops of soldiers at their beck?

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: But when the duke is slain, theyll quickly fly.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Far be the thought of this from Henrys heart,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: To make a shambles of the parliament-house!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Cousin of Exeter, frowns, words and threats

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Shall be the war that Henry means to use.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Thou factious Duke of York, descend my throne,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: and kneel for grace and mercy at my feet;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: I am thy sovereign.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: I am thine.

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: For shame, come down: he made thee Duke of York.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Twas my inheritance, as the earldom was.

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: Thy father was a traitor to the crown.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Exeter, thou art a traitor to the crown

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: In following this usurping Henry.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Whom should he follow but his natural king?

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: True, Clifford; and thats Richard Duke of York.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And shall I stand, and thou sit in my throne?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: It must and shall be so: content thyself.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Be Duke of Lancaster; let him be king.

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: He is both king and Duke of Lancaster;

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: And that the Lord of Westmoreland shall maintain.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And Warwick shall disprove it. You forget

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: That we are those which chased you from the field

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And slew your fathers, and with colours spread

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Marchd through the city to the palace gates.

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Yes, Warwick, I remember it to my grief;

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: And, by his soul, thou and thy house shall rue it.

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: Plantagenet, of thee and these thy sons,

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: Thy kinsman and thy friends, Ill have more lives

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: Than drops of blood were in my fathers veins.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Urge it no more; lest that, instead of words,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: I send thee, Warwick, such a messenger

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: As shall revenge his death before I stir.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Poor Clifford! how I scorn his worthless threats!

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Will you we show our title to the crown?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: If not, our swords shall plead it in the field.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: What title hast thou, traitor, to the crown?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Thy father was, as thou art, Duke of York;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Thy grandfather, Roger Mortimer, Earl of March:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: I am the son of Henry the Fifth,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Who made the Dauphin and the French to stoop

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And seized upon their towns and provinces.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Talk not of France, sith thou hast lost it all.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: The lord protector lost it, and not I:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: When I was crownd I was but nine months old.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: You are old enough now, and yet, methinks, you lose.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Father, tear the crown from the usurpers head.

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: Sweet father, do so; set it on your head.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Good brother, as thou lovest and honourest arms,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Lets fight it out and not stand cavilling thus.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Sound drums and trumpets, and the king will fly.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Sons, peace!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Peace, thou! and give King Henry leave to speak.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Plantagenet shall speak first: hear him, lords;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And be you silent and attentive too,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: For he that interrupts him shall not live.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Thinkst thou that I will leave my kingly throne,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Wherein my grandsire and my father sat?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: No: first shall war unpeople this my realm;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Ay, and their colours, often borne in France,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And now in England to our hearts great sorrow,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Shall be my winding-sheet. Why faint you, lords?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: My titles good, and better far than his.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Prove it, Henry, and thou shalt be king.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Henry the Fourth by conquest got the crown.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Twas by rebellion against his king.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: [Aside]  I know not what to say; my titles weak.--

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Tell me, may not a king adopt an heir?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: What then?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: An if he may, then am I lawful king;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: For Richard, in the view of many lords,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Resignd the crown to Henry the Fourth,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Whose heir my father was, and I am his.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: He rose against him, being his sovereign,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And made him to resign his crown perforce.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Suppose, my lords, he did it unconstraind,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Think you twere prejudicial to his crown?

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: No; for he could not so resign his crown

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: But that the next heir should succeed and reign.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Art thou against us, Duke of Exeter?

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: His is the right, and therefore pardon me.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Why whisper you, my lords, and answer not?

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: My conscience tells me he is lawful king.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: [Aside]  All will revolt from me, and turn to him.

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Plantagenet, for all the claim thou layst,

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Think not that Henry shall be so deposed.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Deposed he shall be, in despite of all.

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Thou art deceived: tis not thy southern power,

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Of Essex, Norfolk, Suffolk, nor of Kent,

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Which makes thee thus presumptuous and proud,

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Can set the duke up in despite of me.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: King Henry, be thy title right or wrong,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Lord Clifford vows to fight in thy defence:

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: May that ground gape and swallow me alive,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Where I shall kneel to him that slew my father!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: O Clifford, how thy words revive my heart!

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Henry of Lancaster, resign thy crown.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: What mutter you, or what conspire you, lords?

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Do right unto this princely Duke of York,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Or I will fill the house with armed men,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And over the chair of state, where now he sits,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Write up his title with usurping blood.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: He stamps with his foot and the soldiers show themselves

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: My Lord of Warwick, hear me but one word:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Let me for this my life-time reign as king.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Confirm the crown to me and to mine heirs,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And thou shalt reign in quiet while thou livest.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: I am content: Richard Plantagenet,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Enjoy the kingdom after my decease.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: What wrong is this unto the prince your son!

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: What good is this to England and himself!

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: Base, fearful and despairing Henry!

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: How hast thou injured both thyself and us!

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: I cannot stay to hear these articles.

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Nor I.

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Come, cousin, let us tell the queen these news.

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: Farewell, faint-hearted and degenerate king,

speaker: WESTMORELAND
text_entry: In whose cold blood no spark of honour bides.

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Be thou a prey unto the house of York,

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: And die in bands for this unmanly deed!

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: In dreadful war mayst thou be overcome,

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Or live in peace abandond and despised!

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Exeunt NORTHUMBERLAND, CLIFFORD, and WESTMORELAND

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Turn this way, Henry, and regard them not.

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: They seek revenge and therefore will not yield.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Ah, Exeter!

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Why should you sigh, my lord?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Not for myself, Lord Warwick, but my son,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Whom I unnaturally shall disinherit.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: But be it as it may: I here entail

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: The crown to thee and to thine heirs for ever;

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Conditionally, that here thou take an oath

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: To cease this civil war, and, whilst I live,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: To honour me as thy king and sovereign,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And neither by treason nor hostility

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: To seek to put me down and reign thyself.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: This oath I willingly take and will perform.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Long live King Henry! Plantagenet embrace him.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And long live thou and these thy forward sons!

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Now York and Lancaster are reconciled.

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: Accursed be he that seeks to make them foes!

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: Sennet. Here they come down

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Farewell, my gracious lord; Ill to my castle.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And Ill keep London with my soldiers.

speaker: NORFOLK
text_entry: And I to Norfolk with my followers.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: And I unto the sea from whence I came.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Exeunt YORK, EDWARD, EDMUND, GEORGE, RICHARD,  WARWICK, NORFOLK, MONTAGUE, their Soldiers, and Attendants

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: And I, with grief and sorrow, to the court.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Enter QUEEN MARGARET and PRINCE EDWARD

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: Here comes the queen, whose looks bewray her anger:

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: Ill steal away.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Exeter, so will I.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Nay, go not from me; I will follow thee.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Be patient, gentle queen, and I will stay.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Who can be patient in such extremes?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Ah, wretched man! would I had died a maid

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And never seen thee, never borne thee son,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Seeing thou hast proved so unnatural a father

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Hath he deserved to lose his birthright thus?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Hadst thou but loved him half so well as I,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Or felt that pain which I did for him once,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Or nourishd him as I did with my blood,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thou wouldst have left thy dearest heart-blood there,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Rather than have that savage duke thine heir

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And disinherited thine only son.

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text_entry: Father, you cannot disinherit me:

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text_entry: If you be king, why should not I succeed?

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Pardon me, Margaret; pardon me, sweet son:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: The Earl of Warwick and the duke enforced me.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Enforced thee! art thou king, and wilt be forced?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: I shame to hear thee speak. Ah, timorous wretch!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thou hast undone thyself, thy son and me;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And given unto the house of York such head

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: As thou shalt reign but by their sufferance.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: To entail him and his heirs unto the crown,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: What is it, but to make thy sepulchre

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And creep into it far before thy time?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Warwick is chancellor and the lord of Calais;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Stern Falconbridge commands the narrow seas;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: The duke is made protector of the realm;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And yet shalt thou be safe? such safety finds

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: The trembling lamb environed with wolves.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Had I been there, which am a silly woman,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: The soldiers should have tossd me on their pikes

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Before I would have granted to that act.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: But thou preferrst thy life before thine honour:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And seeing thou dost, I here divorce myself

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Both from thy table, Henry, and thy bed,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Until that act of parliament be repeald

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Whereby my son is disinherited.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: The northern lords that have forsworn thy colours

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Will follow mine, if once they see them spread;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And spread they shall be, to thy foul disgrace

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And utter ruin of the house of York.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thus do I leave thee. Come, son, lets away;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Our army is ready; come, well after them.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Stay, gentle Margaret, and hear me speak.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thou hast spoke too much already: get thee gone.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Gentle son Edward, thou wilt stay with me?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Ay, to be murderd by his enemies.

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text_entry: When I return with victory from the field

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text_entry: Ill see your grace: till then Ill follow her.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Come, son, away; we may not linger thus.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Exeunt QUEEN MARGARET and PRINCE EDWARD

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Poor queen! how love to me and to her son

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Hath made her break out into terms of rage!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Revenged may she be on that hateful duke,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Whose haughty spirit, winged with desire,

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Will cost my crown, and like an empty eagle

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Tire on the flesh of me and of my son!

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: The loss of those three lords torments my heart:

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Ill write unto them and entreat them fair.

speaker: KING HENRY VI
text_entry: Come, cousin you shall be the messenger.

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: And I, I hope, shall reconcile them all.

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: SCENE II. Sandal Castle.

speaker: EXETER
text_entry: Enter RICHARD, EDWARD, and MONTAGUE

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Brother, though I be youngest, give me leave.

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: No, I can better play the orator.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: But I have reasons strong and forcible.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Enter YORK

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Why, how now, sons and brother! at a strife?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: What is your quarrel? how began it first?

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: No quarrel, but a slight contention.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: About what?

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: About that which concerns your grace and us;

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: The crown of England, father, which is yours.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Mine boy? not till King Henry be dead.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Your right depends not on his life or death.

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: Now you are heir, therefore enjoy it now:

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: By giving the house of Lancaster leave to breathe,

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: It will outrun you, father, in the end.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: I took an oath that he should quietly reign.

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: But for a kingdom any oath may be broken:

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: I would break a thousand oaths to reign one year.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: No; God forbid your grace should be forsworn.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: I shall be, if I claim by open war.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Ill prove the contrary, if youll hear me speak.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Thou canst not, son; it is impossible.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: An oath is of no moment, being not took

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Before a true and lawful magistrate,

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: That hath authority over him that swears:

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Henry had none, but did usurp the place;

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Then, seeing twas he that made you to depose,

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Your oath, my lord, is vain and frivolous.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Therefore, to arms! And, father, do but think

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: How sweet a thing it is to wear a crown;

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Within whose circuit is Elysium

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: And all that poets feign of bliss and joy.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Why do we finger thus? I cannot rest

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Until the white rose that I wear be dyed

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Even in the lukewarm blood of Henrys heart.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Richard, enough; I will be king, or die.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Brother, thou shalt to London presently,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And whet on Warwick to this enterprise.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Thou, Richard, shalt to the Duke of Norfolk,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And tell him privily of our intent.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: You Edward, shall unto my Lord Cobham,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: With whom the Kentishmen will willingly rise:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: In them I trust; for they are soldiers,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Witty, courteous, liberal, full of spirit.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: While you are thus employd, what resteth more,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: But that I seek occasion how to rise,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And yet the king not privy to my drift,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Nor any of the house of Lancaster?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Enter a Messenger

speaker: YORK
text_entry: But, stay: what news? Why comest thou in such post?

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: The queen with all the northern earls and lords

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Intend here to besiege you in your castle:

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: She is hard by with twenty thousand men;

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: And therefore fortify your hold, my lord.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Ay, with my sword. What! thinkst thou that we fear them?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Edward and Richard, you shall stay with me;

speaker: YORK
text_entry: My brother Montague shall post to London:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Let noble Warwick, Cobham, and the rest,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Whom we have left protectors of the king,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: With powerful policy strengthen themselves,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: And trust not simple Henry nor his oaths.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Brother, I go; Ill win them, fear it not:

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: And thus most humbly I do take my leave.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Enter JOHN MORTIMER and HUGH MORTIMER

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Sir John and Sir Hugh Mortimer, mine uncles,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: You are come to Sandal in a happy hour;

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: The army of the queen mean to besiege us.

speaker: JOHN MORTIMER
text_entry: She shall not need; well meet her in the field.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: What, with five thousand men?

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Ay, with five hundred, father, for a need:

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: A womans general; what should we fear?

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: A march afar off

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: I hear their drums: lets set our men in order,

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: And issue forth and bid them battle straight.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Five men to twenty! though the odds be great,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: I doubt not, uncle, of our victory.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Many a battle have I won in France,

speaker: YORK
text_entry: When as the enemy hath been ten to one:

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Why should I not now have the like success?

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Alarum. Exeunt

speaker: YORK
text_entry: SCENE III. Field of battle betwixt Sandal Castle and Wakefield.

speaker: YORK
text_entry: Alarums. Enter RUTLAND and his Tutor

speaker: RUTLAND
text_entry: Ah, whither shall I fly to scape their hands?

speaker: RUTLAND
text_entry: Ah, tutor, look where bloody Clifford comes!

speaker: RUTLAND
text_entry: Enter CLIFFORD and Soldiers

speaker: CLIFFORD
text_entry: Chaplain, away! thy priesthood saves thy life.

speaker: CLIFFORD

text_entry: And burns me up with flames that tears would quench.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: To weep is to make less the depth of grief:

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Tears then for babes; blows and revenge for me

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Richard, I bear thy name; Ill venge thy death,

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Or die renowned by attempting it.

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: His name that valiant duke hath left with thee;

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: His dukedom and his chair with me is left.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Nay, if thou be that princely eagles bird,

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Show thy descent by gazing gainst the sun:

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: For chair and dukedom, throne and kingdom say;

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Either that is thine, or else thou wert not his.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: March. Enter WARWICK, MONTAGUE, and their army

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: How now, fair lords! What fare? what news abroad?

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Great Lord of Warwick, if we should recount

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Our baleful news, and at each words deliverance

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Stab poniards in our flesh till all were told,

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: The words would add more anguish than the wounds.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: O valiant lord, the Duke of York is slain!

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: O Warwick, Warwick! that Plantagenet,

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: Which held three dearly as his souls redemption,

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: Is by the stern Lord Clifford done to death.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Ten days ago I drownd these news in tears;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And now, to add more measure to your woes,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: I come to tell you things sith then befalln.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: After the bloody fray at Wakefield fought,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Where your brave father breathed his latest gasp,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Tidings, as swiftly as the posts could run,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Were brought me of your loss and his depart.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: I, then in London keeper of the king,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Musterd my soldiers, gatherd flocks of friends,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And very well appointed, as I thought,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Marchd toward Saint Albans to intercept the queen,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Bearing the king in my behalf along;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: For by my scouts I was advertised

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: That she was coming with a full intent

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: To dash our late decree in parliament

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Touching King Henrys oath and your succession.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Short tale to make, we at Saint Albans met

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Our battles joind, and both sides fiercely fought:

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: But whether twas the coldness of the king,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Who lookd full gently on his warlike queen,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: That robbd my soldiers of their heated spleen;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Or whether twas report of her success;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Or more than common fear of Cliffords rigour,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Who thunders to his captives blood and death,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: I cannot judge: but to conclude with truth,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Their weapons like to lightning came and went;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Our soldiers, like the night-owls lazy flight,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Or like an idle thresher with a flail,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Fell gently down, as if they struck their friends.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: I cheerd them up with justice of our cause,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: With promise of high pay and great rewards:

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: But all in vain; they had no heart to fight,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And we in them no hope to win the day;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: So that we fled; the king unto the queen;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Lord George your brother, Norfolk and myself,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: In haste, post-haste, are come to join with you:

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: For in the marches here we heard you were,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Making another head to fight again.

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: Where is the Duke of Norfolk, gentle Warwick?

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: And when came George from Burgundy to England?

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Some six miles off the duke is with the soldiers;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And for your brother, he was lately sent

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: From your kind aunt, Duchess of Burgundy,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: With aid of soldiers to this needful war.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Twas odds, belike, when valiant Warwick fled:

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Oft have I heard his praises in pursuit,

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: But neer till now his scandal of retire.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Nor now my scandal, Richard, dost thou hear;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: For thou shalt know this strong right hand of mine

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Can pluck the diadem from faint Henrys head,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And wring the awful sceptre from his fist,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Were he as famous and as bold in war

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: As he is famed for mildness, peace, and prayer.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: I know it well, Lord Warwick; blame me not:

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Tis love I bear thy glories makes me speak.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: But in this troublous time whats to be done?

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Shall we go throw away our coats of steel,

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: And wrap our bodies in black mourning gowns,

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Numbering our Ave-Maries with our beads?

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Or shall we on the helmets of our foes

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Tell our devotion with revengeful arms?

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: If for the last, say ay, and to it, lords.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Why, therefore Warwick came to seek you out;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And therefore comes my brother Montague.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Attend me, lords. The proud insulting queen,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: With Clifford and the haught Northumberland,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And of their feather many more proud birds,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Have wrought the easy-melting king like wax.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: He swore consent to your succession,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: His oath enrolled in the parliament;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And now to London all the crew are gone,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: To frustrate both his oath and what beside

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: May make against the house of Lancaster.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Their power, I think, is thirty thousand strong:

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Now, if the help of Norfolk and myself,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: With all the friends that thou, brave Earl of March,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Amongst the loving Welshmen canst procure,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Will but amount to five and twenty thousand,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Why, Via! to London will we march amain,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And once again bestride our foaming steeds,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And once again cry Charge upon our foes!

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: But never once again turn back and fly.

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Ay, now methinks I hear great Warwick speak:

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: Neer may he live to see a sunshine day,

speaker: RICHARD
text_entry: That cries Retire, if Warwick bid him stay.

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: Lord Warwick, on thy shoulder will I lean;

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: And when thou failst--as God forbid the hour!--

speaker: EDWARD
text_entry: Must Edward fall, which peril heaven forfend!

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: No longer Earl of March, but Duke of York:

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: The next degree is Englands royal throne;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: For King of England shalt thou be proclaimd

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: In every borough as we pass along;

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: And he that throws not up his cap for joy

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Shall for the fault make forfeit of his head.

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: King Edward, valiant Richard, Montague,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: Stay we no longer, dreaming of renown,

speaker: WARWICK
text_entry: But sound the trumpets, and about our task.

speaker: RICHARD
