text_entry: Come hither, come hither, come hither:

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: Here shall he see No enemy

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: But winter and rough weather.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: More, more, I prithee, more.

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: It will make you melancholy, Monsieur Jaques.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: I thank it. More, I prithee, more. I can suck

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: melancholy out of a song, as a weasel sucks eggs.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: More, I prithee, more.

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: My voice is ragged: I know I cannot please you.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: I do not desire you to please me; I do desire you to

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: sing. Come, more; another stanzo: call you em stanzos?

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: What you will, Monsieur Jaques.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Nay, I care not for their names; they owe me

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: nothing. Will you sing?

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: More at your request than to please myself.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Well then, if ever I thank any man, Ill thank you;

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: but that they call compliment is like the encounter

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: of two dog-apes, and when a man thanks me heartily,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: methinks I have given him a penny and he renders me

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: the beggarly thanks. Come, sing; and you that will

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: not, hold your tongues.

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: Well, Ill end the song. Sirs, cover the while; the

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: duke will drink under this tree. He hath been all

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: this day to look you.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And I have been all this day to avoid him. He is

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: too disputable for my company: I think of as many

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: matters as he, but I give heaven thanks and make no

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: boast of them. Come, warble, come.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: SONG.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Who doth ambition shun

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: All together here

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And loves to live i the sun,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Seeking the food he eats

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And pleased with what he gets,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Come hither, come hither, come hither:

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Here shall he see No enemy

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: But winter and rough weather.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Ill give you a verse to this note that I made

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: yesterday in despite of my invention.

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: And Ill sing it.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Thus it goes:--

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: If it do come to pass

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: That any man turn ass,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Leaving his wealth and ease,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: A stubborn will to please,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Ducdame, ducdame, ducdame:

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Here shall he see

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Gross fools as he,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: An if he will come to me.

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: Whats that ducdame?

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Tis a Greek invocation, to call fools into a

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: circle. Ill go sleep, if I can; if I cannot, Ill

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: rail against all the first-born of Egypt.

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: And Ill go seek the duke: his banquet is prepared.

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: Exeunt severally

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: SCENE VI. The forest.

speaker: AMIENS
text_entry: Enter ORLANDO and ADAM

speaker: ADAM
text_entry: Dear master, I can go no further. O, I die for food!

speaker: ADAM
text_entry: Here lie I down, and measure out my grave. Farewell,

speaker: ADAM
text_entry: kind master.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Why, how now, Adam! no greater heart in thee? Live

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: a little; comfort a little; cheer thyself a little.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: If this uncouth forest yield any thing savage, I

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: will either be food for it or bring it for food to

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: thee. Thy conceit is nearer death than thy powers.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: For my sake be comfortable; hold death awhile at

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: the arms end: I will here be with thee presently;

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: and if I bring thee not something to eat, I will

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: give thee leave to die: but if thou diest before I

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: come, thou art a mocker of my labour. Well said!

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: thou lookest cheerly, and Ill be with thee quickly.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Yet thou liest in the bleak air: come, I will bear

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: thee to some shelter; and thou shalt not die for

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: lack of a dinner, if there live any thing in this

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: desert. Cheerly, good Adam!

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: SCENE VII. The forest.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: A table set out. Enter DUKE SENIOR, AMIENS, and Lords like outlaws

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: I think he be transformd into a beast;

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: For I can no where find him like a man.

speaker: First Lord
text_entry: My lord, he is but even now gone hence:

speaker: First Lord
text_entry: Here was he merry, hearing of a song.

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: If he, compact of jars, grow musical,

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: We shall have shortly discord in the spheres.

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: Go, seek him: tell him I would speak with him.

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: Enter JAQUES

speaker: First Lord
text_entry: He saves my labour by his own approach.

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: Why, how now, monsieur! what a life is this,

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: That your poor friends must woo your company?

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: What, you look merrily!

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: A fool, a fool! I met a fool i the forest,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: A motley fool; a miserable world!

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: As I do live by food, I met a fool

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Who laid him down and baskd him in the sun,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And raild on Lady Fortune in good terms,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: In good set terms and yet a motley fool.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Good morrow, fool, quoth I. No, sir, quoth he,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Call me not fool till heaven hath sent me fortune:

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And then he drew a dial from his poke,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And, looking on it with lack-lustre eye,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Says very wisely, It is ten oclock:

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Thus we may see, quoth he, how the world wags:

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Tis but an hour ago since it was nine,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And after one hour more twill be eleven;

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And so, from hour to hour, we ripe and ripe,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And then, from hour to hour, we rot and rot;

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And thereby hangs a tale. When I did hear

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: The motley fool thus moral on the time,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: My lungs began to crow like chanticleer,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: That fools should be so deep-contemplative,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And I did laugh sans intermission

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: An hour by his dial. O noble fool!

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: A worthy fool! Motleys the only wear.

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: What fool is this?

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: O worthy fool! One that hath been a courtier,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And says, if ladies be but young and fair,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: They have the gift to know it: and in his brain,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Which is as dry as the remainder biscuit

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: After a voyage, he hath strange places crammd

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: With observation, the which he vents

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: In mangled forms. O that I were a fool!

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: I am ambitious for a motley coat.

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: Thou shalt have one.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: It is my only suit;

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Provided that you weed your better judgments

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Of all opinion that grows rank in them

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: That I am wise. I must have liberty

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Withal, as large a charter as the wind,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: To blow on whom I please; for so fools have;

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And they that are most galled with my folly,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: They most must laugh. And why, sir, must they so?

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: The why is plain as way to parish church:

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: He that a fool doth very wisely hit

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Doth very foolishly, although he smart,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Not to seem senseless of the bob: if not,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: The wise mans folly is anatomized

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Even by the squandering glances of the fool.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Invest me in my motley; give me leave

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: To speak my mind, and I will through and through

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Cleanse the foul body of the infected world,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: If they will patiently receive my medicine.

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: Fie on thee! I can tell what thou wouldst do.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: What, for a counter, would I do but good?

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: Most mischievous foul sin, in chiding sin:

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: For thou thyself hast been a libertine,

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: As sensual as the brutish sting itself;

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: And all the embossed sores and headed evils,

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: That thou with licence of free foot hast caught,

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: Wouldst thou disgorge into the general world.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Why, who cries out on pride,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: That can therein tax any private party?

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Doth it not flow as hugely as the sea,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Till that the weary very means do ebb?

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: What woman in the city do I name,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: When that I say the city-woman bears

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: The cost of princes on unworthy shoulders?

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Who can come in and say that I mean her,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: When such a one as she such is her neighbour?

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Or what is he of basest function

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: That says his bravery is not of my cost,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Thinking that I mean him, but therein suits

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: His folly to the mettle of my speech?

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: There then; how then? what then? Let me see wherein

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: My tongue hath wrongd him: if it do him right,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Then he hath wrongd himself; if he be free,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Why then my taxing like a wild-goose flies,

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Unclaimd of any man. But who comes here?

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Enter ORLANDO, with his sword drawn

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Forbear, and eat no more.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Why, I have eat none yet.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Nor shalt not, till necessity be served.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Of what kind should this cock come of?

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: Art thou thus boldend, man, by thy distress,

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: Or else a rude despiser of good manners,

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: That in civility thou seemst so empty?

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: You touchd my vein at first: the thorny point

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Of bare distress hath taen from me the show

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Of smooth civility: yet am I inland bred

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: And know some nurture. But forbear, I say:

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: He dies that touches any of this fruit

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Till I and my affairs are answered.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: An you will not be answered with reason, I must die.

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: What would you have? Your gentleness shall force

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: More than your force move us to gentleness.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: I almost die for food; and let me have it.

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: Sit down and feed, and welcome to our table.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Speak you so gently? Pardon me, I pray you:

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: I thought that all things had been savage here;

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: And therefore put I on the countenance

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Of stern commandment. But whateer you are

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: That in this desert inaccessible,

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Under the shade of melancholy boughs,

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Lose and neglect the creeping hours of time

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: If ever you have lookd on better days,

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: If ever been where bells have knolld to church,

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: If ever sat at any good mans feast,

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: If ever from your eyelids wiped a tear

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: And know what tis to pity and be pitied,

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Let gentleness my strong enforcement be:

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: In the which hope I blush, and hide my sword.

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: True is it that we have seen better days,

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: And have with holy bell been knolld to church

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: And sat at good mens feasts and wiped our eyes

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: Of drops that sacred pity hath engenderd:

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: And therefore sit you down in gentleness

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: And take upon command what help we have

speaker: DUKE SENIOR
text_entry: That to your wanting may be ministerd.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Then but forbear your food a little while,

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Whiles, like a doe, I go to find my fawn

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: And give it food. There is an old poor man,

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Who after me hath many a weary step

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Limpd in pure love: till he be first sufficed,

speaker: ORLANDO

text_entry: Proceed.

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: There lay he, stretched along, like a wounded knight.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Though it be pity to see such a sight, it well

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: becomes the ground.

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: Cry holla to thy tongue, I prithee; it curvets

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: unseasonably. He was furnished like a hunter.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: O, ominous! he comes to kill my heart.

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: I would sing my song without a burden: thou bringest

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: me out of tune.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Do you not know I am a woman? when I think, I must

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: speak. Sweet, say on.

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: You bring me out. Soft! comes he not here?

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: Enter ORLANDO and JAQUES

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Tis he: slink by, and note him.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: I thank you for your company; but, good faith, I had

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: as lief have been myself alone.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: And so had I; but yet, for fashion sake, I thank you

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: too for your society.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: God be wi you: lets meet as little as we can.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: I do desire we may be better strangers.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: I pray you, mar no more trees with writing

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: love-songs in their barks.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: I pray you, mar no more of my verses with reading

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: them ill-favouredly.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Rosalind is your loves name?

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Yes, just.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: I do not like her name.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: There was no thought of pleasing you when she was

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: christened.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: What stature is she of?

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Just as high as my heart.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: You are full of pretty answers. Have you not been

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: acquainted with goldsmiths wives, and conned them

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: out of rings?

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Not so; but I answer you right painted cloth, from

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: whence you have studied your questions.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: You have a nimble wit: I think twas made of

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Atalantas heels. Will you sit down with me? and

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: we two will rail against our mistress the world and

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: all our misery.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: I will chide no breather in the world but myself,

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: against whom I know most faults.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: The worst fault you have is to be in love.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Tis a fault I will not change for your best virtue.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: I am weary of you.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: By my troth, I was seeking for a fool when I found

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: you.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: He is drowned in the brook: look but in, and you

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: shall see him.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: There I shall see mine own figure.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Which I take to be either a fool or a cipher.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Ill tarry no longer with you: farewell, good

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Signior Love.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: I am glad of your departure: adieu, good Monsieur

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Melancholy.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Exit JAQUES

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: [Aside to CELIA]  I will speak to him, like a saucy

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: lackey and under that habit play the knave with him.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Do you hear, forester?

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Very well: what would you?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: I pray you, what ist oclock?

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: You should ask me what time o day: theres no clock

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: in the forest.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Then there is no true lover in the forest; else

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: sighing every minute and groaning every hour would

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: detect the lazy foot of Time as well as a clock.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: And why not the swift foot of Time? had not that

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: been as proper?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: By no means, sir: Time travels in divers paces with

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: divers persons. Ill tell you who Time ambles

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: withal, who Time trots withal, who Time gallops

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: withal and who he stands still withal.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: I prithee, who doth he trot withal?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Marry, he trots hard with a young maid between the

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: contract of her marriage and the day it is

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: solemnized: if the interim be but a sennight,

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Times pace is so hard that it seems the length of

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: seven year.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Who ambles Time withal?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: With a priest that lacks Latin and a rich man that

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: hath not the gout, for the one sleeps easily because

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: he cannot study, and the other lives merrily because

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: he feels no pain, the one lacking the burden of lean

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: and wasteful learning, the other knowing no burden

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: of heavy tedious penury; these Time ambles withal.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Who doth he gallop withal?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: With a thief to the gallows, for though he go as

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: softly as foot can fall, he thinks himself too soon there.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Who stays it still withal?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: With lawyers in the vacation, for they sleep between

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: term and term and then they perceive not how Time moves.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Where dwell you, pretty youth?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: With this shepherdess, my sister; here in the

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: skirts of the forest, like fringe upon a petticoat.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Are you native of this place?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: As the cony that you see dwell where she is kindled.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Your accent is something finer than you could

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: purchase in so removed a dwelling.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: I have been told so of many: but indeed an old

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: religious uncle of mine taught me to speak, who was

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: in his youth an inland man; one that knew courtship

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: too well, for there he fell in love. I have heard

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: him read many lectures against it, and I thank God

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: I am not a woman, to be touched with so many

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: giddy offences as he hath generally taxed their

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: whole sex withal.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Can you remember any of the principal evils that he

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: laid to the charge of women?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: There were none principal; they were all like one

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: another as half-pence are, every one fault seeming

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: monstrous till his fellow fault came to match it.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: I prithee, recount some of them.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: No, I will not cast away my physic but on those that

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: are sick. There is a man haunts the forest, that

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: abuses our young plants with carving Rosalind on

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: their barks; hangs odes upon hawthorns and elegies

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: on brambles, all, forsooth, deifying the name of

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Rosalind: if I could meet that fancy-monger I would

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: give him some good counsel, for he seems to have the

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: quotidian of love upon him.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: I am he that is so love-shaked: I pray you tell me

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: your remedy.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: There is none of my uncles marks upon you: he

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: taught me how to know a man in love; in which cage

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: of rushes I am sure you are not prisoner.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: What were his marks?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: A lean cheek, which you have not, a blue eye and

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: sunken, which you have not, an unquestionable

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: spirit, which you have not, a beard neglected,

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: which you have not; but I pardon you for that, for

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: simply your having in beard is a younger brothers

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: revenue: then your hose should be ungartered, your

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: bonnet unbanded, your sleeve unbuttoned, your shoe

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: untied and every thing about you demonstrating a

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: careless desolation; but you are no such man; you

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: are rather point-device in your accoutrements as

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: loving yourself than seeming the lover of any other.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Fair youth, I would I could make thee believe I love.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Me believe it! you may as soon make her that you

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: love believe it; which, I warrant, she is apter to

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: do than to confess she does: that is one of the

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: points in the which women still give the lie to

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: their consciences. But, in good sooth, are you he

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: that hangs the verses on the trees, wherein Rosalind

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: is so admired?

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: I swear to thee, youth, by the white hand of

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Rosalind, I am that he, that unfortunate he.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: But are you so much in love as your rhymes speak?

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Neither rhyme nor reason can express how much.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Love is merely a madness, and, I tell you, deserves

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: as well a dark house and a whip as madmen do: and

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: the reason why they are not so punished and cured

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: is, that the lunacy is so ordinary that the whippers

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: are in love too. Yet I profess curing it by counsel.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Did you ever cure any so?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Yes, one, and in this manner. He was to imagine me

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: his love, his mistress; and I set him every day to

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: woo me: at which time would I, being but a moonish

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: youth, grieve, be effeminate, changeable, longing

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: and liking, proud, fantastical, apish, shallow,

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: inconstant, full of tears, full of smiles, for every

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: passion something and for no passion truly any

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: thing, as boys and women are for the most part

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: cattle of this colour; would now like him, now loathe

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: him; then entertain him, then forswear him; now weep

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: for him, then spit at him; that I drave my suitor

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: from his mad humour of love to a living humour of

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: madness; which was, to forswear the full stream of

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: the world, and to live in a nook merely monastic.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: And thus I cured him; and this way will I take upon

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: me to wash your liver as clean as a sound sheeps

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: heart, that there shall not be one spot of love int.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: I would not be cured, youth.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: I would cure you, if you would but call me Rosalind

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: and come every day to my cote and woo me.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Now, by the faith of my love, I will: tell me

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: where it is.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Go with me to it and Ill show it you and by the way

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: you shall tell me where in the forest you live.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Will you go?

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: With all my heart, good youth.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Nay you must call me Rosalind. Come, sister, will you go?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: SCENE III. The forest.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Enter TOUCHSTONE and AUDREY; JAQUES behind

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Come apace, good Audrey: I will fetch up your

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: goats, Audrey. And how, Audrey? am I the man yet?

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: doth my simple feature content you?

speaker: AUDREY
text_entry: Your features! Lord warrant us! what features!

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: I am here with thee and thy goats, as the most

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: capricious poet, honest Ovid, was among the Goths.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: [Aside]  O knowledge ill-inhabited, worse than Jove

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: in a thatched house!

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: When a mans verses cannot be understood, nor a

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: mans good wit seconded with the forward child

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Understanding, it strikes a man more dead than a

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: great reckoning in a little room. Truly, I would

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: the gods had made thee poetical.

speaker: AUDREY
text_entry: I do not know what poetical is: is it honest in

speaker: AUDREY
text_entry: deed and word? is it a true thing?

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: No, truly; for the truest poetry is the most

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: feigning; and lovers are given to poetry, and what

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: they swear in poetry may be said as lovers they do feign.

speaker: AUDREY
text_entry: Do you wish then that the gods had made me poetical?

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: I do, truly; for thou swearest to me thou art

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: honest: now, if thou wert a poet, I might have some

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: hope thou didst feign.

speaker: AUDREY
text_entry: Would you not have me honest?

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: No, truly, unless thou wert hard-favoured; for

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: honesty coupled to beauty is to have honey a sauce to sugar.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: [Aside]  A material fool!

speaker: AUDREY
text_entry: Well, I am not fair; and therefore I pray the gods

speaker: AUDREY
text_entry: make me honest.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Truly, and to cast away honesty upon a foul slut

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: were to put good meat into an unclean dish.

speaker: AUDREY
text_entry: I am not a slut, though I thank the gods I am foul.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Well, praised be the gods for thy foulness!

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: sluttishness may come hereafter. But be it as it may

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: be, I will marry thee, and to that end I have been

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: with Sir Oliver Martext, the vicar of the next

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: village, who hath promised to meet me in this place

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: of the forest and to couple us.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: [Aside]  I would fain see this meeting.

speaker: AUDREY
text_entry: Well, the gods give us joy!

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Amen. A man may, if he were of a fearful heart,

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: stagger in this attempt; for here we have no temple

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: but the wood, no assembly but horn-beasts. But what

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: though? C ourage! As horns are odious, they are

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: necessary. It is said, many a man knows no end of

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: his goods: right; many a man has good horns, and

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: knows no end of them. Well, that is the dowry of

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: his wife; tis none of his own getting. Horns?

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Even so. Poor men alone? No, no; the noblest deer

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: hath them as huge as the rascal. Is the single man

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: therefore blessed? No: as a walled town is more

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: worthier than a village, so is the forehead of a

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: married man more honourable than the bare brow of a

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: bachelor; and by how much defence is better than no

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: skill, by so much is a horn more precious than to

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: want. Here comes Sir Oliver.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Enter SIR OLIVER MARTEXT

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Sir Oliver Martext, you are well met: will you

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: dispatch us here under this tree, or shall we go

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: with you to your chapel?

speaker: SIR OLIVER MARTEXT
text_entry: Is there none here to give the woman?

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: I will not take her on gift of any man.

speaker: SIR OLIVER MARTEXT
text_entry: Truly, she must be given, or the marriage is not lawful.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: [Advancing]

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Proceed, proceedIll give her.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Good even, good Master What-ye-callt: how do you,

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: sir? You are very well met: God ild you for your

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: last company: I am very glad to see you: even a

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: toy in hand here, sir: nay, pray be covered.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Will you be married, motley?

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: As the ox hath his bow, sir, the horse his curb and

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: the falcon her bells, so man hath his desires; and

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: as pigeons bill, so wedlock would be nibbling.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: And will you, being a man of your breeding, be

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: married under a bush like a beggar? Get you to

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: church, and have a good priest that can tell you

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: what marriage is: this fellow will but join you

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: together as they join wainscot; then one of you will

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: prove a shrunk panel and, like green timber, warp, warp.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: [Aside]  I am not in the mind but I were better to be

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: married of him than of another: for he is not like

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: to marry me well; and not being well married, it

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: will be a good excuse for me hereafter to leave my wife.

speaker: JAQUES
text_entry: Go thou with me, and let me counsel thee.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Come, sweet Audrey:

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: We must be married, or we must live in bawdry.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Farewell, good Master Oliver: not,--

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: O sweet Oliver,

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: O brave Oliver,

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Leave me not behind thee: but,--

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Wind away,

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Begone, I say,

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: I will not to wedding with thee.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Exeunt JAQUES, TOUCHSTONE and AUDREY

speaker: SIR OLIVER MARTEXT
text_entry: Tis no matter: neer a fantastical knave of them

speaker: SIR OLIVER MARTEXT
text_entry: all shall flout me out of my calling.

speaker: SIR OLIVER MARTEXT
text_entry: Exit

speaker: SIR OLIVER MARTEXT
text_entry: SCENE IV. The forest.

speaker: SIR OLIVER MARTEXT
text_entry: Enter ROSALIND and CELIA

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Never talk to me; I will weep.

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: Do, I prithee; but yet have the grace to consider

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: that tears do not become a man.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: But have I not cause to weep?

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: As good cause as one would desire; therefore weep.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: His very hair is of the dissembling colour.

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: Something browner than Judass marry, his kisses are

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: Judass own children.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: I faith, his hair is of a good colour.

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: An excellent colour: your chestnut was ever the only colour.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: And his kissing is as full of sanctity as the touch

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: of holy bread.

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: He hath bought a pair of cast lips of Diana: a nun

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: of winters sisterhood kisses not more religiously;

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: the very ice of chastity is in them.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: But why did he swear he would come this morning, and

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: comes not?

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: Nay, certainly, there is no truth in him.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Do you think so?

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: Yes; I think he is not a pick-purse nor a

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: horse-stealer, but for his verity in love, I do

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: think him as concave as a covered goblet or a

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: worm-eaten nut.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: Not true in love?

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: Yes, when he is in; but I think he is not in.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: You have heard him swear downright he was.

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: Was is not is: besides, the oath of a lover is

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: no stronger than the word of a tapster; they are

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: both the confirmer of false reckonings. He attends

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: here in the forest on the duke your father.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: I met the duke yesterday and had much question with

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: him: he asked me of what parentage I was; I told

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: him, of as good as he; so he laughed and let me go.

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: But what talk we of fathers, when there is such a

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: man as Orlando?

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: O, thats a brave man! he writes brave verses,

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: speaks brave words, swears brave oaths and breaks

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: them bravely, quite traverse, athwart the heart of

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: his lover; as a puisny tilter, that spurs his horse

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: but on one side, breaks his staff like a noble

speaker: CELIA
text_entry: goose: but alls brave that youth mounts and folly

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: death! Two oclock is your hour?

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: minute behind your hour, I will think you the most

speaker: ROSALIND

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: unfaithful: therefore beware my censure and keep

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: your promise.

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: With no less religion than if thou wert indeed my

speaker: ORLANDO
text_entry: Rosalind: so adieu.

speaker: ROSALIND

speaker: ROSALIND
text_entry: offenders, and let Time try: adieu.

text_entry: The opening of his mouth; but suddenly,

text_entry: As how I came into that desert place:--

text_entry: Enter TOUCHSTONE and AUDREY

text_entry: gentlemans saying.

text_entry: A most wicked Sir Oliver, Audrey, a most vile

text_entry: Martext. But, Audrey, there is a youth here in the

text_entry: forest lays claim to you.

text_entry: Ay, I know who tis; he hath no interest in me in

text_entry: troth, we that have good wits have much to answer

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: head; nay, prithee, be covered. How old are you, friend?

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: A ripe age. Is thy name William?

speaker: WILLIAM
text_entry: William, sir.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: A fair name. Wast born i the forest here?

text_entry: Ay, sir, I thank God.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Thank God; a good answer. Art rich?

speaker: WILLIAM
text_entry: Faith, sir, so so.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: So so is good, very good, very excellent good; and

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: yet it is not; it is but so so. Art thou wise?

speaker: WILLIAM
text_entry: Ay, sir, I have a pretty wit.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Why, thou sayest well. I do now remember a saying,

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: The fool doth think he is wise, but the wise man

speaker: TOUCHSTONE

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: would open his lips when he put it into his mouth;

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: meaning thereby that grapes were made to eat and

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: lips to open. You do love this maid?

speaker: WILLIAM
text_entry: I do, sir.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: Give me your hand. Art thou learned?

speaker: WILLIAM
text_entry: No, sir.

speaker: TOUCHSTONE

text_entry: is a figure in rhetoric that drink, being poured out

speaker: TOUCHSTONE

speaker: TOUCHSTONE

speaker: WILLIAM
text_entry: Which he, sir?

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: He, sir, that must marry this woman. Therefore, you

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: clown, abandon,--which is in the vulgar leave,--the

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: society,--which in the boorish is company,--of this

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: female,--which in the common is woman; which

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: together is, abandon the society of this female, or,

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: clown, thou perishest; or, to thy better

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: understanding, diest; or, to wit I kill thee, make

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: thee away, translate thy life into death, thy

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: liberty into bondage: I will deal in poison with

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: thee, or in bastinado, or in steel; I will bandy

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: with thee in faction; I will oerrun thee with

speaker: TOUCHSTONE
text_entry: policy; I will kill thee a hundred and fifty ways:

speaker: TOUCHSTONE

speaker: AUDREY

speaker: WILLIAM

speaker: WILLIAM

speaker: DOMITIUS ENOBARBUS

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Yet this my comfort: when your words are done,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: My woes end likewise with the evening sun.

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Well, Syracusian, say in brief the cause

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Why thou departedst from thy native home

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: And for what cause thou camest to Ephesus.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: A heavier task could not have been imposed

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Than I to speak my griefs unspeakable:

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Yet, that the world may witness that my end

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Was wrought by nature, not by vile offence,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Ill utter what my sorrows give me leave.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: In Syracusa was I born, and wed

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Unto a woman, happy but for me,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And by me, had not our hap been bad.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: With her I lived in joy; our wealth increased

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: By prosperous voyages I often made

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: To Epidamnum; till my factors death

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And the great care of goods at random left

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Drew me from kind embracements of my spouse:

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: From whom my absence was not six months old

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Before herself, almost at fainting under

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: The pleasing punishment that women bear,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Had made provision for her following me

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And soon and safe arrived where I was.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: There had she not been long, but she became

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: A joyful mother of two goodly sons;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And, which was strange, the one so like the other,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: As could not be distinguishd but by names.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: That very hour, and in the self-same inn,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: A meaner woman was delivered

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Of such a burden, male twins, both alike:

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Those,--for their parents were exceeding poor,--

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: I bought and brought up to attend my sons.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: My wife, not meanly proud of two such boys,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Made daily motions for our home return:

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Unwilling I agreed. Alas! too soon,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: We came aboard.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: A league from Epidamnum had we saild,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Before the always wind-obeying deep

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Gave any tragic instance of our harm:

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: But longer did we not retain much hope;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: For what obscured light the heavens did grant

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Did but convey unto our fearful minds

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: A doubtful warrant of immediate death;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Which though myself would gladly have embraced,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Yet the incessant weepings of my wife,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Weeping before for what she saw must come,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And piteous plainings of the pretty babes,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: That mournd for fashion, ignorant what to fear,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Forced me to seek delays for them and me.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And this it was, for other means was none:

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: The sailors sought for safety by our boat,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And left the ship, then sinking-ripe, to us:

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: My wife, more careful for the latter-born,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Had fastend him unto a small spare mast,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Such as seafaring men provide for storms;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: To him one of the other twins was bound,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Whilst I had been like heedful of the other:

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: The children thus disposed, my wife and I,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Fixing our eyes on whom our care was fixd,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Fastend ourselves at either end the mast;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And floating straight, obedient to the stream,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Was carried towards Corinth, as we thought.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: At length the sun, gazing upon the earth,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Dispersed those vapours that offended us;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And by the benefit of his wished light,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: The seas waxd calm, and we discovered

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Two ships from far making amain to us,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Of Corinth that, of Epidaurus this:

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: But ere they came,--O, let me say no more!

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Gather the sequel by that went before.

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Nay, forward, old man; do not break off so;

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: For we may pity, though not pardon thee.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: O, had the gods done so, I had not now

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Worthily termd them merciless to us!

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: For, ere the ships could meet by twice five leagues,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: We were encounterd by a mighty rock;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Which being violently borne upon,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Our helpful ship was splitted in the midst;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: So that, in this unjust divorce of us,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Fortune had left to both of us alike

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: What to delight in, what to sorrow for.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Her part, poor soul! seeming as burdened

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: With lesser weight but not with lesser woe,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Was carried with more speed before the wind;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And in our sight they three were taken up

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: By fishermen of Corinth, as we thought.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: At length, another ship had seized on us;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And, knowing whom it was their hap to save,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Gave healthful welcome to their shipwreckd guests;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And would have reft the fishers of their prey,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Had not their bark been very slow of sail;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And therefore homeward did they bend their course.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Thus have you heard me severd from my bliss;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: That by misfortunes was my life prolongd,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: To tell sad stories of my own mishaps.

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: And for the sake of them thou sorrowest for,

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Do me the favour to dilate at full

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: What hath befalln of them and thee till now.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: My youngest boy, and yet my eldest care,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: At eighteen years became inquisitive

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: After his brother: and importuned me

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: That his attendant--so his case was like,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Reft of his brother, but retaind his name--

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Might bear him company in the quest of him:

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Whom whilst I labourd of a love to see,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: I hazarded the loss of whom I loved.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Five summers have I spent in furthest Greece,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Roaming clean through the bounds of Asia,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And, coasting homeward, came to Ephesus;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Hopeless to find, yet loath to leave unsought

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Or that or any place that harbours men.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: But here must end the story of my life;

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: And happy were I in my timely death,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Could all my travels warrant me they live.

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Hapless AEgeon, whom the fates have markd

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: To bear the extremity of dire mishap!

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Now, trust me, were it not against our laws,

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Against my crown, my oath, my dignity,

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Which princes, would they, may not disannul,

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: My soul would sue as advocate for thee.

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: But, though thou art adjudged to the death

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: And passed sentence may not be recalld

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: But to our honours great disparagement,

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Yet I will favour thee in what I can.

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Therefore, merchant, Ill limit thee this day

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: To seek thy life by beneficial help:

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Try all the friends thou hast in Ephesus;

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Beg thou, or borrow, to make up the sum,

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: And live; if no, then thou art doomd to die.

speaker: DUKE SOLINUS
text_entry: Gaoler, take him to thy custody.

speaker: Gaoler
text_entry: I will, my lord.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Hopeless and helpless doth AEgeon wend,

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: But to procrastinate his lifeless end.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: SCENE II. The Mart.

speaker: AEGEON
text_entry: Enter ANTIPHOLUS of Syracuse, DROMIO of Syracuse, and First Merchant

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: Therefore give out you are of Epidamnum,

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: Lest that your goods too soon be confiscate.

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: This very day a Syracusian merchant

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: Is apprehended for arrival here;

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: And not being able to buy out his life

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: According to the statute of the town,

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: Dies ere the weary sun set in the west.

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: There is your money that I had to keep.

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Go bear it to the Centaur, where we host,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And stay there, Dromio, till I come to thee.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Within this hour it will be dinner-time:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Till that, Ill view the manners of the town,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Peruse the traders, gaze upon the buildings,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And then return and sleep within mine inn,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: For with long travel I am stiff and weary.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Get thee away.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Many a man would take you at your word,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And go indeed, having so good a mean.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: A trusty villain, sir, that very oft,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: When I am dull with care and melancholy,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Lightens my humour with his merry jests.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What, will you walk with me about the town,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And then go to my inn and dine with me?

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: I am invited, sir, to certain merchants,

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: Of whom I hope to make much benefit;

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: I crave your pardon. Soon at five oclock,

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: Please you, Ill meet with you upon the mart

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: And afterward consort you till bed-time:

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: My present business calls me from you now.

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Farewell till then: I will go lose myself

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And wander up and down to view the city.

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: Sir, I commend you to your own content.

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: Exit

speaker: First Merchant
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: He that commends me to mine own content

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Commends me to the thing I cannot get.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I to the world am like a drop of water

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: That in the ocean seeks another drop,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Who, falling there to find his fellow forth,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Unseen, inquisitive, confounds himself:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: So I, to find a mother and a brother,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: In quest of them, unhappy, lose myself.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Enter DROMIO of Ephesus

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Here comes the almanac of my true date.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What now? how chance thou art returnd so soon?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Returnd so soon! rather approachd too late:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: The capon burns, the pig falls from the spit,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: The clock hath strucken twelve upon the bell;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: My mistress made it one upon my cheek:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: She is so hot because the meat is cold;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: The meat is cold because you come not home;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: You come not home because you have no stomach;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: You have no stomach having broke your fast;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But we that know what tis to fast and pray

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Are penitent for your default to-day.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Stop in your wind, sir: tell me this, I pray:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Where have you left the money that I gave you?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: O,--sixpence, that I had o Wednesday last

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: To pay the saddler for my mistress crupper?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: The saddler had it, sir; I kept it not.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I am not in a sportive humour now:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Tell me, and dally not, where is the money?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: We being strangers here, how darest thou trust

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: So great a charge from thine own custody?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I pray you, air, as you sit at dinner:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I from my mistress come to you in post;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: If I return, I shall be post indeed,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: For she will score your fault upon my pate.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Methinks your maw, like mine, should be your clock,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And strike you home without a messenger.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Come, Dromio, come, these jests are out of season;

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Reserve them till a merrier hour than this.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Where is the gold I gave in charge to thee?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: To me, sir? why, you gave no gold to me.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Come on, sir knave, have done your foolishness,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And tell me how thou hast disposed thy charge.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: My charge was but to fetch you from the mart

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Home to your house, the Phoenix, sir, to dinner:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: My mistress and her sister stays for you.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: In what safe place you have bestowd my money,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Or I shall break that merry sconce of yours

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: That stands on tricks when I am undisposed:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Where is the thousand marks thou hadst of me?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I have some marks of yours upon my pate,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Some of my mistress marks upon my shoulders,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But not a thousand marks between you both.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: If I should pay your worship those again,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Perchance you will not bear them patiently.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Thy mistress marks? what mistress, slave, hast thou?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Your worships wife, my mistress at the Phoenix;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: She that doth fast till you come home to dinner,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And prays that you will hie you home to dinner.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What, wilt thou flout me thus unto my face,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Being forbid? There, take you that, sir knave.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: What mean you, sir? for Gods sake, hold your hands!

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Nay, and you will not, sir, Ill take my heels.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Upon my life, by some device or other

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: The villain is oer-raught of all my money.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: They say this town is full of cozenage,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: As, nimble jugglers that deceive the eye,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Dark-working sorcerers that change the mind,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Soul-killing witches that deform the body,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Disguised cheaters, prating mountebanks,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And many such-like liberties of sin:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: If it prove so, I will be gone the sooner.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Ill to the Centaur, to go seek this slave:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I greatly fear my money is not safe.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ACT II

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: SCENE I. The house of ANTIPHOLUS of Ephesus.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Enter ADRIANA and LUCIANA

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Neither my husband nor the slave returnd,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: That in such haste I sent to seek his master!

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Sure, Luciana, it is two oclock.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Perhaps some merchant hath invited him,

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: And from the mart hes somewhere gone to dinner.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Good sister, let us dine and never fret:

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: A man is master of his liberty:

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Time is their master, and, when they see time,

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Theyll go or come: if so, be patient, sister.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Why should their liberty than ours be more?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Because their business still lies out o door.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Look, when I serve him so, he takes it ill.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: O, know he is the bridle of your will.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Theres none but asses will be bridled so.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Why, headstrong liberty is lashd with woe.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Theres nothing situate under heavens eye

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: But hath his bound, in earth, in sea, in sky:

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: The beasts, the fishes, and the winged fowls,

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Are their males subjects and at their controls:

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Men, more divine, the masters of all these,

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Lords of the wide world and wild watery seas,

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Indued with intellectual sense and souls,

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Of more preeminence than fish and fowls,

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Are masters to their females, and their lords:

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Then let your will attend on their accords.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: This servitude makes you to keep unwed.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Not this, but troubles of the marriage-bed.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: But, were you wedded, you would bear some sway.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Ere I learn love, Ill practise to obey.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: How if your husband start some other where?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Till he come home again, I would forbear.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Patience unmoved! no marvel though she pause;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: They can be meek that have no other cause.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: A wretched soul, bruised with adversity,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: We bid be quiet when we hear it cry;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: But were we burdened with like weight of pain,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: As much or more would we ourselves complain:

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: So thou, that hast no unkind mate to grieve thee,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: With urging helpless patience wouldst relieve me,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: But, if thou live to see like right bereft,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: This fool-beggd patience in thee will be left.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Well, I will marry one day, but to try.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Here comes your man; now is your husband nigh.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Enter DROMIO of Ephesus

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Say, is your tardy master now at hand?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Nay, hes at two hands with me, and that my two ears

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: can witness.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Say, didst thou speak with him? knowst thou his mind?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Ay, ay, he told his mind upon mine ear:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Beshrew his hand, I scarce could understand it.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Spake he so doubtfully, thou couldst not feel his meaning?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Nay, he struck so plainly, I could too well feel his

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: blows; and withal so doubtfully that I could scarce

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: understand them.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: But say, I prithee, is he coming home? It seems he

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: hath great care to please his wife.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Why, mistress, sure my master is horn-mad.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Horn-mad, thou villain!

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I mean not cuckold-mad;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But, sure, he is stark mad.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: When I desired him to come home to dinner,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: He askd me for a thousand marks in gold:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Tis dinner-time, quoth I; My gold! quoth he;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Your meat doth burn, quoth I; My gold! quoth he:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Will you come home? quoth I; My gold! quoth he.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Where is the thousand marks I gave thee, villain?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: The pig, quoth I, is burnd; My gold! quoth he:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: My mistress, sir quoth I; Hang up thy mistress!

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I know not thy mistress; out on thy mistress!

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Quoth who?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Quoth my master:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I know, quoth he, no house, no wife, no mistress.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: So that my errand, due unto my tongue,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I thank him, I bare home upon my shoulders;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: For, in conclusion, he did beat me there.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Go back again, thou slave, and fetch him home.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Go back again, and be new beaten home?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: For Gods sake, send some other messenger.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Back, slave, or I will break thy pate across.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And he will bless that cross with other beating:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Between you I shall have a holy head.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Hence, prating peasant! fetch thy master home.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Am I so round with you as you with me,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: That like a football you do spurn me thus?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: You spurn me hence, and he will spurn me hither:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: If I last in this service, you must case me in leather.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Fie, how impatience loureth in your face!

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: His company must do his minions grace,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Whilst I at home starve for a merry look.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Hath homely age the alluring beauty took

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: From my poor cheek? then he hath wasted it:

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Are my discourses dull? barren my wit?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: If voluble and sharp discourse be marrd,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Unkindness blunts it more than marble hard:

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Do their gay vestments his affections bait?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Thats not my fault: hes master of my state:

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: What ruins are in me that can be found,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: By him not ruind? then is he the ground

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Of my defeatures. My decayed fair

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: A sunny look of his would soon repair

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: But, too unruly deer, he breaks the pale

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And feeds from home; poor I am but his stale.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Self-harming jealousy! fie, beat it hence!

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Unfeeling fools can with such wrongs dispense.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: I know his eye doth homage otherwhere,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Or else what lets it but he would be here?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Sister, you know he promised me a chain;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Would that alone, alone he would detain,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: So he would keep fair quarter with his bed!

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: I see the jewel best enamelled

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Will lose his beauty; yet the gold bides still,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: That others touch, and often touching will

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Wear gold: and no man that hath a name,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: By falsehood and corruption doth it shame.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Since that my beauty cannot please his eye,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Ill weep whats left away, and weeping die.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: How many fond fools serve mad jealousy!

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: SCENE II. A public place.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Enter ANTIPHOLUS of Syracuse

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: The gold I gave to Dromio is laid up

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Safe at the Centaur; and the heedful slave

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Is wanderd forth, in care to seek me out

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: By computation and mine hosts report.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I could not speak with Dromio since at first

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I sent him from the mart. See, here he comes.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Enter DROMIO of Syracuse

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: How now sir! is your merry humour alterd?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: As you love strokes, so jest with me again.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: You know no Centaur? you received no gold?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Your mistress sent to have me home to dinner?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: My house was at the Phoenix? Wast thou mad,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: That thus so madly thou didst answer me?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What answer, sir? when spake I such a word?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Even now, even here, not half an hour since.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I did not see you since you sent me hence,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Home to the Centaur, with the gold you gave me.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Villain, thou didst deny the golds receipt,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And toldst me of a mistress and a dinner;

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: For which, I hope, thou feltst I was displeased.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I am glad to see you in this merry vein:

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What means this jest? I pray you, master, tell me.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Yea, dost thou jeer and flout me in the teeth?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Thinkst thou I jest? Hold, take thou that, and that.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Beating him

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Hold, sir, for Gods sake! now your jest is earnest:

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Upon what bargain do you give it me?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Because that I familiarly sometimes

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Do use you for my fool and chat with you,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Your sauciness will jest upon my love

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And make a common of my serious hours.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: When the sun shines let foolish gnats make sport,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: But creep in crannies when he hides his beams.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: If you will jest with me, know my aspect,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And fashion your demeanor to my looks,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Or I will beat this method in your sconce.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Sconce call you it? so you would leave battering, I

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: had rather have it a head: an you use these blows

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: long, I must get a sconce for my head and ensconce

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: it too; or else I shall seek my wit in my shoulders.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: But, I pray, sir why am I beaten?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Dost thou not know?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Nothing, sir, but that I am beaten.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Shall I tell you why?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Ay, sir, and wherefore; for they say every why hath

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: a wherefore.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Why, first,--for flouting me; and then, wherefore--

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: For urging it the second time to me.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Was there ever any man thus beaten out of season,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: When in the why and the wherefore is neither rhyme

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: nor reason?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Well, sir, I thank you.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Thank me, sir, for what?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Marry, sir, for this something that you gave me for nothing.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Ill make you amends next, to give you nothing for

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: something. But say, sir, is it dinner-time?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: No, sir; I think the meat wants that I have.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: In good time, sir; whats that?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Basting.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Well, sir, then twill be dry.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: If it be, sir, I pray you, eat none of it.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Your reason?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Lest it make you choleric and purchase me another

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: dry basting.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Well, sir, learn to jest in good time: theres a

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: time for all things.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I durst have denied that, before you were so choleric.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: By what rule, sir?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Marry, sir, by a rule as plain as the plain bald

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: pate of father Time himself.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Lets hear it.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Theres no time for a man to recover his hair that

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: grows bald by nature.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: May he not do it by fine and recovery?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Yes, to pay a fine for a periwig and recover the

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: lost hair of another man.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Why is Time such a niggard of hair, being, as it is,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: so plentiful an excrement?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Because it is a blessing that he bestows on beasts;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: and what he hath scanted men in hair he hath given them in wit.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Why, but theres many a man hath more hair than wit.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Not a man of those but he hath the wit to lose his hair.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Why, thou didst conclude hairy men plain dealers without wit.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: The plainer dealer, the sooner lost: yet he loseth

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: it in a kind of jollity.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: For what reason?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: For two; and sound ones too.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Nay, not sound, I pray you.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Sure ones, then.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Nay, not sure, in a thing falsing.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Certain ones then.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Name them.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: The one, to save the money that he spends in

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: trimming; the other, that at dinner they should not

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: drop in his porridge.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: You would all this time have proved there is no

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: time for all things.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Marry, and did, sir; namely, no time to recover hair

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: lost by nature.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: But your reason was not substantial, why there is no

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: time to recover.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Thus I mend it: Time himself is bald and therefore

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: to the worlds end will have bald followers.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I knew twould be a bald conclusion:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: But, soft! who wafts us yonder?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Enter ADRIANA and LUCIANA

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Ay, ay, Antipholus, look strange and frown:

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Some other mistress hath thy sweet aspects;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: I am not Adriana nor thy wife.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: The time was once when thou unurged wouldst vow

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: That never words were music to thine ear,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: That never object pleasing in thine eye,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: That never touch well welcome to thy hand,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: That never meat sweet-savord in thy taste,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Unless I spake, or lookd, or touchd, or carved to thee.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: How comes it now, my husband, O, how comes it,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: That thou art thus estranged from thyself?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Thyself I call it, being strange to me,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: That, undividable, incorporate,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Am better than thy dear selfs better part.

speaker: ADRIANA
