text_entry: Ah, do not tear away thyself from me!

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: For know, my love, as easy mayest thou fall

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: A drop of water in the breaking gulf,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And take unmingled that same drop again,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Without addition or diminishing,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: As take from me thyself and not me too.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: How dearly would it touch me to the quick,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Shouldst thou but hear I were licentious

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And that this body, consecrate to thee,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: By ruffian lust should be contaminate!

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Wouldst thou not spit at me and spurn at me

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And hurl the name of husband in my face

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And tear the staind skin off my harlot-brow

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And from my false hand cut the wedding-ring

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And break it with a deep-divorcing vow?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: I know thou canst; and therefore see thou do it.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: I am possessd with an adulterate blot;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: My blood is mingled with the crime of lust:

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: For if we too be one and thou play false,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: I do digest the poison of thy flesh,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Being strumpeted by thy contagion.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Keep then far league and truce with thy true bed;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: I live unstaind, thou undishonoured.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Plead you to me, fair dame? I know you not:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: In Ephesus I am but two hours old,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: As strange unto your town as to your talk;

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Who, every word by all my wit being scannd,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Want wit in all one word to understand.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Fie, brother! how the world is changed with you!

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: When were you wont to use my sister thus?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: She sent for you by Dromio home to dinner.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: By Dromio?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: By me?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: By thee; and this thou didst return from him,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: That he did buffet thee, and, in his blows,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Denied my house for his, me for his wife.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Did you converse, sir, with this gentlewoman?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What is the course and drift of your compact?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I, sir? I never saw her till this time.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Villain, thou liest; for even her very words

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Didst thou deliver to me on the mart.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I never spake with her in all my life.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: How can she thus then call us by our names,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Unless it be by inspiration.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: How ill agrees it with your gravity

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: To counterfeit thus grossly with your slave,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Abetting him to thwart me in my mood!

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Be it my wrong you are from me exempt,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: But wrong not that wrong with a more contempt.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Come, I will fasten on this sleeve of thine:

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Thou art an elm, my husband, I a vine,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Whose weakness, married to thy stronger state,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Makes me with thy strength to communicate:

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: If aught possess thee from me, it is dross,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Usurping ivy, brier, or idle moss;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Who, all for want of pruning, with intrusion

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Infect thy sap and live on thy confusion.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: To me she speaks; she moves me for her theme:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What, was I married to her in my dream?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Or sleep I now and think I hear all this?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What error drives our eyes and ears amiss?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Until I know this sure uncertainty,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Ill entertain the offerd fallacy.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Dromio, go bid the servants spread for dinner.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: O, for my beads! I cross me for a sinner.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: This is the fairy land: O spite of spites!

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: We talk with goblins, owls and sprites:

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: If we obey them not, this will ensue,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Theyll suck our breath, or pinch us black and blue.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Why pratest thou to thyself and answerst not?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Dromio, thou drone, thou snail, thou slug, thou sot!

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I am transformed, master, am I not?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I think thou art in mind, and so am I.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Nay, master, both in mind and in my shape.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Thou hast thine own form.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: No, I am an ape.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: If thou art changed to aught, tis to an ass.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Tis true; she rides me and I long for grass.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Tis so, I am an ass; else it could never be

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: But I should know her as well as she knows me.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Come, come, no longer will I be a fool,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: To put the finger in the eye and weep,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Whilst man and master laugh my woes to scorn.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Come, sir, to dinner. Dromio, keep the gate.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Husband, Ill dine above with you to-day

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And shrive you of a thousand idle pranks.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Sirrah, if any ask you for your master,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Say he dines forth, and let no creature enter.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Come, sister. Dromio, play the porter well.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Am I in earth, in heaven, or in hell?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Sleeping or waking? mad or well-advised?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Known unto these, and to myself disguised!

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Ill say as they say and persever so,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And in this mist at all adventures go.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Master, shall I be porter at the gate?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Ay; and let none enter, lest I break your pate.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Come, come, Antipholus, we dine too late.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ACT III

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: SCENE I. Before the house of ANTIPHOLUS of Ephesus.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Enter ANTIPHOLUS of Ephesus, DROMIO of Ephesus, ANGELO, and BALTHAZAR

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Good Signior Angelo, you must excuse us all;

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: My wife is shrewish when I keep not hours:

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Say that I lingerd with you at your shop

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: To see the making of her carcanet,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And that to-morrow you will bring it home.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But heres a villain that would face me down

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: He met me on the mart, and that I beat him,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And charged him with a thousand marks in gold,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And that I did deny my wife and house.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Thou drunkard, thou, what didst thou mean by this?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Say what you will, sir, but I know what I know;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: That you beat me at the mart, I have your hand to show:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: If the skin were parchment, and the blows you gave were ink,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Your own handwriting would tell you what I think.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I think thou art an ass.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Marry, so it doth appear

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: By the wrongs I suffer and the blows I bear.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I should kick, being kickd; and, being at that pass,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: You would keep from my heels and beware of an ass.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Youre sad, Signior Balthazar: pray God our cheer

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: May answer my good will and your good welcome here.

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: I hold your dainties cheap, sir, and your

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: welcome dear.

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: O, Signior Balthazar, either at flesh or fish,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: A table full of welcome make scarce one dainty dish.

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: Good meat, sir, is common; that every churl affords.

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And welcome more common; for thats nothing but words.

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: Small cheer and great welcome makes a merry feast.

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Ay, to a niggardly host, and more sparing guest:

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But though my cates be mean, take them in good part;

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Better cheer may you have, but not with better heart.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But, soft! my door is lockd. Go bid them let us in.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Maud, Bridget, Marian, Cicel, Gillian, Ginn!

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: [Within]  Mome, malt-horse, capon, coxcomb,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: idiot, patch!

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Either get thee from the door, or sit down at the hatch.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Dost thou conjure for wenches, that thou callst

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: for such store,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: When one is one too many? Go, get thee from the door.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: What patch is made our porter? My master stays in

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: the street.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: [Within]  Let him walk from whence he came, lest he

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: catch cold ons feet.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Who talks within there? ho, open the door!

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: [Within]  Right, sir; Ill tell you when, an you tell

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: me wherefore.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Wherefore? for my dinner: I have not dined to-day.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: [Within]  Nor to-day here you must not; come again

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: when you may.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: What art thou that keepest me out from the house I owe?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: [Within]  The porter for this time, sir, and my name

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: is Dromio.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: O villain! thou hast stolen both mine office and my name.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: The one neer got me credit, the other mickle blame.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: If thou hadst been Dromio to-day in my place,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Thou wouldst have changed thy face for a name or thy

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: name for an ass.

speaker: LUCE
text_entry: [Within]  What a coil is there, Dromio? who are those

speaker: LUCE
text_entry: at the gate?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Let my master in, Luce.

speaker: LUCE
text_entry: [Within]  Faith, no; he comes too late;

speaker: LUCE
text_entry: And so tell your master.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: O Lord, I must laugh!

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Have at you with a proverb--Shall I set in my staff?

speaker: LUCE
text_entry: [Within]  Have at you with another; thats--When?

speaker: LUCE
text_entry: can you tell?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: [Within]  If thy name be calld Luce--Luce, thou hast

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: answered him well.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS
text_entry: Do you hear, you minion? youll let us in, I hope?

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS
text_entry: OF EPHESUS

speaker: LUCE
text_entry: [Within]  I thought to have asked you.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: [Within]  And you said no.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: So, come, help: well struck! there was blow for blow.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Thou baggage, let me in.

speaker: LUCE
text_entry: [Within]  Can you tell for whose sake?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Master, knock the door hard.

speaker: LUCE
text_entry: [Within]  Let him knock till it ache.

speaker: LUCE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Youll cry for this, minion, if I beat the door down.

speaker: LUCE
text_entry: [Within]  What needs all that, and a pair of stocks in the town?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: [Within]  Who is that at the door that keeps all

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: this noise?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: [Within]  By my troth, your town is troubled with

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: unruly boys.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Are you there, wife? you might have come before.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: [Within]  Your wife, sir knave! go get you from the door.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: If you went in pain, master, this knave would go sore.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Here is neither cheer, sir, nor welcome: we would

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: fain have either.

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: In debating which was best, we shall part with neither.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: They stand at the door, master; bid them welcome hither.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: There is something in the wind, that we cannot get in.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: You would say so, master, if your garments were thin.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Your cake there is warm within; you stand here in the cold:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: It would make a man mad as a buck, to be so bought and sold.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Go fetch me something: Ill break ope the gate.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: [Within]  Break any breaking here, and Ill break your

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: knaves pate.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: A man may break a word with you, sir, and words are but wind,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Ay, and break it in your face, so he break it not behind.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: [Within]  It seems thou wantst breaking: out upon

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: thee, hind!

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Heres too much out upon thee! I pray thee,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: let me in.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: [Within]  Ay, when fowls have no feathers and fish have no fin.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Well, Ill break in: go borrow me a crow.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: A crow without feather? Master, mean you so?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: For a fish without a fin, theres a fowl without a feather;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: If a crow help us in, sirrah, well pluck a crow together.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Go get thee gone; fetch me an iron crow.

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: Have patience, sir; O, let it not be so!

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: Herein you war against your reputation

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: And draw within the compass of suspect

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: The unviolated honour of your wife.

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: Once this,--your long experience of her wisdom,

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: Her sober virtue, years and modesty,

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: Plead on her part some cause to you unknown:

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: And doubt not, sir, but she will well excuse

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: Why at this time the doors are made against you.

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: Be ruled by me: depart in patience,

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: And let us to the Tiger all to dinner,

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: And about evening come yourself alone

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: To know the reason of this strange restraint.

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: If by strong hand you offer to break in

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: Now in the stirring passage of the day,

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: A vulgar comment will be made of it,

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: And that supposed by the common rout

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: Against your yet ungalled estimation

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: That may with foul intrusion enter in

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: And dwell upon your grave when you are dead;

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: For slander lives upon succession,

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: For ever housed where it gets possession.

speaker: BALTHAZAR
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: You have prevailed: I will depart in quiet,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And, in despite of mirth, mean to be merry.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I know a wench of excellent discourse,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Pretty and witty; wild, and yet, too, gentle:

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: There will we dine. This woman that I mean,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: My wife--but, I protest, without desert--

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Hath oftentimes upbraided me withal:

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: To her will we to dinner.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: To Angelo

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Get you home

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And fetch the chain; by this I know tis made:

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Bring it, I pray you, to the Porpentine;

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: For theres the house: that chain will I bestow--

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Be it for nothing but to spite my wife--

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Upon mine hostess there: good sir, make haste.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Since mine own doors refuse to entertain me,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Ill knock elsewhere, to see if theyll disdain me.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Ill meet you at that place some hour hence.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Do so. This jest shall cost me some expense.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: SCENE II. The same.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Enter LUCIANA and ANTIPHOLUS of Syracuse

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: And may it be that you have quite forgot

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: A husbands office? shall, Antipholus.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Even in the spring of love, thy love-springs rot?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Shall love, in building, grow so ruinous?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: If you did wed my sister for her wealth,

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Then for her wealths sake use her with more kindness:

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Or if you like elsewhere, do it by stealth;

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Muffle your false love with some show of blindness:

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Let not my sister read it in your eye;

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Be not thy tongue thy own shames orator;

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Look sweet, be fair, become disloyalty;

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Apparel vice like virtues harbinger;

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Bear a fair presence, though your heart be tainted;

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Teach sin the carriage of a holy saint;

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Be secret-false: what need she be acquainted?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: What simple thief brags of his own attaint?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Tis double wrong, to truant with your bed

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: And let her read it in thy looks at board:

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Shame hath a bastard fame, well managed;

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Ill d eeds are doubled with an evil word.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Alas, poor women! make us but believe,

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Being compact of credit, that you love us;

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Though others have the arm, show us the sleeve;

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: We in your motion turn and you may move us.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Then, gentle brother, get you in again;

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Comfort my sister, cheer her, call her wife:

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Tis holy sport to be a little vain,

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: When the sweet breath of flattery conquers strife.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Sweet mistress--what your name is else, I know not,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Nor by what wonder you do hit of mine,--

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Less in your knowledge and your grace you show not

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Than our earths wonder, more than earth divine.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Teach me, dear creature, how to think and speak;

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Lay open to my earthy-gross conceit,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Smotherd in errors, feeble, shallow, weak,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: The folded meaning of your words deceit.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Against my souls pure truth why labour you

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: To make it wander in an unknown field?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Are you a god? would you create me new?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Transform me then, and to your power Ill yield.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: But if that I am I, then well I know

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Your weeping sister is no wife of mine,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Nor to her bed no homage do I owe

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Far more, far more to you do I decline.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: O, train me not, sweet mermaid, with thy note,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: To drown me in thy sisters flood of tears:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Sing, siren, for thyself and I will dote:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Spread oer the silver waves thy golden hairs,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And as a bed Ill take them and there lie,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And in that glorious supposition think

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: He gains by death that hath such means to die:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Let Love, being light, be drowned if she sink!

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: What, are you mad, that you do reason so?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Not mad, but mated; how, I do not know.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: It is a fault that springeth from your eye.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: For gazing on your beams, fair sun, being by.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Gaze where you should, and that will clear your sight.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: As good to wink, sweet love, as look on night.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Why call you me love? call my sister so.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Thy sisters sister.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Thats my sister.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: No;

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: It is thyself, mine own selfs better part,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Mine eyes clear eye, my dear hearts dearer heart,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: My food, my fortune and my sweet hopes aim,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: My sole earths heaven and my heavens claim.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: All this my sister is, or else should be.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Call thyself sister, sweet, for I am thee.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Thee will I love and with thee lead my life:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Thou hast no husband yet nor I no wife.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Give me thy hand.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: O, soft, air! hold you still:

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Ill fetch my sister, to get her good will.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Exit

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Enter DROMIO of Syracuse

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Why, how now, Dromio! where runnst thou so fast?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Do you know me, sir? am I Dromio? am I your man?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: am I myself?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Thou art Dromio, thou art my man, thou art thyself.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I am an ass, I am a womans man and besides myself.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS
text_entry: What womans man? and how besides thyself? besides thyself?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Marry, sir, besides myself, I am due to a woman; one

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: that claims me, one that haunts me, one that will have me.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What claim lays she to thee?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Marry sir, such claim as you would lay to your

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: horse; and she would have me as a beast: not that, I

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: being a beast, she would have me; but that she,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: being a very beastly creature, lays claim to me.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What is she?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: A very reverent body; ay, such a one as a man may

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: not speak of without he say Sir-reverence. I have

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: but lean luck in the match, and yet is she a

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: wondrous fat marriage.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: How dost thou mean a fat marriage?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Marry, sir, shes the kitchen wench and all grease;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: and I know not what use to put her to but to make a

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: lamp of her and run from her by her own light. I

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: warrant, her rags and the tallow in them will burn a

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Poland winter: if she lives till doomsday,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: shell burn a week longer than the whole world.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What complexion is she of?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Swart, like my shoe, but her face nothing half so

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: clean kept: for why, she sweats; a man may go over

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: shoes in the grime of it.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Thats a fault that water will mend.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: No, sir, tis in grain; Noahs flood could not do it.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Whats her name?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Nell, sir; but her name and three quarters, thats

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: an ell and three quarters, will not measure her from

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: hip to hip.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Then she bears some breadth?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: No longer from head to foot than from hip to hip:

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: she is spherical, like a globe; I could find out

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: countries in her.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: In what part of her body stands Ireland?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Marry, in her buttocks: I found it out by the bogs.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Where Scotland?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I found it by the barrenness; hard in the palm of the hand.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Where France?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: In her forehead; armed and reverted, making war

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: against her heir.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Where England?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I looked for the chalky cliffs, but I could find no

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: whiteness in them; but I guess it stood in her chin,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: by the salt rheum that ran between France and it.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Where Spain?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Faith, I saw it not; but I felt it hot in her breath.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Where America, the Indies?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Oh, sir, upon her nose all oer embellished with

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: rubies, carbuncles, sapphires, declining their rich

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: aspect to the hot breath of Spain; who sent whole

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: armadoes of caracks to be ballast at her nose.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Where stood Belgia, the Netherlands?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Oh, sir, I did not look so low. To conclude, this

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: drudge, or diviner, laid claim to me, calld me

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Dromio; swore I was assured to her; told me what

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: privy marks I had about me, as, the mark of my

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: shoulder, the mole in my neck, the great wart on my

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: left arm, that I amazed ran from her as a witch:

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And, I think, if my breast had not been made of

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: faith and my heart of steel,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: She had transformd me to a curtal dog and made

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: me turn i the wheel.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Go hie thee presently, post to the road:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: An if the wind blow any way from shore,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I will not harbour in this town to-night:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: If any bark put forth, come to the mart,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Where I will walk till thou return to me.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: If every one knows us and we know none,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Tis time, I think, to trudge, pack and be gone.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: As from a bear a man would run for life,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: So fly I from her that would be my wife.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Theres none but witches do inhabit here;

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And therefore tis high time that I were hence.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: She that doth call me husband, even my soul

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Doth for a wife abhor. But her fair sister,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Possessd with such a gentle sovereign grace,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Of such enchanting presence and discourse,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Hath almost made me traitor to myself:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: But, lest myself be guilty to self-wrong,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Ill stop mine ears against the mermaids song.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Enter ANGELO with the chain

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Master Antipholus,--

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Ay, thats my name.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: I know it well, sir, lo, here is the chain.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: I thought to have taen you at the Porpentine:

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: The chain unfinishd made me stay thus long.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What is your will that I shall do with this?

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: What please yourself, sir: I have made it for you.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Made it for me, sir! I bespoke it not.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Not once, nor twice, but twenty times you have.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Go home with it and please your wife withal;

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: And soon at supper-time Ill visit you

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: And then receive my money for the chain.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I pray you, sir, receive the money now,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: For fear you neer see chain nor money more.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: You are a merry man, sir: fare you well.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Exit

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What I should think of this, I cannot tell:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: But this I think, theres no man is so vain

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: That would refuse so fair an offerd chain.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I see a man here needs not live by shifts,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: When in the streets he meets such golden gifts.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Ill to the mart, and there for Dromio stay

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: If any ship put out, then straight away.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ACT IV

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: SCENE I. A public place.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Enter Second Merchant, ANGELO, and an Officer

speaker: Second Merchant
text_entry: You know since Pentecost the sum is due,

speaker: Second Merchant
text_entry: And since I have not much importuned you;

speaker: Second Merchant
text_entry: Nor now I had not, but that I am bound

speaker: Second Merchant
text_entry: To Persia, and want guilders for my voyage:

speaker: Second Merchant
text_entry: Therefore make present satisfaction,

speaker: Second Merchant
text_entry: Or Ill attach you by this officer.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Even just the sum that I do owe to you

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Is growing to me by Antipholus,

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: And in the instant that I met with you

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: He had of me a chain: at five oclock

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: I shall receive the money for the same.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Pleaseth you walk with me down to his house,

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: I will discharge my bond and thank you too.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Enter ANTIPHOLUS of Ephesus and DROMIO of Ephesus from the courtezans

speaker: Officer
text_entry: That labour may you save: see where he comes.

speaker: Officer
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: While I go to the goldsmiths house, go thou

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And buy a ropes end: that will I bestow

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Among my wife and her confederates,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: For locking me out of my doors by day.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But, soft! I see the goldsmith. Get thee gone;

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Buy thou a rope and bring it home to me.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I buy a thousand pound a year: I buy a rope.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: A man is well holp up that trusts to you:

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I promised your presence and the chain;

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But neither chain nor goldsmith came to me.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Belike you thought our love would last too long,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: If it were chaind together, and therefore came not.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Saving your merry humour, heres the note

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: How much your chain weighs to the utmost carat,

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: The fineness of the gold and chargeful fashion.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Which doth amount to three odd ducats more

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Than I stand debted to this gentleman:

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: I pray you, see him presently discharged,

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: For he is bound to sea and stays but for it.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I am not furnishd with the present money;

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Besides, I have some business in the town.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Good signior, take the stranger to my house

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And with you take the chain and bid my wife

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Disburse the sum on the receipt thereof:

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Perchance I will be there as soon as you.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Then you will bring the chain to her yourself?

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: No; bear it with you, lest I come not time enough.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Well, sir, I will. Have you the chain about you?

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: An if I have not, sir, I hope you have;

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Or else you may return without your money.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Nay, come, I pray you, sir, give me the chain:

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Both wind and tide stays for this gentleman,

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: And I, to blame, have held him here too long.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Good Lord! you use this dalliance to excuse

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Your breach of promise to the Porpentine.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I should have chid you for not bringing it,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But, like a shrew, you first begin to brawl.

speaker: Second Merchant
text_entry: The hour steals on; I pray you, sir, dispatch.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: You hear how he importunes me;--the chain!

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Why, give it to my wife and fetch your money.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Come, come, you know I gave it you even now.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Either send the chain or send me by some token.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Fie, now you run this humour out of breath,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: wheres the chain? I pray you, let me see it.

speaker: Second Merchant
text_entry: My business cannot brook this dalliance.

speaker: Second Merchant
text_entry: Good sir, say whether youll answer me or no:

speaker: Second Merchant
text_entry: If not, Ill leave him to the officer.

speaker: Second Merchant
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I answer you! what should I answer you?

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: The money that you owe me for the chain.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I owe you none till I receive the chain.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: You know I gave it you half an hour since.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: You gave me none: you wrong me much to say so.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: You wrong me more, sir, in denying it:

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Consider how it stands upon my credit.

speaker: Second Merchant
text_entry: Well, officer, arrest him at my suit.

speaker: Officer
text_entry: I do; and charge you in the dukes name to obey me.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: This touches me in reputation.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Either consent to pay this sum for me

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Or I attach you by this officer.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Consent to pay thee that I never had!

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Arrest me, foolish fellow, if thou darest.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Here is thy fee; arrest him, officer,

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: I would not spare my brother in this case,

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: If he should scorn me so apparently.

speaker: Officer
text_entry: I do arrest you, sir: you hear the suit.

speaker: Officer
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I do obey thee till I give thee bail.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But, sirrah, you shall buy this sport as dear

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: As all the metal in your shop will answer.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Sir, sir, I will have law in Ephesus,

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: To your notorious shame; I doubt it not.

speaker: ANGELO
text_entry: Enter DROMIO of Syracuse, from the bay

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Master, there is a bark of Epidamnum

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: That stays but till her owner comes aboard,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And then, sir, she bears away. Our fraughtage, sir,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I have conveyd aboard; and I have bought

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: The oil, the balsamum and aqua-vitae.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: The ship is in her trim; the merry wind

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Blows fair from land: they stay for nought at all

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: But for their owner, master, and yourself.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: How now! a madman! Why, thou peevish sheep,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: What ship of Epidamnum stays for me?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: A ship you sent me to, to hire waftage.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Thou drunken slave, I sent thee for a rope;

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And told thee to what purpose and what end.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: You sent me for a ropes end as soon:

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: You sent me to the bay, sir, for a bark.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I will debate this matter at more leisure

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And teach your ears to list me with more heed.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: To Adriana, villain, hie thee straight:

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Give her this key, and tell her, in the desk

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Thats coverd oer with Turkish tapestry,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: There is a purse of ducats; let her send it:

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Tell her I am arrested in the street

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And that shall bail me; hie thee, slave, be gone!

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: On, officer, to prison till it come.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Exeunt Second Merchant, Angelo, Officer, and Antipholus of Ephesus

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: To Adriana! that is where we dined,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Where Dowsabel did claim me for her husband:

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: She is too big, I hope, for me to compass.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Thither I must, although against my will,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: For servants must their masters minds fulfil.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: SCENE II. The house of ANTIPHOLUS of Ephesus.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Enter ADRIANA and LUCIANA

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Ah, Luciana, did he tempt thee so?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Mightst thou perceive austerely in his eye

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: That he did plead in earnest? yea or no?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Lookd he or red or pale, or sad or merrily?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: What observation madest thou in this case

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Of his hearts meteors tilting in his face?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: First he denied you had in him no right.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: He meant he did me none; the more my spite.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Then swore he that he was a stranger here.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And true he swore, though yet forsworn he were.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Then pleaded I for you.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And what said he?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: That love I beggd for you he beggd of me.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: With what persuasion did he tempt thy love?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: With words that in an honest suit might move.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: First he did praise my beauty, then my speech.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Didst speak him fair?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Have patience, I beseech.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: I cannot, nor I will not, hold me still;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: My tongue, though not my heart, shall have his will.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: He is deformed, crooked, old and sere,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Ill-faced, worse bodied, shapeless everywhere;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Vicious, ungentle, foolish, blunt, unkind;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Stigmatical in making, worse in mind.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Who would be jealous then of such a one?

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: No evil lost is waild when it is gone.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Ah, but I think him better than I say,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And yet would herein others eyes were worse.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Far from her nest the lapwing cries away:

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: My heart prays for him, though my tongue do curse.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Enter DROMIO of Syracuse

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Here! go; the desk, the purse! sweet, now, make haste.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: How hast thou lost thy breath?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: By running fast.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Where is thy master, Dromio? is he well?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: No, hes in Tartar limbo, worse than hell.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: A devil in an everlasting garment hath him;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: One whose hard heart is buttond up with steel;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: A fiend, a fury, pitiless and rough;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: A wolf, nay, worse, a fellow all in buff;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: A back-friend, a shoulder-clapper, one that

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: countermands

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: The passages of alleys, creeks and narrow lands;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: A hound that runs counter and yet draws dryfoot well;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: One that before the judgement carries poor souls to hell.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Why, man, what is the matter?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I do not know the matter: he is rested on the case.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: What, is he arrested? Tell me at whose suit.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I know not at whose suit he is arrested well;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: But hes in a suit of buff which rested him, that can I tell.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Will you send him, mistress, redemption, the money in his desk?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Go fetch it, sister.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Exit Luciana

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: This I wonder at,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: That he, unknown to me, should be in debt.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Tell me, was he arrested on a band?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Not on a band, but on a stronger thing;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: A chain, a chain! Do you not hear it ring?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: What, the chain?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: No, no, the bell: tis time that I were gone:

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: It was two ere I left him, and now the clock

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: strikes one.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: The hours come back! that did I never hear.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: O, yes; if any hour meet a sergeant, a turns back for

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: very fear.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: As if Time were in debt! how fondly dost thou reason!

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Time is a very bankrupt, and owes more than hes

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: worth, to season.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Nay, hes a thief too: have you not heard men say

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: That Time comes stealing on by night and day?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: If Time be in debt and theft, and a sergeant in the way,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Hath he not reason to turn back an hour in a day?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Re-enter LUCIANA with a purse

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Go, Dromio; theres the money, bear it straight;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And bring thy master home immediately.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Come, sister: I am pressd down with conceit--

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Conceit, my comfort and my injury.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: SCENE III. A public place.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Enter ANTIPHOLUS of Syracuse

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Theres not a man I meet but doth salute me

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: As if I were their well-acquainted friend;

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And every one doth call me by my name.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Some tender money to me; some invite me;

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Some other give me thanks for kindnesses;

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Some offer me commodities to buy:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Even now a tailor calld me in his shop

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And showd me silks that he had bought for me,

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And therewithal took measure of my body.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Sure, these are but imaginary wiles

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And Lapland sorcerers inhabit here.

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Enter DROMIO OF SYRACUSE

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Master, heres the gold you sent me for. What, have

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: you got the picture of old Adam new-apparelled?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What gold is this? what Adam dost thou mean?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Not that Adam that kept the Paradise but that Adam

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: that keeps the prison: he that goes in the calfs

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: skin that was killed for the Prodigal; he that came

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: behind you, sir, like an evil angel, and bid you

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: forsake your liberty.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I understand thee not.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: No? why, tis a plain case: he that went, like a

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: bass-viol, in a case of leather; the man, sir,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: that, when gentlemen are tired, gives them a sob

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: and rests them; he, sir, that takes pity on decayed

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: men and gives them suits of durance; he that sets up

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: his rest to do more exploits with his mace than a

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: morris-pike.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: What, thou meanest an officer?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Ay, sir, the sergeant of the band, he that brings

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: any man to answer it that breaks his band; one that

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: thinks a man always going to bed, and says, God

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: give you good rest!

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Well, sir, there rest in your foolery. Is there any

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Why, sir, I brought you word an hour since that the

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: bark Expedition put forth to-night; and then were

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: you hindered by the sergeant, to tarry for the hoy

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Delay. Here are the angels that you sent for to

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: deliver you.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: The fellow is distract, and so am I;

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: And here we wander in illusions:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Some blessed power deliver us from hence!

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Enter a Courtezan

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Well met, well met, Master Antipholus.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: I see, sir, you have found the goldsmith now:

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Is that the chain you promised me to-day?

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Satan, avoid! I charge thee, tempt me not.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Master, is this Mistress Satan?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: It is the devil.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Nay, she is worse, she is the devils dam; and here

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: she comes in the habit of a light wench: and thereof

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: comes that the wenches say God damn me; thats as

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: much to say God make me a light wench. It is

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: written, they appear to men like angels of light:

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: light is an effect of fire, and fire will burn;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ergo, light wenches will burn. Come not near her.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Your man and you are marvellous merry, sir.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Will you go with me? Well mend our dinner here?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Master, if you do, expect spoon-meat; or bespeak a

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: long spoon.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Why, Dromio?

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Marry, he must have a long spoon that must eat with

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: the devil.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Avoid then, fiend! what tellst thou me of supping?

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Thou art, as you are all, a sorceress:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I conjure thee to leave me and be gone.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Give me the ring of mine you had at dinner,

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Or, for my diamond, the chain you promised,

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: And Ill be gone, sir, and not trouble you.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Some devils ask but the parings of ones nail,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: A rush, a hair, a drop of blood, a pin,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: A nut, a cherry-stone;

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: But she, more covetous, would have a chain.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Master, be wise: an if you give it her,

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: The devil will shake her chain and fright us with it.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: I pray you, sir, my ring, or else the chain:

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: I hope you do not mean to cheat me so.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Avaunt, thou witch! Come, Dromio, let us go.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Fly pride, says the peacock: mistress, that you know.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Exeunt Antipholus of Syracuse and Dromio of Syracuse

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Now, out of doubt Antipholus is mad,

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Else would he never so demean himself.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: A ring he hath of mine worth forty ducats,

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: And for the same he promised me a chain:

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Both one and other he denies me now.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: The reason that I gather he is mad,

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Besides this present instance of his rage,

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Is a mad tale he told to-day at dinner,

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Of his own doors being shut against his entrance.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Belike his wife, acquainted with his fits,

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: On purpose shut the doors against his way.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: My way is now to hie home to his house,

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: And tell his wife that, being lunatic,

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: He rushd into my house and took perforce

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: My ring away. This course I fittest choose;

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: For forty ducats is too much to lose.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Exit

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: SCENE IV. A street.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Enter ANTIPHOLUS of Ephesus and the Officer

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Fear me not, man; I will not break away:

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Ill give thee, ere I leave thee, so much money,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: To warrant thee, as I am rested for.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: My wife is in a wayward mood to-day,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And will not lightly trust the messenger

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: That I should be attachd in Ephesus,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I tell you, twill sound harshly in her ears.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Enter DROMIO of Ephesus with a ropes-end

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Here comes my man; I think he brings the money.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: How now, sir! have you that I sent you for?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Heres that, I warrant you, will pay them all.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But wheres the money?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Why, sir, I gave the money for the rope.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Five hundred ducats, villain, for a rope?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Ill serve you, sir, five hundred at the rate.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: To what end did I bid thee hie thee home?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: To a ropes-end, sir; and to that end am I returned.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And to that end, sir, I will welcome you.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Beating him

speaker: Officer
text_entry: Good sir, be patient.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Nay, tis for me to be patient; I am in adversity.

speaker: Officer
text_entry: Good, now, hold thy tongue.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Nay, rather persuade him to hold his hands.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Thou whoreson, senseless villain!

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I would I were senseless, sir, that I might not feel

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: your blows.

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS
text_entry: Thou art sensible in nothing but blows, and so is an

speaker: ANTIPHOLUS
text_entry: ass.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I am an ass, indeed; you may prove it by my long

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ears. I have served him from the hour of my

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: nativity to this instant, and have nothing at his

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: hands for my service but blows. When I am cold, he

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: heats me with beating; when I am warm, he cools me

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: with beating; I am waked with it when I sleep;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: raised with it when I sit; driven out of doors with

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: it when I go from home; welcomed home with it when

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I return; nay, I bear it on my shoulders, as a

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: beggar wont her brat; and, I think when he hath

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: lamed me, I shall beg with it from door to door.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Come, go along; my wife is coming yonder.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Enter ADRIANA, LUCIANA, the Courtezan, and PINCH

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Mistress, respice finem, respect your end; or

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: rather, the prophecy like the parrot, beware the

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ropes-end.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Wilt thou still talk?

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Beating him

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: How say you now? is not your husband mad?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: His incivility confirms no less.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Good Doctor Pinch, you are a conjurer;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Establish him in his true sense again,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And I will please you what you will demand.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Alas, how fiery and how sharp he looks!

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Mark how he trembles in his ecstasy!

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: Give me your hand and let me feel your pulse.

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: There is my hand, and let it feel your ear.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Striking him

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: I charge thee, Satan, housed within this man,

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: To yield possession to my holy prayers

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: And to thy state of darkness hie thee straight:

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: I conjure thee by all the saints in heaven!

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Peace, doting wizard, peace! I am not mad.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: O, that thou wert not, poor distressed soul!

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: You minion, you, are these your customers?

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Did this companion with the saffron face

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Revel and feast it at my house to-day,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Whilst upon me the guilty doors were shut

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And I denied to enter in my house?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: O husband, God doth know you dined at home;

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Where would you had remaind until this time,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Free from these slanders and this open shame!

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Dined at home! Thou villain, what sayest thou?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Sir, sooth to say, you did not dine at home.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Were not my doors lockd up and I shut out?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Perdie, your doors were lockd and you shut out.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And did not she herself revile me there?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Sans fable, she herself reviled you there.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Did not her kitchen-maid rail, taunt, and scorn me?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Certes, she did; the kitchen-vestal scornd you.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And did not I in rage depart from thence?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: In verity you did; my bones bear witness,

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: That since have felt the vigour of his rage.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Ist good to soothe him in these contraries?

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: It is no shame: the fellow finds his vein,

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: And yielding to him humours well his frenzy.

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Thou hast subornd the goldsmith to arrest me.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Alas, I sent you money to redeem you,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: By Dromio here, who came in haste for it.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Money by me! heart and goodwill you might;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But surely master, not a rag of money.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Wentst not thou to her for a purse of ducats?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: He came to me and I deliverd it.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: And I am witness with her that she did.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: God and the rope-maker bear me witness

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: That I was sent for nothing but a rope!

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: Mistress, both man and master is possessd;

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: I know it by their pale and deadly looks:

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: They must be bound and laid in some dark room.

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Say, wherefore didst thou lock me forth to-day?

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And why dost thou deny the bag of gold?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: I did not, gentle husband, lock thee forth.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And, gentle master, I received no gold;

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But I confess, sir, that we were lockd out.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Dissembling villain, thou speakst false in both.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Dissembling harlot, thou art false in all;

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: And art confederate with a damned pack

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: To make a loathsome abject scorn of me:

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: But with these nails Ill pluck out these false eyes

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: That would behold in me this shameful sport.

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Enter three or four, and offer to bind him. He strives

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: O, bind him, bind him! let him not come near me.

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: More company! The fiend is strong within him.

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: Ay me, poor man, how pale and wan he looks!

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: What, will you murder me? Thou gaoler, thou,

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: I am thy prisoner: wilt thou suffer them

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: To make a rescue?

speaker: Officer
text_entry: Masters, let him go

speaker: Officer
text_entry: He is my prisoner, and you shall not have him.

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: Go bind this man, for he is frantic too.

speaker: PINCH
text_entry: They offer to bind Dromio of Ephesus

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: What wilt thou do, thou peevish officer?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Hast thou delight to see a wretched man

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Do outrage and displeasure to himself?

speaker: Officer
text_entry: He is my prisoner: if I let him go,

speaker: Officer
text_entry: The debt he owes will be required of me.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: I will discharge thee ere I go from thee:

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Bear me forthwith unto his creditor,

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And, knowing how the debt grows, I will pay it.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Good master doctor, see him safe conveyd

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Home to my house. O most unhappy day!

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: O most unhappy strumpet!

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Master, I am here entered in bond for you.

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Out on thee, villain! wherefore dost thou mad me?

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: Will you be bound for nothing? be mad, good master:

speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
text_entry: cry The devil!

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: God help, poor souls, how idly do they talk!

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Go bear him hence. Sister, go you with me.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Exeunt all but Adriana, Luciana, Officer and Courtezan

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Say now, whose suit is he arrested at?

speaker: Officer
text_entry: One Angelo, a goldsmith: do you know him?

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: I know the man. What is the sum he owes?

speaker: Officer
text_entry: Two hundred ducats.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Say, how grows it due?

speaker: Officer
text_entry: Due for a chain your husband had of him.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: He did bespeak a chain for me, but had it not.

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: When as your husband all in rage to-day

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Came to my house and took away my ring--

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: The ring I saw upon his finger now--

speaker: Courtezan
text_entry: Straight after did I meet him with a chain.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: It may be so, but I did never see it.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Come, gaoler, bring me where the goldsmith is:

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: I long to know the truth hereof at large.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Enter ANTIPHOLUS of Syracuse with his rapier drawn, and DROMIO of Syracuse

speaker: LUCIANA
text_entry: God, for thy mercy! they are loose again.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: And come with naked swords.

speaker: ADRIANA
text_entry: Lets call more help to have them bound again.

speaker: Officer
text_entry: Away! theyll kill us.

speaker: Officer
text_entry: Exeunt all but Antipholus of Syracuse and Dromio of Syracuse

speaker: Officer
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I see these witches are afraid of swords.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: She that would be your wife now ran from you.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: ANTIPHOLUS

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Come to the Centaur; fetch our stuff from thence:

speaker: OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: I long that we were safe and sound aboard.

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
text_entry: Faith, stay here this night; they will surely do us

speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
