text_entry: Markd ye his words? He would not take the crown;

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: Therefore tis certain he was not ambitious.

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: If it be found so, some will dear abide it.

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: Poor soul! his eyes are red as fire with weeping.

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: Theres not a nobler man in Rome than Antony.

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: Now mark him, he begins again to speak.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: But yesterday the word of Caesar might

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Have stood against the world; now lies he there.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And none so poor to do him reverence.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: O masters, if I were disposed to stir

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Your hearts and minds to mutiny and rage,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: I should do Brutus wrong, and Cassius wrong,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Who, you all know, are honourable men:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: I will not do them wrong; I rather choose

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: To wrong the dead, to wrong myself and you,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Than I will wrong such honourable men.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: But heres a parchment with the seal of Caesar;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: I found it in his closet, tis his will:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Let but the commons hear this testament--

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Which, pardon me, I do not mean to read--

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And they would go and kiss dead Caesars wounds

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And dip their napkins in his sacred blood,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Yea, beg a hair of him for memory,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And, dying, mention it within their wills,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Bequeathing it as a rich legacy

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Unto their issue.

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: Well hear the will: read it, Mark Antony.

speaker: All
text_entry: The will, the will! we will hear Caesars will.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Have patience, gentle friends, I must not read it;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: It is not meet you know how Caesar loved you.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: You are not wood, you are not stones, but men;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And, being men, bearing the will of Caesar,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: It will inflame you, it will make you mad:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Tis good you know not that you are his heirs;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: For, if you should, O, what would come of it!

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: Read the will; well hear it, Antony;

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: You shall read us the will, Caesars will.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Will you be patient? will you stay awhile?

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: I have oershot myself to tell you of it:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: I fear I wrong the honourable men

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Whose daggers have stabbd Caesar; I do fear it.

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: They were traitors: honourable men!

speaker: All
text_entry: The will! the testament!

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: They were villains, murderers: the will! read the will.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: You will compel me, then, to read the will?

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Then make a ring about the corpse of Caesar,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And let me show you him that made the will.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Shall I descend? and will you give me leave?

speaker: Several Citizens
text_entry: Come down.

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: Descend.

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: You shall have leave.

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: ANTONY comes down

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: A ring; stand round.

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: Stand from the hearse, stand from the body.

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: Room for Antony, most noble Antony.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Nay, press not so upon me; stand far off.

speaker: Several Citizens
text_entry: Stand back; room; bear back.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: If you have tears, prepare to shed them now.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: You all do know this mantle: I remember

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: The first time ever Caesar put it on;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Twas on a summers evening, in his tent,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: That day he overcame the Nervii:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Look, in this place ran Cassius dagger through:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: See what a rent the envious Casca made:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Through this the well-beloved Brutus stabbd;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And as he pluckd his cursed steel away,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Mark how the blood of Caesar followd it,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: As rushing out of doors, to be resolved

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: If Brutus so unkindly knockd, or no;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: For Brutus, as you know, was Caesars angel:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Judge, O you gods, how dearly Caesar loved him!

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: This was the most unkindest cut of all;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: For when the noble Caesar saw him stab,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Ingratitude, more strong than traitors arms,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Quite vanquishd him: then burst his mighty heart;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And, in his mantle muffling up his face,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Even at the base of Pompeys statua,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Which all the while ran blood, great Caesar fell.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: O, what a fall was there, my countrymen!

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Then I, and you, and all of us fell down,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Whilst bloody treason flourishd over us.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: O, now you weep; and, I perceive, you feel

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: The dint of pity: these are gracious drops.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Kind souls, what, weep you when you but behold

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Our Caesars vesture wounded? Look you here,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Here is himself, marrd, as you see, with traitors.

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: O piteous spectacle!

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: O noble Caesar!

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: O woful day!

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: O traitors, villains!

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: O most bloody sight!

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: We will be revenged.

speaker: All
text_entry: Revenge! About! Seek! Burn! Fire! Kill! Slay!

speaker: All
text_entry: Let not a traitor live!

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Stay, countrymen.

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: Peace there! hear the noble Antony.

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: Well hear him, well follow him, well die with him.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Good friends, sweet friends, let me not stir you up

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: To such a sudden flood of mutiny.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: They that have done this deed are honourable:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: What private griefs they have, alas, I know not,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: That made them do it: they are wise and honourable,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And will, no doubt, with reasons answer you.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: I come not, friends, to steal away your hearts:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: I am no orator, as Brutus is;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: But, as you know me all, a plain blunt man,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: That love my friend; and that they know full well

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: That gave me public leave to speak of him:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: For I have neither wit, nor words, nor worth,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Action, nor utterance, nor the power of speech,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: To stir mens blood: I only speak right on;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: I tell you that which you yourselves do know;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Show you sweet Caesars wounds, poor poor dumb mouths,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And bid them speak for me: but were I Brutus,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And Brutus Antony, there were an Antony

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Would ruffle up your spirits and put a tongue

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: In every wound of Caesar that should move

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: The stones of Rome to rise and mutiny.

speaker: All
text_entry: Well mutiny.

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: Well burn the house of Brutus.

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: Away, then! come, seek the conspirators.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Yet hear me, countrymen; yet hear me speak.

speaker: All
text_entry: Peace, ho! Hear Antony. Most noble Antony!

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Why, friends, you go to do you know not what:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Wherein hath Caesar thus deserved your loves?

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Alas, you know not: I must tell you then:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: You have forgot the will I told you of.

speaker: All
text_entry: Most true. The will! Lets stay and hear the will.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Here is the will, and under Caesars seal.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: To every Roman citizen he gives,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: To every several man, seventy-five drachmas.

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: Most noble Caesar! Well revenge his death.

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: O royal Caesar!

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Hear me with patience.

speaker: All
text_entry: Peace, ho!

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Moreover, he hath left you all his walks,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: His private arbours and new-planted orchards,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: On this side Tiber; he hath left them you,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And to your heirs for ever, common pleasures,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: To walk abroad, and recreate yourselves.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Here was a Caesar! when comes such another?

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: Never, never. Come, away, away!

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: Well burn his body in the holy place,

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: And with the brands fire the traitors houses.

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: Take up the body.

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: Go fetch fire.

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: Pluck down benches.

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: Pluck down forms, windows, any thing.

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: Exeunt Citizens with the body

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Now let it work. Mischief, thou art afoot,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Take thou what course thou wilt!

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Enter a Servant

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: How now, fellow!

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Sir, Octavius is already come to Rome.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Where is he?

speaker: Servant
text_entry: He and Lepidus are at Caesars house.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And thither will I straight to visit him:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: He comes upon a wish. Fortune is merry,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And in this mood will give us any thing.

speaker: Servant
text_entry: I heard him say, Brutus and Cassius

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Are rid like madmen through the gates of Rome.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Belike they had some notice of the people,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: How I had moved them. Bring me to Octavius.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: SCENE III. A street.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Enter CINNA the poet

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: I dreamt to-night that I did feast with Caesar,

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: And things unlucky charge my fantasy:

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: I have no will to wander forth of doors,

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: Yet something leads me forth.

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: Enter Citizens

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: What is your name?

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: Whither are you going?

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: Where do you dwell?

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: Are you a married man or a bachelor?

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: Answer every man directly.

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: Ay, and briefly.

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: Ay, and wisely.

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: Ay, and truly, you were best.

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: What is my name? Whither am I going? Where do I

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: dwell? Am I a married man or a bachelor? Then, to

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: answer every man directly and briefly, wisely and

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: truly: wisely I say, I am a bachelor.

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: Thats as much as to say, they are fools that marry:

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: youll bear me a bang for that, I fear. Proceed; directly.

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: Directly, I am going to Caesars funeral.

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: As a friend or an enemy?

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: As a friend.

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: That matter is answered directly.

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: For your dwelling,--briefly.

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: Briefly, I dwell by the Capitol.

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: Your name, sir, truly.

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: Truly, my name is Cinna.

speaker: First Citizen
text_entry: Tear him to pieces; hes a conspirator.

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: I am Cinna the poet, I am Cinna the poet.

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: Tear him for his bad verses, tear him for his bad verses.

speaker: CINNA THE POET
text_entry: I am not Cinna the conspirator.

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: It is no matter, his names Cinna; pluck but his

speaker: Fourth Citizen
text_entry: name out of his heart, and turn him going.

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: Tear him, tear him! Come, brands ho! fire-brands:

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: to Brutus, to Cassius; burn all: some to Decius

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: house, and some to Cascas; some to Ligarius: away, go!

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: ACT IV

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: SCENE I. A house in Rome.

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: ANTONY, OCTAVIUS, and LEPIDUS, seated at a table

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: These many, then, shall die; their names are prickd.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Your brother too must die; consent you, Lepidus?

speaker: LEPIDUS
text_entry: I do consent--

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Prick him down, Antony.

speaker: LEPIDUS
text_entry: Upon condition Publius shall not live,

speaker: LEPIDUS
text_entry: Who is your sisters son, Mark Antony.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: He shall not live; look, with a spot I damn him.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: But, Lepidus, go you to Caesars house;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Fetch the will hither, and we shall determine

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: How to cut off some charge in legacies.

speaker: LEPIDUS
text_entry: What, shall I find you here?

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Or here, or at the Capitol.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Exit LEPIDUS

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: This is a slight unmeritable man,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Meet to be sent on errands: is it fit,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: The three-fold world divided, he should stand

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: One of the three to share it?

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: So you thought him;

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: And took his voice who should be prickd to die,

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: In our black sentence and proscription.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Octavius, I have seen more days than you:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And though we lay these honours on this man,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: To ease ourselves of divers slanderous loads,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: He shall but bear them as the ass bears gold,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: To groan and sweat under the business,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Either led or driven, as we point the way;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And having brought our treasure where we will,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Then take we down his load, and turn him off,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Like to the empty ass, to shake his ears,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And graze in commons.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: You may do your will;

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: But hes a tried and valiant soldier.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: So is my horse, Octavius; and for that

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: I do appoint him store of provender:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: It is a creature that I teach to fight,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: To wind, to stop, to run directly on,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: His corporal motion governd by my spirit.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And, in some taste, is Lepidus but so;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: He must be taught and traind and bid go forth;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: A barren-spirited fellow; one that feeds

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: On abjects, orts and imitations,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Which, out of use and staled by other men,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Begin his fashion: do not talk of him,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: But as a property. And now, Octavius,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Listen great things:--Brutus and Cassius

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Are levying powers: we must straight make head:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Therefore let our alliance be combined,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Our best friends made, our means stretchd

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And let us presently go sit in council,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: How covert matters may be best disclosed,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And open perils surest answered.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Let us do so: for we are at the stake,

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: And bayd about with many enemies;

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: And some that smile have in their hearts, I fear,

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Millions of mischiefs.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: SCENE II. Camp near Sardis. Before BRUTUSs tent.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Drum. Enter BRUTUS, LUCILIUS, LUCIUS, and Soldiers; TITINIUS and PINDARUS meeting them

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Stand, ho!

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: Give the word, ho! and stand.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: What now, Lucilius! is Cassius near?

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: He is at hand; and Pindarus is come

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: To do you salutation from his master.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: He greets me well. Your master, Pindarus,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: In his own change, or by ill officers,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Hath given me some worthy cause to wish

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Things done, undone: but, if he be at hand,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I shall be satisfied.

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: I do not doubt

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: But that my noble master will appear

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Such as he is, full of regard and honour.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: He is not doubted. A word, Lucilius;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: How he received you, let me be resolved.

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: With courtesy and with respect enough;

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: But not with such familiar instances,

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: Nor with such free and friendly conference,

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: As he hath used of old.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Thou hast described

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: A hot friend cooling: ever note, Lucilius,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: When love begins to sicken and decay,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: It useth an enforced ceremony.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: There are no tricks in plain and simple faith;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: But hollow men, like horses hot at hand,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Make gallant show and promise of their mettle;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: But when they should endure the bloody spur,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: They fall their crests, and, like deceitful jades,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Sink in the trial. Comes his army on?

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: They mean this night in Sardis to be quarterd;

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: The greater part, the horse in general,

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: Are come with Cassius.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Hark! he is arrived.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Low march within

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: March gently on to meet him.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Enter CASSIUS and his powers

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Stand, ho!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Stand, ho! Speak the word along.

speaker: First Soldier
text_entry: Stand!

speaker: Second Soldier
text_entry: Stand!

speaker: Third Soldier
text_entry: Stand!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Most noble brother, you have done me wrong.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Judge me, you gods! wrong I mine enemies?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And, if not so, how should I wrong a brother?

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Brutus, this sober form of yours hides wrongs;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And when you do them--

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Cassius, be content.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Speak your griefs softly: I do know you well.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Before the eyes of both our armies here,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Which should perceive nothing but love from us,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Let us not wrangle: bid them move away;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Then in my tent, Cassius, enlarge your griefs,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And I will give you audience.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Pindarus,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Bid our commanders lead their charges off

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: A little from this ground.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Lucilius, do you the like; and let no man

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Come to our tent till we have done our conference.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Let Lucius and Titinius guard our door.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: SCENE III. Brutuss tent.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Enter BRUTUS and CASSIUS

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: That you have wrongd me doth appear in this:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: You have condemnd and noted Lucius Pella

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: For taking bribes here of the Sardians;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Wherein my letters, praying on his side,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Because I knew the man, were slighted off.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: You wronged yourself to write in such a case.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: In such a time as this it is not meet

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: That every nice offence should bear his comment.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Let me tell you, Cassius, you yourself

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Are much condemnd to have an itching palm;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: To sell and mart your offices for gold

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: To undeservers.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I an itching palm!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: You know that you are Brutus that speak this,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Or, by the gods, this speech were else your last.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: The name of Cassius honours this corruption,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And chastisement doth therefore hide his head.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Chastisement!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Remember March, the ides of March remember:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Did not great Julius bleed for justice sake?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: What villain touchd his body, that did stab,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And not for justice? What, shall one of us

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: That struck the foremost man of all this world

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: But for supporting robbers, shall we now

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Contaminate our fingers with base bribes,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And sell the mighty space of our large honours

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: For so much trash as may be grasped thus?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I had rather be a dog, and bay the moon,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Than such a Roman.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Brutus, bay not me;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Ill not endure it: you forget yourself,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: To hedge me in; I am a soldier, I,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Older in practise, abler than yourself

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: To make conditions.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Go to; you are not, Cassius.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I am.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I say you are not.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Urge me no more, I shall forget myself;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Have mind upon your health, tempt me no further.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Away, slight man!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Ist possible?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Hear me, for I will speak.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Must I give way and room to your rash choler?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Shall I be frighted when a madman stares?

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: O ye gods, ye gods! must I endure all this?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: All this! ay, more: fret till your proud heart break;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Go show your slaves how choleric you are,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And make your bondmen tremble. Must I budge?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Must I observe you? must I stand and crouch

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Under your testy humour? By the gods

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: You shall digest the venom of your spleen,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Though it do split you; for, from this day forth,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Ill use you for my mirth, yea, for my laughter,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: When you are waspish.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Is it come to this?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: You say you are a better soldier:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Let it appear so; make your vaunting true,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And it shall please me well: for mine own part,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I shall be glad to learn of noble men.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: You wrong me every way; you wrong me, Brutus;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I said, an elder soldier, not a better:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Did I say better?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: If you did, I care not.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: When Caesar lived, he durst not thus have moved me.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Peace, peace! you durst not so have tempted him.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I durst not!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: No.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: What, durst not tempt him!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: For your life you durst not!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Do not presume too much upon my love;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I may do that I shall be sorry for.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: You have done that you should be sorry for.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: There is no terror, Cassius, in your threats,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: For I am armd so strong in honesty

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: That they pass by me as the idle wind,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Which I respect not. I did send to you

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: For certain sums of gold, which you denied me:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: For I can raise no money by vile means:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: By heaven, I had rather coin my heart,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And drop my blood for drachmas, than to wring

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: From the hard hands of peasants their vile trash

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: By any indirection: I did send

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: To you for gold to pay my legions,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Which you denied me: was that done like Cassius?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Should I have answerd Caius Cassius so?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: When Marcus Brutus grows so covetous,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: To lock such rascal counters from his friends,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Be ready, gods, with all your thunderbolts;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Dash him to pieces!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I denied you not.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: You did.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I did not: he was but a fool that brought

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: My answer back. Brutus hath rived my heart:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: A friend should bear his friends infirmities,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: But Brutus makes mine greater than they are.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I do not, till you practise them on me.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: You love me not.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I do not like your faults.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: A friendly eye could never see such faults.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: A flatterers would not, though they do appear

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: As huge as high Olympus.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Come, Antony, and young Octavius, come,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Revenge yourselves alone on Cassius,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: For Cassius is aweary of the world;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Hated by one he loves; braved by his brother;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Chequed like a bondman; all his faults observed,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Set in a note-book, learnd, and connd by rote,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: To cast into my teeth. O, I could weep

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: My spirit from mine eyes! There is my dagger,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And here my naked breast; within, a heart

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Dearer than Plutus mine, richer than gold:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: If that thou best a Roman, take it forth;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I, that denied thee gold, will give my heart:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Strike, as thou didst at Caesar; for, I know,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: When thou didst hate him worst, thou lovedst him better

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Than ever thou lovedst Cassius.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Sheathe your dagger:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Be angry when you will, it shall have scope;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Do what you will, dishonour shall be humour.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: O Cassius, you are yoked with a lamb

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: That carries anger as the flint bears fire;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Who, much enforced, shows a hasty spark,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And straight is cold again.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Hath Cassius lived

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: To be but mirth and laughter to his Brutus,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: When grief, and blood ill-temperd, vexeth him?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: When I spoke that, I was ill-temperd too.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Do you confess so much? Give me your hand.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And my heart too.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: O Brutus!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Whats the matter?

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Have not you love enough to bear with me,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: When that rash humour which my mother gave me

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Makes me forgetful?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Yes, Cassius; and, from henceforth,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: When you are over-earnest with your Brutus,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Hell think your mother chides, and leave you so.

speaker: Poet
text_entry: [Within]  Let me go in to see the generals;

speaker: Poet
text_entry: There is some grudge between em, tis not meet

speaker: Poet
text_entry: They be alone.

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: [Within]  You shall not come to them.

speaker: Poet
text_entry: [Within]  Nothing but death shall stay me.

speaker: Poet
text_entry: Enter Poet, followed by LUCILIUS, TITINIUS, and LUCIUS

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: How now! whats the matter?

speaker: Poet
text_entry: For shame, you generals! what do you mean?

speaker: Poet
text_entry: Love, and be friends, as two such men should be;

speaker: Poet
text_entry: For I have seen more years, Im sure, than ye.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Ha, ha! how vilely doth this cynic rhyme!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Get you hence, sirrah; saucy fellow, hence!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Bear with him, Brutus; tis his fashion.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Ill know his humour, when he knows his time:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: What should the wars do with these jigging fools?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Companion, hence!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Away, away, be gone.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Exit Poet

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Lucilius and Titinius, bid the commanders

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Prepare to lodge their companies to-night.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And come yourselves, and bring Messala with you

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Immediately to us.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Exeunt LUCILIUS and TITINIUS

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Lucius, a bowl of wine!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Exit LUCIUS

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I did not think you could have been so angry.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: O Cassius, I am sick of many griefs.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Of your philosophy you make no use,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: If you give place to accidental evils.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: No man bears sorrow better. Portia is dead.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Ha! Portia!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: She is dead.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: How scaped I killing when I crossd you so?

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: O insupportable and touching loss!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Upon what sickness?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Impatient of my absence,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And grief that young Octavius with Mark Antony

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Have made themselves so strong:--for with her death

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: That tidings came;--with this she fell distract,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And, her attendants absent, swallowd fire.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And died so?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Even so.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: O ye immortal gods!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Re-enter LUCIUS, with wine and taper

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Speak no more of her. Give me a bowl of wine.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: In this I bury all unkindness, Cassius.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: My heart is thirsty for that noble pledge.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Fill, Lucius, till the wine oerswell the cup;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I cannot drink too much of Brutus love.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Come in, Titinius!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Exit LUCIUS

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Re-enter TITINIUS, with MESSALA

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Welcome, good Messala.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Now sit we close about this taper here,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And call in question our necessities.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Portia, art thou gone?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: No more, I pray you.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Messala, I have here received letters,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: That young Octavius and Mark Antony

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Come down upon us with a mighty power,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Bending their expedition toward Philippi.

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Myself have letters of the selfsame tenor.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: With what addition?

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: That by proscription and bills of outlawry,

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Octavius, Antony, and Lepidus,

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Have put to death an hundred senators.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Therein our letters do not well agree;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Mine speak of seventy senators that died

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: By their proscriptions, Cicero being one.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Cicero one!

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Cicero is dead,

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: And by that order of proscription.

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Had you your letters from your wife, my lord?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: No, Messala.

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Nor nothing in your letters writ of her?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Nothing, Messala.

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: That, methinks, is strange.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Why ask you? hear you aught of her in yours?

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: No, my lord.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Now, as you are a Roman, tell me true.

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Then like a Roman bear the truth I tell:

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: For certain she is dead, and by strange manner.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Why, farewell, Portia. We must die, Messala:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: With meditating that she must die once,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I have the patience to endure it now.

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Even so great men great losses should endure.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I have as much of this in art as you,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: But yet my nature could not bear it so.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Well, to our work alive. What do you think

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Of marching to Philippi presently?

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I do not think it good.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Your reason?

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: This it is:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Tis better that the enemy seek us:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: So shall he waste his means, weary his soldiers,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Doing himself offence; whilst we, lying still,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Are full of rest, defense, and nimbleness.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Good reasons must, of force, give place to better.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: The people twixt Philippi and this ground

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Do stand but in a forced affection;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: For they have grudged us contribution:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: The enemy, marching along by them,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: By them shall make a fuller number up,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Come on refreshd, new-added, and encouraged;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: From which advantage shall we cut him off,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: If at Philippi we do face him there,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: These people at our back.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Hear me, good brother.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Under your pardon. You must note beside,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: That we have tried the utmost of our friends,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Our legions are brim-full, our cause is ripe:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: The enemy increaseth every day;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: We, at the height, are ready to decline.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: There is a tide in the affairs of men,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Which, taken at the flood, leads on to fortune;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Omitted, all the voyage of their life

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Is bound in shallows and in miseries.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: On such a full sea are we now afloat;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And we must take the current when it serves,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Or lose our ventures.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Then, with your will, go on;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Well along ourselves, and meet them at Philippi.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: The deep of night is crept upon our talk,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And nature must obey necessity;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Which we will niggard with a little rest.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: There is no more to say?

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: No more. Good night:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Early to-morrow will we rise, and hence.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Lucius!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Enter LUCIUS

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: My gown.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Exit LUCIUS

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Farewell, good Messala:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Good night, Titinius. Noble, noble Cassius,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Good night, and good repose.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: O my dear brother!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: This was an ill beginning of the night:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Never come such division tween our souls!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Let it not, Brutus.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Every thing is well.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Good night, my lord.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Good night, good brother.

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Good night, Lord Brutus.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Farewell, every one.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Exeunt all but BRUTUS

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Re-enter LUCIUS, with the gown

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Give me the gown. Where is thy instrument?

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Here in the tent.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: What, thou speakst drowsily?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Poor knave, I blame thee not; thou art oer-watchd.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Call Claudius and some other of my men:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Ill have them sleep on cushions in my tent.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Varro and Claudius!

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Enter VARRO and CLAUDIUS

speaker: VARRO
text_entry: Calls my lord?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I pray you, sirs, lie in my tent and sleep;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: It may be I shall raise you by and by

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: On business to my brother Cassius.

speaker: VARRO
text_entry: So please you, we will stand and watch your pleasure.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I will not have it so: lie down, good sirs;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: It may be I shall otherwise bethink me.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Look, Lucius, heres the book I sought for so;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I put it in the pocket of my gown.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: VARRO and CLAUDIUS lie down

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: I was sure your lordship did not give it me.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Bear with me, good boy, I am much forgetful.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Canst thou hold up thy heavy eyes awhile,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And touch thy instrument a strain or two?

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Ay, my lord, ant please you.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: It does, my boy:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I trouble thee too much, but thou art willing.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: It is my duty, sir.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I should not urge thy duty past thy might;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I know young bloods look for a time of rest.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: I have slept, my lord, already.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: It was well done; and thou shalt sleep again;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I will not hold thee long: if I do live,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I will be good to thee.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Music, and a song

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: This is a sleepy tune. O murderous slumber,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Layst thou thy leaden mace upon my boy,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: That plays thee music? Gentle knave, good night;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I will not do thee so much wrong to wake thee:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: If thou dost nod, thou breakst thy instrument;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Ill take it from thee; and, good boy, good night.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Let me see, let me see; is not the leaf turnd down

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Where I left reading? Here it is, I think.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Enter the Ghost of CAESAR

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: How ill this taper burns! Ha! who comes here?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I think it is the weakness of mine eyes

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: That shapes this monstrous apparition.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: It comes upon me. Art thou any thing?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Art thou some god, some angel, or some devil,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: That makest my blood cold and my hair to stare?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Speak to me what thou art.

speaker: GHOST
text_entry: Thy evil spirit, Brutus.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Why comest thou?

speaker: GHOST
text_entry: To tell thee thou shalt see me at Philippi.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Well; then I shall see thee again?

speaker: GHOST
text_entry: Ay, at Philippi.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Why, I will see thee at Philippi, then.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Exit Ghost

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Now I have taken heart thou vanishest:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Ill spirit, I would hold more talk with thee.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Boy, Lucius! Varro! Claudius! Sirs, awake! Claudius!

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: The strings, my lord, are false.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: He thinks he still is at his instrument.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Lucius, awake!

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: My lord?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Didst thou dream, Lucius, that thou so criedst out?

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: My lord, I do not know that I did cry.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Yes, that thou didst: didst thou see any thing?

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Nothing, my lord.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Sleep again, Lucius. Sirrah Claudius!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: To VARRO

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Fellow thou, awake!

speaker: VARRO
text_entry: My lord?

speaker: CLAUDIUS
text_entry: My lord?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Why did you so cry out, sirs, in your sleep?

speaker: CLAUDIUS
text_entry: Did we, my lord?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Ay: saw you any thing?

speaker: VARRO
text_entry: No, my lord, I saw nothing.

speaker: CLAUDIUS
text_entry: Nor I, my lord.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Go and commend me to my brother Cassius;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Bid him set on his powers betimes before,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And we will follow.

speaker: CLAUDIUS
text_entry: It shall be done, my lord.

speaker: CLAUDIUS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: CLAUDIUS
text_entry: ACT V

speaker: CLAUDIUS
text_entry: SCENE I. The plains of Philippi.

speaker: CLAUDIUS
text_entry: Enter OCTAVIUS, ANTONY, and their army

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Now, Antony, our hopes are answered:

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: You said the enemy would not come down,

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: But keep the hills and upper regions;

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: It proves not so: their battles are at hand;

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: They mean to warn us at Philippi here,

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Answering before we do demand of them.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Tut, I am in their bosoms, and I know

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Wherefore they do it: they could be content

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: To visit other places; and come down

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: With fearful bravery, thinking by this face

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: To fasten in our thoughts that they have courage;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: But tis not so.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Enter a Messenger

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Prepare you, generals:

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: The enemy comes on in gallant show;

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Their bloody sign of battle is hung out,

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: And something to be done immediately.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Octavius, lead your battle softly on,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Upon the left hand of the even field.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Upon the right hand I; keep thou the left.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Why do you cross me in this exigent?

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: I do not cross you; but I will do so.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: March

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Drum. Enter BRUTUS, CASSIUS, and their Army; LUCILIUS, TITINIUS, MESSALA, and others

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: They stand, and would have parley.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Stand fast, Titinius: we must out and talk.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Mark Antony, shall we give sign of battle?

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: No, Caesar, we will answer on their charge.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Make forth; the generals would have some words.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Stir not until the signal.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Words before blows: is it so, countrymen?

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Not that we love words better, as you do.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Good words are better than bad strokes, Octavius.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: In your bad strokes, Brutus, you give good words:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Witness the hole you made in Caesars heart,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Crying Long live! hail, Caesar!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Antony,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: The posture of your blows are yet unknown;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: But for your words, they rob the Hybla bees,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And leave them honeyless.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Not stingless too.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: O, yes, and soundless too;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: For you have stoln their buzzing, Antony,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And very wisely threat before you sting.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Villains, you did not so, when your vile daggers

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Hackd one another in the sides of Caesar:

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: You showd your teeth like apes, and fawnd like hounds,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And bowd like bondmen, kissing Caesars feet;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Whilst damned Casca, like a cur, behind

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Struck Caesar on the neck. O you flatterers!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Flatterers! Now, Brutus, thank yourself:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: This tongue had not offended so to-day,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: If Cassius might have ruled.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Come, come, the cause: if arguing make us sweat,

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: The proof of it will turn to redder drops. Look;

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: I draw a sword against conspirators;

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: When think you that the sword goes up again?

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Never, till Caesars three and thirty wounds

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Be well avenged; or till another Caesar

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Have added slaughter to the sword of traitors.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Caesar, thou canst not die by traitors hands,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Unless thou bringst them with thee.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: So I hope;

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: I was not born to die on Brutus sword.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: O, if thou wert the noblest of thy strain,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Young man, thou couldst not die more honourable.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: A peevish schoolboy, worthless of such honour,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Joind with a masker and a reveller!

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Old Cassius still!

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Come, Antony, away!

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Defiance, traitors, hurl we in your teeth:

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: If you dare fight to-day, come to the field;

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: If not, when you have stomachs.

speaker: OCTAVIUS
text_entry: Exeunt OCTAVIUS, ANTONY, and their army

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Why, now, blow wind, swell billow and swim bark!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: The storm is up, and all is on the hazard.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Ho, Lucilius! hark, a word with you.

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: [Standing forth]My lord?

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: BRUTUS and LUCILIUS converse apart

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Messala!

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: [Standing forth]  What says my general?

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Messala,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: This is my birth-day; as this very day

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Was Cassius born. Give me thy hand, Messala:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Be thou my witness that against my will,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: As Pompey was, am I compelld to set

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Upon one battle all our liberties.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: You know that I held Epicurus strong

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And his opinion: now I change my mind,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And partly credit things that do presage.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Coming from Sardis, on our former ensign

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Two mighty eagles fell, and there they perchd,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Gorging and feeding from our soldiers hands;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Who to Philippi here consorted us:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: This morning are they fled away and gone;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And in their steads do ravens, crows and kites,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Fly oer our heads and downward look on us,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: As we were sickly prey: their shadows seem

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: A canopy most fatal, under which

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Our army lies, ready to give up the ghost.

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Believe not so.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I but believe it partly;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: For I am fresh of spirit and resolved

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: To meet all perils very constantly.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Even so, Lucilius.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Now, most noble Brutus,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: The gods to-day stand friendly, that we may,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Lovers in peace, lead on our days to age!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: But since the affairs of men rest still incertain,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Lets reason with the worst that may befall.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: If we do lose this battle, then is this

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: The very last time we shall speak together:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: What are you then determined to do?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Even by the rule of that philosophy

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: By which I did blame Cato for the death

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Which he did give himself, I know not how,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: But I do find it cowardly and vile,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: For fear of what might fall, so to prevent

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: The time of life: arming myself with patience

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: To stay the providence of some high powers

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: That govern us below.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Then, if we lose this battle,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: You are contented to be led in triumph

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Thorough the streets of Rome?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: No, Cassius, no: think not, thou noble Roman,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: That ever Brutus will go bound to Rome;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: He bears too great a mind. But this same day

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Must end that work the ides of March begun;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And whether we shall meet again I know not.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Therefore our everlasting farewell take:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: For ever, and for ever, farewell, Cassius!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: If we do meet again, why, we shall smile;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: If not, why then, this parting was well made.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: For ever, and for ever, farewell, Brutus!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: If we do meet again, well smile indeed;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: If not, tis true this parting was well made.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Why, then, lead on. O, that a man might know

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: The end of this days business ere it come!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: But it sufficeth that the day will end,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And then the end is known. Come, ho! away!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: SCENE II. The same. The field of battle.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Alarum. Enter BRUTUS and MESSALA

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Ride, ride, Messala, ride, and give these bills

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Unto the legions on the other side.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Loud alarum

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Let them set on at once; for I perceive

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: But cold demeanor in Octavius wing,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And sudden push gives them the overthrow.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Ride, ride, Messala: let them all come down.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: SCENE III. Another part of the field.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Alarums. Enter CASSIUS and TITINIUS

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: O, look, Titinius, look, the villains fly!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Myself have to mine own turnd enemy:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: This ensign here of mine was turning back;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: I slew the coward, and did take it from him.

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: O Cassius, Brutus gave the word too early;

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Who, having some advantage on Octavius,

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Took it too eagerly: his soldiers fell to spoil,

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Whilst we by Antony are all enclosed.

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Enter PINDARUS

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Fly further off, my lord, fly further off;

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Mark Antony is in your tents, my lord

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Fly, therefore, noble Cassius, fly far off.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: This hill is far enough. Look, look, Titinius;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Are those my tents where I perceive the fire?

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: They are, my lord.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Titinius, if thou lovest me,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Mount thou my horse, and hide thy spurs in him,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Till he have brought thee up to yonder troops,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And here again; that I may rest assured

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Whether yond troops are friend or enemy.

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: I will be here again, even with a thought.

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Go, Pindarus, get higher on that hill;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: My sight was ever thick; regard Titinius,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And tell me what thou notest about the field.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: PINDARUS ascends the hill

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: This day I breathed first: time is come round,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And where I did begin, there shall I end;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: My life is run his compass. Sirrah, what news?

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: [Above]  O my lord!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: What news?

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: [Above]  Titinius is enclosed round about

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: With horsemen, that make to him on the spur;

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Yet he spurs on. Now they are almost on him.

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Now, Titinius! Now some light. O, he lights too.

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Hes taen.

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Shout

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: And, hark! they shout for joy.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Come down, behold no more.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: O, coward that I am, to live so long,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: To see my best friend taen before my face!

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: PINDARUS descends

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Come hither, sirrah:

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: In Parthia did I take thee prisoner;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And then I swore thee, saving of thy life,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: That whatsoever I did bid thee do,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Thou shouldst attempt it. Come now, keep thine oath;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Now be a freeman: and with this good sword,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: That ran through Caesars bowels, search this bosom.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Stand not to answer: here, take thou the hilts;

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: And, when my face is coverd, as tis now,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Guide thou the sword.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: PINDARUS stabs him

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Caesar, thou art revenged,

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Even with the sword that killd thee.

speaker: CASSIUS
text_entry: Dies

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: So, I am free; yet would not so have been,

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Durst I have done my will. O Cassius,

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Far from this country Pindarus shall run,

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Where never Roman shall take note of him.

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: PINDARUS
text_entry: Re-enter TITINIUS with MESSALA

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: It is but change, Titinius; for Octavius

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Is overthrown by noble Brutus power,

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: As Cassius legions are by Antony.

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: These tidings will well comfort Cassius.

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Where did you leave him?

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: All disconsolate,

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: With Pindarus his bondman, on this hill.

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Is not that he t hat lies upon the ground?

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: He lies not like the living. O my heart!

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Is not that he?

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: No, this was he, Messala,

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: But Cassius is no more. O setting sun,

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: As in thy red rays thou dost sink to-night,

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: So in his red blood Cassius day is set;

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: The sun of Rome is set! Our day is gone;

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Clouds, dews, and dangers come; our deeds are done!

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Mistrust of my success hath done this deed.

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Mistrust of good success hath done this deed.

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: O hateful error, melancholys child,

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Why dost thou show to the apt thoughts of men

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: The things that are not? O error, soon conceived,

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Thou never comest unto a happy birth,

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: But killst the mother that engenderd thee!

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: What, Pindarus! where art thou, Pindarus?

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Seek him, Titinius, whilst I go to meet

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: The noble Brutus, thrusting this report

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Into his ears; I may say, thrusting it;

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: For piercing steel and darts envenomed

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Shall be as welcome to the ears of Brutus

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: As tidings of this sight.

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Hie you, Messala,

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: And I will seek for Pindarus the while.

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Exit MESSALA

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Why didst thou send me forth, brave Cassius?

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Did I not meet thy friends? and did not they

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Put on my brows this wreath of victory,

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: And bid me give it thee? Didst thou not hear their shouts?

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Alas, thou hast misconstrued every thing!

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: But, hold thee, take this garland on thy brow;

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Thy Brutus bid me give it thee, and I

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Will do his bidding. Brutus, come apace,

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: And see how I regarded Caius Cassius.

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: By your leave, gods:--this is a Romans part

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Come, Cassius sword, and find Titinius heart.

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Kills himself

speaker: TITINIUS
text_entry: Alarum. Re-enter MESSALA, with BRUTUS, CATO, STRATO, VOLUMNIUS, and LUCILIUS

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Where, where, Messala, doth his body lie?

speaker: MESSALA
text_entry: Lo, yonder, and Titinius mourning it.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Titinius face is upward.

speaker: CATO
text_entry: He is slain.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: O Julius Caesar, thou art mighty yet!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Thy spirit walks abroad and turns our swords

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: In our own proper entrails.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Low alarums

speaker: CATO
text_entry: Brave Titinius!

speaker: CATO
text_entry: Look, whether he have not crownd dead Cassius!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Are yet two Romans living such as these?

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: The last of all the Romans, fare thee well!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: It is impossible that ever Rome

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Should breed thy fellow. Friends, I owe more tears

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: To this dead man than you shall see me pay.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: I shall find time, Cassius, I shall find time.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Come, therefore, and to Thasos send his body:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: His funerals shall not be in our camp,

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Lest it discomfort us. Lucilius, come;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And come, young Cato; let us to the field.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Labeo and Flavius, set our battles on:

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Tis three oclock; and, Romans, yet ere night

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: We shall try fortune in a second fight.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: SCENE IV. Another part of the field.

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Alarum. Enter fighting, Soldiers of both armies; then BRUTUS, CATO, LUCILIUS, and others

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Yet, countrymen, O, yet hold up your heads!

speaker: CATO
text_entry: What bastard doth not? Who will go with me?

speaker: CATO
text_entry: I will proclaim my name about the field:

speaker: CATO
text_entry: I am the son of Marcus Cato, ho!

speaker: CATO
text_entry: A foe to tyrants, and my countrys friend;

speaker: CATO
text_entry: I am the son of Marcus Cato, ho!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: And I am Brutus, Marcus Brutus, I;

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Brutus, my countrys friend; know me for Brutus!

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: O young and noble Cato, art thou down?

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: Why, now thou diest as bravely as Titinius;

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: And mayst be honourd, being Catos son.

speaker: First Soldier
text_entry: Yield, or thou diest.

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: Only I yield to die:

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: There is so much that thou wilt kill me straight;

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: Offering money

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: Kill Brutus, and be honourd in his death.

speaker: First Soldier
text_entry: We must not. A noble prisoner!

speaker: Second Soldier
text_entry: Room, ho! Tell Antony, Brutus is taen.

speaker: First Soldier
text_entry: Ill tell the news. Here comes the general.

speaker: First Soldier
text_entry: Enter ANTONY

speaker: First Soldier
text_entry: Brutus is taen, Brutus is taen, my lord.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Where is he?

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: Safe, Antony; Brutus is safe enough:

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: I dare assure thee that no enemy

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: Shall ever take alive the noble Brutus:

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: The gods defend him from so great a shame!

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: When you do find him, or alive or dead,

speaker: LUCILIUS
text_entry: He will be found like Brutus, like himself.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: This is not Brutus, friend; but, I assure you,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: A prize no less in worth: keep this man safe;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Give him all kindness: I had rather have

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Such men my friends than enemies. Go on,

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And see whether Brutus be alive or dead;

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: And bring us word unto Octavius tent

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: How every thing is chanced.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: SCENE V. Another part of the field.

speaker: ANTONY
text_entry: Enter BRUTUS, DARDANIUS, CLITUS, STRATO, and VOLUMNIUS

speaker: BRUTUS
text_entry: Come, poor remains of friends, rest on this rock.

speaker: CLITUS
text_entry: Statilius showd the torch-light, but, my lord,

speaker: CLITUS

text_entry: That his own hand may strike his honour down

text_entry: If you are armd to do as sworn to do,

text_entry: Fat paunches have lean pates, and dainty bits

text_entry: The grosser manner of these worlds delights

speaker: DUMAIN

text_entry: I can but say their protestation over;

text_entry: And not be seen to wink of all the day--

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Which I hope well is not enrolled there:

text_entry: To know the thing I am forbid to know:

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: When I to feast expressly am forbid;

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Or study where to meet some mistress fine,

speaker: BIRON

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Or, having sworn too hard a keeping oath,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Study to break it and not break my troth.

text_entry: If studys gain be thus and this be so,

text_entry: By fixing it upon a fairer eye,

text_entry: Die when you will, a smock shall be your shroud.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: You leer upon me, do you? theres an eye

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Wounds like a leaden sword.

speaker: BOYET
text_entry: Full merrily

speaker: BOYET
text_entry: Hath this brave manage, this career, been run.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Lo, he is tilting straight! Peace! I have done.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Enter COSTARD

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Welcome, pure wit! thou partest a fair fray.

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: O Lord, sir, they would know

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: Whether the three Worthies shall come in or no.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: What, are there but three?

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: No, sir; but it is vara fine,

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: For every one pursents three.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: And three times thrice is nine.

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: Not so, sir; under correction, sir; I hope it is not so.

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: You cannot beg us, sir, I can assure you, sir we know

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: what we know:

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: I hope, sir, three times thrice, sir,--

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Is not nine.

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: Under correction, sir, we know whereuntil it doth amount.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: By Jove, I always took three threes for nine.

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: O Lord, sir, it were pity you should get your living

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: by reckoning, sir.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: How much is it?

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: O Lord, sir, the parties themselves, the actors,

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: sir, will show whereuntil it doth amount: for mine

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: own part, I am, as they say, but to parfect one man

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: in one poor man, Pompion the Great, sir.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Art thou one of the Worthies?

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: It pleased them to think me worthy of Pompion the

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: Great: for mine own part, I know not the degree of

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: the Worthy, but I am to stand for him.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Go, bid them prepare.

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: We will turn it finely off, sir; we will take

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: some care.

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: Exit

speaker: FERDINAND
text_entry: Biron, they will shame us: let them not approach.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: We are shame-proof, my lord: and tis some policy

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: To have one show worse than the kings and his company.

speaker: FERDINAND
text_entry: I say they shall not come.

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: Nay, my good lord, let me oerrule you now:

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: That sport best pleases that doth least know how:

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: Where zeal strives to content, and the contents

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: Dies in the zeal of that which it presents:

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: Their form confounded makes most form in mirth,

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: When great things labouring perish in their birth.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: A right description of our sport, my lord.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Enter DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: DON

speaker: BIRON

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: He speaks not like a man of Gods making.

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: DON

speaker: ADRIANO DE ARMADO
text_entry: That is all one, my fair, sweet, honey monarch; for,

speaker: ADRIANO DE ARMADO
text_entry: I protest, the schoolmaster is exceeding

speaker: ADRIANO DE ARMADO
text_entry: fantastical; too, too vain, too too vain: but we

speaker: ADRIANO DE ARMADO
text_entry: will put it, as they say, to fortuna de la guerra.

speaker: ADRIANO DE ARMADO
text_entry: I wish you the peace of mind, most royal couplement!

speaker: ADRIANO DE ARMADO

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: There is five in the first show.

speaker: FERDINAND
text_entry: You are deceived; tis not so.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: The pedant, the braggart, the hedge-priest, the fool

speaker: BIRON

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Abate throw at novum, and the whole world again

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Cannot pick out five such, take each one in his vein.

speaker: FERDINAND

text_entry: with thee.

text_entry: Pompey surnamed the Great;

text_entry: my foe to sweat:

text_entry: My hat to a halfpenny, Pompey proves the best Worthy.

speaker: SIR NATHANIEL
text_entry: When in the world I lived, I was the worlds

speaker: SIR NATHANIEL
text_entry: commander,--

text_entry: Pompey the Great,--

text_entry: the painted cloth for this: your lion, that holds

text_entry: to Ajax: he will be the ninth Worthy. A conqueror,

speaker: COSTARD

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: There, ant shall please you; a foolish mild man; an

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: honest man, look you, and soon dashed. He is a

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: marvellous good neighbour, faith, and a very good

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: bowler: but, for Alisander,--alas, you see how

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: tis,--a little oerparted. But there are Worthies

speaker: COSTARD

speaker: COSTARD
text_entry: Enter HOLOFERNES, for Judas; and MOTH, for Hercules

speaker: HOLOFERNES

speaker: HOLOFERNES

speaker: HOLOFERNES

text_entry: Judas I am,--

text_entry: What mean you, sir?

text_entry: To make Judas hang himself.

speaker: HOLOFERNES

speaker: BIRON

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text_entry: I will not be put out of countenance.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Because thou hast no face.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text_entry: What is this?

speaker: BOYET
text_entry: A cittern-head.

speaker: DUMAIN
text_entry: The head of a bodkin.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: A Deaths face in a ring.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text_entry: The face of an old Roman coin, scarce seen.

speaker: BOYET
text_entry: The pommel of Caesars falchion.

speaker: DUMAIN
text_entry: The carved-bone face on a flask.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Saint Georges half-cheek in a brooch.

speaker: DUMAIN
text_entry: Ay, and in a brooch of lead.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Ay, and worn in the cap of a tooth-drawer.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: And now forward; for we have put thee in countenance.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text_entry: You have put me out of countenance.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: False; we have given thee faces.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text_entry: But you have out-faced them all.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: An thou wert a lion, we would do so.

speaker: BOYET
text_entry: Therefore, as he is an ass, let him go.

speaker: BOYET
text_entry: And so adieu, sweet Jude! nay, why dost thou stay?

speaker: DUMAIN

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: For the ass to the Jude; give it him:--Jud-as, away!

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text_entry: This is not generous, not gentle, not humble.

speaker: BOYET

speaker: BOYET
text_entry: HOLOFERNES retires

speaker: PRINCESS

speaker: PRINCESS

text_entry: DON

text_entry: DON

speaker: ADRIANO DE ARMADO

text_entry: wench is cast away: shes quick; the child brags in

text_entry: DON

text_entry: Ill slash; Ill do it by the sword. I bepray you,

text_entry: DON

text_entry: seen the day of wrong through the little hole of

text_entry: Madam, not so; I do beseech you, stay.

text_entry: Prepare, I say. I thank you, gracious lords,

text_entry: For all your fair endeavors; and entreat,

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: Out of a new-sad soul, that you vouchsafe

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: In your rich wisdom to excuse or hide

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: The liberal opposition of our spirits,

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: If over-boldly we have borne ourselves

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: In the converse of breath: your gentleness

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: Was guilty of it. Farewell worthy lord!

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: A heavy heart bears not a nimble tongue:

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: Excuse me so, coming too short of thanks

text_entry: The extreme parts of time extremely forms

text_entry: All causes to the purpose of his speed,

text_entry: And often at his very loose decides

text_entry: And though the mourning brow of progeny

text_entry: Forbid the smiling courtesy of love

speaker: FERDINAND
text_entry: The holy suit which fain it would convince,

text_entry: Yet, since loves argument was first on foot,

speaker: FERDINAND
text_entry: Let not the cloud of sorrow justle it

text_entry: From what it purposed; since, to wail friends lost

speaker: FERDINAND
text_entry: Is not by much so wholesome-profitable

speaker: FERDINAND
text_entry: As to rejoice at friends but newly found.

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: I understand you not: my griefs are double.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Honest plain words best pierce the ear of grief;

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: And by these badges understand the king.

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: For your fair sakes have we neglected time,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Playd foul play with our oaths: your beauty, ladies,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Hath much deformd us, fashioning our humours

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Even to the opposed end of our intents:

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: And what in us hath seemd ridiculous,--

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: As love is full of unbefitting strains,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: All wanton as a child, skipping and vain,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Formd by the eye and therefore, like the eye,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Full of strange shapes, of habits and of forms,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Varying in subjects as the eye doth roll

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: To every varied object in his glance:

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Which parti-coated presence of loose love

text_entry: Put on by us, if, in your heavenly eyes,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Have misbecomed our oaths and gravities,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Those heavenly eyes, that look into these faults,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Suggested us to make. Therefore, ladies,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Our love being yours, the error that love makes

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Is likewise yours: we to ourselves prove false,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: By being once false for ever to be true

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: To those that make us both,--fair ladies, you:

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: And even that falsehood, in itself a sin,

speaker: BIRON
text_entry: Thus purifies itself and turns to grace.

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: We have received your letters full of love;

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: Your favours, the ambassadors of love;

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: And, in our maiden council, rated them

speaker: PRINCESS
text_entry: At courtship, pleasant jest and courtesy,

speaker: PRINCESS
