text_entry: We trifle time: I pray thee, pursue sentence.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: A pound of that same merchants flesh is thine:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: The court awards it, and the law doth give it.

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: Most rightful judge!

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And you must cut this flesh from off his breast:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: The law allows it, and the court awards it.

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: Most learned judge! A sentence! Come, prepare!

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Tarry a little; there is something else.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: This bond doth give thee here no jot of blood;

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: The words expressly are a pound of flesh:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Take then thy bond, take thou thy pound of flesh;

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: But, in the cutting it, if thou dost shed

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: One drop of Christian blood, thy lands and goods

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Are, by the laws of Venice, confiscate

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Unto the state of Venice.

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: O upright judge! Mark, Jew: O learned judge!

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: Is that the law?

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Thyself shalt see the act:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: For, as thou urgest justice, be assured

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Thou shalt have justice, more than thou desirest.

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: O learned judge! Mark, Jew: a learned judge!

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: I take this offer, then; pay the bond thrice

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: And let the Christian go.

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Here is the money.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Soft!

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: The Jew shall have all justice; soft! no haste:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: He shall have nothing but the penalty.

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: O Jew! an upright judge, a learned judge!

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Therefore prepare thee to cut off the flesh.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Shed thou no blood, nor cut thou less nor more

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: But just a pound of flesh: if thou cutst more

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Or less than a just pound, be it but so much

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: As makes it light or heavy in the substance,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Or the division of the twentieth part

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Of one poor scruple, nay, if the scale do turn

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: But in the estimation of a hair,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Thou diest and all thy goods are confiscate.

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: A second Daniel, a Daniel, Jew!

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: Now, infidel, I have you on the hip.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Why doth the Jew pause? take thy forfeiture.

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: Give me my principal, and let me go.

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: I have it ready for thee; here it is.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: He hath refused it in the open court:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: He shall have merely justice and his bond.

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: A Daniel, still say I, a second Daniel!

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: I thank thee, Jew, for teaching me that word.

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: Shall I not have barely my principal?

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Thou shalt have nothing but the forfeiture,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: To be so taken at thy peril, Jew.

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: Why, then the devil give him good of it!

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: Ill stay no longer question.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Tarry, Jew:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: The law hath yet another hold on you.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: It is enacted in the laws of Venice,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: If it be proved against an alien

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: That by direct or indirect attempts

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: He seek the life of any citizen,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: The party gainst the which he doth contrive

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Shall seize one half his goods; the other half

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Comes to the privy coffer of the state;

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And the offenders life lies in the mercy

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Of the duke only, gainst all other voice.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: In which predicament, I say, thou standst;

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: For it appears, by manifest proceeding,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: That indirectly and directly too

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Thou hast contrived against the very life

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Of the defendant; and thou hast incurrd

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: The danger formerly by me rehearsed.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Down therefore and beg mercy of the duke.

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: Beg that thou mayst have leave to hang thyself:

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: And yet, thy wealth being forfeit to the state,

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: Thou hast not left the value of a cord;

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: Therefore thou must be hangd at the states charge.

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: That thou shalt see the difference of our spirits,

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: I pardon thee thy life before thou ask it:

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: For half thy wealth, it is Antonios;

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: The other half comes to the general state,

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: Which humbleness may drive unto a fine.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Ay, for the state, not for Antonio.

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: Nay, take my life and all; pardon not that:

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: You take my house when you do take the prop

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: That doth sustain my house; you take my life

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: When you do take the means whereby I live.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: What mercy can you render him, Antonio?

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: A halter gratis; nothing else, for Gods sake.

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: So please my lord the duke and all the court

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: To quit the fine for one half of his goods,

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: I am content; so he will let me have

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: The other half in use, to render it,

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: Upon his death, unto the gentleman

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: That lately stole his daughter:

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: Two things provided more, that, for this favour,

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: He presently become a Christian;

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: The other, that he do record a gift,

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: Here in the court, of all he dies possessd,

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: Unto his son Lorenzo and his daughter.

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: He shall do this, or else I do recant

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: The pardon that I late pronounced here.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Art thou contented, Jew? what dost thou say?

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: I am content.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Clerk, draw a deed of gift.

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: I pray you, give me leave to go from hence;

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: I am not well: send the deed after me,

speaker: SHYLOCK
text_entry: And I will sign it.

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: Get thee gone, but do it.

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: In christening shalt thou have two god-fathers:

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: Had I been judge, thou shouldst have had ten more,

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: To bring thee to the gallows, not the font.

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: Exit SHYLOCK

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: Sir, I entreat you home with me to dinner.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: I humbly do desire your grace of pardon:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: I must away this night toward Padua,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And it is meet I presently set forth.

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: I am sorry that your leisure serves you not.

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: Antonio, gratify this gentleman,

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: For, in my mind, you are much bound to him.

speaker: DUKE
text_entry: Exeunt Duke and his train

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Most worthy gentleman, I and my friend

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Have by your wisdom been this day acquitted

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Of grievous penalties; in lieu whereof,

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Three thousand ducats, due unto the Jew,

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: We freely cope your courteous pains withal.

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: And stand indebted, over and above,

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: In love and service to you evermore.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: He is well paid that is well satisfied;

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And I, delivering you, am satisfied

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And therein do account myself well paid:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: My mind was never yet more mercenary.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: I pray you, know me when we meet again:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: I wish you well, and so I take my leave.

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Dear sir, of force I must attempt you further:

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Take some remembrance of us, as a tribute,

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Not as a fee: grant me two things, I pray you,

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Not to deny me, and to pardon me.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: You press me far, and therefore I will yield.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: To ANTONIO

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Give me your gloves, Ill wear them for your sake;

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: To BASSANIO

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And, for your love, Ill take this ring from you:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Do not draw back your hand; Ill take no more;

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And you in love shall not deny me this.

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: This ring, good sir, alas, it is a trifle!

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: I will not shame myself to give you this.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: I will have nothing else but only this;

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And now methinks I have a mind to it.

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Theres more depends on this than on the value.

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: The dearest ring in Venice will I give you,

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: And find it out by proclamation:

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Only for this, I pray you, pardon me.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: I see, sir, you are liberal in offers

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: You taught me first to beg; and now methinks

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: You teach me how a beggar should be answerd.

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Good sir, this ring was given me by my wife;

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: And when she put it on, she made me vow

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: That I should neither sell nor give nor lose it.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: That scuse serves many men to save their gifts.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: An if your wife be not a mad-woman,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And know how well I have deserved the ring,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: She would not hold out enemy for ever,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: For giving it to me. Well, peace be with you!

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Exeunt Portia and Nerissa

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: My Lord Bassanio, let him have the ring:

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: Let his deservings and my love withal

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: Be valued against your wifes commandment.

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Go, Gratiano, run and overtake him;

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Give him the ring, and bring him, if thou canst,

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Unto Antonios house: away! make haste.

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Exit Gratiano

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Come, you and I will thither presently;

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: And in the morning early will we both

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Fly toward Belmont: come, Antonio.

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: SCENE II. The same. A street.

speaker: BASSANIO
text_entry: Enter PORTIA and NERISSA

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Inquire the Jews house out, give him this deed

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And let him sign it: well away to-night

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And be a day before our husbands home:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: This deed will be well welcome to Lorenzo.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Enter GRATIANO

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: Fair sir, you are well oertaen

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: My Lord Bassanio upon more advice

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: Hath sent you here this ring, and doth entreat

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: Your company at dinner.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: That cannot be:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: His ring I do accept most thankfully:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And so, I pray you, tell him: furthermore,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: I pray you, show my youth old Shylocks house.

speaker: GRATIANO
text_entry: That will I do.

speaker: NERISSA
text_entry: Sir, I would speak with you.

speaker: NERISSA
text_entry: Aside to PORTIA

speaker: NERISSA
text_entry: Ill see if I can get my husbands ring,

speaker: NERISSA
text_entry: Which I did make him swear to keep for ever.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: [Aside to NERISSA]  Thou mayst, I warrant.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: We shall have old swearing

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: That they did give the rings away to men;

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: But well outface them, and outswear them too.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Aloud

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Away! make haste: thou knowist where I will tarry.

speaker: NERISSA
text_entry: Come, good sir, will you show me to this house?

speaker: NERISSA
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: NERISSA
text_entry: ACT V

speaker: NERISSA
text_entry: SCENE I. Belmont. Avenue to PORTIAS house.

speaker: NERISSA
text_entry: Enter LORENZO and JESSICA

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: The moon shines bright: in such a night as this,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: When the sweet wind did gently kiss the trees

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: And they did make no noise, in such a night

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Troilus methinks mounted the Troyan walls

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: And sighd his soul toward the Grecian tents,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Where Cressid lay that night.

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: In such a night

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: Did Thisbe fearfully oertrip the dew

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: And saw the lions shadow ere himself

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: And ran dismayd away.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: In such a night

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Stood Dido with a willow in her hand

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Upon the wild sea banks and waft her love

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: To come again to Carthage.

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: In such a night

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: Medea gatherd the enchanted herbs

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: That did renew old AEson.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: In such a night

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Did Jessica steal from the wealthy Jew

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: And with an unthrift love did run from Venice

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: As far as Belmont.

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: In such a night

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: Did young Lorenzo swear he loved her well,

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: Stealing her soul with many vows of faith

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: And neer a true one.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: In such a night

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Did pretty Jessica, like a little shrew,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Slander her love, and he forgave it her.

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: I would out-night you, did no body come;

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: But, hark, I hear the footing of a man.

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: Enter STEPHANO

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Who comes so fast in silence of the night?

speaker: STEPHANO
text_entry: A friend.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: A friend! what friend? your name, I pray you, friend?

speaker: STEPHANO
text_entry: Stephano is my name; and I bring word

speaker: STEPHANO
text_entry: My mistress will before the break of day

speaker: STEPHANO
text_entry: Be here at Belmont; she doth stray about

speaker: STEPHANO
text_entry: By holy crosses, where she kneels and prays

speaker: STEPHANO
text_entry: For happy wedlock hours.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Who comes with her?

speaker: STEPHANO
text_entry: None but a holy hermit and her maid.

speaker: STEPHANO
text_entry: I pray you, is my master yet returnd?

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: He is not, nor we have not heard from him.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: But go we in, I pray thee, Jessica,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: And ceremoniously let us prepare

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Some welcome for the mistress of the house.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Enter LAUNCELOT

speaker: LAUNCELOT
text_entry: Sola, sola! wo ha, ho! sola, sola!

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Who calls?

speaker: LAUNCELOT
text_entry: Sola! did you see Master Lorenzo?

speaker: LAUNCELOT
text_entry: Master Lorenzo, sola, sola!

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Leave hollaing, man: here.

speaker: LAUNCELOT
text_entry: Sola! where? where?

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Here.

speaker: LAUNCELOT
text_entry: Tell him theres a post come from my master, with

speaker: LAUNCELOT
text_entry: his horn full of good news: my master will be here

speaker: LAUNCELOT
text_entry: ere morning.

speaker: LAUNCELOT
text_entry: Exit

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Sweet soul, lets in, and there expect their coming.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: And yet no matter: why should we go in?

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: My friend Stephano, signify, I pray you,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Within the house, your mistress is at hand;

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: And bring your music forth into the air.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Exit Stephano

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: How sweet the moonlight sleeps upon this bank!

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Here will we sit and let the sounds of music

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Creep in our ears: soft stillness and the night

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Become the touches of sweet harmony.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Sit, Jessica. Look how the floor of heaven

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Is thick inlaid with patines of bright gold:

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Theres not the smallest orb which thou beholdst

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: But in his motion like an angel sings,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Still quiring to the young-eyed cherubins;

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Such harmony is in immortal souls;

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: But whilst this muddy vesture of decay

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Doth grossly close it in, we cannot hear it.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Enter Musicians

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Come, ho! and wake Diana with a hymn!

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: With sweetest touches pierce your mistress ear,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: And draw her home with music.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Music

speaker: JESSICA
text_entry: I am never merry when I hear sweet music.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: The reason is, your spirits are attentive:

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: For do but note a wild and wanton herd,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Or race of youthful and unhandled colts,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Fetching mad bounds, bellowing and neighing loud,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Which is the hot condition of their blood;

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: If they but hear perchance a trumpet sound,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Or any air of music touch their ears,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: You shall perceive them make a mutual stand,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Their savage eyes turnd to a modest gaze

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: By the sweet power of music: therefore the poet

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Did feign that Orpheus drew trees, stones and floods;

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Since nought so stockish, hard and full of rage,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: But music for the time doth change his nature.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: The man that hath no music in himself,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Nor is not moved with concord of sweet sounds,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Is fit for treasons, stratagems and spoils;

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: The motions of his spirit are dull as night

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: And his affections dark as Erebus:

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Let no such man be trusted. Mark the music.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Enter PORTIA and NERISSA

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: That light we see is burning in my hall.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: How far that little candle throws his beams!

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: So shines a good deed in a naughty world.

speaker: NERISSA
text_entry: When the moon shone, we did not see the candle.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: So doth the greater glory dim the less:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: A substitute shines brightly as a king

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Unto the king be by, and then his state

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Empties itself, as doth an inland brook

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Into the main of waters. Music! hark!

speaker: NERISSA
text_entry: It is your music, madam, of the house.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Nothing is good, I see, without respect:

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Methinks it sounds much sweeter than by day.

speaker: NERISSA
text_entry: Silence bestows that virtue on it, madam.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: The crow doth sing as sweetly as the lark,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: When neither is attended, and I think

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: The nightingale, if she should sing by day,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: When every goose is cackling, would be thought

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: No better a musician than the wren.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: How many things by season seasond are

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: To their right praise and true perfection!

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Peace, ho! the moon sleeps with Endymion

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: And would not be awaked.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Music ceases

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: That is the voice,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Or I am much deceived, of Portia.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: He knows me as the blind man knows the cuckoo,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: By the bad voice.

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Dear lady, welcome home.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: We have been praying for our husbands healths,

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Which speed, we hope, the better for our words.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Are they returnd?

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Madam, they are not yet;

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: But there is come a messenger before,

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: To signify their coming.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Go in, Nerissa;

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Give order to my servants that they take

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: No note at all of our being absent hence;

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: Nor you, Lorenzo; Jessica, nor you.

speaker: PORTIA
text_entry: A tucket sounds

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: Your husband is at hand; I hear his trumpet:

speaker: LORENZO
text_entry: We are no tell-tales, madam; fear you not.

speaker: PORTIA

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: go and vetch me in my closet un boitier vert, a box,

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: a green-a box: do intend vat I speak? a green-a box.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Ay, forsooth; Ill fetch it you.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Aside

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: I am glad he went not in himself: if he had found

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: the young man, he would have been horn-mad.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Fe, fe, fe, fe! ma foi, il fait fort chaud. Je

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: men vais a la cour--la grande affaire.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Is it this, sir?

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Oui; mette le au mon pocket: depeche, quickly. Vere

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: is dat knave Rugby?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: What, John Rugby! John!

speaker: RUGBY
text_entry: Here, sir!

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: You are John Rugby, and you are Jack Rugby. Come,

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: take-a your rapier, and come after my heel to the court.

speaker: RUGBY
text_entry: Tis ready, sir, here in the porch.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: By my trot, I tarry too long. Ods me!

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Quai-joublie! dere is some simples in my closet,

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: dat I vill not for the varld I shall leave behind.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Ay me, hell find the young man here, and be mad!

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: O diable, diable! vat is in my closet? Villain! larron!

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Pulling SIMPLE out

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Rugby, my rapier!

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Good master, be content.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Wherefore shall I be content-a?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: The young man is an honest man.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: What shall de honest man do in my closet? dere is

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: no honest man dat shall come in my closet.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: I beseech you, be not so phlegmatic. Hear the truth

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: of it: he came of an errand to me from Parson Hugh.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Vell.

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: Ay, forsooth; to desire her to--

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Peace, I pray you.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Peace-a your tongue. Speak-a your tale.

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: To desire this honest gentlewoman, your maid, to

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: speak a good word to Mistress Anne Page for my

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: master in the way of marriage.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: This is all, indeed, la! but Ill neer put my

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: finger in the fire, and need not.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Sir Hugh send-a you? Rugby, baille me some paper.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Tarry you a little-a while.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Writes

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: [Aside to SIMPLE]  I am glad he is so quiet: if he

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: had been thoroughly moved, you should have heard him

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: so loud and so melancholy. But notwithstanding,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: man, Ill do you your master what good I can: and

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: the very yea and the no is, the French doctor, my

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: master,--I may call him my master, look you, for I

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: keep his house; and I wash, wring, brew, bake,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: scour, dress meat and drink, make the beds and do

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: all myself,--

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: [Aside to MISTRESS QUICKLY]  Tis a great charge to

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: come under one bodys hand.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: [Aside to SIMPLE]  Are you avised o that? you

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: shall find it a great charge: and to be up early

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: and down late; but notwithstanding,--to tell you in

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: your ear; I would have no words of it,--my master

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: himself is in love with Mistress Anne Page: but

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: notwithstanding that, I know Annes mind,--thats

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: neither here nor there.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: You jacknape, give-a this letter to Sir Hugh; by

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: gar, it is a shallenge: I will cut his troat in dee

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: park; and I will teach a scurvy jack-a-nape priest

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: to meddle or make. You may be gone; it is not good

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: you tarry here. By gar, I will cut all his two

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: stones; by gar, he shall not have a stone to throw

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: at his dog:

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Exit SIMPLE

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Alas, he speaks but for his friend.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: It is no matter-a ver dat: do not you tell-a me

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: dat I shall have Anne Page for myself? By gar, I

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: vill kill de Jack priest; and I have appointed mine

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: host of de Jarteer to measure our weapon. By gar, I

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: will myself have Anne Page.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Sir, the maid loves you, and all shall be well. We

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: must give folks leave to prate: what, the good-jer!

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Rugby, come to the court with me. By gar, if I have

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: not Anne Page, I shall turn your head out of my

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: door. Follow my heels, Rugby.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Exeunt DOCTOR CAIUS and RUGBY

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: You shall have An fools-head of your own. No, I

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: know Annes mind for that: never a woman in Windsor

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: knows more of Annes mind than I do; nor can do more

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: than I do with her, I thank heaven.

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: [Within]  Whos within there? ho!

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Whos there, I trow! Come near the house, I pray you.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Enter FENTON

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: How now, good woman? how dost thou?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: The better that it pleases your good worship to ask.

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: What news? how does pretty Mistress Anne?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: In truth, sir, and she is pretty, and honest, and

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: gentle; and one that is your friend, I can tell you

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: that by the way; I praise heaven for it.

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Shall I do any good, thinkest thou? shall I not lose my suit?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Troth, sir, all is in his hands above: but

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: notwithstanding, Master Fenton, Ill be sworn on a

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: book, she loves you. Have not your worship a wart

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: above your eye?

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Yes, marry, have I; what of that?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Well, thereby hangs a tale: good faith, it is such

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: another Nan; but, I detest, an honest maid as ever

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: broke bread: we had an hours talk of that wart. I

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: shall never laugh but in that maids company! But

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: indeed she is given too much to allicholy and

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: musing: but for you--well, go to.

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Well, I shall see her to-day. Hold, theres money

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: for thee; let me have thy voice in my behalf: if

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: thou seest her before me, commend me.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Will I? ifaith, that we will; and I will tell your

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: worship more of the wart the next time we have

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: confidence; and of other wooers.

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Well, farewell; I am in great haste now.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Farewell to your worship.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Exit FENTON

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Truly, an honest gentleman: but Anne loves him not;

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: for I know Annes mind as well as another does. Out

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: upont! what have I forgot?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Exit

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: ACT II

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: SCENE I. Before PAGES house.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Enter MISTRESS PAGE, with a letter

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: What, have I scaped love-letters in the holiday-

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: time of my beauty, and am I now a subject for them?

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Let me see.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Reads

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Ask me no reason why I love you; for though

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Love use Reason for his physician, he admits him

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: not for his counsellor. You are not young, no more

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: am I; go to then, theres sympathy: you are merry,

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: so am I; ha, ha! then theres more sympathy: you

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: love sack, and so do I; would you desire better

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: sympathy? Let it suffice thee, Mistress Page,--at

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: the least, if the love of soldier can suffice,--

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: that I love thee. I will not say, pity me; tis

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: not a soldier-like phrase: but I say, love me. By me,

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Thine own true knight,

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: By day or night,

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Or any kind of light,

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: With all his might

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: For thee to fight,    JOHN FALSTAFF

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: What a Herod of Jewry is this! O wicked

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: world! One that is well-nigh worn to pieces with

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: age to show himself a young gallant! What an

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: unweighed behavior hath this Flemish drunkard

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: picked--with the devils name!--out of my

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: conversation, that he dares in this manner assay me?

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Why, he hath not been thrice in my company! What

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: should I say to him? I was then frugal of my

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: mirth: Heaven forgive me! Why, Ill exhibit a bill

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: in the parliament for the putting down of men. How

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: shall I be revenged on him? for revenged I will be,

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: as sure as his guts are made of puddings.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Enter MISTRESS FORD

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Mistress Page! trust me, I was going to your house.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: And, trust me, I was coming to you. You look very

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: ill.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Nay, Ill neer believe that; I have to show to the contrary.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Faith, but you do, in my mind.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Well, I do then; yet I say I could show you to the

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: contrary. O Mistress Page, give me some counsel!

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Whats the matter, woman?

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: O woman, if it were not for one trifling respect, I

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: could come to such honour!

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Hang the trifle, woman! take the honour. What is

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: it? dispense with trifles; what is it?

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: If I would but go to hell for an eternal moment or so,

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: I could be knighted.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: What? thou liest! Sir Alice Ford! These knights

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: will hack; and so thou shouldst not alter the

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: article of thy gentry.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: We burn daylight: here, read, read; perceive how I

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: might be knighted. I shall think the worse of fat

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: men, as long as I have an eye to make difference of

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: mens liking: and yet he would not swear; praised

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: womens modesty; and gave such orderly and

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: well-behaved reproof to all uncomeliness, that I

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: would have sworn his disposition would have gone to

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: the truth of his words; but they do no more adhere

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: and keep place together than the Hundredth Psalm to

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: the tune of Green Sleeves. What tempest, I trow,

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: threw this whale, with so many tuns of oil in his

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: belly, ashore at Windsor? How shall I be revenged

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: on him? I think the best way were to entertain him

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: with hope, till the wicked fire of lust have melted

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: him in his own grease. Did you ever hear the like?

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Letter for letter, but that the name of Page and

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Ford differs! To thy great comfort in this mystery

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: of ill opinions, heres the twin-brother of thy

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: letter: but let thine inherit first; for, I

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: protest, mine never shall. I warrant he hath a

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: thousand of these letters, writ with blank space for

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: different names--sure, more,--and these are of the

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: second edition: he will print them, out of doubt;

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: for he cares not what he puts into the press, when

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: he would put us two. I had rather be a giantess,

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: and lie under Mount Pelion. Well, I will find you

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: twenty lascivious turtles ere one chaste man.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Why, this is the very same; the very hand, the very

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: words. What doth he think of us?

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Nay, I know not: it makes me almost ready to

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: wrangle with mine own honesty. Ill entertain

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: myself like one that I am not acquainted withal;

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: for, sure, unless he know some strain in me, that I

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: know not myself, he would never have boarded me in this fury.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Boarding, call you it? Ill be sure to keep him

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: above deck.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: So will Iif he come under my hatches, Ill never

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: to sea again. Lets be revenged on him: lets

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: appoint him a meeting; give him a show of comfort in

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: his suit and lead him on with a fine-baited delay,

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: till he hath pawned his horses to mine host of the Garter.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Nay, I will consent to act any villany against him,

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: that may not sully the chariness of our honesty. O,

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: that my husband saw this letter! it would give

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: eternal food to his jealousy.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Why, look where he comes; and my good man too: hes

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: as far from jealousy as I am from giving him cause;

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: and that I hope is an unmeasurable distance.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: You are the happier woman.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Lets consult together against this greasy knight.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Come hither.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: They retire

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Enter FORD with PISTOL, and PAGE with NYM

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Well, I hope it be not so.

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Hope is a curtal dog in some affairs:

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Sir John affects thy wife.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Why, sir, my wife is not young.

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: He wooes both high and low, both rich and poor,

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Both young and old, one with another, Ford;

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: He loves the gallimaufry: Ford, perpend.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Love my wife!

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: With liver burning hot. Prevent, or go thou,

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Like Sir Actaeon he, with Ringwood at thy heels:

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: O, odious is the name!

speaker: FORD
text_entry: What name, sir?

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: The horn, I say. Farewell.

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Take heed, have open eye, for thieves do foot by night:

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Take heed, ere summer comes or cuckoo-birds do sing.

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Away, Sir Corporal Nym!

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Believe it, Page; he speaks sense.

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Exit

speaker: FORD
text_entry: [Aside]  I will be patient; I will find out this.

speaker: NYM
text_entry: [To PAGE]  And this is true; I like not the humour

speaker: NYM
text_entry: of lying. He hath wronged me in some humours: I

speaker: NYM
text_entry: should have borne the humoured letter to her; but I

speaker: NYM
text_entry: have a sword and it shall bite upon my necessity.

speaker: NYM
text_entry: He loves your wife; theres the short and the long.

speaker: NYM
text_entry: My name is Corporal Nym; I speak and I avouch; tis

speaker: NYM
text_entry: true: my name is Nym and Falstaff loves your wife.

speaker: NYM
text_entry: Adieu. I love not the humour of bread and cheese,

speaker: NYM
text_entry: and theres the humour of it. Adieu.

speaker: NYM
text_entry: Exit

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: The humour of it, quoth a! heres a fellow

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: frights English out of his wits.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: I will seek out Falstaff.

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: I never heard such a drawling, affecting rogue.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: If I do find it: well.

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: I will not believe such a Cataian, though the priest

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: o the town commended him for a true man.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Twas a good sensible fellow: well.

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: How now, Meg!

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: MISTRESS PAGE and MISTRESS FORD come forward

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Whither go you, George? Hark you.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: How now, sweet Frank! why art thou melancholy?

speaker: FORD
text_entry: I melancholy! I am not melancholy. Get you home, go.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Faith, thou hast some crotchets in thy head. Now,

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: will you go, Mistress Page?

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Have with you. Youll come to dinner, George.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Aside to MISTRESS FORD

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Look who comes yonder: she shall be our messenger

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: to this paltry knight.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: [Aside to MISTRESS PAGE]  Trust me, I thought on her:

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: shell fit it.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Enter MISTRESS QUICKLY

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: You are come to see my daughter Anne?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Ay, forsooth; and, I pray, how does good Mistress Anne?

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Go in with us and see: we have an hours talk with

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: you.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Exeunt MISTRESS PAGE, MISTRESS FORD, and MISTRESS QUICKLY

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: How now, Master Ford!

speaker: FORD
text_entry: You heard what this knave told me, did you not?

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Yes: and you heard what the other told me?

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Do you think there is truth in them?

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Hang em, slaves! I do not think the knight would

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: offer it: but these that accuse him in his intent

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: towards our wives are a yoke of his discarded men;

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: very rogues, now they be out of service.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Were they his men?

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Marry, were they.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: I like it never the better for that. Does he lie at

speaker: FORD
text_entry: the Garter?

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Ay, marry, does he. If he should intend this voyage

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: towards my wife, I would turn her loose to him; and

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: what he gets more of her than sharp words, let it

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: lie on my head.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: I do not misdoubt my wife; but I would be loath to

speaker: FORD
text_entry: turn them together. A man may be too confident: I

speaker: FORD
text_entry: would have nothing lie on my head: I cannot be thus satisfied.

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Look where my ranting host of the Garter comes:

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: there is either liquor in his pate or money in his

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: purse when he looks so merrily.

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Enter Host

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: How now, mine host!

speaker: Host
text_entry: How now, bully-rook! thourt a gentleman.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Cavaleiro-justice, I say!

speaker: Host
text_entry: Enter SHALLOW

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: I follow, mine host, I follow. Good even and

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: twenty, good Master Page! Master Page, will you go

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: with us? we have sport in hand.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Tell him, cavaleiro-justice; tell him, bully-rook.

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: Sir, there is a fray to be fought between Sir Hugh

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: the Welsh priest and Caius the French doctor.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Good mine host o the Garter, a word with you.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Drawing him aside

speaker: Host
text_entry: What sayest thou, my bully-rook?

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: [To PAGE]  Will you go with us to behold it? My

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: merry host hath had the measuring of their weapons;

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: and, I think, hath appointed them contrary places;

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: for, believe me, I hear the parson is no jester.

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: Hark, I will tell you what our sport shall be.

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: They converse apart

speaker: Host
text_entry: Hast thou no suit against my knight, my

speaker: Host
text_entry: guest-cavaleire?

speaker: FORD
text_entry: None, I protest: but Ill give you a pottle of

speaker: FORD
text_entry: burnt sack to give me recourse to him and tell him

speaker: FORD
text_entry: my name is Brook; only for a jest.

speaker: Host
text_entry: My hand, bully; thou shalt have egress and regress;

speaker: Host
text_entry: --said I well?--and thy name shall be Brook. It is

speaker: Host
text_entry: a merry knight. Will you go, An-heires?

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: Have with you, mine host.

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: I have heard the Frenchman hath good skill in

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: his rapier.

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: Tut, sir, I could have told you more. In these times

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: you stand on distance, your passes, stoccadoes, and

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: I know not what: tis the heart, Master Page; tis

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: here, tis here. I have seen the time, with my long

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: sword I would have made you four tall fellows skip like rats.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Here, boys, here, here! shall we wag?

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Have with you. I would rather hear them scold than fight.

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Exeunt Host, SHALLOW, and PAGE

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Though Page be a secure fool, an stands so firmly

speaker: FORD
text_entry: on his wifes frailty, yet I cannot put off my

speaker: FORD
text_entry: opinion so easily: she was in his company at Pages

speaker: FORD
text_entry: house; and what they made there, I know not. Well,

speaker: FORD
text_entry: I will look further intot: and I have a disguise

speaker: FORD
text_entry: to sound Falstaff. If I find her honest, I lose not

speaker: FORD
text_entry: my labour; if she be otherwise, tis labour well bestowed.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Exit

speaker: FORD
text_entry: SCENE II. A room in the Garter Inn.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Enter FALSTAFF and PISTOL

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: I will not lend thee a penny.

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Why, then the worlds mine oyster.

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Which I with sword will open.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Not a penny. I have been content, sir, you should

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: lay my countenance to pawn; I have grated upon my

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: good friends for three reprieves for you and your

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: coach-fellow Nym; or else you had looked through

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: the grate, like a geminy of baboons. I am damned in

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: hell for swearing to gentlemen my friends, you were

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: good soldiers and tall fellows; and when Mistress

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Bridget lost the handle of her fan, I tookt upon

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: mine honour thou hadst it not.

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Didst not thou share? hadst thou not fifteen pence?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Reason, you rogue, reason: thinkest thou Ill

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: endanger my soul gratis? At a word, hang no more

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: about me, I am no gibbet for you. Go. A short knife

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: and a throng! To your manor of Pickt-hatch! Go.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Youll not bear a letter for me, you rogue! you

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: stand upon your honour! Why, thou unconfinable

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: baseness, it is as much as I can do to keep the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: terms of my honour precise: I, I, I myself

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: sometimes, leaving the fear of God on the left hand

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: and hiding mine honour in my necessity, am fain to

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: shuffle, to hedge and to lurch; and yet you, rogue,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: will ensconce your rags, your cat-a-mountain

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: looks, your red-lattice phrases, and your

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: bold-beating oaths, under the shelter of your

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: honour! You will not do it, you!

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: I do relent: what would thou more of man?

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Enter ROBIN

speaker: ROBIN
text_entry: Sir, heres a woman would speak with you.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Let her approach.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter MISTRESS QUICKLY

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Give your worship good morrow.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Good morrow, good wife.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Not so, ant please your worship.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Good maid, then.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Ill be sworn,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: As my mother was, the first hour I was born.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: I do believe the swearer. What with me?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Shall I vouchsafe your worship a word or two?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Two thousand, fair woman: and Ill vouchsafe thee

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: the hearing.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: There is one Mistress Ford, sir:--I pray, come a

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: little nearer this ways:--I myself dwell with master

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Doctor Caius,--

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Well, on: Mistress Ford, you say,--

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Your worship says very true: I pray your worship,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: come a little nearer this ways.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: I warrant thee, nobody hears; mine own people, mine

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: own people.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Are they so? God bless them and make them his servants!

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Well, Mistress Ford; what of her?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Why, sir, shes a good creature. Lord Lord! your

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: worships a wanton! Well, heaven forgive you and all

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: of us, I pray!

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Mistress Ford; come, Mistress Ford,--

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Marry, this is the short and the long of it; you

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: have brought her into such a canaries as tis

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: wonderful. The best courtier of them all, when the

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: court lay at Windsor, could never have brought her

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: to such a canary. Yet there has been knights, and

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: lords, and gentlemen, with their coaches, I warrant

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: you, coach after coach, letter after letter, gift

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: after gift; smelling so sweetly, all musk, and so

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: rushling, I warrant you, in silk and gold; and in

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: such alligant terms; and in such wine and sugar of

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: the best and the fairest, that would have won any

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: womans heart; and, I warrant you, they could never

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: get an eye-wink of her: I had myself twenty angels

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: given me this morning; but I defy all angels, in

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: any such sort, as they say, but in the way of

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: honesty: and, I warrant you, they could never get

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: her so much as sip on a cup with the proudest of

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: them all: and yet there has been earls, nay, which

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: is more, pensioners; but, I warrant you, all is one with her.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: But what says she to me? be brief, my good

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: she-Mercury.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Marry, she hath received your letter, for the which

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: she thanks you a thousand times; and she gives you

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: to notify that her husband will be absence from his

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: house between ten and eleven.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Ten and eleven?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Ay, forsooth; and then you may come and see the

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: picture, she says, that you wot of: Master Ford,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: her husband, will be from home. Alas! the sweet

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: woman leads an ill life with him: hes a very

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: jealousy man: she leads a very frampold life with

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: him, good heart.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Ten and eleven. Woman, commend me to her; I will

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: not fail her.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Why, you say well. But I have another messenger to

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: your worship. Mistress Page hath her hearty

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: commendations to you too: and let me tell you in

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: your ear, shes as fartuous a civil modest wife, and

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: one, I tell you, that will not miss you morning nor

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: evening prayer, as any is in Windsor, whoeer be the

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: other: and she bade me tell your worship that her

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: husband is seldom from home; but she hopes there

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: will come a time. I never knew a woman so dote upon

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: a man: surely I think you have charms, la; yes, in truth.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Not I, I assure thee: setting the attractions of my

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: good parts aside I have no other charms.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Blessing on your heart fort!

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: But, I pray thee, tell me this: has Fords wife and

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Pages wife acquainted each other how they love me?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: That were a jest indeed! they have not so little

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: grace, I hope: that were a trick indeed! but

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Mistress Page would desire you to send her your

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: little page, of all loves: her husband has a

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: marvellous infection to the little page; and truly

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Master Page is an honest man. Never a wife in

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Windsor leads a better life than she does: do what

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: she will, say what she will, take all, pay all, go

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: to bed when she list, rise when she list, all is as

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: she will: and truly she deserves it; for if there

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: be a kind woman in Windsor, she is one. You must

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: send her your page; no remedy.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Why, I will.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Nay, but do so, then: and, look you, he may come and

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: go between you both; and in any case have a

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: nay-word, that you may know one anothers mind, and

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: the boy never need to understand any thing; for

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: tis not good that children should know any

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: wickedness: old folks, you know, have discretion,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: as they say, and know the world.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Fare thee well: commend me to them both: theres

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: my purse; I am yet thy debtor. Boy, go along with

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: this woman.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Exeunt MISTRESS QUICKLY and ROBIN

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: This news distracts me!

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: This punk is one of Cupids carriers:

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Clap on more sails; pursue; up with your fights:

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Give fire: she is my prize, or ocean whelm them all!

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Exit

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Sayest thou so, old Jack? go thy ways; Ill make

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: more of thy old body than I have done. Will they

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: yet look after thee? Wilt thou, after the expense

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: of so much money, be now a gainer? Good body, I

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: thank thee. Let them say tis grossly done; so it be

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: fairly done, no matter.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter BARDOLPH

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: Sir John, theres one Master Brook below would fain

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: speak with you, and be acquainted with you; and hath

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: sent your worship a mornings draught of sack.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Brook is his name?

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: Ay, sir.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Call him in.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Exit BARDOLPH

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Such Brooks are welcome to me, that oerflow such

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: liquor. Ah, ha! Mistress Ford and Mistress Page

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: have I encompassed you? go to; via!

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Re-enter BARDOLPH, with FORD disguised

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Bless you, sir!

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: And you, sir! Would you speak with me?

speaker: FORD
text_entry: I make bold to press with so little preparation upon

speaker: FORD
text_entry: you.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Youre welcome. Whats your will? Give us leave, drawer.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Exit BARDOLPH

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Sir, I am a gentleman that have spent much; my name is Brook.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Good Master Brook, I desire more acquaintance of you.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Good Sir John, I sue for yours: not to charge you;

speaker: FORD
text_entry: for I must let you understand I think myself in

speaker: FORD
text_entry: better plight for a lender than you are: the which

speaker: FORD
text_entry: hath something emboldend me to this unseasoned

speaker: FORD
text_entry: intrusion; for they say, if money go before, all

speaker: FORD
text_entry: ways do lie open.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Money is a good soldier, sir, and will on.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Troth, and I have a bag of money here troubles me:

speaker: FORD
text_entry: if you will help to bear it, Sir John, take all, or

speaker: FORD
text_entry: half, for easing me of the carriage.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Sir, I know not how I may deserve to be your porter.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: I will tell you, sir, if you will give me the hearing.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Speak, good Master Brook: I shall be glad to be

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: your servant.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Sir, I hear you are a scholar,--I will be brief

speaker: FORD
text_entry: with you,--and you have been a man long known to me,

speaker: FORD
text_entry: though I had never so good means, as desire, to make

speaker: FORD
text_entry: myself acquainted with you. I shall discover a

speaker: FORD
text_entry: thing to you, wherein I must very much lay open mine

speaker: FORD
text_entry: own imperfection: but, good Sir John, as you have

speaker: FORD
text_entry: one eye upon my follies, as you hear them unfolded,

speaker: FORD
text_entry: turn another into the register of your own; that I

speaker: FORD
text_entry: may pass with a reproof the easier, sith you

speaker: FORD
text_entry: yourself know how easy it is to be such an offender.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Very well, sir; proceed.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: There is a gentlewoman in this town; her husbands

speaker: FORD
text_entry: name is Ford.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Well, sir.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: I have long loved her, and, I protest to you,

speaker: FORD
text_entry: bestowed much on her; followed her with a doting

speaker: FORD
text_entry: observance; engrossed opportunities to meet her;

speaker: FORD
text_entry: feed every slight occasion that could but niggardly

speaker: FORD
text_entry: give me sight of her; not only bought many presents

speaker: FORD
text_entry: to give her, but have given largely to many to know

speaker: FORD
text_entry: what she would have given; briefly, I have pursued

speaker: FORD
text_entry: her as love hath pursued me; which hath been on the

speaker: FORD
text_entry: wing of all occasions. But whatsoever I have

speaker: FORD
text_entry: merited, either in my mind or, in my means, meed,

speaker: FORD
text_entry: I am sure, I have received none; unless experience

speaker: FORD
text_entry: be a jewel that I have purchased at an infinite

speaker: FORD
text_entry: rate, and that hath taught me to say this:

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Love like a shadow flies when substance love pursues;

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Pursuing that that flies, and flying what pursues.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Have you received no promise of satisfaction at her hands?

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Never.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Have you importuned her to such a purpose?

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Never.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Of what quality was your love, then?

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Like a fair house built on another mans ground; so

speaker: FORD
text_entry: that I have lost my edifice by mistaking the place

speaker: FORD
text_entry: where I erected it.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: To what purpose have you unfolded this to me?

speaker: FORD
text_entry: When I have told you that, I have told you all.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Some say, that though she appear honest to me, yet in

speaker: FORD
text_entry: other places she enlargeth her mirth so far that

speaker: FORD
text_entry: there is shrewd construction made of her. Now, Sir

speaker: FORD
text_entry: John, here is the heart of my purpose: you are a

speaker: FORD
text_entry: gentleman of excellent breeding, admirable

speaker: FORD
text_entry: discourse, of great admittance, authentic in your

speaker: FORD
text_entry: place and person, generally allowed for your many

speaker: FORD
text_entry: war-like, court-like, and learned preparations.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: O, sir!

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Believe it, for you know it. There is money; spend

speaker: FORD
text_entry: it, spend it; spend more; spend all I have; only

speaker: FORD
text_entry: give me so much of your time in exchange of it, as

speaker: FORD
text_entry: to lay an amiable siege to the honesty of this

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Fords wife: use your art of wooing; win her to

speaker: FORD
text_entry: consent to you: if any man may, you may as soon as

speaker: FORD
text_entry: any.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Would it apply well to the vehemency of your

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: affection, that I should win what you would enjoy?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Methinks you prescribe to yourself very preposterously.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: O, understand my drift. She dwells so securely on

speaker: FORD
text_entry: the excellency of her honour, that the folly of my

speaker: FORD
text_entry: soul dares not present itself: she is too bright to

speaker: FORD
text_entry: be looked against. Now, could I could come to her

speaker: FORD
text_entry: with any detection in my hand, my desires had

speaker: FORD
text_entry: instance and argument to commend themselves: I

speaker: FORD
text_entry: could drive her then from the ward of her purity,

speaker: FORD
text_entry: her reputation, her marriage-vow, and a thousand

speaker: FORD
text_entry: other her defences, which now are too too strongly

speaker: FORD
text_entry: embattled against me. What say you tot, Sir John?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Master Brook, I will first make bold with your

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: money; next, give me your hand; and last, as I am a

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: gentleman, you shall, if you will, enjoy Fords wife.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: O good sir!

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: I say you shall.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Want no money, Sir John; you shall want none.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Want no Mistress Ford, Master Brook; you shall want

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: none. I shall be with her, I may tell you, by her

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: own appointment; even as you came in to me, her

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: assistant or go-between parted from me: I say I

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: shall be with her between ten and eleven; for at

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: that time the jealous rascally knave her husband

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: will be forth. Come you to me at night; you shall

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: know how I speed.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: I am blest in your acquaintance. Do you know Ford,

speaker: FORD
text_entry: sir?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Hang him, poor cuckoldly knave! I know him not:

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: yet I wrong him to call him poor; they say the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: jealous wittolly knave hath masses of money; for the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: which his wife seems to me well-favored. I will

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: use her as the key of the cuckoldly rogues coffer;

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: and theres my harvest-home.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: I would you knew Ford, sir, that you might avoid him

speaker: FORD
text_entry: if you saw him.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Hang him, mechanical salt-butter rogue! I will

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: stare him out of his wits; I will awe him with my

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: cudgel: it shall hang like a meteor oer the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: cuckolds horns. Master Brook, thou shalt know I

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: will predominate over the peasant, and thou shalt

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: lie with his wife. Come to me soon at night.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Fords a knave, and I will aggravate his style;

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: thou, Master Brook, shalt know him for knave and

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: cuckold. Come to me soon at night.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Exit

speaker: FORD
text_entry: What a damned Epicurean rascal is this! My heart is

speaker: FORD
text_entry: ready to crack with impatience. Who says this is

speaker: FORD
text_entry: improvident jealousy? my wife hath sent to him; the

speaker: FORD
text_entry: hour is fixed; the match is made. Would any man

speaker: FORD
text_entry: have thought this? See the hell of having a false

speaker: FORD
text_entry: woman! My bed shall be abused, my coffers

speaker: FORD
text_entry: ransacked, my reputation gnawn at; and I shall not

speaker: FORD
text_entry: only receive this villanous wrong, but stand under

speaker: FORD
text_entry: the adoption of abominable terms, and by him that

speaker: FORD
text_entry: does me this wrong. Terms! names! Amaimon sounds

speaker: FORD
text_entry: well; Lucifer, well; Barbason, well; yet they are

speaker: FORD
text_entry: devils additions, the names of fiends: but

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Cuckold! Wittol!--Cuckold! the devil himself hath

speaker: FORD
text_entry: not such a name. Page is an ass, a secure ass: he

speaker: FORD
text_entry: will trust his wife; he will not be jealous. I will

speaker: FORD
text_entry: rather trust a Fleming with my butter, Parson Hugh

speaker: FORD
text_entry: the Welshman with my cheese, an Irishman with my

speaker: FORD
text_entry: aqua-vitae bottle, or a thief to walk my ambling

speaker: FORD
text_entry: gelding, than my wife with herself; then she plots,

speaker: FORD
text_entry: then she ruminates, then she devises; and what they

speaker: FORD
text_entry: think in their hearts they may effect, they will

speaker: FORD
text_entry: break their hearts but they will effect. God be

speaker: FORD
text_entry: praised for my jealousy! Eleven oclock the hour.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: I will prevent this, detect my wife, be revenged on

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Falstaff, and laugh at Page. I will about it;

speaker: FORD
text_entry: better three hours too soon than a minute too late.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Fie, fie, fie! cuckold! cuckold! cuckold!

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Exit

speaker: FORD
text_entry: SCENE III. A field near Windsor.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Enter DOCTOR CAIUS and RUGBY

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Jack Rugby!

speaker: RUGBY
text_entry: Sir?

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Vat is de clock, Jack?

speaker: RUGBY
text_entry: Tis past the hour, sir, that Sir Hugh promised to meet.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: By gar, he has save his soul, dat he is no come; he

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: has pray his Pible well, dat he is no come: by gar,

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Jack Rugby, he is dead already, if he be come.

speaker: RUGBY
text_entry: He is wise, sir; he knew your worship would kill

speaker: RUGBY
text_entry: him, if he came.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: By gar, de herring is no dead so as I vill kill him.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Take your rapier, Jack; I vill tell you how I vill kill him.

speaker: RUGBY
text_entry: Alas, sir, I cannot fence.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Villany, take your rapier.

speaker: RUGBY
text_entry: Forbear; heres company.

speaker: RUGBY
text_entry: Enter Host, SHALLOW, SLENDER, and PAGE

speaker: Host
text_entry: Bless thee, bully doctor!

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: Save you, Master Doctor Caius!

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Now, good master doctor!

speaker: SLENDER
text_entry: Give you good morrow, sir.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Vat be all you, one, two, tree, four, come for?

speaker: Host
text_entry: To see thee fight, to see thee foin, to see thee

speaker: Host
text_entry: traverse; to see thee here, to see thee there; to

speaker: Host
text_entry: see thee pass thy punto, thy stock, thy reverse, thy

speaker: Host
text_entry: distance, thy montant. Is he dead, my Ethiopian? is

speaker: Host
text_entry: he dead, my Francisco? ha, bully! What says my

speaker: Host
text_entry: AEsculapius? my Galen? my heart of elder? ha! is

speaker: Host
text_entry: he dead, bully stale? is he dead?

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: By gar, he is de coward Jack priest of de vorld; he

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: is not show his face.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Thou art a Castalion-King-Urinal. Hector of Greece, my boy!

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: I pray you, bear vitness that me have stay six or

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: seven, two, tree hours for him, and he is no come.

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: He is the wiser man, master doctor: he is a curer of

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: souls, and you a curer of bodies; if you should

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: fight, you go against the hair of your professions.

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: Is it not true, Master Page?

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Master Shallow, you have yourself been a great

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: fighter, though now a man of peace.

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: Bodykins, Master Page, though I now be old and of

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: the peace, if I see a sword out, my finger itches to

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: make one. Though we are justices and doctors and

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: churchmen, Master Page, we have some salt of our

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: youth in us; we are the sons of women, Master Page.

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Tis true, Master Shallow.

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: It will be found so, Master Page. Master Doctor

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: Caius, I am come to fetch you home. I am sworn of

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: the peace: you have showed yourself a wise

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: physician, and Sir Hugh hath shown himself a wise

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: and patient churchman. You must go with me, master doctor.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Pardon, guest-justice. A word, Mounseur Mockwater.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Mock-vater! vat is dat?

speaker: Host
text_entry: Mock-water, in our English tongue, is valour, bully.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: By gar, den, I have as mush mock-vater as de

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Englishman. Scurvy jack-dog priest! by gar, me

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: vill cut his ears.

speaker: Host
text_entry: He will clapper-claw thee tightly, bully.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Clapper-de-claw! vat is dat?

speaker: Host
text_entry: That is, he will make thee amends.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: By gar, me do look he shall clapper-de-claw me;

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: for, by gar, me vill have it.

speaker: Host
text_entry: And I will provoke him tot, or let him wag.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Me tank you for dat.

speaker: Host
text_entry: And, moreover, bully,--but first, master guest, and

speaker: Host
text_entry: Master Page, and eke Cavaleiro Slender, go you

speaker: Host
text_entry: through the town to Frogmore.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Aside to them

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Sir Hugh is there, is he?

speaker: Host
text_entry: He is there: see what humour he is in; and I will

speaker: Host
text_entry: bring the doctor about by the fields. Will it do well?

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: We will do it.

speaker: SLENDER
text_entry: Adieu, good master doctor.

speaker: SLENDER
text_entry: Exeunt PAGE, SHALLOW, and SLENDER

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: By gar, me vill kill de priest; for he speak for a

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: jack-an-ape to Anne Page.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Let him die: sheathe thy impatience, throw cold

speaker: Host
text_entry: water on thy choler: go about the fields with me

speaker: Host
text_entry: through Frogmore: I will bring thee where Mistress

speaker: Host
text_entry: Anne Page is, at a farm-house a-feasting; and thou

speaker: Host
text_entry: shalt woo her. Cried I aim? said I well?

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: By gar, me dank you for dat: by gar, I love you;

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: and I shall procure-a you de good guest, de earl,

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: de knight, de lords, de gentlemen, my patients.

speaker: Host
text_entry: For the which I will be thy adversary toward Anne

speaker: Host
text_entry: Page. Said I well?

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: By gar, tis good; vell said.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Let us wag, then.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Come at my heels, Jack Rugby.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: ACT III

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: SCENE I. A field near Frogmore.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Enter SIR HUGH EVANS and SIMPLE

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: I pray you now, good master Slenders serving-man,

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: and friend Simple by your name, which way have you

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: looked for Master Caius, that calls himself doctor of physic?

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: Marry, sir, the pittie-ward, the park-ward, every

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: way; old Windsor way, and every way but the town

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: way.

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: I most fehemently desire you you will also look that

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: way.

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: I will, sir.

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Pless my soul, how full of chollors I am, and

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: trempling of mind! I shall be glad if he have

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: deceived me. How melancholies I am! I will knog

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: his urinals about his knaves costard when I have

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: good opportunities for the ork. Pless my soul!

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Sings

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: To shallow rivers, to whose falls

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Melodious birds sings madrigals;

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: There will we make our peds of roses,

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: And a thousand fragrant posies.

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: To shallow--

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Mercy on me! I have a great dispositions to cry.

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Sings
