text_entry: I had other things to have spoken with her too from

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: him.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: What are they? let us know.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Ay, come; quick.

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: I may not conceal them, sir.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Conceal them, or thou diest.

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: Why, sir, they were nothing but about Mistress Anne

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: Page; to know if it were my masters fortune to

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: have her or no.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Tis, tis his fortune.

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: What, sir?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: To have her, or no. Go; say the woman told me so.

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: May I be bold to say so, sir?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Ay, sir; like who more bold.

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: I thank your worship: I shall make my master glad

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: with these tidings.

speaker: SIMPLE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: Host
text_entry: Thou art clerkly, thou art clerkly, Sir John. Was

speaker: Host
text_entry: there a wise woman with thee?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Ay, that there was, mine host; one that hath taught

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: me more wit than ever I learned before in my life;

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: and I paid nothing for it neither, but was paid for

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: my learning.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter BARDOLPH

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: Out, alas, sir! cozenage, mere cozenage!

speaker: Host
text_entry: Where be my horses? speak well of them, varletto.

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: Run away with the cozeners; for so soon as I came

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: beyond Eton, they threw me off from behind one of

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: them, in a slough of mire; and set spurs and away,

speaker: BARDOLPH
text_entry: like three German devils, three Doctor Faustuses.

speaker: Host
text_entry: They are gone but to meet the duke, villain: do not

speaker: Host
text_entry: say they be fled; Germans are honest men.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Enter SIR HUGH EVANS

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Where is mine host?

speaker: Host
text_entry: What is the matter, sir?

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Have a care of your entertainments: there is a

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: friend of mine come to town tells me there is three

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: cozen-germans that has cozened all the hosts of

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Readins, of Maidenhead, of Colebrook, of horses and

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: money. I tell you for good will, look you: you

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: are wise and full of gibes and vlouting-stocks, and

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: tis not convenient you should be cozened. Fare you well.

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Enter DOCTOR CAIUS

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Vere is mine host de Jarteer?

speaker: Host
text_entry: Here, master doctor, in perplexity and doubtful dilemma.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: I cannot tell vat is dat: but it is tell-a me dat

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: you make grand preparation for a duke de Jamany: by

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: my trot, dere is no duke dat the court is know to

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: come. I tell you for good vill: adieu.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: Host
text_entry: Hue and cry, villain, go! Assist me, knight. I am

speaker: Host
text_entry: undone! Fly, run, hue and cry, villain! I am undone!

speaker: Host
text_entry: Exeunt Host and BARDOLPH

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: I would all the world might be cozened; for I have

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: been cozened and beaten too. If it should come to

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: the ear of the court, how I have been transformed

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: and how my transformation hath been washed and

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: cudgelled, they would melt me out of my fat drop by

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: drop and liquor fishermens boots with me; I warrant

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: they would whip me with their fine wits till I were

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: as crest-fallen as a dried pear. I never prospered

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: since I forswore myself at primero. Well, if my

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: wind were but long enough to say my prayers, I would repent.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter MISTRESS QUICKLY

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Now, whence come you?

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: From the two parties, forsooth.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: The devil take one party and his dam the other! and

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: so they shall be both bestowed. I have suffered more

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: for their sakes, more than the villanous inconstancy

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: of mans disposition is able to bear.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: And have not they suffered? Yes, I warrant;

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: speciously one of them; Mistress Ford, good heart,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: is beaten black and blue, that you cannot see a

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: white spot about her.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: What tellest thou me of black and blue? I was

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: beaten myself into all the colours of the rainbow;

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: and I was like to be apprehended for the witch of

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Brentford: but that my admirable dexterity of wit,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: my counterfeiting the action of an old woman,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: delivered me, the knave constable had set me i the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: stocks, i the common stocks, for a witch.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Sir, let me speak with you in your chamber: you

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: shall hear how things go; and, I warrant, to your

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: content. Here is a letter will say somewhat. Good

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: hearts, what ado here is to bring you together!

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Sure, one of you does not serve heaven well, that

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: you are so crossed.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Come up into my chamber.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: SCENE VI. Another room in the Garter Inn.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter FENTON and Host

speaker: Host
text_entry: Master Fenton, talk not to me; my mind is heavy: I

speaker: Host
text_entry: will give over all.

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Yet hear me speak. Assist me in my purpose,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: And, as I am a gentleman, Ill give thee

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: A hundred pound in gold more than your loss.

speaker: Host
text_entry: I will hear you, Master Fenton; and I will at the

speaker: Host
text_entry: least keep your counsel.

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: From time to time I have acquainted you

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: With the dear love I bear to fair Anne Page;

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Who mutually hath answerd my affection,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: So far forth as herself might be her chooser,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Even to my wish: I have a letter from her

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Of such contents as you will wonder at;

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: The mirth whereof so larded with my matter,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: That neither singly can be manifested,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Without the show of both; fat Falstaff

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Hath a great scene: the image of the jest

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Ill show you here at large. Hark, good mine host.

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: To-night at Hernes oak, just twixt twelve and one,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Must my sweet Nan present the Fairy Queen;

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: The purpose why, is here: in which disguise,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: While other jests are something rank on foot,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Her father hath commanded her to slip

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Away with Slender and with him at Eton

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Immediately to marry: she hath consented: Now, sir,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Her mother, ever strong against that match

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: And firm for Doctor Caius, hath appointed

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: That he shall likewise shuffle her away,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: While other sports are tasking of their minds,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: And at the deanery, where a priest attends,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Straight marry her: to this her mothers plot

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: She seemingly obedient likewise hath

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Made promise to the doctor. Now, thus it rests:

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Her father means she shall be all in white,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: And in that habit, when Slender sees his time

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: To take her by the hand and bid her go,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: She shall go with him: her mother hath intended,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: The better to denote her to the doctor,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: For they must all be maskd and vizarded,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: That quaint in green she shall be loose enrobed,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: With ribands pendent, flaring bout her head;

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: And when the doctor spies his vantage ripe,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: To pinch her by the hand, and, on that token,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: The maid hath given consent to go with him.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Which means she to deceive, father or mother?

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Both, my good host, to go along with me:

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: And here it rests, that youll procure the vicar

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: To stay for me at church twixt twelve and one,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: And, in the lawful name of marrying,

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: To give our hearts united ceremony.

speaker: Host
text_entry: Well, husband your device; Ill to the vicar:

speaker: Host
text_entry: Bring you the maid, you shall not lack a priest.

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: So shall I evermore be bound to thee;

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Besides, Ill make a present recompense.

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: ACT V

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: SCENE I. A room in the Garter Inn.

speaker: FENTON
text_entry: Enter FALSTAFF and MISTRESS QUICKLY

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Prithee, no more prattling; go. Ill hold. This is

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: the third time; I hope good luck lies in odd

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: numbers. Away I go. They say there is divinity in

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: odd numbers, either in nativity, chance, or death. Away!

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Ill provide you a chain; and Ill do what I can to

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: get you a pair of horns.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Away, I say; time wears: hold up your head, and mince.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Exit MISTRESS QUICKLY

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter FORD

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: How now, Master Brook! Master Brook, the matter

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: will be known to-night, or never. Be you in the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Park about midnight, at Hernes oak, and you shall

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: see wonders.

speaker: FORD
text_entry: Went you not to her yesterday, sir, as you told me

speaker: FORD
text_entry: you had appointed?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: I went to her, Master Brook, as you see, like a poor

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: old man: but I came from her, Master Brook, like a

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: poor old woman. That same knave Ford, her husband,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: hath the finest mad devil of jealousy in him,

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Master Brook, that ever governed frenzy. I will tell

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: you: he beat me grievously, in the shape of a

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: woman; for in the shape of man, Master Brook, I fear

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: not Goliath with a weavers beam; because I know

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: also life is a shuttle. I am in haste; go along

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: with me: Ill tell you all, Master Brook. Since I

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: plucked geese, played truant and whipped top, I knew

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: not what twas to be beaten till lately. Follow

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: me: Ill tell you strange things of this knave

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Ford, on whom to-night I will be revenged, and I

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: will deliver his wife into your hand. Follow.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Strange things in hand, Master Brook! Follow.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: SCENE II. Windsor Park.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter PAGE, SHALLOW, and SLENDER

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Come, come; well couch i the castle-ditch till we

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: see the light of our fairies. Remember, son Slender,

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: my daughter.

speaker: SLENDER
text_entry: Ay, forsooth; I have spoke with her and we have a

speaker: SLENDER
text_entry: nay-word how to know one another: I come to her in

speaker: SLENDER
text_entry: white, and cry mum; she cries budget; and by

speaker: SLENDER
text_entry: that we know one another.

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: Thats good too: but what needs either your mum

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: or her budget? the white will decipher her well

speaker: SHALLOW
text_entry: enough. It hath struck ten oclock.

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: The night is dark; light and spirits will become it

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: well. Heaven prosper our sport! No man means evil

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: but the devil, and we shall know him by his horns.

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Lets away; follow me.

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: SCENE III. A street leading to the Park.

speaker: PAGE
text_entry: Enter MISTRESS PAGE, MISTRESS FORD, and DOCTOR CAIUS

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Master doctor, my daughter is in green: when you

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: see your time, take her by the band, away with her

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: to the deanery, and dispatch it quickly. Go before

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: into the Park: we two must go together.

speaker: DOCTOR CAIUS
text_entry: I know vat I have to do. Adieu.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Fare you well, sir.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Exit DOCTOR CAIUS

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: My husband will not rejoice so much at the abuse of

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Falstaff as he will chafe at the doctors marrying

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: my daughter: but tis no matter; better a little

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: chiding than a great deal of heart-break.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Where is Nan now and her troop of fairies, and the

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Welsh devil Hugh?

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: They are all couched in a pit hard by Hernes oak,

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: with obscured lights; which, at the very instant of

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Falstaffs and our meeting, they will at once

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: display to the night.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: That cannot choose but amaze him.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: If he be not amazed, he will be mocked; if he be

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: amazed, he will every way be mocked.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Well betray him finely.

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Against such lewdsters and their lechery

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Those that betray them do no treachery.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: The hour draws on. To the oak, to the oak!

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: SCENE IV. Windsor Park.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Enter SIR HUGH EVANS, disguised, with others as Fairies

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Trib, trib, fairies; come; and remember your parts:

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: be pold, I pray you; follow me into the pit; and

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: when I give the watch-ords, do as I pid you:

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: come, come; trib, trib.

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: SCENE V. Another part of the Park.

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Enter FALSTAFF disguised as Herne

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: The Windsor bell hath struck twelve; the minute

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: draws on. Now, the hot-blooded gods assist me!

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Remember, Jove, thou wast a bull for thy Europa; love

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: set on thy horns. O powerful love! that, in some

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: respects, makes a beast a man, in some other, a man

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: a beast. You were also, Jupiter, a swan for the love

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: of Leda. O omnipotent Love! how near the god drew

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: to the complexion of a goose! A fault done first in

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: the form of a beast. O Jove, a beastly fault! And

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: then another fault in the semblance of a fowl; think

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: on t, Jove; a foul fault! When gods have hot

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: backs, what shall poor men do? For me, I am here a

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Windsor stag; and the fattest, I think, i the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: forest. Send me a cool rut-time, Jove, or who can

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: blame me to piss my tallow? Who comes here? my

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: doe?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter MISTRESS FORD and MISTRESS PAGE

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Sir John! art thou there, my deer? my male deer?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: My doe with the black scut! Let the sky rain

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: potatoes; let it thunder to the tune of Green

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Sleeves, hail kissing-comfits and snow eringoes; let

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: there come a tempest of provocation, I will shelter me here.

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Mistress Page is come with me, sweetheart.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Divide me like a bribe buck, each a haunch: I will

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: keep my sides to myself, my shoulders for the fellow

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: of this walk, and my horns I bequeath your husbands.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Am I a woodman, ha? Speak I like Herne the hunter?

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Why, now is Cupid a child of conscience; he makes

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: restitution. As I am a true spirit, welcome!

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Noise within

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Alas, what noise?

speaker: MISTRESS FORD
text_entry: Heaven forgive our sins

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: What should this be?

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: Away, away!

speaker: MISTRESS PAGE
text_entry: They run off

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: I think the devil will not have me damned, lest the

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: oil thats in me should set hell on fire; he would

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: never else cross me thus.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Enter SIR HUGH EVANS, disguised as before; PISTOL,  as Hobgoblin; MISTRESS QUICKLY, ANNE PAGE, and others, as Fairies, with tapers

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Fairies, black, grey, green, and white,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: You moonshine revellers and shades of night,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: You orphan heirs of fixed destiny,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Attend your office and your quality.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Crier Hobgoblin, make the fairy oyes.

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Elves, list your names; silence, you airy toys.

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Cricket, to Windsor chimneys shalt thou leap:

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Where fires thou findst unraked and hearths unswept,

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: There pinch the maids as blue as bilberry:

speaker: PISTOL
text_entry: Our radiant queen hates sluts and sluttery.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: They are fairies; he that speaks to them shall die:

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Ill wink and couch: no man their works must eye.

speaker: FALSTAFF
text_entry: Lies down upon his face

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Wheres Bede? Go you, and where you find a maid

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: That, ere she sleep, has thrice her prayers said,

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Raise up the organs of her fantasy;

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Sleep she as sound as careless infancy:

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: But those as sleep and think not on their sins,

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS
text_entry: Pinch them, arms, legs, backs, shoulders, sides and shins.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: About, about;

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Search Windsor Castle, elves, within and out:

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Strew good luck, ouphes, on every sacred room:

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: That it may stand till the perpetual doom,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: In state as wholesome as in state tis fit,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Worthy the owner, and the owner it.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: The several chairs of order look you scour

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: With juice of balm and every precious flower:

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Each fair instalment, coat, and several crest,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: With loyal blazon, evermore be blest!

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: And nightly, meadow-fairies, look you sing,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Like to the Garters compass, in a ring:

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: The expressure that it bears, green let it be,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: More fertile-fresh than all the field to see;

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: And Honi soit qui mal y pense write

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: In emerald tufts, flowers purple, blue and white;

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Let sapphire, pearl and rich embroidery,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Buckled below fair knighthoods bending knee:

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Fairies use flowers for their charactery.

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Away; disperse: but till tis one oclock,

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Our dance of custom round about the oak

speaker: MISTRESS QUICKLY
text_entry: Of Herne the hunter, let us not forget.

speaker: SIR HUGH EVANS

text_entry: To stubborn harshness: and, my gracious duke,

text_entry: Or to her death, according to our law

text_entry: What say you, Hermia? be advised fair maid:

text_entry: One that composed your beauties, yea, and one

text_entry: To whom you are but as a form in wax

text_entry: By him imprinted and within his power

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: To leave the figure or disfigure it.

text_entry: Demetrius is a worthy gentleman.

text_entry: So is Lysander.

text_entry: In himself he is;

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: But in this kind, wanting your fathers voice,

text_entry: I would my father lookd but with my eyes.

text_entry: Rather your eyes must with his judgment look.

text_entry: I know not by what power I am made bold,

text_entry: Nor how it may concern my modesty,

text_entry: The worst that may befall me in this case,

text_entry: If I refuse to wed Demetrius.

text_entry: Either to die the death or to abjure

text_entry: For ever the society of men.

text_entry: Know of your youth, examine well your blood,

text_entry: Whether, if you yield not to your fathers choice,

text_entry: You can endure the livery of a nun,

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: For aye to be in shady cloister mewd,

text_entry: To live a barren sister all your life,

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: Chanting faint hymns to the cold fruitless moon.

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: Thrice-blessed they that master so their blood,

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: To undergo such maiden pilgrimage;

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: But earthlier happy is the rose distilld,

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: Than that which withering on the virgin thorn

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: Grows, lives and dies in single blessedness.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: So will I grow, so live, so die, my lord,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Ere I will my virgin patent up

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Unto his lordship, whose unwished yoke

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: My soul consents not to give sovereignty.

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: Take time to pause; and, by the nest new moon--

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: The sealing-day betwixt my love and me,

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: For everlasting bond of fellowship--

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: Upon that day either prepare to die

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: For disobedience to your fathers will,

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: Or else to wed Demetrius, as he would;

text_entry: Or on Dianas altar to protest

speaker: THESEUS

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Relent, sweet Hermia: and, Lysander, yield

text_entry: Thy crazed title to my certain right.

text_entry: Let me have Hermias: do you marry him.

text_entry: Scornful Lysander! true, he hath my love,

text_entry: And she is mine, and all my right of her

text_entry: I do estate unto Demetrius.

speaker: LYSANDER

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: My fortunes every way as fairly rankd,

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: If not with vantage, as Demetrius;

text_entry: And, which is more than all these boasts can be,

speaker: LYSANDER

speaker: THESEUS

speaker: THESEUS
text_entry: Against our nuptial and confer with you

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: How now, my love! why is your cheek so pale?

text_entry: Belike for want of rain, which I could well

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Beteem them from the tempest of my eyes.

text_entry: Ay me! for aught that I could ever read,

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Could ever hear by tale or history,

text_entry: But, either it was different in blood,--

text_entry: O cross! too high to be enthralld to low.

text_entry: Making it momentany as a sound,

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Swift as a shadow, short as any dream;

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Brief as the lightning in the collied night,

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: That, in a spleen, unfolds both heaven and earth,

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: And ere a man hath power to say Behold!

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: The jaws of darkness do devour it up:

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: So quick bright things come to confusion.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: If then true lovers have been ever crossd,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: It stands as an edict in destiny:

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Then let us teach our trial patience,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Because it is a customary cross,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: As due to love as thoughts and dreams and sighs,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Wishes and tears, poor fancys followers.

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: A good persuasion: therefore, hear me, Hermia.

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: I have a widow aunt, a dowager

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Of great revenue, and she hath no child:

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: From Athens is her house remote seven leagues;

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: And she respects me as her only son.

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: There, gentle Hermia, may I marry thee;

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: And to that place the sharp Athenian law

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Cannot pursue us. If thou lovest me then,

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Steal forth thy fathers house to-morrow night;

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: And in the wood, a league without the town,

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Where I did meet thee once with Helena,

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: To do observance to a morn of May,

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: There will I stay for thee.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: My good Lysander!

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: I swear to thee, by Cupids strongest bow,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: By his best arrow with the golden head,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: By the simplicity of Venus doves,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: By that which knitteth souls and prospers loves,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: And by that fire which burnd the Carthage queen,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: When the false Troyan under sail was seen,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: By all the vows that ever men have broke,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: In number more than ever women spoke,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: In that same place thou hast appointed me,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: To-morrow truly will I meet with thee.

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Keep promise, love. Look, here comes Helena.

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Enter HELENA

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: God speed fair Helena! whither away?

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Call you me fair? that fair again unsay.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Demetrius loves your fair: O happy fair!

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Your eyes are lode-stars; and your tongues sweet air

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: More tuneable than lark to shepherds ear,

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: When wheat is green, when hawthorn buds appear.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Sickness is catching: O, were favour so,

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Yours would I catch, fair Hermia, ere I go;

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: My ear should catch your voice, my eye your eye,

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: My tongue should catch your tongues sweet melody.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Were the world mine, Demetrius being bated,

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: The rest Id give to be to you translated.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: O, teach me how you look, and with what art

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: You sway the motion of Demetrius heart.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: I frown upon him, yet he loves me still.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: O that your frowns would teach my smiles such skill!

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: I give him curses, yet he gives me love.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: O that my prayers could such affection move!

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: The more I hate, the more he follows me.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: The more I love, the more he hateth me.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: His folly, Helena, is no fault of mine.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: None, but your beauty: would that fault were mine!

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Take comfort: he no more shall see my face;

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Lysander and myself will fly this place.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Before the time I did Lysander see,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Seemd Athens as a paradise to me:

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: O, then, what graces in my love do dwell,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: That he hath turnd a heaven unto a hell!

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Helen, to you our minds we will unfold:

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: To-morrow night, when Phoebe doth behold

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Her silver visage in the watery glass,

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Decking with liquid pearl the bladed grass,

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: A time that lovers flights doth still conceal,

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Through Athens gates have we devised to steal.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: And in the wood, where often you and I

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Upon faint primrose-beds were wont to lie,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Emptying our bosoms of their counsel sweet,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: There my Lysander and myself shall meet;

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: And thence from Athens turn away our eyes,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: To seek new friends and stranger companies.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Farewell, sweet playfellow: pray thou for us;

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: And good luck grant thee thy Demetrius!

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Keep word, Lysander: we must starve our sight

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: From lovers food till morrow deep midnight.

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: I will, my Hermia.

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Exit HERMIA

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Helena, adieu:

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: As you on him, Demetrius dote on you!

speaker: LYSANDER
text_entry: Exit

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: How happy some oer other some can be!

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Through Athens I am thought as fair as she.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: But what of that? Demetrius thinks not so;

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: He will not know what all but he do know:

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: And as he errs, doting on Hermias eyes,

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: So I, admiring of his qualities:

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Things base and vile, folding no quantity,

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Love can transpose to form and dignity:

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Love looks not with the eyes, but with the mind;

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: And therefore is wingd Cupid painted blind:

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Nor hath Loves mind of any judgement taste;

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Wings and no eyes figure unheedy haste:

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: And therefore is Love said to be a child,

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Because in choice he is so oft beguiled.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: As waggish boys in game themselves forswear,

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: So the boy Love is perjured every where:

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: For ere Demetrius lookd on Hermias eyne,

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: He haild down oaths that he was only mine;

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: And when this hail some heat from Hermia felt,

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: So he dissolved, and showers of oaths did melt.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: I will go tell him of fair Hermias flight:

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Then to the wood will he to-morrow night

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Pursue her; and for this intelligence

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: If I have thanks, it is a dear expense:

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: But herein mean I to enrich my pain,

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: To have his sight thither and back again.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Exit

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: SCENE II. Athens. QUINCES house.

speaker: HELENA
text_entry: Enter QUINCE, SNUG, BOTTOM, FLUTE, SNOUT, and STARVELING

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Is all our company here?

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: You were best to call them generally, man by man,

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: according to the scrip.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Here is the scroll of every mans name, which is

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: thought fit, through all Athens, to play in our

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: interlude before the duke and the duchess, on his

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: wedding-day at night.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: First, good Peter Quince, say what the play treats

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: on, then read the names of the actors, and so grow

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: to a point.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Marry, our play is, The most lamentable comedy, and

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: most cruel death of Pyramus and Thisby.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: A very good piece of work, I assure you, and a

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: merry. Now, good Peter Quince, call forth your

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: actors by the scroll. Masters, spread yourselves.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Answer as I call you. Nick Bottom, the weaver.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Ready. Name what part I am for, and proceed.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: You, Nick Bottom, are set down for Pyramus.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: What is Pyramus? a lover, or a tyrant?

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: A lover, that kills himself most gallant for love.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: That will ask some tears in the true performing of

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: it: if I do it, let the audience look to their

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: eyes; I will move storms, I will condole in some

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: measure. To the rest: yet my chief humour is for a

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: tyrant: I could play Ercles rarely, or a part to

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: tear a cat in, to make all split.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: The raging rocks

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: And shivering shocks

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Shall break the locks

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Of prison gates;

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: And Phibbus car

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Shall shine from far

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: And make and mar

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: The foolish Fates.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: This was lofty! Now name the rest of the players.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: This is Ercles vein, a tyrants vein; a lover is

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: more condoling.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Francis Flute, the bellows-mender.

speaker: FLUTE
text_entry: Here, Peter Quince.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Flute, you must take Thisby on you.

speaker: FLUTE
text_entry: What is Thisby? a wandering knight?

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: It is the lady that Pyramus must love.

speaker: FLUTE
text_entry: Nay, faith, let me not play a woman; I have a beard coming.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Thats all one: you shall play it in a mask, and

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: you may speak as small as you will.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: An I may hide my face, let me play Thisby too, Ill

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: speak in a monstrous little voice. Thisne,

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Thisne; Ah, Pyramus, lover dear! thy Thisby dear,

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: and lady dear!

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: No, no; you must play Pyramus: and, Flute, you Thisby.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Well, proceed.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Robin Starveling, the tailor.

speaker: STARVELING
text_entry: Here, Peter Quince.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Robin Starveling, you must play Thisbys mother.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Tom Snout, the tinker.

speaker: SNOUT
text_entry: Here, Peter Quince.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: You, Pyramus father: myself, Thisbys father:

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Snug, the joiner; you, the lions part: and, I

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: hope, here is a play fitted.

speaker: SNUG
text_entry: Have you the lions part written? pray you, if it

speaker: SNUG
text_entry: be, give it me, for I am slow of study.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: You may do it extempore, for it is nothing but roaring.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Let me play the lion too: I will roar, that I will

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: do any mans heart good to hear me; I will roar,

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: that I will make the duke say Let him roar again,

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: let him roar again.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: An you should do it too terribly, you would fright

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: the duchess and the ladies, that they would shriek;

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: and that were enough to hang us all.

speaker: ALL
text_entry: That would hang us, every mothers son.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: I grant you, friends, if that you should fright the

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: ladies out of their wits, they would have no more

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: discretion but to hang us: but I will aggravate my

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: voice so that I will roar you as gently as any

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: sucking dove; I will roar you an twere any

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: nightingale.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: You can play no part but Pyramus; for Pyramus is a

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: sweet-faced man; a proper man, as one shall see in a

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: summers day; a most lovely gentleman-like man:

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: therefore you must needs play Pyramus.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Well, I will undertake it. What beard were I best

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: to play it in?

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Why, what you will.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: I will discharge it in either your straw-colour

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: beard, your orange-tawny beard, your purple-in-grain

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: beard, or your French-crown-colour beard, your

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: perfect yellow.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Some of your French crowns have no hair at all, and

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: then you will play bare-faced. But, masters, here

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: are your parts: and I am to entreat you, request

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: you and desire you, to con them by to-morrow night;

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: and meet me in the palace wood, a mile without the

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: town, by moonlight; there will we rehearse, for if

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: we meet in the city, we shall be dogged with

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: company, and our devices known. In the meantime I

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: will draw a bill of properties, such as our play

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: wants. I pray you, fail me not.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: We will meet; and there we may rehearse most

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: obscenely and courageously. Take pains; be perfect: adieu.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: At the dukes oak we meet.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Enough; hold or cut bow-strings.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: ACT II

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: SCENE I. A wood near Athens.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Enter, from opposite sides, a Fairy, and PUCK

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: How now, spirit! whither wander you?

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Over hill, over dale,

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Thorough bush, thorough brier,

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Over park, over pale,

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Thorough flood, thorough fire,

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: I do wander everywhere,

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Swifter than the moons sphere;

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: And I serve the fairy queen,

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: To dew her orbs upon the green.

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: The cowslips tall her pensioners be:

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: In their gold coats spots you see;

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Those be rubies, fairy favours,

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: In those freckles live their savours:

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: I must go seek some dewdrops here

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: And hang a pearl in every cowslips ear.

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Farewell, thou lob of spirits; Ill be gone:

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Our queen and all our elves come here anon.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: The king doth keep his revels here to-night:

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Take heed the queen come not within his sight;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: For Oberon is passing fell and wrath,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Because that she as her attendant hath

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: A lovely boy, stolen from an Indian king;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: She never had so sweet a changeling;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And jealous Oberon would have the child

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Knight of his train, to trace the forests wild;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: But she perforce withholds the loved boy,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Crowns him with flowers and makes him all her joy:

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And now they never meet in grove or green,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: By fountain clear, or spangled starlight sheen,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: But, they do square, that all their elves for fear

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Creep into acorn-cups and hide them there.

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Either I mistake your shape and making quite,

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Or else you are that shrewd and knavish sprite

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Calld Robin Goodfellow: are not you he

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: That frights the maidens of the villagery;

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Skim milk, and sometimes labour in the quern

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: And bootless make the breathless housewife churn;

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: And sometime make the drink to bear no barm;

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Mislead night-wanderers, laughing at their harm?

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Those that Hobgoblin call you and sweet Puck,

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: You do their work, and they shall have good luck:

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Are not you he?

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Thou speakst aright;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: I am that merry wanderer of the night.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: I jest to Oberon and make him smile

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: When I a fat and bean-fed horse beguile,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Neighing in likeness of a filly foal:

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And sometime lurk I in a gossips bowl,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: In very likeness of a roasted crab,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And when she drinks, against her lips I bob

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And on her witherd dewlap pour the ale.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: The wisest aunt, telling the saddest tale,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Sometime for three-foot stool mistaketh me;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Then slip I from her bum, down topples she,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And tailor cries, and falls into a cough;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And then the whole quire hold their hips and laugh,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And waxen in their mirth and neeze and swear

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: A merrier hour was never wasted there.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: But, room, fairy! here comes Oberon.

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: And here my mistress. Would that he were gone!

speaker: Fairy
text_entry: Enter, from one side, OBERON, with his train; from the other, TITANIA, with hers

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Ill met by moonlight, proud Titania.

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: What, jealous Oberon! Fairies, skip hence:

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: I have forsworn his bed and company.

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Tarry, rash wanton: am not I thy lord?

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Then I must be thy lady: but I know

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: When thou hast stolen away from fairy land,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And in the shape of Corin sat all day,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Playing on pipes of corn and versing love

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: To amorous Phillida. Why art thou here,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Come from the farthest Steppe of India?

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: But that, forsooth, the bouncing Amazon,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Your buskind mistress and your warrior love,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: To Theseus must be wedded, and you come

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: To give their bed joy and prosperity.

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: How canst thou thus for shame, Titania,

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Glance at my credit with Hippolyta,

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Knowing I know thy love to Theseus?

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Didst thou not lead him through the glimmering night

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: From Perigenia, whom he ravished?

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: And make him with fair AEgle break his faith,

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: With Ariadne and Antiopa?

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: These are the forgeries of jealousy:

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And never, since the middle summers spring,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Met we on hill, in dale, forest or mead,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: By paved fountain or by rushy brook,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Or in the beached margent of the sea,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: To dance our ringlets to the whistling wind,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: But with thy brawls thou hast disturbd our sport.

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Therefore the winds, piping to us in vain,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: As in revenge, have suckd up from the sea

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Contagious fogs; which falling in the land

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Have every pelting river made so proud

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: That they have overborne their continents:

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: The ox hath therefore stretchd his yoke in vain,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: The ploughman lost his sweat, and the green corn

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Hath rotted ere his youth attaind a beard;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: The fold stands empty in the drowned field,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And crows are fatted with the murrion flock;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: The nine mens morris is filld up with mud,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And the quaint mazes in the wanton green

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: For lack of tread are undistinguishable:

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: The human mortals want their winter here;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: No night is now with hymn or carol blest:

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Therefore the moon, the governess of floods,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Pale in her anger, washes all the air,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: That rheumatic diseases do abound:

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And thorough this distemperature we see

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: The seasons alter: hoary-headed frosts

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Far in the fresh lap of the crimson rose,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And on old Hiems thin and icy crown

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: An odorous chaplet of sweet summer buds

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Is, as in mockery, set: the spring, the summer,

speaker: TITANIA

text_entry: What, out of hearing? gone? no sound, no word?

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Alack, where are you speak, an if you hear;

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Speak, of all loves! I swoon almost with fear.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: No? then I well perceive you all not nigh

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Either death or you Ill find immediately.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Exit

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: ACT III

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: SCENE I. The wood. TITANIA lying asleep.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Enter QUINCE, SNUG, BOTTOM, FLUTE, SNOUT, and STARVELING

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Are we all met?

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Pat, pat; and heres a marvellous convenient place

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: for our rehearsal. This green plot shall be our

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: stage, this hawthorn-brake our tiring-house; and we

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: will do it in action as we will do it before the duke.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Peter Quince,--

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: What sayest thou, bully Bottom?

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: There are things in this comedy of Pyramus and

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Thisby that will never please. First, Pyramus must

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: draw a sword to kill himself; which the ladies

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: cannot abide. How answer you that?

speaker: SNOUT
text_entry: Byr lakin, a parlous fear.

speaker: STARVELING
text_entry: I believe we must leave the killing out, when all is done.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Not a whit: I have a device to make all well.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Write me a prologue; and let the prologue seem to

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: say, we will do no harm with our swords, and that

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Pyramus is not killed indeed; and, for the more

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: better assurance, tell them that I, Pyramus, am not

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Pyramus, but Bottom the weaver: this will put them

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: out of fear.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Well, we will have such a prologue; and it shall be

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: written in eight and six.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: No, make it two more; let it be written in eight and eight.

speaker: SNOUT
text_entry: Will not the ladies be afeard of the lion?

speaker: STARVELING
text_entry: I fear it, I promise you.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Masters, you ought to consider with yourselves: to

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: bring in--God shield us!--a lion among ladies, is a

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: most dreadful thing; for there is not a more fearful

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: wild-fowl than your lion living; and we ought to

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: look to t.

speaker: SNOUT
text_entry: Therefore another prologue must tell he is not a lion.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Nay, you must name his name, and half his face must

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: be seen through the lions neck: and he himself

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: must speak through, saying thus, or to the same

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: defect,--Ladies,--or Fair-ladies--I would wish

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: You,--or I would request you,--or I would

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: entreat you,--not to fear, not to tremble: my life

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: for yours. If you think I come hither as a lion, it

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: were pity of my life: no I am no such thing; I am a

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: man as other men are; and there indeed let him name

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: his name, and tell them plainly he is Snug the joiner.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Well it shall be so. But there is two hard things;

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: that is, to bring the moonlight into a chamber; for,

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: you know, Pyramus and Thisby meet by moonlight.

speaker: SNOUT
text_entry: Doth the moon shine that night we play our play?

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: A calendar, a calendar! look in the almanac; find

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: out moonshine, find out moonshine.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Yes, it doth shine that night.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Why, then may you leave a casement of the great

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: chamber window, where we play, open, and the moon

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: may shine in at the casement.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Ay; or else one must come in with a bush of thorns

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: and a lanthorn, and say he comes to disfigure, or to

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: present, the person of Moonshine. Then, there is

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: another thing: we must have a wall in the great

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: chamber; for Pyramus and Thisby says the story, did

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: talk through the chink of a wall.

speaker: SNOUT
text_entry: You can never bring in a wall. What say you, Bottom?

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Some man or other must present Wall: and let him

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: have some plaster, or some loam, or some rough-cast

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: about him, to signify wall; and let him hold his

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: fingers thus, and through that cranny shall Pyramus

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: and Thisby whisper.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: If that may be, then all is well. Come, sit  down,

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: every mothers son, and rehearse your parts.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Pyramus, you begin: when you have spoken your

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: speech, enter into that brake: and so every one

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: according to his cue.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Enter PUCK behind

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: What hempen home-spuns have we swaggering here,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: So near the cradle of the fairy queen?

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: What, a play toward! Ill be an auditor;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: An actor too, perhaps, if I see cause.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Speak, Pyramus. Thisby, stand forth.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Thisby, the flowers of odious savours sweet,--

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Odours, odours.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: --odours savours sweet:

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: So hath thy breath, my dearest Thisby dear.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: But hark, a voice! stay thou but here awhile,

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: And by and by I will to thee appear.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Exit

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: A stranger Pyramus than eer played here.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Exit

speaker: FLUTE
text_entry: Must I speak now?

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Ay, marry, must you; for you must understand he goes

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: but to see a noise that he heard, and is to come again.

speaker: FLUTE
text_entry: Most radiant Pyramus, most lily-white of hue,

speaker: FLUTE
text_entry: Of colour like the red rose on triumphant brier,

speaker: FLUTE
text_entry: Most brisky juvenal and eke most lovely Jew,

speaker: FLUTE
text_entry: As true as truest horse that yet would never tire,

speaker: FLUTE
text_entry: Ill meet thee, Pyramus, at Ninnys tomb.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Ninus tomb, man: why, you must not speak that

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: yet; that you answer to Pyramus: you speak all your

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: part at once, cues and all Pyramus enter: your cue

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: is past; it is, never tire.

speaker: FLUTE
text_entry: O,--As true as truest horse, that yet would

speaker: FLUTE
text_entry: never tire.

speaker: FLUTE
text_entry: Re-enter PUCK, and BOTTOM with an asss head

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: If I were fair, Thisby, I were only thine.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: O monstrous! O strange! we are haunted. Pray,

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: masters! fly, masters! Help!

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Exeunt QUINCE, SNUG, FLUTE, SNOUT, and STARVELING

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Ill follow you, Ill lead you about a round,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Through bog, through bush, through brake, through brier:

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Sometime a horse Ill be, sometime a hound,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: A hog, a headless bear, sometime a fire;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And neigh, and bark, and grunt, and roar, and burn,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Like horse, hound, hog, bear, fire, at every turn.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Exit

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Why do they run away? this is a knavery of them to

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: make me afeard.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Re-enter SNOUT

speaker: SNOUT
text_entry: O Bottom, thou art changed! what do I see on thee?

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: What do you see? you see an asshead of your own, do

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: you?

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Exit SNOUT

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Re-enter QUINCE

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Bless thee, Bottom! bless thee! thou art

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: translated.

speaker: QUINCE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: I see their knavery: this is to make an ass of me;

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: to fright me, if they could. But I will not stir

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: from this place, do what they can: I will walk up

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: and down here, and I will sing, that they shall hear

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: I am not afraid.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Sings

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: The ousel cock so black of hue,

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: With orange-tawny bill,

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: The throstle with his note so true,

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: The wren with little quill,--

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: [Awaking]  What angel wakes me from my flowery bed?

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: [Sings]

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: The finch, the sparrow and the lark,

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: The plain-song cuckoo gray,

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Whose note full many a man doth mark,

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: And dares not answer nay;--

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: for, indeed, who would set his wit to so foolish

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: a bird? who would give a bird the lie, though he cry

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: cuckoo never so?

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: I pray thee, gentle mortal, sing again:

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Mine ear is much enamourd of thy note;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: So is mine eye enthralled to thy shape;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And thy fair virtues force perforce doth move me

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: On the first view to say, to swear, I love thee.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Methinks, mistress, you should have little reason

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: for that: and yet, to say the truth, reason and

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: love keep little company together now-a-days; the

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: more the pity that some honest neighbours will not

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: make them friends. Nay, I can gleek upon occasion.

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Thou art as wise as thou art beautiful.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Not so, neither: but if I had wit enough to get out

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: of this wood, I have enough to serve mine own turn.

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Out of this wood do not desire to go:

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Thou shalt remain here, whether thou wilt or no.

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: I am a spirit of no common rate;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: The summer still doth tend upon my state;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And I do love thee: therefore, go with me;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Ill give thee fairies to attend on thee,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And they shall fetch thee jewels from the deep,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And sing while thou on pressed flowers dost sleep;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And I will purge thy mortal grossness so

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: That thou shalt like an airy spirit go.

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Peaseblossom! Cobweb! Moth! and Mustardseed!

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Enter PEASEBLOSSOM, COBWEB, MOTH, and MUSTARDSEED

speaker: PEASEBLOSSOM
text_entry: Ready.

speaker: COBWEB
text_entry: And I.

speaker: MOTH
text_entry: And I.

speaker: MUSTARDSEED
text_entry: And I.

speaker: ALL
text_entry: Where shall we go?

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Be kind and courteous to this gentleman;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Hop in his walks and gambol in his eyes;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Feed him with apricocks and dewberries,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: With purple grapes, green figs, and mulberries;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: The honey-bags steal from the humble-bees,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And for night-tapers crop their waxen thighs

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And light them at the fiery glow-worms eyes,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: To have my love to bed and to arise;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And pluck the wings from Painted butterflies

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: To fan the moonbeams from his sleeping eyes:

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Nod to him, elves, and do him courtesies.

speaker: PEASEBLOSSOM
text_entry: Hail, mortal!

speaker: COBWEB
text_entry: Hail!

speaker: MOTH
text_entry: Hail!

speaker: MUSTARDSEED
text_entry: Hail!

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: I cry your worships mercy, heartily: I beseech your

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: worships name.

speaker: COBWEB
text_entry: Cobweb.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: I shall desire you of more acquaintance, good Master

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Cobweb: if I cut my finger, I shall make bold with

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: you. Your name, honest gentleman?

speaker: PEASEBLOSSOM
text_entry: Peaseblossom.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: I pray you, commend me to Mistress Squash, your

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: mother, and to Master Peascod, your father. Good

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Master Peaseblossom, I shall desire you of more

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: acquaintance too. Your name, I beseech you, sir?

speaker: MUSTARDSEED
text_entry: Mustardseed.

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Good Master Mustardseed, I know your patience well:

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: that same cowardly, giant-like ox-beef hath

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: devoured many a gentleman of your house: I promise

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: you your kindred had made my eyes water ere now. I

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: desire your more acquaintance, good Master

speaker: BOTTOM
text_entry: Mustardseed.

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Come, wait upon him; lead him to my bower.

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: The moon methinks looks with a watery eye;

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: And when she weeps, weeps every little flower,

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Lamenting some enforced chastity.

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Tie up my loves tongue bring him silently.

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: SCENE II. Another part of the wood.

speaker: TITANIA
text_entry: Enter OBERON

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: I wonder if Titania be awaked;

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Then, what it was that next came in her eye,

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Which she must dote on in extremity.

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Enter PUCK

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Here comes my messenger.

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: How now, mad spirit!

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: What night-rule now about this haunted grove?

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: My mistress with a monster is in love.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Near to her close and consecrated bower,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: While she was in her dull and sleeping hour,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: A crew of patches, rude mechanicals,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: That work for bread upon Athenian stalls,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Were met together to rehearse a play

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Intended for great Theseus nuptial-day.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: The shallowest thick-skin of that barren sort,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Who Pyramus presented, in their sport

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Forsook his scene and enterd in a brake

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: When I did him at this advantage take,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: An asss nole I fixed on his head:

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Anon his Thisbe must be answered,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And forth my mimic comes. When they him spy,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: As wild geese that the creeping fowler eye,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Or russet-pated choughs, many in sort,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Rising and cawing at the guns report,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Sever themselves and madly sweep the sky,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: So, at his sight, away his fellows fly;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And, at our stamp, here oer and oer one falls;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: He murder cries and help from Athens calls.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Their sense thus weak, lost with their fears

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: thus strong,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Made senseless things begin to do them wrong;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: For briers and thorns at their apparel snatch;

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Some sleeves, some hats, from yielders all

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: things catch.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: I led them on in this distracted fear,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And left sweet Pyramus translated there:

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: When in that moment, so it came to pass,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Titania waked and straightway loved an ass.

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: This falls out better than I could devise.

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: But hast thou yet latchd the Athenians eyes

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: With the love-juice, as I did bid thee do?

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: I took him sleeping,--that is finishd too,--

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: And the Athenian woman by his side:

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: That, when he waked, of force she must be eyed.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Enter HERMIA and DEMETRIUS

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Stand close: this is the same Athenian.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: This is the woman, but not this the man.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: O, why rebuke you him that loves you so?

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Lay breath so bitter on your bitter foe.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Now I but chide; but I should use thee worse,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: For thou, I fear, hast given me cause to curse,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: If thou hast slain Lysander in his sleep,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Being oer shoes in blood, plunge in the deep,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: And kill me too.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: The sun was not so true unto the day

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: As he to me: would he have stolen away

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: From sleeping Hermia? Ill believe as soon

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: This whole earth may be bored and that the moon

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: May through the centre creep and so displease

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Her brothers noontide with Antipodes.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: It cannot be but thou hast murderd him;

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: So should a murderer look, so dead, so grim.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: So should the murderd look, and so should I,

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Pierced through the heart with your stern cruelty:

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Yet you, the murderer, look as bright, as clear,

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: As yonder Venus in her glimmering sphere.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Whats this to my Lysander? where is he?

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Ah, good Demetrius, wilt thou give him me?

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: I had rather give his carcass to my hounds.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Out, dog! out, cur! thou drivest me past the bounds

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Of maidens patience. Hast thou slain him, then?

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Henceforth be never numberd among men!

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: O, once tell true, tell true, even for my sake!

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Durst thou have lookd upon him being awake,

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: And hast thou killd him sleeping? O brave touch!

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Could not a worm, an adder, do so much?

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: An adder did it; for with doubler tongue

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Than thine, thou serpent, never adder stung.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: You spend your passion on a misprised mood:

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: I am not guilty of Lysanders blood;

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Nor is he dead, for aught that I can tell.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: I pray thee, tell me then that he is well.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: An if I could, what should I get therefore?

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: A privilege never to see me more.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: And from thy hated presence part I so:

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: See me no more, whether he be dead or no.

speaker: HERMIA
text_entry: Exit

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: There is no following her in this fierce vein:

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Here therefore for a while I will remain.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: So sorrows heaviness doth heavier grow

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: For debt that bankrupt sleep doth sorrow owe:

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Which now in some slight measure it will pay,

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: If for his tender here I make some stay.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Lies down and sleeps

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: What hast thou done? thou hast mistaken quite

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: And laid the love-juice on some true-loves sight:

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Of thy misprision must perforce ensue

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Some true love turnd and not a false turnd true.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Then fate oer-rules, that, one man holding troth,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: A million fail, confounding oath on oath.

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: About the wood go swifter than the wind,

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: And Helena of Athens look thou find:

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: All fancy-sick she is and pale of cheer,

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: With sighs of love, that costs the fresh blood dear:

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: By some illusion see thou bring her here:

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Ill charm his eyes against she do appear.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: I go, I go; look how I go,

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Swifter than arrow from the Tartars bow.

speaker: PUCK
text_entry: Exit

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Flower of this purple dye,

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Hit with Cupids archery,

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Sink in apple of his eye.

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: When his love he doth espy,

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: Let her shine as gloriously

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: As the Venus of the sky.

speaker: OBERON
text_entry: When thou wakest, if she be by,

speaker: OBERON

text_entry: Enter LEONATO, HERO, and BEATRICE, with a Messenger

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: I learn in this letter that Don Peter of Arragon

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: comes this night to Messina.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: He is very near by this: he was not three leagues off

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: when I left him.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: How many gentlemen have you lost in this action?

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: But few of any sort, and none of name.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: A victory is twice itself when the achiever brings

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: home full numbers. I find here that Don Peter hath

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: bestowed much honour on a young Florentine called Claudio.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Much deserved on his part and equally remembered by

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Don Pedro: he hath borne himself beyond the

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: promise of his age, doing, in the figure of a lamb,

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: the feats of a lion: he hath indeed better

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: bettered expectation than you must expect of me to

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: tell you how.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: He hath an uncle here in Messina will be very much

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: glad of it.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: I have already delivered him letters, and there

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: appears much joy in him; even so much that joy could

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: not show itself modest enough without a badge of

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: bitterness.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Did he break out into tears?

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: In great measure.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: A kind overflow of kindness: there are no faces

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: truer than those that are so washed. How much

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: better is it to weep at joy than to joy at weeping!

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: I pray you, is Signior Mountanto returned from the

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: wars or no?

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: I know none of that name, lady: there was none such

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: in the army of any sort.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: What is he that you ask for, niece?

speaker: HERO
text_entry: My cousin means Signior Benedick of Padua.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: O, hes returned; and as pleasant as ever he was.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: He set up his bills here in Messina and challenged

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Cupid at the flight; and my uncles fool, reading

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: the challenge, subscribed for Cupid, and challenged

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: him at the bird-bolt. I pray you, how many hath he

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: killed and eaten in these wars? But how many hath

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: he killed? for indeed I promised to eat all of his killing.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Faith, niece, you tax Signior Benedick too much;

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: but hell be meet with you, I doubt it not.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: He hath done good service, lady, in these wars.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: You had musty victual, and he hath holp to eat it:

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: he is a very valiant trencherman; he hath an

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: excellent stomach.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: And a good soldier too, lady.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: And a good soldier to a lady: but what is he to a lord?

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: A lord to a lord, a man to a man; stuffed with all

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: honourable virtues.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: It is so, indeed; he is no less than a stuffed man:

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: but for the stuffing,--well, we are all mortal.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: You must not, sir, mistake my niece. There is a

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: kind of merry war betwixt Signior Benedick and her:

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: they never meet but theres a skirmish of wit

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: between them.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Alas! he gets nothing by that. In our last

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: conflict four of his five wits went halting off, and

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: now is the whole man governed with one: so that if

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: he have wit enough to keep himself warm, let him

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: bear it for a difference between himself and his

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: horse; for it is all the wealth that he hath left,

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: to be known a reasonable creature. Who is his

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: companion now? He hath every month a new sworn brother.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Ist possible?

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Very easily possible: he wears his faith but as

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: the fashion of his hat; it ever changes with the

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: next block.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: I see, lady, the gentleman is not in your books.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: No; an he were, I would burn my study. But, I pray

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: you, who is his companion? Is there no young

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: squarer now that will make a voyage with him to the devil?

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: He is most in the company of the right noble Claudio.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: O Lord, he will hang upon him like a disease: he

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: is sooner caught than the pestilence, and the taker

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: runs presently mad. God help the noble Claudio! if

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: he have caught the Benedick, it will cost him a

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: thousand pound ere a be cured.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: I will hold friends with you, lady.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Do, good friend.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: You will never run mad, niece.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: No, not till a hot January.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Good Signior Leonato, you are come to meet your

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: trouble: the fashion of the world is to avoid

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: cost, and you encounter it.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Never came trouble to my house in the likeness of

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: your grace: for trouble being gone, comfort should

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: remain; but when you depart from me, sorrow abides

text_entry: and happiness takes his leave.

text_entry: You embrace your charge too willingly. I think this

text_entry: is your daughter.
