text_entry: Her mother hath many times told me so.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Were you in doubt, sir, that you asked her?

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Signior Benedick, no; for then were you a child.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: You have it full, Benedick: we may guess by this

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: what you are, being a man. Truly, the lady fathers

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: herself. Be happy, lady; for you are like an

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: honourable father.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: If Signior Leonato be her father, she would not

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: have his head on her shoulders for all Messina, as

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: like him as she is.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: I wonder that you will still be talking, Signior

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Benedick: nobody marks you.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: What, my dear Lady Disdain! are you yet living?

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Is it possible disdain should die while she hath

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: such meet food to feed it as Signior Benedick?

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Courtesy itself must convert to disdain, if you come

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: in her presence.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Then is courtesy a turncoat. But it is certain I

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: am loved of all ladies, only you excepted: and I

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: would I could find in my heart that I had not a hard

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: heart; for, truly, I love none.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: A dear happiness to women: they would else have

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: been troubled with a pernicious suitor. I thank God

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: and my cold blood, I am of your humour for that: I

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: had rather hear my dog bark at a crow than a man

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: swear he loves me.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: God keep your ladyship still in that mind! so some

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: gentleman or other shall scape a predestinate

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: scratched face.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Scratching could not make it worse, an twere such

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: a face as yours were.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Well, you are a rare parrot-teacher.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: A bird of my tongue is better than a beast of yours.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I would my horse had the speed of your tongue, and

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: so good a continuer. But keep your way, i Gods

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: name; I have done.

text_entry: You always end with a jades trick: I know you of old.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: That is the sum of all, Leonato. Signior Claudio

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: and Signior Benedick, my dear friend Leonato hath

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: invited you all. I tell him we shall stay here at

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: the least a month; and he heartily prays some

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: occasion may detain us longer. I dare swear he is no

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: hypocrite, but prays from his heart.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: If you swear, my lord, you shall not be forsworn.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: To DON JOHN

text_entry: Let me bid you welcome, my lord: being reconciled to

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: the prince your brother, I owe you all duty.

text_entry: I thank you: I am not of many words, but I thank

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: you.

text_entry: Please it your grace lead on?

text_entry: Your hand, Leonato; we will go together.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Benedick, didst thou note the daughter of Signior Leonato?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I noted her not; but I looked on her.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Is she not a modest young lady?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Do you question me, as an honest man should do, for

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: my simple true judgment; or would you have me speak

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: after my custom, as being a professed tyrant to their sex?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: No; I pray thee speak in sober judgment.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Why, i faith, methinks shes too low for a high

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: praise, too brown for a fair praise and too little

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: for a great praise: only this commendation I can

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: afford her, that were she other than she is, she

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: were unhandsome; and being no other but as she is, I

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: do not like her.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Thou thinkest I am in sport: I pray thee tell me

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: truly how thou likest her.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Would you buy her, that you inquire after her?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Can the world buy such a jewel?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Yea, and a case to put it into. But speak you this

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: with a sad brow? or do you play the flouting Jack,

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: to tell us Cupid is a good hare-finder and Vulcan a

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: rare carpenter? Come, in what key shall a man take

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: you, to go in the song?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: In mine eye she is the sweetest lady that ever I

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: looked on.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I can see yet without spectacles and I see no such

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: matter: theres her cousin, an she were not

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: possessed with a fury, exceeds her as much in beauty

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: as the first of May doth the last of December. But I

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: hope you have no intent to turn husband, have you?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: I would scarce trust myself, though I had sworn the

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: contrary, if Hero would be my wife.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Ist come to this? In faith, hath not the world

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: one man but he will wear his cap with suspicion?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Shall I never see a bachelor of three-score again?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Go to, i faith; an thou wilt needs thrust thy neck

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: into a yoke, wear the print of it and sigh away

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Sundays. Look Don Pedro is returned to seek you.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: What secret hath held you here, that you followed

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: not to Leonatos?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I would your grace would constrain me to tell.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: I charge thee on thy allegiance.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: You hear, Count Claudio: I can be secret as a dumb

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: man; I would have you think so; but, on my

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: allegiance, mark you this, on my allegiance. He is

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: in love. With who? now that is your graces part.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Mark how short his answer is;--With Hero, Leonatos

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: short daughter.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: If this were so, so were it uttered.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Like the old tale, my lord: it is not so, nor

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: twas not so, but, indeed, God forbid it should be

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: so.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: If my passion change not shortly, God forbid it

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: should be otherwise.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Amen, if you love her; for the lady is very well worthy.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: You speak this to fetch me in, my lord.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: By my troth, I speak my thought.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: And, in faith, my lord, I spoke mine.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: And, by my two faiths and troths, my lord, I spoke mine.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: That I love her, I feel.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: That she is worthy, I know.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: That I neither feel how she should be loved nor

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: know how she should be worthy, is the opinion that

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: fire cannot melt out of me: I will die in it at the stake.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Thou wast ever an obstinate heretic in the despite

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: of beauty.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: And never could maintain his part but in the force

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: of his will.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: That a woman conceived me, I thank her; that she

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: brought me up, I likewise give her most humble

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: thanks: but that I will have a recheat winded in my

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: forehead, or hang my bugle in an invisible baldrick,

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: all women shall pardon me. Because I will not do

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: them the wrong to mistrust any, I will do myself the

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: right to trust none; and the fine is, for the which

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I may go the finer, I will live a bachelor.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: I shall see thee, ere I die, look pale with love.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: With anger, with sickness, or with hunger, my lord,

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: not with love: prove that ever I lose more blood

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: with love than I will get again with drinking, pick

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: out mine eyes with a ballad-makers pen and hang me

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: up at the door of a brothel-house for the sign of

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: blind Cupid.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Well, if ever thou dost fall from this faith, thou

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: wilt prove a notable argument.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: If I do, hang me in a bottle like a cat and shoot

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: at me; and he that hits me, let him be clapped on

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: the shoulder, and called Adam.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Well, as time shall try: In time the savage bull

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: doth bear the yoke.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: The savage bull may; but if ever the sensible

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Benedick bear it, pluck off the bulls horns and set

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: them in my forehead: and let me be vilely painted,

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: and in such great letters as they write Here is

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: good horse to hire, let them signify under my sign

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Here you may see Benedick the married man.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: If this should ever happen, thou wouldst be horn-mad.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Nay, if Cupid have not spent all his quiver in

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Venice, thou wilt quake for this shortly.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I look for an earthquake too, then.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Well, you temporize with the hours. In the

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: meantime, good Signior Benedick, repair to

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Leonatos: commend me to him and tell him I will

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: not fail him at supper; for indeed he hath made

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: great preparation.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I have almost matter enough in me for such an

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: embassage; and so I commit you--

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: To the tuition of God: From my house, if I had it,--

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: The sixth of July: Your loving friend, Benedick.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Nay, mock not, mock not. The body of your

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: discourse is sometime guarded with fragments, and

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: the guards are but slightly basted on neither: ere

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: you flout old ends any further, examine your

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: conscience: and so I leave you.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Exit

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: My liege, your highness now may do me good.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: My love is thine to teach: teach it but how,

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And thou shalt see how apt it is to learn

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Any hard lesson that may do thee good.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Hath Leonato any son, my lord?

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: No child but Hero; shes his only heir.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Dost thou affect her, Claudio?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: O, my lord,

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: When you went onward on this ended action,

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: I lookd upon her with a soldiers eye,

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: That liked, but had a rougher task in hand

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Than to drive liking to the name of love:

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: But now I am returnd and that war-thoughts

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Have left their places vacant, in their rooms

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Come thronging soft and delicate desires,

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: All prompting me how fair young Hero is,

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Saying, I liked her ere I went to wars.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Thou wilt be like a lover presently

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And tire the hearer with a book of words.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: If thou dost love fair Hero, cherish it,

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And I will break with her and with her father,

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And thou shalt have her. Wast not to this end

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: That thou beganst to twist so fine a story?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: How sweetly you do minister to love,

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: That know loves grief by his complexion!

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: But lest my liking might too sudden seem,

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: I would have salved it with a longer treatise.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: What need the bridge much broader than the flood?

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: The fairest grant is the necessity.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Look, what will serve is fit: tis once, thou lovest,

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And I will fit thee with the remedy.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: I know we shall have revelling to-night:

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: I will assume thy part in some disguise

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And tell fair Hero I am Claudio,

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And in her bosom Ill unclasp my heart

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And take her hearing prisoner with the force

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And strong encounter of my amorous tale:

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Then after to her father will I break;

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And the conclusion is, she shall be thine.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: In practise let us put it presently.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: SCENE II. A room in LEONATOs house.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Enter LEONATO and ANTONIO, meeting

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: How now, brother! Where is my cousin, your son?

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: hath he provided this music?

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: He is very busy about it. But, brother, I can tell

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: you strange news that you yet dreamt not of.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Are they good?

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: As the event stamps them: but they have a good

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: cover; they show well outward. The prince and Count

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: Claudio, walking in a thick-pleached alley in mine

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: orchard, were thus much overheard by a man of mine:

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: the prince discovered to Claudio that he loved my

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: niece your daughter and meant to acknowledge it

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: this night in a dance: and if he found her

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: accordant, he meant to take the present time by the

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: top and instantly break with you of it.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Hath the fellow any wit that told you this?

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: A good sharp fellow: I will send for him; and

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: question him yourself.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: No, no; we will hold it as a dream till it appear

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: itself: but I will acquaint my daughter withal,

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: that she may be the better prepared for an answer,

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: if peradventure this be true. Go you and tell her of it.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Enter Attendants

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Cousins, you know what you have to do. O, I cry you

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: mercy, friend; go you with me, and I will use your

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: skill. Good cousin, have a care this busy time.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: SCENE III. The same.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Enter DON JOHN and CONRADE

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: What the good-year, my lord! why are you thus out

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: of measure sad?

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: There is no measure in the occasion that breeds;

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: therefore the sadness is without limit.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: You should hear reason.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: And when I have heard it, what blessing brings it?

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: If not a present remedy, at least a patient

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: sufferance.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: I wonder that thou, being, as thou sayest thou art,

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: born under Saturn, goest about to apply a moral

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: medicine to a mortifying mischief. I cannot hide

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: what I am: I must be sad when I have cause and smile

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: at no mans jests, eat when I have stomach and wait

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: for no mans leisure, sleep when I am drowsy and

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: tend on no mans business, laugh when I am merry and

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: claw no man in his humour.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: Yea, but you must not make the full show of this

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: till you may do it without controlment. You have of

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: late stood out against your brother, and he hath

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: taen you newly into his grace; where it is

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: impossible you should take true root but by the

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: fair weather that you make yourself: it is needful

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: that you frame the season for your own harvest.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: I had rather be a canker in a hedge than a rose in

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: his grace, and it better fits my blood to be

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: disdained of all than to fashion a carriage to rob

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: love from any: in this, though I cannot be said to

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: be a flattering honest man, it must not be denied

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: but I am a plain-dealing villain. I am trusted with

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: a muzzle and enfranchised with a clog; therefore I

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: have decreed not to sing in my cage. If I had my

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: mouth, I would bite; if I had my liberty, I would do

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: my liking: in the meantime let me be that I am and

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: seek not to alter me.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: Can you make no use of your discontent?

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: I make all use of it, for I use it only.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Who comes here?

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Enter BORACHIO

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: What news, Borachio?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: I came yonder from a great supper: the prince your

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: brother is royally entertained by Leonato: and I

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: can give you intelligence of an intended marriage.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Will it serve for any model to build mischief on?

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: What is he for a fool that betroths himself to

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: unquietness?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Marry, it is your brothers right hand.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Who? the most exquisite Claudio?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Even he.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: A proper squire! And who, and who? which way looks

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: he?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Marry, on Hero, the daughter and heir of Leonato.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: A very forward March-chick! How came you to this?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Being entertained for a perfumer, as I was smoking a

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: musty room, comes me the prince and Claudio, hand

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: in hand in sad conference: I whipt me behind the

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: arras; and there heard it agreed upon that the

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: prince should woo Hero for himself, and having

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: obtained her, give her to Count Claudio.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Come, come, let us thither: this may prove food to

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: my displeasure. That young start-up hath all the

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: glory of my overthrow: if I can cross him any way, I

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: bless myself every way. You are both sure, and will assist me?

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: To the death, my lord.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Let us to the great supper: their cheer is the

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: greater that I am subdued. Would the cook were of

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: my mind! Shall we go prove whats to be done?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Well wait upon your lordship.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: ACT II

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: SCENE I. A hall in LEONATOS house.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Enter LEONATO, ANTONIO, HERO, BEATRICE, and others

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Was not Count John here at supper?

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: I saw him not.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: How tartly that gentleman looks! I never can see

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: him but I am heart-burned an hour after.

speaker: HERO
text_entry: He is of a very melancholy disposition.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: He were an excellent man that were made just in the

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: midway between him and Benedick: the one is too

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: like an image and says nothing, and the other too

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: like my ladys eldest son, evermore tattling.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Then half Signior Benedicks tongue in Count Johns

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: mouth, and half Count Johns melancholy in Signior

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Benedicks face,--

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: With a good leg and a good foot, uncle, and money

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: enough in his purse, such a man would win any woman

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: in the world, if a could get her good-will.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: By my troth, niece, thou wilt never get thee a

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: husband, if thou be so shrewd of thy tongue.

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: In faith, shes too curst.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Too curst is more than curst: I shall lessen Gods

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: sending that way; for it is said, God sends a curst

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: cow short horns; but to a cow too curst he sends none.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: So, by being too curst, God will send you no horns.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Just, if he send me no husband; for the which

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: blessing I am at him upon my knees every morning and

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: evening. Lord, I could not endure a husband with a

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: beard on his face: I had rather lie in the woollen.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: You may light on a husband that hath no beard.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: What should I do with him? dress him in my apparel

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: and make him my waiting-gentlewoman? He that hath a

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: beard is more than a youth, and he that hath no

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: beard is less than a man: and he that is more than

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: a youth is not for me, and he that is less than a

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: man, I am not for him: therefore, I will even take

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: sixpence in earnest of the bear-ward, and lead his

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: apes into hell.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Well, then, go you into hell?

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: No, but to the gate; and there will the devil meet

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: me, like an old cuckold, with horns on his head, and

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: say Get you to heaven, Beatrice, get you to

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: heaven; heres no place for you maids: so deliver

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: I up my apes, and away to Saint Peter for the

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: heavens; he shows me where the bachelors sit, and

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: there live we as merry as the day is long.

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: [To HERO]  Well, niece, I trust you will be ruled

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: by your father.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Yes, faith; it is my cousins duty to make curtsy

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: and say Father, as it please you. But yet for all

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: that, cousin, let him be a handsome fellow, or else

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: make another curtsy and say Father, as it please

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: me.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Well, niece, I hope to see you one day fitted with a husband.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Not till God make men of some other metal than

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: earth. Would it not grieve a woman to be

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: overmastered with a pierce of valiant dust? to make

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: an account of her life to a clod of wayward marl?

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: No, uncle, Ill none: Adams sons are my brethren;

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: and, truly, I hold it a sin to match in my kindred.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Daughter, remember what I told you: if the prince

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: do solicit you in that kind, you know your answer.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: The fault will be in the music, cousin, if you be

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: not wooed in good time: if the prince be too

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: important, tell him there is measure in every thing

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: and so dance out the answer. For, hear me, Hero:

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: wooing, wedding, and repenting, is as a Scotch jig,

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: a measure, and a cinque pace: the first suit is hot

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: and hasty, like a Scotch jig, and full as

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: fantastical; the wedding, mannerly-modest, as a

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: measure, full of state and ancientry; and then comes

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: repentance and, with his bad legs, falls into the

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: cinque pace faster and faster, till he sink into his grave.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Cousin, you apprehend passing shrewdly.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: I have a good eye, uncle; I can see a church by daylight.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: The revellers are entering, brother: make good room.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: All put on their masks

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Enter DON PEDRO, CLAUDIO, BENEDICK, BALTHASAR, DON JOHN, BORACHIO, MARGARET, URSULA and others, masked

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Lady, will you walk about with your friend?

speaker: HERO
text_entry: So you walk softly and look sweetly and say nothing,

speaker: HERO
text_entry: I am yours for the walk; and especially when I walk away.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: With me in your company?

speaker: HERO
text_entry: I may say so, when I please.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And when please you to say so?

speaker: HERO
text_entry: When I like your favour; for God defend the lute

speaker: HERO
text_entry: should be like the case!

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: My visor is Philemons roof; within the house is Jove.

speaker: HERO
text_entry: Why, then, your visor should be thatched.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Speak low, if you speak love.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Drawing her aside

speaker: BALTHASAR
text_entry: Well, I would you did like me.

speaker: MARGARET
text_entry: So would not I, for your own sake; for I have many

speaker: MARGARET
text_entry: ill-qualities.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text_entry: Which is one?

speaker: MARGARET
text_entry: I say my prayers aloud.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text_entry: I love you the better: the hearers may cry, Amen.

speaker: MARGARET
text_entry: God match me with a good dancer!

speaker: BALTHASAR
text_entry: Amen.

speaker: MARGARET
text_entry: And God keep him out of my sight when the dance is

speaker: MARGARET
text_entry: done! Answer, clerk.

speaker: BALTHASAR
text_entry: No more words: the clerk is answered.

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: I know you well enough; you are Signior Antonio.

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: At a word, I am not.

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: I know you by the waggling of your head.

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: To tell you true, I counterfeit him.

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: You could never do him so ill-well, unless you were

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: the very man. Heres his dry hand up and down: you

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: are he, you are he.

speaker: ANTONIO
text_entry: At a word, I am not.

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: Come, come, do you think I do not know you by your

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: excellent wit? can virtue hide itself? Go to,

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: mum, you are he: graces will appear, and theres an

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: end.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Will you not tell me who told you so?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: No, you shall pardon me.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Nor will you not tell me who you are?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Not now.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: That I was disdainful, and that I had my good wit

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: out of the Hundred Merry Tales:--well this was

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Signior Benedick that said so.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Whats he?

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: I am sure you know him well enough.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Not I, believe me.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Did he never make you laugh?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I pray you, what is he?

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Why, he is the princes jester: a very dull fool;

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: only his gift is in devising impossible slanders:

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: none but libertines delight in him; and the

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: commendation is not in his wit, but in his villany;

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: for he both pleases men and angers them, and then

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: they laugh at him and beat him. I am sure he is in

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: the fleet: I would he had boarded me.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: When I know the gentleman, Ill tell him what you say.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Do, do: hell but break a comparison or two on me;

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: which, peradventure not marked or not laughed at,

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: strikes him into melancholy; and then theres a

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: partridge wing saved, for the fool will eat no

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: supper that night.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Music

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: We must follow the leaders.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: In every good thing.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Nay, if they lead to any ill, I will leave them at

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: the next turning.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Dance. Then exeunt all except DON JOHN, BORACHIO, and CLAUDIO

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Sure my brother is amorous on Hero and hath

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: withdrawn her father to break with him about it.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: The ladies follow her and but one visor remains.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: And that is Claudio: I know him by his bearing.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Are not you Signior Benedick?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: You know me well; I am he.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Signior, you are very near my brother in his love:

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: he is enamoured on Hero; I pray you, dissuade him

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: from her: she is no equal for his birth: you may

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: do the part of an honest man in it.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: How know you he loves her?

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: I heard him swear his affection.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: So did I too; and he swore he would marry her to-night.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Come, let us to the banquet.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Exeunt DON JOHN and BORACHIO

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Thus answer I in the name of Benedick,

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: But hear these ill news with the ears of Claudio.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Tis certain so; the prince wooes for himself.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Friendship is constant in all other things

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Save in the office and affairs of love:

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Therefore, all hearts in love use their own tongues;

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Let every eye negotiate for itself

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: And trust no agent; for beauty is a witch

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Against whose charms faith melteth into blood.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: This is an accident of hourly proof,

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Which I mistrusted not. Farewell, therefore, Hero!

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Re-enter BENEDICK

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Count Claudio?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Yea, the same.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Come, will you go with me?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Whither?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Even to the next willow, about your own business,

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: county. What fashion will you wear the garland of?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: about your neck, like an usurers chain? or under

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: your arm, like a lieutenants scarf? You must wear

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: it one way, for the prince hath got your Hero.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: I wish him joy of her.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Why, thats spoken like an honest drovier: so they

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: sell bullocks. But did you think the prince would

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: have served you thus?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: I pray you, leave me.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Ho! now you strike like the blind man: twas the

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: boy that stole your meat, and youll beat the post.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: If it will not be, Ill leave you.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Exit

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Alas, poor hurt fowl! now will he creep into sedges.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: But that my Lady Beatrice should know me, and not

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: know me! The princes fool! Ha? It may be I go

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: under that title because I am merry. Yea, but so I

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: am apt to do myself wrong; I am not so reputed: it

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: is the base, though bitter, disposition of Beatrice

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: that puts the world into her person and so gives me

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: out. Well, Ill be revenged as I may.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Re-enter DON PEDRO

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Now, signior, wheres the count? did you see him?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Troth, my lord, I have played the part of Lady Fame.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I found him here as melancholy as a lodge in a

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: warren: I told him, and I think I told him true,

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: that your grace had got the good will of this young

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: lady; and I offered him my company to a willow-tree,

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: either to make him a garland, as being forsaken, or

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: to bind him up a rod, as being worthy to be whipped.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: To be whipped! Whats his fault?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: The flat transgression of a schoolboy, who, being

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: overjoyed with finding a birds nest, shows it his

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: companion, and he steals it.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Wilt thou make a trust a transgression? The

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: transgression is in the stealer.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Yet it had not been amiss the rod had been made,

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: and the garland too; for the garland he might have

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: worn himself, and the rod he might have bestowed on

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: you, who, as I take it, have stolen his birds nest.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: I will but teach them to sing, and restore them to

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: the owner.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: If their singing answer your saying, by my faith,

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: you say honestly.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: The Lady Beatrice hath a quarrel to you: the

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: gentleman that danced with her told her she is much

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: wronged by you.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: O, she misused me past the endurance of a block!

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: an oak but with one green leaf on it would have

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: answered her; my very visor began to assume life and

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: scold with her. She told me, not thinking I had been

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: myself, that I was the princes jester, that I was

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: duller than a great thaw; huddling jest upon jest

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: with such impossible conveyance upon me that I stood

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: like a man at a mark, with a whole army shooting at

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: me. She speaks poniards, and every word stabs:

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: if her breath were as terrible as her terminations,

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: there were no living near her; she would infect to

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: the north star. I would not marry her, though she

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: were endowed with all that Adam bad left him before

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: he transgressed: she would have made Hercules have

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: turned spit, yea, and have cleft his club to make

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: the fire too. Come, talk not of her: you shall find

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: her the infernal Ate in good apparel. I would to God

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: some scholar would conjure her; for certainly, while

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: she is here, a man may live as quiet in hell as in a

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: sanctuary; and people sin upon purpose, because they

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: would go thither; so, indeed, all disquiet, horror

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: and perturbation follows her.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Look, here she comes.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Enter CLAUDIO, BEATRICE, HERO, and LEONATO

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Will your grace command me any service to the

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: worlds end? I will go on the slightest errand now

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: to the Antipodes that you can devise to send me on;

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I will fetch you a tooth-picker now from the

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: furthest inch of Asia, bring you the length of

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Prester Johns foot, fetch you a hair off the great

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Chams beard, do you any embassage to the Pigmies,

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: rather than hold three words conference with this

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: harpy. You have no employment for me?

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: None, but to desire your good company.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: O God, sir, heres a dish I love not: I cannot

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: endure my Lady Tongue.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Exit

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Come, lady, come; you have lost the heart of

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Signior Benedick.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Indeed, my lord, he lent it me awhile; and I gave

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: him use for it, a double heart for his single one:

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: marry, once before he won it of me with false dice,

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: therefore your grace may well say I have lost it.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: You have put him down, lady, you have put him down.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: So I would not he should do me, my lord, lest I

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: should prove the mother of fools. I have brought

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Count Claudio, whom you sent me to seek.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Why, how now, count! wherefore are you sad?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Not sad, my lord.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: How then? sick?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Neither, my lord.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: The count is neither sad, nor sick, nor merry, nor

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: well; but civil count, civil as an orange, and

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: something of that jealous complexion.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: I faith, lady, I think your blazon to be true;

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: though, Ill be sworn, if he be so, his conceit is

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: false. Here, Claudio, I have wooed in thy name, and

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: fair Hero is won: I have broke with her father,

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: and his good will obtained: name the day of

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: marriage, and God give thee joy!

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Count, take of me my daughter, and with her my

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: fortunes: his grace hath made the match, and an

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: grace say Amen to it.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Speak, count, tis your cue.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Silence is the perfectest herald of joy: I were

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: but little happy, if I could say how much. Lady, as

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: you are mine, I am yours: I give away myself for

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: you and dote upon the exchange.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Speak, cousin; or, if you cannot, stop his mouth

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: with a kiss, and let not him speak neither.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: In faith, lady, you have a merry heart.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Yea, my lord; I thank it, poor fool, it keeps on

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: the windy side of care. My cousin tells him in his

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: ear that he is in her heart.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: And so she doth, cousin.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Good Lord, for alliance! Thus goes every one to the

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: world but I, and I am sunburnt; I may sit in a

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: corner and cry heigh-ho for a husband!

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Lady Beatrice, I will get you one.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: I would rather have one of your fathers getting.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Hath your grace neer a brother like you? Your

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: father got excellent husbands, if a maid could come by them.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Will you have me, lady?

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: No, my lord, unless I might have another for

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: working-days: your grace is too costly to wear

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: every day. But, I beseech your grace, pardon me: I

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: was born to speak all mirth and no matter.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Your silence most offends me, and to be merry best

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: becomes you; for, out of question, you were born in

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: a merry hour.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: No, sure, my lord, my mother cried; but then there

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: was a star danced, and under that was I born.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Cousins, God give you joy!

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Niece, will you look to those things I told you of?

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: I cry you mercy, uncle. By your graces pardon.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: By my troth, a pleasant-spirited lady.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Theres little of the melancholy element in her, my

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: lord: she is never sad but when she sleeps, and

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: not ever sad then; for I have heard my daughter say,

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: she hath often dreamed of unhappiness and waked

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: herself with laughing.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: She cannot endure to hear tell of a husband.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: O, by no means: she mocks all her wooers out of suit.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: She were an excellent wife for Benedict.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: O Lord, my lord, if they were but a week married,

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: they would talk themselves mad.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: County Claudio, when mean you to go to church?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: To-morrow, my lord: time goes on crutches till love

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: have all his rites.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Not till Monday, my dear son, which is hence a just

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: seven-night; and a time too brief, too, to have all

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: things answer my mind.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Come, you shake the head at so long a breathing:

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: but, I warrant thee, Claudio, the time shall not go

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: dully by us. I will in the interim undertake one of

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Hercules labours; which is, to bring Signior

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Benedick and the Lady Beatrice into a mountain of

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: affection the one with the other. I would fain have

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: it a match, and I doubt not but to fashion it, if

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: you three will but minister such assistance as I

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: shall give you direction.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: My lord, I am for you, though it cost me ten

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: nights watchings.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: And I, my lord.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And you too, gentle Hero?

speaker: HERO
text_entry: I will do any modest office, my lord, to help my

speaker: HERO
text_entry: cousin to a good husband.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And Benedick is not the unhopefullest husband that

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: I know. Thus far can I praise him; he is of a noble

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: strain, of approved valour and confirmed honesty. I

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: will teach you how to humour your cousin, that she

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: shall fall in love with Benedick; and I, with your

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: two helps, will so practise on Benedick that, in

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: despite of his quick wit and his queasy stomach, he

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: shall fall in love with Beatrice. If we can do this,

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Cupid is no longer an archer: hi s glory shall be

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: ours, for we are the only love-gods. Go in with me,

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: and I will tell you my drift.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: SCENE II. The same.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Enter DON JOHN and BORACHIO

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: It is so; the Count Claudio shall marry the

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: daughter of Leonato.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Yea, my lord; but I can cross it.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Any bar, any cross, any impediment will be

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: medicinable to me: I am sick in displeasure to him,

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: and whatsoever comes athwart his affection ranges

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: evenly with mine. How canst thou cross this marriage?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Not honestly, my lord; but so covertly that no

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: dishonesty shall appear in me.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Show me briefly how.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: I think I told your lordship a year since, how much

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: I am in the favour of Margaret, the waiting

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: gentlewoman to Hero.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: I remember.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: I can, at any unseasonable instant of the night,

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: appoint her to look out at her ladys chamber window.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: What life is in that, to be the death of this marriage?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: The poison of that lies in you to temper. Go you to

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: the prince your brother; spare not to tell him that

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: he hath wronged his honour in marrying the renowned

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Claudio--whose estimation do you mightily hold

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: up--to a contaminated stale, such a one as Hero.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: What proof shall I make of that?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Proof enough to misuse the prince, to vex Claudio,

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: to undo Hero and kill Leonato. Look you for any

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: other issue?

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Only to despite them, I will endeavour any thing.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Go, then; find me a meet hour to draw Don Pedro and

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: the Count Claudio alone: tell them that you know

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: that Hero loves me; intend a kind of zeal both to the

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: prince and Claudio, as,--in love of your brothers

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: honour, who hath made this match, and his friends

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: reputation, who is thus like to be cozened with the

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: semblance of a maid,--that you have discovered

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: thus. They will scarcely believe this without trial:

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: offer them instances; which shall bear no less

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: likelihood than to see me at her chamber-window,

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: hear me call Margaret Hero, hear Margaret term me

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Claudio; and bring them to see this the very night

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: before the intended wedding,--for in the meantime I

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: will so fashion the matter that Hero shall be

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: absent,--and there shall appear such seeming truth

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: of Heros disloyalty that jealousy shall be called

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: assurance and all the preparation overthrown.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Grow this to what adverse issue it can, I will put

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: it in practise. Be cunning in the working this, and

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: thy fee is a thousand ducats.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Be you constant in the accusation, and my cunning

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: shall not shame me.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: I will presently go learn their day of marriage.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: SCENE III. LEONATOS orchard.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Enter BENEDICK

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Boy!

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Enter Boy

speaker: Boy
text_entry: Signior?

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: In my chamber-window lies a book: bring it hither

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: to me in the orchard.

speaker: Boy
text_entry: I am here already, sir.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I know that; but I would have thee hence, and here again.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Exit Boy

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I do much wonder that one man, seeing how much

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: another man is a fool when he dedicates his

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: behaviors to love, will, after he hath laughed at

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: such shallow follies in others, become the argument

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: of his own scorn by failing in love: and such a man

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: is Claudio. I have known when there was no music

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: with him but the drum and the fife; and now had he

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: rather hear the tabour and the pipe: I have known

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: when he would have walked ten mile a-foot to see a

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: good armour; and now will he lie ten nights awake,

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: carving the fashion of a new doublet. He was wont to

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: speak plain and to the purpose, like an honest man

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: and a soldier; and now is he turned orthography; his

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: words are a very fantastical banquet, just so many

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: strange dishes. May I be so converted and see with

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: these eyes? I cannot tell; I think not: I will not

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: be sworn, but love may transform me to an oyster; but

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Ill take my oath on it, till he have made an oyster

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: of me, he shall never make me such a fool. One woman

speaker: BENEDICK

text_entry: How much an ill word may empoison liking.

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: O, do not do your cousin such a wrong.

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: She cannot be so much without true judgment--

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: Having so swift and excellent a wit

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: As she is prized to have--as to refuse

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: So rare a gentleman as Signior Benedick.

speaker: HERO
text_entry: He is the only man of Italy.

speaker: HERO
text_entry: Always excepted my dear Claudio.

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: I pray you, be not angry with me, madam,

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: Speaking my fancy: Signior Benedick,

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: For shape, for bearing, argument and valour,

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: Goes foremost in report through Italy.

speaker: HERO
text_entry: Indeed, he hath an excellent good name.

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: His excellence did earn it, ere he had it.

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: When are you married, madam?

speaker: HERO
text_entry: Why, every day, to-morrow. Come, go in:

speaker: HERO
text_entry: Ill show thee some attires, and have thy counsel

speaker: HERO
text_entry: Which is the best to furnish me to-morrow.

speaker: URSULA
text_entry: Shes limed, I warrant you: we have caught her, madam.

speaker: HERO
text_entry: If it proves so, then loving goes by haps:

speaker: HERO
text_entry: Some Cupid kills with arrows, some with traps.

speaker: HERO
text_entry: Exeunt HERO and URSULA

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: [Coming forward]

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: What fire is in mine ears? Can this be true?

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Stand I condemnd for pride and scorn so much?

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Contempt, farewell! and maiden pride, adieu!

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: No glory lives behind the back of such.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: And, Benedick, love on; I will requite thee,

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Taming my wild heart to thy loving hand:

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: If thou dost love, my kindness shall incite thee

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: To bind our loves up in a holy band;

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: For others say thou dost deserve, and I

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Believe it better than reportingly.

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Exit

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: SCENE II. A room in LEONATOS house

speaker: BEATRICE
text_entry: Enter DON PEDRO, CLAUDIO, BENEDICK, and LEONATO

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: I do but stay till your marriage be consummate, and

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: then go I toward Arragon.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Ill bring you thither, my lord, if youll

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: vouchsafe me.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Nay, that would be as great a soil in the new gloss

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: of your marriage as to show a child his new coat

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: and forbid him to wear it. I will only be bold

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: with Benedick for his company; for, from the crown

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: of his head to the sole of his foot, he is all

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: mirth: he hath twice or thrice cut Cupids

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: bow-string and the little hangman dare not shoot at

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: him; he hath a heart as sound as a bell and his

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: tongue is the clapper, for what his heart thinks his

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: tongue speaks.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Gallants, I am not as I have been.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: So say Imethinks you are sadder.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: I hope he be in love.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Hang him, truant! theres no true drop of blood in

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: him, to be truly touched with love: if he be sad,

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: he wants money.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: I have the toothache.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Draw it.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Hang it!

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: You must hang it first, and draw it afterwards.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: What! sigh for the toothache?

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Where is but a humour or a worm.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Well, every one can master a grief but he that has

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: it.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Yet say I, he is in love.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: There is no appearance of fancy in him, unless it be

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: a fancy that he hath to strange disguises; as, to be

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: a Dutchman today, a Frenchman to-morrow, or in the

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: shape of two countries at once, as, a German from

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: the waist downward, all slops, and a Spaniard from

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: the hip upward, no doublet. Unless he have a fancy

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: to this foolery, as it appears he hath, he is no

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: fool for fancy, as you would have it appear he is.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: If he be not in love with some woman, there is no

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: believing old signs: a brushes his hat o

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: mornings; what should that bode?

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Hath any man seen him at the barbers?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: No, but the barbers man hath been seen with him,

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: and the old ornament of his cheek hath already

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: stuffed tennis-balls.

speaker: LEONATO
text_entry: Indeed, he looks younger than he did, by the loss of a beard.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Nay, a rubs himself with civet: can you smell him

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: out by that?

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Thats as much as to say, the sweet youths in love.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: The greatest note of it is his melancholy.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: And when was he wont to wash his face?

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Yea, or to paint himself? for the which, I hear

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: what they say of him.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Nay, but his jesting spirit; which is now crept into

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: a lute-string and now governed by stops.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Indeed, that tells a heavy tale for him: conclude,

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: conclude he is in love.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Nay, but I know who loves him.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: That would I know too: I warrant, one that knows him not.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Yes, and his ill conditions; and, in despite of

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: all, dies for him.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: She shall be buried with her face upwards.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Yet is this no charm for the toothache. Old

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: signior, walk aside with me: I have studied eight

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: or nine wise words to speak to you, which these

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: hobby-horses must not hear.

speaker: BENEDICK
text_entry: Exeunt BENEDICK and LEONATO

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: For my life, to break with him about Beatrice.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Tis even so. Hero and Margaret have by this

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: played their parts with Beatrice; and then the two

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: bears will not bite one another when they meet.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Enter DON JOHN

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: My lord and brother, God save you!

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Good den, brother.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: If your leisure served, I would speak with you.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: In private?

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: If it please you: yet Count Claudio may hear; for

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: what I would speak of concerns him.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Whats the matter?

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: [To CLAUDIO]  Means your lordship to be married

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: to-morrow?

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: You know he does.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: I know not that, when he knows what I know.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: If there be any impediment, I pray you discover it.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: You may think I love you not: let that appear

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: hereafter, and aim better at me by that I now will

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: manifest. For my brother, I think he holds you

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: well, and in dearness of heart hath holp to effect

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: your ensuing marriage;--surely suit ill spent and

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: labour ill bestowed.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Why, whats the matter?

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: I came hither to tell you; and, circumstances

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: shortened, for she has been too long a talking of,

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: the lady is disloyal.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Who, Hero?

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: Even she; Leonatos Hero, your Hero, every mans Hero:

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: Disloyal?

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: The word is too good to paint out her wickedness; I

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: could say she were worse: think you of a worse

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: title, and I will fit her to it. Wonder not till

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: further warrant: go but with me to-night, you shall

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: see her chamber-window entered, even the night

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: before her wedding-day: if you love her then,

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: to-morrow wed her; but it would better fit your honour

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: to change your mind.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: May this be so?

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: I will not think it.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: If you dare not trust that you see, confess not

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: that you know: if you will follow me, I will show

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: you enough; and when you have seen more and heard

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: more, proceed accordingly.

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: If I see any thing to-night why I should not marry

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: her to-morrow in the congregation, where I should

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: wed, there will I shame her.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: And, as I wooed for thee to obtain her, I will join

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: with thee to disgrace her.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: I will disparage her no farther till you are my

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: witnesses: bear it coldly but till midnight, and

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: let the issue show itself.

speaker: DON PEDRO
text_entry: O day untowardly turned!

speaker: CLAUDIO
text_entry: O mischief strangely thwarting!

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: O plague right well prevented! so will you say when

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: you have seen the sequel.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: SCENE III. A street.

speaker: DON JOHN
text_entry: Enter DOGBERRY and VERGES with the Watch

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Are you good men and true?

speaker: VERGES
text_entry: Yea, or else it were pity but they should suffer

speaker: VERGES
text_entry: salvation, body and soul.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Nay, that were a punishment too good for them, if

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: they should have any allegiance in them, being

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: chosen for the princes watch.

speaker: VERGES
text_entry: Well, give them their charge, neighbour Dogberry.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: First, who think you the most desertless man to be

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: constable?

speaker: First Watchman
text_entry: Hugh Otecake, sir, or George Seacole; for they can

speaker: First Watchman
text_entry: write and read.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Come hither, neighbour Seacole. God hath blessed

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: you with a good name: to be a well-favoured man is

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: the gift of fortune; but to write and read comes by nature.

speaker: Second Watchman
text_entry: Both which, master constable,--

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: You have: I knew it would be your answer. Well,

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: for your favour, sir, why, give God thanks, and make

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: no boast of it; and for your writing and reading,

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: let that appear when there is no need of such

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: vanity. You are thought here to be the most

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: senseless and fit man for the constable of the

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: watch; therefore bear you the lantern. This is your

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: charge: you shall comprehend all vagrom men; you are

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: to bid any man stand, in the princes name.

speaker: Second Watchman
text_entry: How if a will not stand?

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Why, then, take no note of him, but let him go; and

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: presently call the rest of the watch together and

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: thank God you are rid of a knave.

speaker: VERGES
text_entry: If he will not stand when he is bidden, he is none

speaker: VERGES
text_entry: of the princes subjects.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: True, and they are to meddle with none but the

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: princes subjects. You shall also make no noise in

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: the streets; for, for the watch to babble and to

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: talk is most tolerable and not to be endured.

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: We will rather sleep than talk: we know what

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: belongs to a watch.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Why, you speak like an ancient and most quiet

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: watchman; for I cannot see how sleeping should

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: offend: only, have a care that your bills be not

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: stolen. Well, you are to call at all the

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: ale-houses, and bid those that are drunk get them to bed.

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: How if they will not?

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Why, then, let them alone till they are sober: if

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: they make you not then the better answer, you may

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: say they are not the men you took them for.

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: Well, sir.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: If you meet a thief, you may suspect him, by virtue

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: of your office, to be no true man; and, for such

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: kind of men, the less you meddle or make with them,

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: why the more is for your honesty.

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: If we know him to be a thief, shall we not lay

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: hands on him?

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Truly, by your office, you may; but I think they

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: that touch pitch will be defiled: the most peaceable

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: way for you, if you do take a thief, is to let him

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: show himself what he is and steal out of your company.

speaker: VERGES
text_entry: You have been always called a merciful man, partner.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Truly, I would not hang a dog by my will, much more

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: a man who hath any honesty in him.

speaker: VERGES
text_entry: If you hear a child cry in the night, you must call

speaker: VERGES
text_entry: to the nurse and bid her still it.

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: How if the nurse be asleep and will not hear us?

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Why, then, depart in peace, and let the child wake

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: her with crying; for the ewe that will not hear her

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: lamb when it baes will never answer a calf when he bleats.

speaker: VERGES
text_entry: Tis very true.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: This is the end of the charge:--you, constable, are

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: to present the princes own person: if you meet the

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: prince in the night, you may stay him.

speaker: VERGES
text_entry: Nay, byr our lady, that I think a cannot.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Five shillings to one ont, with any man that knows

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: the statutes, he may stay him: marry, not without

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: the prince be willing; for, indeed, the watch ought

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: to offend no man; and it is an offence to stay a

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: man against his will.

speaker: VERGES
text_entry: Byr lady, I think it be so.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Ha, ha, ha! Well, masters, good night: an there be

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: any matter of weight chances, call up me: keep your

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: fellows counsels and your own; and good night.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Come, neighbour.

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: Well, masters, we hear our charge: let us go sit here

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: upon the church-bench till two, and then all to bed.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: One word more, honest neighbours. I pray you watch

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: about Signior Leonatos door; for the wedding being

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: there to-morrow, there is a great coil to-night.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Adieu: be vigitant, I beseech you.

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Exeunt DOGBERRY and VERGES

speaker: DOGBERRY
text_entry: Enter BORACHIO and CONRADE

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: What Conrade!

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: [Aside]  Peace! stir not.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Conrade, I say!

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: Here, man; I am at thy elbow.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Mass, and my elbow itched; I thought there would a

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: scab follow.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: I will owe thee an answer for that: and now forward

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: with thy tale.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Stand thee close, then, under this pent-house, for

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: it drizzles rain; and I will, like a true drunkard,

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: utter all to thee.

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: [Aside]  Some treason, masters: yet stand close.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Therefore know I have earned of Don John a thousand ducats.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: Is it possible that any villany should be so dear?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Thou shouldst rather ask if it were possible any

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: villany should be so rich; for when rich villains

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: have need of poor ones, poor ones may make what

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: price they will.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: I wonder at it.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: That shows thou art unconfirmed. Thou knowest that

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: the fashion of a doublet, or a hat, or a cloak, is

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: nothing to a man.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: Yes, it is apparel.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: I mean, the fashion.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: Yes, the fashion is the fashion.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Tush! I may as well say the fools the fool. But

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: seest thou not what a deformed thief this fashion

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: is?

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: [Aside]  I know that Deformed; a has been a vile

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: thief this seven year; a goes up and down like a

speaker: Watchman
text_entry: gentleman: I remember his name.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Didst thou not hear somebody?

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: No; twas the vane on the house.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Seest thou not, I say, what a deformed thief this

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: fashion is? how giddily a turns about all the hot

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: bloods between fourteen and five-and-thirty?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: sometimes fashioning them like Pharaohs soldiers

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: in the reeky painting, sometime like god Bels

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: priests in the old church-window, sometime like the

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: shaven Hercules in the smirched worm-eaten tapestry,

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: where his codpiece seems as massy as his club?

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: All this I see; and I see that the fashion wears

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: out more apparel than the man. But art not thou

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: thyself giddy with the fashion too, that thou hast

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: shifted out of thy tale into telling me of the fashion?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Not so, neither: but know that I have to-night

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: wooed Margaret, the Lady Heros gentlewoman, by the

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: name of Hero: she leans me out at her mistress

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: chamber-window, bids me a thousand times good

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: night,--I tell this tale vilely:--I should first

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: tell thee how the prince, Claudio and my master,

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: planted and placed and possessed by my master Don

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: John, saw afar off in the orchard this amiable encounter.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: And thought they Margaret was Hero?

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Two of them did, the prince and Claudio; but the

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: devil my master knew she was Margaret; and partly

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: by his oaths, which first possessed them, partly by

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: the dark night, which did deceive them, but chiefly

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: by my villany, which did confirm any slander that

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: Don John had made, away went Claudio enraged; swore

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: he would meet her, as he was appointed, next morning

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: at the temple, and there, before the whole

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: congregation, shame her with what he saw oer night

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: and send her home again without a husband.

speaker: First Watchman
text_entry: We charge you, in the princes name, stand!

speaker: Second Watchman
text_entry: Call up the right master constable. We have here

speaker: Second Watchman
text_entry: recovered the most dangerous piece of lechery that

speaker: Second Watchman
text_entry: ever was known in the commonwealth.

speaker: First Watchman
text_entry: And one Deformed is one of them: I know him; a

speaker: First Watchman
text_entry: wears a lock.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: Masters, masters,--

speaker: Second Watchman
text_entry: Youll be made bring Deformed forth, I warrant you.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: Masters,--

speaker: First Watchman
text_entry: Never speak: we charge you let us obey you to go with us.

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: We are like to prove a goodly commodity, being taken

speaker: BORACHIO
text_entry: up of these mens bills.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: A commodity in question, I warrant you. Come, well obey you.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: SCENE IV. HEROs apartment.

speaker: CONRADE
text_entry: Enter HERO, MARGARET, and URSULA

speaker: HERO
text_entry: Good Ursula, wake my cousin Beatrice, and desire

speaker: HERO
text_entry: her to rise.

speaker: URSULA

text_entry: I will be hangd, if some eternal villain,

text_entry: Some busy and insinuating rogue,

text_entry: Have not devised this slander; Ill be hangd else.

text_entry: Why should he call her whore? who keeps her company?

text_entry: What place? what time? what form? what likelihood?

text_entry: The Moors abused by some most villanous knave,

speaker: EMILIA
text_entry: Some base notorious knave, some scurvy fellow.

text_entry: O heaven, that such companions thouldst unfold,

text_entry: O, fie upon them! Some such squire he was

text_entry: And made you to suspect me with the Moor.

speaker: IAGO
text_entry: You are a fool; go to.

text_entry: O good Iago,

text_entry: What shall I do to win my lord again?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text_entry: Good friend, go to him; for, by this light of heaven,

text_entry: I know not how I lost him. Here I kneel:

text_entry: If eer my will did trespass gainst his love,

text_entry: Or that mine eyes, mine ears, or any sense,

text_entry: Delighted them in any other form;

speaker: DESDEMONA
text_entry: Or that I do not yet, and ever did.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text_entry: And ever will--though he do shake me off

speaker: DESDEMONA
text_entry: To beggarly divorcement--love him dearly,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text_entry: Comfort forswear me! Unkindness may do much;

speaker: DESDEMONA
text_entry: And his unkindness may defeat my life,

speaker: DESDEMONA
text_entry: But never taint my love. I cannot say whore:

speaker: DESDEMONA
text_entry: It does abhor me now I speak the word;

speaker: DESDEMONA
text_entry: To do the act that might the addition earn

text_entry: Not the worlds mass of vanity could make me.

speaker: IAGO
text_entry: I pray you, be content; tis but his humour:

speaker: IAGO
text_entry: The business of the state does him offence,

speaker: IAGO
