speaker: Gardener
text_entry: Of Bolingbroke: their fortunes both are weighd:

speaker: Gardener
text_entry: In your lords scale is nothing but himself,

speaker: Gardener
text_entry: And some few vanities that make him light;

speaker: Gardener
text_entry: But in the balance of great Bolingbroke,

speaker: Gardener
text_entry: Besides himself, are all the English peers,

speaker: Gardener
text_entry: And with that odds he weighs King Richard down.

speaker: Gardener
text_entry: Post you to London, and you will find it so;

speaker: Gardener
text_entry: I speak no more than every one doth know.

speaker: QUEEN
text_entry: Nimble mischance, that art so light of foot,

speaker: QUEEN
text_entry: Doth not thy embassage belong to me,

speaker: QUEEN
text_entry: And am I last that knows it? O, thou thinkst

speaker: QUEEN
text_entry: To serve me last, that I may longest keep

speaker: QUEEN
text_entry: Thy sorrow in my breast. Come, ladies, go,

speaker: QUEEN
text_entry: To meet at London Londons king in woe.

speaker: QUEEN
text_entry: What, was I born to this, that my sad look

speaker: QUEEN
text_entry: Should grace the triumph of great Bolingbroke?

speaker: QUEEN
text_entry: Gardener, for telling me these news of woe,

speaker: QUEEN
text_entry: Pray God the plants thou graftst may never grow.

speaker: QUEEN
text_entry: Exeunt QUEEN and Ladies

speaker: GARDENER
text_entry: Poor queen! so that thy state might be no worse,

speaker: GARDENER
text_entry: I would my skill were subject to thy curse.

speaker: GARDENER
text_entry: Here did she fall a tear; here in this place

speaker: GARDENER
text_entry: Ill set a bank of rue, sour herb of grace:

speaker: GARDENER
text_entry: Rue, even for ruth, here shortly shall be seen,

speaker: GARDENER
text_entry: In the remembrance of a weeping queen.

speaker: GARDENER
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: GARDENER
text_entry: ACT IV

speaker: GARDENER
text_entry: SCENE I. Westminster Hall.

speaker: GARDENER
text_entry: Enter, as to the Parliament, HENRY BOLINGBROKE,  DUKE OF AUMERLE, NORTHUMBERLAND, HENRY PERCY, LORD  FITZWATER, DUKE OF SURREY, the BISHOP OF CARLISLE,  the Abbot Of Westminster, and another Lord, Herald, Officers, and BAGOT

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Call forth Bagot.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Now, Bagot, freely speak thy mind;

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: What thou dost know of noble Gloucesters death,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Who wrought it with the king, and who performd

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: The bloody office of his timeless end.

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: Then set before my face the Lord Aumerle.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Cousin, stand forth, and look upon that man.

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: My Lord Aumerle, I know your daring tongue

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: Scorns to unsay what once it hath deliverd.

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: In that dead time when Gloucesters death was plotted,

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: I heard you say, Is not my arm of length,

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: That reacheth from the restful English court

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: As far as Calais, to mine uncles head?

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: Amongst much other talk, that very time,

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: I heard you say that you had rather refuse

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: The offer of an hundred thousand crowns

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: Than Bolingbrokes return to England;

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: Adding withal how blest this land would be

speaker: BAGOT
text_entry: In this your cousins death.

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Princes and noble lords,

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: What answer shall I make to this base man?

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Shall I so much dishonour my fair stars,

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: On equal terms to give him chastisement?

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Either I must, or have mine honour soild

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: With the attainder of his slanderous lips.

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: There is my gage, the manual seal of death,

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: That marks thee out for hell: I say, thou liest,

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: And will maintain what thou hast said is false

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: In thy heart-blood, though being all too base

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: To stain the temper of my knightly sword.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Bagot, forbear; thou shalt not take it up.

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Excepting one, I would he were the best

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: In all this presence that hath moved me so.

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: If that thy valour stand on sympathy,

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: There is my gage, Aumerle, in gage to thine:

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: By that fair sun which shows me where thou standst,

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: I heard thee say, and vauntingly thou spakest it

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: That thou wert cause of noble Gloucesters death.

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: If thou denyst it twenty times, thou liest;

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: And I will turn thy falsehood to thy heart,

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: Where it was forged, with my rapiers point.

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Thou darest not, coward, live to see that day.

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: Now by my soul, I would it were this hour.

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Fitzwater, thou art damnd to hell for this.

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: Aumerle, thou liest; his honour is as true

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: In this appeal as thou art all unjust;

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: And that thou art so, there I throw my gage,

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: To prove it on thee to the extremest point

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: Of mortal breathing: seize it, if thou darest.

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: An if I do not, may my hands rot off

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: And never brandish more revengeful steel

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Over the glittering helmet of my foe!

speaker: Lord
text_entry: I task the earth to the like, forsworn Aumerle;

speaker: Lord
text_entry: And spur thee on with full as many lies

speaker: Lord
text_entry: As may be holload in thy treacherous ear

speaker: Lord
text_entry: From sun to sun: there is my honours pawn;

speaker: Lord
text_entry: Engage it to the trial, if thou darest.

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Who sets me else? by heaven, Ill throw at all:

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: I have a thousand spirits in one breast,

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: To answer twenty thousand such as you.

speaker: DUKE OF SURREY
text_entry: My Lord Fitzwater, I do remember well

speaker: DUKE OF SURREY
text_entry: The very time Aumerle and you did talk.

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: Tis very true: you were in presence then;

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: And you can witness with me this is true.

speaker: DUKE OF SURREY
text_entry: As false, by heaven, as heaven itself is true.

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: Surrey, thou liest.

speaker: DUKE OF SURREY
text_entry: Dishonourable boy!

speaker: DUKE OF SURREY
text_entry: That lie shall lie so heavy on my sword,

speaker: DUKE OF SURREY
text_entry: That it shall render vengeance and revenge

speaker: DUKE OF SURREY
text_entry: Till thou the lie-giver and that lie do lie

speaker: DUKE OF SURREY
text_entry: In earth as quiet as thy fathers skull:

speaker: DUKE OF SURREY
text_entry: In proof whereof, there is my honours pawn;

speaker: DUKE OF SURREY
text_entry: Engage it to the trial, if thou darest.

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: How fondly dost thou spur a forward horse!

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: If I dare eat, or drink, or breathe, or live,

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: I dare meet Surrey in a wilderness,

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: And spit upon him, whilst I say he lies,

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: And lies, and lies: there is my bond of faith,

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: To tie thee to my strong correction.

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: As I intend to thrive in this new world,

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: Aumerle is guilty of my true appeal:

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: Besides, I heard the banishd Norfolk say

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: That thou, Aumerle, didst send two of thy men

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: To execute the noble duke at Calais.

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Some honest Christian trust me with a gage

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: That Norfolk lies: here do I throw down this,

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: If he may be repeald, to try his honour.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: These differences shall all rest under gage

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Till Norfolk be repeald: repeald he shall be,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: And, though mine enemy, restored again

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: To all his lands and signories: when hes returnd,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Against Aumerle we will enforce his trial.

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: That honourable day shall neer be seen.

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Many a time hath banishd Norfolk fought

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: For Jesu Christ in glorious Christian field,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Streaming the ensign of the Christian cross

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Against black pagans, Turks, and Saracens:

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: And toild with works of war, retired himself

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: To Italy; and there at Venice gave

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: His body to that pleasant countrys earth,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: And his pure soul unto his captain Christ,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Under whose colours he had fought so long.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Why, bishop, is Norfolk dead?

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: As surely as I live, my lord.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Sweet peace conduct his sweet soul to the bosom

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Of good old Abraham! Lords appellants,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Your differences shall all rest under gage

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Till we assign you to your days of trial.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Enter DUKE OF YORK, attended

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Great Duke of Lancaster, I come to thee

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: From plume-pluckd Richard; who with willing soul

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Adopts thee heir, and his high sceptre yields

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: To the possession of thy royal hand:

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Ascend his throne, descending now from him;

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: And long live Henry, fourth of that name!

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: In Gods name, Ill ascend the regal throne.

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Marry. God forbid!

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Worst in this royal presence may I speak,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Yet best beseeming me to speak the truth.

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Would God that any in this noble presence

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Were enough noble to be upright judge

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Of noble Richard! then true noblesse would

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Learn him forbearance from so foul a wrong.

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: What subject can give sentence on his king?

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: And who sits here that is not Richards subject?

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Thieves are not judged but they are by to hear,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Although apparent guilt be seen in them;

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: And shall the figure of Gods majesty,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: His captain, steward, deputy-elect,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Anointed, crowned, planted many years,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Be judged by subject and inferior breath,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: And he himself not present? O, forfend it, God,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: That in a Christian climate souls refined

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Should show so heinous, black, obscene a deed!

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: I speak to subjects, and a subject speaks,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Stirrd up by God, thus boldly for his king:

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: My Lord of Hereford here, whom you call king,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Is a foul traitor to proud Herefords king:

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: And if you crown him, let me prophesy:

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: The blood of English shall manure the ground,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: And future ages groan for this foul act;

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Peace shall go sleep with Turks and infidels,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: And in this seat of peace tumultuous wars

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Shall kin with kin and kind with kind confound;

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Disorder, horror, fear and mutiny

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Shall here inhabit, and this land be calld

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: The field of Golgotha and dead mens skulls.

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: O, if you raise this house against this house,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: It will the woefullest division prove

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: That ever fell upon this cursed earth.

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Prevent it, resist it, let it not be so,

speaker: BISHOP OF CARLISLE
text_entry: Lest child, childs children, cry against you woe!

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Well have you argued, sir; and, for your pains,

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Of capital treason we arrest you here.

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: My Lord of Westminster, be it your charge

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: To keep him safely till his day of trial.

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: May it please you, lords, to grant the commons suit.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Fetch hither Richard, that in common view

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: He may surrender; so we shall proceed

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Without suspicion.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: I will be his conduct.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Exit

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Lords, you that here are under our arrest,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Procure your sureties for your days of answer.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Little are we beholding to your love,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: And little lookd for at your helping hands.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Re-enter DUKE OF YORK, with KING RICHARD II, and Officers bearing the regalia

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Alack, why am I sent for to a king,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Before I have shook off the regal thoughts

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Wherewith I reignd? I hardly yet have learnd

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: To insinuate, flatter, bow, and bend my limbs:

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Give sorrow leave awhile to tutor me

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: To this submission. Yet I well remember

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: The favours of these men: were they not mine?

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Did they not sometime cry, all hail! to me?

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: So Judas did to Christ: but he, in twelve,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Found truth in all but one: I, in twelve thousand, none.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: God save the king! Will no man say amen?

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Am I both priest and clerk? well then, amen.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: God save the king! although I be not he;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And yet, amen, if heaven do think him me.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: To do what service am I sent for hither?

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: To do that office of thine own good will

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Which tired majesty did make thee offer,

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: The resignation of thy state and crown

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: To Henry Bolingbroke.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Give me the crown. Here, cousin, seize the crown;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Here cousin:

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: On this side my hand, and on that side yours.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Now is this golden crown like a deep well

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: That owes two buckets, filling one another,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: The emptier ever dancing in the air,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: The other down, unseen and full of water:

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: That bucket down and full of tears am I,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Drinking my griefs, whilst you mount up on high.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: I thought you had been willing to resign.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: My crown I am; but still my griefs are mine:

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: You may my glories and my state depose,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: But not my griefs; still am I king of those.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Part of your cares you give me with your crown.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Your cares set up do not pluck my cares down.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: My care is loss of care, by old care done;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Your care is gain of care, by new care won:

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: The cares I give I have, though given away;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: They tend the crown, yet still with me they stay.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Are you contented to resign the crown?

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Ay, no; no, ay; for I must nothing be;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Therefore no no, for I resign to thee.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Now mark me, how I will undo myself;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: I give this heavy weight from off my head

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And this unwieldy sceptre from my hand,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: The pride of kingly sway from out my heart;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: With mine own tears I wash away my balm,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: With mine own hands I give away my crown,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: With mine own tongue deny my sacred state,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: With mine own breath release all dutys rites:

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: All pomp and majesty I do forswear;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: My manors, rents, revenues I forego;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: My acts, decrees, and statutes I deny:

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: God pardon all oaths that are broke to me!

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: God keep all vows unbroke that swear to thee!

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Make me, that nothing have, with nothing grieved,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And thou with all pleased, that hast all achieved!

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Long mayst thou live in Richards seat to sit,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And soon lie Richard in an earthly pit!

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: God save King Harry, unkingd Richard says,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And send him many years of sunshine days!

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: What more remains?

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: No more, but that you read

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: These accusations and these grievous crimes

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Committed by your person and your followers

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: Against the state and profit of this land;

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: That, by confessing them, the souls of men

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: May deem that you are worthily deposed.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Must I do so? and must I ravel out

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: My weaved-up folly? Gentle Northumberland,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: If thy offences were upon record,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Would it not shame thee in so fair a troop

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: To read a lecture of them? If thou wouldst,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: There shouldst thou find one heinous article,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Containing the deposing of a king

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And cracking the strong warrant of an oath,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Markd with a blot, damnd in the book of heaven:

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Nay, all of you that stand and look upon,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Whilst that my wretchedness doth bait myself,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Though some of you with Pilate wash your hands

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Showing an outward pity; yet you Pilates

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Have here deliverd me to my sour cross,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And water cannot wash away your sin.

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: My lord, dispatch; read oer these articles.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Mine eyes are full of tears, I cannot see:

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And yet salt water blinds them not so much

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: But they can see a sort of traitors here.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Nay, if I turn mine eyes upon myself,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: I find myself a traitor with the rest;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: For I have given here my souls consent

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: To undeck the pompous body of a king;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Made glory base and sovereignty a slave,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Proud majesty a subject, state a peasant.

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: My lord,--

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: No lord of thine, thou haught insulting man,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Nor no mans lord; I have no name, no title,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: No, not that name was given me at the font,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: But tis usurpd: alack the heavy day,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: That I have worn so many winters out,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And know not now what name to call myself!

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: O that I were a mockery king of snow,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Sweet York, sweet husband, be not of that mind:

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: He is as like thee as a man may be,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Not like to me, or any of my kin,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: And yet I love him.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Make way, unruly woman!

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Exit

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: After, Aumerle! mount thee upon his horse;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Spur post, and get before him to the king,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: And beg thy pardon ere he do accuse thee.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Ill not be long behind; though I be old,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: I doubt not but to ride as fast as York:

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: And never will I rise up from the ground

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Till Bolingbroke have pardond thee. Away, be gone!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: SCENE III. A royal palace.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Enter HENRY BOLINGBROKE, HENRY PERCY, and other Lords

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Can no man tell me of my unthrifty son?

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Tis full three months since I did see him last;

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: If any plague hang over us, tis he.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: I would to God, my lords, he might be found:

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Inquire at London, mongst the taverns there,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: For there, they say, he daily doth frequent,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: With unrestrained loose companions,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Even such, they say, as stand in narrow lanes,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: And beat our watch, and rob our passengers;

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Which he, young wanton and effeminate boy,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Takes on the point of honour to support

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: So dissolute a crew.

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: My lord, some two days since I saw the prince,

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: And told him of those triumphs held at Oxford.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: And what said the gallant?

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: His answer was, he would unto the stews,

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: And from the commonst creature pluck a glove,

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: And wear it as a favour; and with that

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: He would unhorse the lustiest challenger.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: As dissolute as desperate; yet through both

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: I see some sparks of better hope, which elder years

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: May happily bring forth. But who comes here?

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Enter DUKE OF AUMERLE

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Where is the king?

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: What means our cousin, that he stares and looks

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: So wildly?

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: God save your grace! I do beseech your majesty,

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: To have some conference with your grace alone.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Withdraw yourselves, and leave us here alone.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Exeunt HENRY PERCY and Lords

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: What is the matter with our cousin now?

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: For ever may my knees grow to the earth,

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: My tongue cleave to my roof within my mouth

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Unless a pardon ere I rise or speak.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Intended or committed was this fault?

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: If on the first, how heinous eer it be,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: To win thy after-love I pardon thee.

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Then give me leave that I may turn the key,

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: That no man enter till my tale be done.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Have thy desire.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: [Within]  My liege, beware; look to thyself;

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Thou hast a traitor in thy presence there.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Villain, Ill make thee safe.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Drawing

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Stay thy revengeful hand; thou hast no cause to fear.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: [Within]  Open the door, secure, foolhardy king:

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Shall I for love speak treason to thy face?

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Open the door, or I will break it open.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Enter DUKE OF YORK

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: What is the matter, uncle? speak;

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Recover breath; tell us how near is danger,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: That we may arm us to encounter it.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Peruse this writing here, and thou shalt know

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: The treason that my haste forbids me show.

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Remember, as thou readst, thy promise passd:

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: I do repent me; read not my name there

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: My heart is not confederate with my hand.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: It was, villain, ere thy hand did set it down.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: I tore it from the traitors bosom, king;

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Fear, and not love, begets his penitence:

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Forget to pity him, lest thy pity prove

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: A serpent that will sting thee to the heart.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: O heinous, strong and bold conspiracy!

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: O loyal father of a treacherous son!

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Thou sheer, immaculate and silver fountain,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: From when this stream through muddy passages

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Hath held his current and defiled himself!

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Thy overflow of good converts to bad,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: And thy abundant goodness shall excuse

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: This deadly blot in thy digressing son.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: So shall my virtue be his vices bawd;

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: And he shall spend mine honour with his shame,

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: As thriftless sons their scraping fathers gold.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Mine honour lives when his dishonour dies,

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Or my shamed life in his dishonour lies:

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Thou killst me in his life; giving him breath,

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: The traitor lives, the true mans put to death.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: [Within]  What ho, my liege! for Gods sake,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: let me in.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: What shrill-voiced suppliant makes this eager cry?

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: A woman, and thy aunt, great king; tis I.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Speak with me, pity me, open the door.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: A beggar begs that never beggd before.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Our scene is alterd from a serious thing,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: And now changed to The Beggar and the King.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: My dangerous cousin, let your mother in:

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: I know she is come to pray for your foul sin.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: If thou do pardon, whosoever pray,

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: More sins for this forgiveness prosper may.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: This festerd joint cut off, the rest rest sound;

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: This let alone will all the rest confound.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Enter DUCHESS OF YORK

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: O king, believe not this hard-hearted man!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Love loving not itself none other can.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Thou frantic woman, what dost thou make here?

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Shall thy old dugs once more a traitor rear?

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Sweet York, be patient. Hear me, gentle liege.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Kneels

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Rise up, good aunt.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Not yet, I thee beseech:

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: For ever will I walk upon my knees,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: And never see day that the happy sees,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Till thou give joy; until thou bid me joy,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: By pardoning Rutland, my transgressing boy.

speaker: DUKE OF AUMERLE
text_entry: Unto my mothers prayers I bend my knee.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Against them both my true joints bended be.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Ill mayst thou thrive, if thou grant any grace!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Pleads he in earnest? look upon his face;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: His eyes do drop no tears, his prayers are in jest;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: His words come from his mouth, ours from our breast:

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: He prays but faintly and would be denied;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: We pray with heart and soul and all beside:

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: His weary joints would gladly rise, I know;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Our knees shall kneel till to the ground they grow:

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: His prayers are full of false hypocrisy;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Ours of true zeal and deep integrity.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Our prayers do out-pray his; then let them have

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: That mercy which true prayer ought to have.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Good aunt, stand up.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Nay, do not say, stand up;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Say, pardon first, and afterwards stand up.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: And if I were thy nurse, thy tongue to teach,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Pardon should be the first word of thy speech.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: I never longd to hear a word till now;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Say pardon, king; let pity teach thee how:

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: The word is short, but not so short as sweet;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: No word like pardon for kings mouths so meet.

speaker: DUKE OF YORK
text_entry: Speak it in French, king; say, pardonne moi.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Dost thou teach pardon pardon to destroy?

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Ah, my sour husband, my hard-hearted lord,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: That setst the word itself against the word!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Speak pardon as tis current in our land;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: The chopping French we do not understand.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Thine eye begins to speak; set thy tongue there;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Or in thy piteous heart plant thou thine ear;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: That hearing how our plaints and prayers do pierce,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Pity may move thee pardon to rehearse.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Good aunt, stand up.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: I do not sue to stand;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Pardon is all the suit I have in hand.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: I pardon him, as God shall pardon me.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: O happy vantage of a kneeling knee!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Yet am I sick for fear: speak it again;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Twice saying pardon doth not pardon twain,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: But makes one pardon strong.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: With all my heart

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: I pardon him.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: A god on earth thou art.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: But for our trusty brother-in-law and the abbot,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: With all the rest of that consorted crew,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Destruction straight shall dog them at the heels.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Good uncle, help to order several powers

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: To Oxford, or whereer these traitors are:

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: They shall not live within this world, I swear,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: But I will have them, if I once know where.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Uncle, farewell: and, cousin too, adieu:

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Your mother well hath prayd, and prove you true.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Come, my old son: I pray God make thee new.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: SCENE IV. The same.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Enter EXTON and Servant

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Didst thou not mark the king, what words he spake,

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Have I no friend will rid me of this living fear?

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Was it not so?

speaker: Servant
text_entry: These were his very words.

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Have I no friend? quoth he: he spake it twice,

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: And urged it twice together, did he not?

speaker: Servant
text_entry: He did.

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: And speaking it, he wistly lookd on me,

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: And who should say, I would thou wert the man

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: That would divorce this terror from my heart;

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Meaning the king at Pomfret. Come, lets go:

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: I am the kings friend, and will rid his foe.

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: SCENE V. Pomfret castle.

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Enter KING RICHARD

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: I have been studying how I may compare

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: This prison where I live unto the world:

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And for because the world is populous

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And here is not a creature but myself,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: I cannot do it; yet Ill hammer it out.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: My brain Ill prove the female to my soul,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: My soul the father; and these two beget

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: A generation of still-breeding thoughts,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And these same thoughts people this little world,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: In humours like the people of this world,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: For no thought is contented. The better sort,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: As thoughts of things divine, are intermixd

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: With scruples and do set the word itself

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Against the word:

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: As thus, Come, little ones, and then again,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: It is as hard to come as for a camel

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: To thread the postern of a small needles eye.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Thoughts tending to ambition, they do plot

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Unlikely wonders; how these vain weak nails

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: May tear a passage through the flinty ribs

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Of this hard world, my ragged prison walls,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And, for they cannot, die in their own pride.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Thoughts tending to content flatter themselves

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: That they are not the first of fortunes slaves,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Nor shall not be the last; like silly beggars

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Who sitting in the stocks refuge their shame,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: That many have and others must sit there;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And in this thought they find a kind of ease,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Bearing their own misfortunes on the back

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Of such as have before endured the like.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Thus play I in one person many people,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And none contented: sometimes am I king;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Then treasons make me wish myself a beggar,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And so I am: then crushing penury

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Persuades me I was better when a king;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Then am I kingd again: and by and by

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Think that I am unkingd by Bolingbroke,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And straight am nothing: but whateer I be,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Nor I nor any man that but man is

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: With nothing shall be pleased, till he be eased

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: With being nothing. Music do I hear?

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Music

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Ha, ha! keep time: how sour sweet music is,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: When time is broke and no proportion kept!

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: So is it in the music of mens lives.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And here have I the daintiness of ear

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: To cheque time broke in a disorderd string;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: But for the concord of my state and time

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Had not an ear to hear my true time broke.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: I wasted time, and now doth time waste me;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: For now hath time made me his numbering clock:

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: My thoughts are minutes; and with sighs they jar

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Their watches on unto mine eyes, the outward watch,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Whereto my finger, like a dials point,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Is pointing still, in cleansing them from tears.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Now sir, the sound that tells what hour it is

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Are clamorous groans, which strike upon my heart,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Which is the bell: so sighs and tears and groans

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Show minutes, times, and hours: but my time

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Runs posting on in Bolingbrokes proud joy,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: While I stand fooling here, his Jack o the clock.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: This music mads me; let it sound no more;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: For though it have holp madmen to their wits,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: In me it seems it will make wise men mad.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Yet blessing on his heart that gives it me!

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: For tis a sign of love; and love to Richard

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Is a strange brooch in this all-hating world.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Enter a Groom of the Stable

speaker: Groom
text_entry: Hail, royal prince!

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Thanks, noble peer;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: The cheapest of us is ten groats too dear.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: What art thou? and how comest thou hither,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Where no man never comes but that sad dog

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: That brings me food to make misfortune live?

speaker: Groom
text_entry: I was a poor groom of thy stable, king,

speaker: Groom
text_entry: When thou wert king; who, travelling towards York,

speaker: Groom
text_entry: With much ado at length have gotten leave

speaker: Groom
text_entry: To look upon my sometimes royal masters face.

speaker: Groom
text_entry: O, how it yearnd my heart when I beheld

speaker: Groom
text_entry: In London streets, that coronation-day,

speaker: Groom
text_entry: When Bolingbroke rode on roan Barbary,

speaker: Groom
text_entry: That horse that thou so often hast bestrid,

speaker: Groom
text_entry: That horse that I so carefully have dressd!

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Rode he on Barbary? Tell me, gentle friend,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: How went he under him?

speaker: Groom
text_entry: So proudly as if he disdaind the ground.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: So proud that Bolingbroke was on his back!

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: That jade hath eat bread from my royal hand;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: This hand hath made him proud with clapping him.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Would he not stumble? would he not fall down,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Since pride must have a fall, and break the neck

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Of that proud man that did usurp his back?

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Forgiveness, horse! why do I rail on thee,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Since thou, created to be awed by man,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Wast born to bear? I was not made a horse;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: And yet I bear a burthen like an ass,

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Spurrd, galld and tired by jouncing Bolingbroke.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Enter Keeper, with a dish

speaker: Keeper
text_entry: Fellow, give place; here is no longer stay.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: If thou love me, tis time thou wert away.

speaker: Groom
text_entry: What my tongue dares not, that my heart shall say.

speaker: Groom
text_entry: Exit

speaker: Keeper
text_entry: My lord, willt please you to fall to?

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Taste of it first, as thou art wont to do.

speaker: Keeper
text_entry: My lord, I dare not: Sir Pierce of Exton, who

speaker: Keeper
text_entry: lately came from the king, commands the contrary.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: The devil take Henry of Lancaster and thee!

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Patience is stale, and I am weary of it.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Beats the keeper

speaker: Keeper
text_entry: Help, help, help!

speaker: Keeper
text_entry: Enter EXTON and Servants, armed

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: How now! what means death in this rude assault?

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Villain, thy own hand yields thy deaths instrument.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Snatching an axe from a Servant and killing him

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Go thou, and fill another room in hell.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: He kills another. Then Exton strikes him down

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: That hand shall burn in never-quenching fire

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: That staggers thus my person. Exton, thy fierce hand

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Hath with the kings blood staind the kings own land.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Mount, mount, my soul! thy seat is up on high;

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Whilst my gross flesh sinks downward, here to die.

speaker: KING RICHARD II
text_entry: Dies

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: As full of valour as of royal blood:

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Both have I spilld; O would the deed were good!

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: For now the devil, that told me I did well,

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Says that this deed is chronicled in hell.

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: This dead king to the living king Ill bear

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Take hence the rest, and give them burial here.

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: SCENE VI. Windsor castle.

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Flourish. Enter HENRY BOLINGBROKE, DUKE OF YORK, with other Lords, and Attendants

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Kind uncle York, the latest news we hear

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Is that the rebels have consumed with fire

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Our town of Cicester in Gloucestershire;

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: But whether they be taen or slain we hear not.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Enter NORTHUMBERLAND

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Welcome, my lordwhat is the news?

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: First, to thy sacred state wish I all happiness.

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: The next news is, I have to London sent

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: The heads of Oxford, Salisbury, Blunt, and Kent:

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: The manner of their taking may appear

speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
text_entry: At large discoursed in this paper here.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: We thank thee, gentle Percy, for thy pains;

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: And to thy worth will add right worthy gains.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Enter LORD FITZWATER

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: My lord, I have from Oxford sent to London

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: The heads of Brocas and Sir Bennet Seely,

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: Two of the dangerous consorted traitors

speaker: LORD FITZWATER
text_entry: That sought at Oxford thy dire overthrow.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Thy pains, Fitzwater, shall not be forgot;

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Right noble is thy merit, well I wot.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Enter HENRY PERCY, and the BISHOP OF CARLISLE

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: The grand conspirator, Abbot of Westminster,

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: With clog of conscience and sour melancholy

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: Hath yielded up his body to the grave;

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: But here is Carlisle living, to abide

speaker: HENRY PERCY
text_entry: Thy kingly doom and sentence of his pride.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Carlisle, this is your doom:

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Choose out some secret place, some reverend room,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: More than thou hast, and with it joy thy life;

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: So as thou livest in peace, die free from strife:

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: For though mine enemy thou hast ever been,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: High sparks of honour in thee have I seen.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Enter EXTON, with persons bearing a coffin

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Great king, within this coffin I present

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Thy buried fear: herein all breathless lies

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: The mightiest of thy greatest enemies,

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: Richard of Bordeaux, by me hither brought.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Exton, I thank thee not; for thou hast wrought

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: A deed of slander with thy fatal hand

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Upon my head and all this famous land.

speaker: EXTON
text_entry: From your own mouth, my lord, did I this deed.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: They love not poison that do poison need,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Nor do I thee: though I did wish him dead,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: I hate the murderer, love him murdered.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: The guilt of conscience take thou for thy labour,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: But neither my good word nor princely favour:

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: With Cain go wander through shades of night,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: And never show thy head by day nor light.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Lords, I protest, my soul is full of woe,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: That blood should sprinkle me to make me grow:

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Come, mourn with me for that I do lament,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: And put on sullen black incontinent:

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Ill make a voyage to the Holy Land,

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: To wash this blood off from my guilty hand:

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: March sadly after; grace my mournings here;

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: In weeping after this untimely bier.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: ACT I

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: SCENE I. London. A street.

speaker: HENRY BOLINGBROKE
text_entry: Enter GLOUCESTER, solus

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Now is the winter of our discontent

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Made glorious summer by this sun of York;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And all the clouds that lourd upon our house

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: In the deep bosom of the ocean buried.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Now are our brows bound with victorious wreaths;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Our bruised arms hung up for monuments;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Our stern alarums changed to merry meetings,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Our dreadful marches to delightful measures.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Grim-visaged war hath smoothd his wrinkled front;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And now, instead of mounting barded steeds

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To fright the souls of fearful adversaries,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: He capers nimbly in a ladys chamber

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To the lascivious pleasing of a lute.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But I, that am not shaped for sportive tricks,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Nor made to court an amorous looking-glass;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I, that am rudely stampd, and want loves majesty

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To strut before a wanton ambling nymph;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I, that am curtaild of this fair proportion,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Cheated of feature by dissembling nature,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Deformed, unfinishd, sent before my time

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Into this breathing world, scarce half made up,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And that so lamely and unfashionable

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: That dogs bark at me as I halt by them;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Why, I, in this weak piping time of peace,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Have no delight to pass away the time,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Unless to spy my shadow in the sun

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And descant on mine own deformity:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And therefore, since I cannot prove a lover,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To entertain these fair well-spoken days,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I am determined to prove a villain

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And hate the idle pleasures of these days.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Plots have I laid, inductions dangerous,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: By drunken prophecies, libels and dreams,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To set my brother Clarence and the king

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: In deadly hate the one against the other:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And if King Edward be as true and just

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: As I am subtle, false and treacherous,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: This day should Clarence closely be mewd up,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: About a prophecy, which says that G

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Of Edwards heirs the murderer shall be.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Dive, thoughts, down to my soul: here

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Clarence comes.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Enter CLARENCE, guarded, and BRAKENBURY

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Brother, good day; what means this armed guard

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: That waits upon your grace?

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: His majesty

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: Tendering my persons safety, hath appointed

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: This conduct to convey me to the Tower.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Upon what cause?

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: Because my name is George.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Alack, my lord, that fault is none of yours;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: He should, for that, commit your godfathers:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: O, belike his majesty hath some intent

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: That you shall be new-christend in the Tower.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But whats the matter, Clarence?  may I know?

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: Yea, Richard, when I know; for I protest

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: As yet I do not: but, as I can learn,

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: He hearkens after prophecies and dreams;

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: And from the cross-row plucks the letter G.

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: And says a wizard told him that by G

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: His issue disinherited should be;

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: And, for my name of George begins with G,

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: It follows in his thought that I am he.

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: These, as I learn, and such like toys as these

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: Have moved his highness to commit me now.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Why, this it is, when men are ruled by women:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Tis not the king that sends you to the Tower:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: My Lady Grey his wife, Clarence, tis she

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: That tempers him to this extremity.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Was it not she and that good man of worship,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Anthony Woodville, her brother there,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: That made him send Lord Hastings to the Tower,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: From whence this present day he is deliverd?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: We are not safe, Clarence; we are not safe.

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: By heaven, I think theres no man is secure

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: But the queens kindred and night-walking heralds

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: That trudge betwixt the king and Mistress Shore.

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: Heard ye not what an humble suppliant

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: Lord hastings was to her for his delivery?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Humbly complaining to her deity

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Got my lord chamberlain his liberty.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Ill tell you what; I think it is our way,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: If we will keep in favour with the king,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To be her men and wear her livery:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: The jealous oerworn widow and herself,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Since that our brother dubbd them gentlewomen.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Are mighty gossips in this monarchy.

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: I beseech your graces both to pardon me;

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: His majesty hath straitly given in charge

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: That no man shall have private conference,

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: Of what degree soever, with his brother.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Even so; ant please your worship, Brakenbury,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: You may partake of any thing we say:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: We speak no treason, man: we say the king

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Is wise and virtuous, and his noble queen

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Well struck in years, fair, and not jealous;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: We say that Shores wife hath a pretty foot,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: A cherry lip, a bonny eye, a passing pleasing tongue;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And that the queens kindred are made gentle-folks:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: How say you sir? Can you deny all this?

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: With this, my lord, myself have nought to do.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Naught to do with mistress Shore! I tell thee, fellow,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: He that doth naught with her, excepting one,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Were best he do it secretly, alone.

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: What one, my lord?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Her husband, knave: wouldst thou betray me?

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: I beseech your grace to pardon me, and withal

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: Forbear your conference with the noble duke.

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: We know thy charge, Brakenbury, and will obey.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: We are the queens abjects, and must obey.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Brother, farewell: I will unto the king;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And whatsoever you will employ me in,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Were it to call King Edwards widow sister,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I will perform it to enfranchise you.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Meantime, this deep disgrace in brotherhood

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Touches me deeper than you can imagine.

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: I know it pleaseth neither of us well.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Well, your imprisonment shall not be long;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Meantime, have patience.

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: I must perforce. Farewell.

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: Exeunt CLARENCE, BRAKENBURY, and Guard

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Go, tread the path that thou shalt neer return.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Simple, plain Clarence! I do love thee so,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: That I will shortly send thy soul to heaven,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: If heaven will take the present at our hands.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But who comes here? the new-deliverd Hastings?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Enter HASTINGS

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: Good time of day unto my gracious lord!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: As much unto my good lord chamberlain!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Well are you welcome to the open air.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: How hath your lordship brookd imprisonment?

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: With patience, noble lord, as prisoners must:

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: But I shall live, my lord, to give them thanks

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: That were the cause of my imprisonment.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: No doubt, no doubt; and so shall Clarence too;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: For they that were your enemies are his,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And have prevaild as much on him as you.

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: More pity that the eagle should be mewd,

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: While kites and buzzards prey at liberty.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: What news abroad?

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: No news so bad abroad as this at home;

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: The King is sickly, weak and melancholy,

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: And his physicians fear him mightily.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Now, by Saint Paul, this news is bad indeed.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: O, he hath kept an evil diet long,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And overmuch consumed his royal person:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Tis very grievous to be thought upon.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: What, is he in his bed?

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: He is.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Go you before, and I will follow you.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Exit HASTINGS

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: He cannot live, I hope; and must not die

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Till George be packd with post-horse up to heaven.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Ill in, to urge his hatred more to Clarence,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: With lies well steeld with weighty arguments;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And, if I fall not in my deep intent,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Clarence hath not another day to live:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Which done, God take King Edward to his mercy,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And leave the world for me to bustle in!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: For then Ill marry Warwicks youngest daughter.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: What though I killd her husband and her father?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: The readiest way to make the wench amends

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Is to become her husband and her father:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: The which will I; not all so much for love

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: As for another secret close intent,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: By marrying her which I must reach unto.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But yet I run before my horse to market:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Clarence still breathes; Edward still lives and reigns:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: When they are gone, then must I count my gains.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Exit

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: SCENE II. The same. Another street.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Enter the corpse of KING HENRY the Sixth, Gentlemen with halberds to guard it; LADY ANNE being the mourner

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Set down, set down your honourable load,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: If honour may be shrouded in a hearse,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Whilst I awhile obsequiously lament

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: The untimely fall of virtuous Lancaster.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Poor key-cold figure of a holy king!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Pale ashes of the house of Lancaster!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Thou bloodless remnant of that royal blood!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Be it lawful that I invocate thy ghost,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: To hear the lamentations of Poor Anne,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Wife to thy Edward, to thy slaughterd son,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Stabbd by the selfsame hand that made these wounds!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Lo, in these windows that let forth thy life,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: I pour the helpless balm of my poor eyes.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Cursed be the hand that made these fatal holes!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Cursed be the heart that had the heart to do it!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Cursed the blood that let this blood from hence!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: More direful hap betide that hated wretch,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: That makes us wretched by the death of thee,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Than I can wish to adders, spiders, toads,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Or any creeping venomd thing that lives!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: If ever he have child, abortive be it,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Prodigious, and untimely brought to light,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Whose ugly and unnatural aspect

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: May fright the hopeful mother at the view;

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: And that be heir to his unhappiness!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: If ever he have wife, let her he made

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: A miserable by the death of him

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: As I am made by my poor lord and thee!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Come, now towards Chertsey with your holy load,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Taken from Pauls to be interred there;

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: And still, as you are weary of the weight,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Rest you, whiles I lament King Henrys corse.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Enter GLOUCESTER

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Stay, you that bear the corse, and set it down.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: What black magician conjures up this fiend,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: To stop devoted charitable deeds?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Villains, set down the corse; or, by Saint Paul,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Ill make a corse of him that disobeys.

speaker: Gentleman
text_entry: My lord, stand back, and let the coffin pass.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Unmannerd dog! stand thou, when I command:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Advance thy halbert higher than my breast,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Or, by Saint Paul, Ill strike thee to my foot,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And spurn upon thee, beggar, for thy boldness.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: What, do you tremble? are you all afraid?

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Alas, I blame you not; for you are mortal,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: And mortal eyes cannot endure the devil.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Avaunt, thou dreadful minister of hell!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Thou hadst but power over his mortal body,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: His soul thou canst not have; therefore be gone.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Sweet saint, for charity, be not so curst.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Foul devil, for Gods sake, hence, and trouble us not;

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: For thou hast made the happy earth thy hell,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Filld it with cursing cries and deep exclaims.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: If thou delight to view thy heinous deeds,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Behold this pattern of thy butcheries.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: O, gentlemen, see, see! dead Henrys wounds

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Open their congeald mouths and bleed afresh!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Blush, Blush, thou lump of foul deformity;

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: For tis thy presence that exhales this blood

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: From cold and empty veins, where no blood dwells;

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Thy deed, inhuman and unnatural,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Provokes this deluge most unnatural.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: O God, which this blood madest, revenge his death!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: O earth, which this blood drinkst revenge his death!

text_entry: And then deny her aiding hand therein,

text_entry: And lay those honours on your high deserts.
