text_entry: What may she not? She may, yea, marry, may she--

speaker: RIVERS
text_entry: What, marry, may she?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: What, marry, may she! marry with a king,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: A bachelor, a handsome stripling too:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I wis your grandam had a worser match.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: My Lord of Gloucester, I have too long borne

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Your blunt upbraidings and your bitter scoffs:

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: By heaven, I will acquaint his majesty

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: With those gross taunts I often have endured.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: I had rather be a country servant-maid

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Than a great queen, with this condition,

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: To be thus taunted, scornd, and baited at:

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Enter QUEEN MARGARET, behind

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Small joy have I in being Englands queen.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And lessend be that small, God, I beseech thee!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thy honour, state and seat is due to me.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: What! threat you me with telling of the king?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Tell him, and spare not: look, what I have said

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I will avouch in presence of the king:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I dare adventure to be sent to the Tower.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Tis time to speak; my pains are quite forgot.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Out, devil! I remember them too well:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thou slewest my husband Henry in the Tower,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And Edward, my poor son, at Tewksbury.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Ere you were queen, yea, or your husband king,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I was a pack-horse in his great affairs;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: A weeder-out of his proud adversaries,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: A liberal rewarder of his friends:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To royalize his blood I spilt mine own.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Yea, and much better blood than his or thine.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: In all which time you and your husband Grey

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Were factious for the house of Lancaster;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And, Rivers, so were you. Was not your husband

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: In Margarets battle at Saint Albans slain?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Let me put in your minds, if you forget,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: What you have been ere now, and what you are;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Withal, what I have been, and what I am.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: A murderous villain, and so still thou art.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Poor Clarence did forsake his father, Warwick;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Yea, and forswore himself,--which Jesu pardon!--

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Which God revenge!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To fight on Edwards party for the crown;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And for his meed, poor lord, he is mewd up.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I would to God my heart were flint, like Edwards;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Or Edwards soft and pitiful, like mine

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I am too childish-foolish for this world.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Hie thee to hell for shame, and leave the world,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thou cacodemon! there thy kingdom is.

speaker: RIVERS
text_entry: My Lord of Gloucester, in those busy days

speaker: RIVERS
text_entry: Which here you urge to prove us enemies,

speaker: RIVERS
text_entry: We followd then our lord, our lawful king:

speaker: RIVERS
text_entry: So should we you, if you should be our king.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: If I should be! I had rather be a pedlar:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Far be it from my heart, the thought of it!

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: As little joy, my lord, as you suppose

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: You should enjoy, were you this countrys king,

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: As little joy may you suppose in me.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: That I enjoy, being the queen thereof.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: A little joy enjoys the queen thereof;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: For I am she, and altogether joyless.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: I can no longer hold me patient.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Advancing

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Hear me, you wrangling pirates, that fall out

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: In sharing that which you have pilld from me!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Which of you trembles not that looks on me?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: If not, that, I being queen, you bow like subjects,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Yet that, by you deposed, you quake like rebels?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O gentle villain, do not turn away!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Foul wrinkled witch, what makest thou in my sight?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: But repetition of what thou hast marrd;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: That will I make before I let thee go.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Wert thou not banished on pain of death?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: I was; but I do find more pain in banishment

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Than death can yield me here by my abode.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: A husband and a son thou owest to me;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And thou a kingdom; all of you allegiance:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: The sorrow that I have, by right is yours,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And all the pleasures you usurp are mine.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: The curse my noble father laid on thee,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: When thou didst crown his warlike brows with paper

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And with thy scorns drewst rivers from his eyes,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And then, to dry them, gavest the duke a clout

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Steepd in the faultless blood of pretty Rutland--

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: His curses, then from bitterness of soul

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Denounced against thee, are all falln upon thee;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And God, not we, hath plagued thy bloody deed.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: So just is God, to right the innocent.

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: O, twas the foulest deed to slay that babe,

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: And the most merciless that eer was heard of!

speaker: RIVERS
text_entry: Tyrants themselves wept when it was reported.

speaker: DORSET
text_entry: No man but prophesied revenge for it.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Northumberland, then present, wept to see it.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: What were you snarling all before I came,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Ready to catch each other by the throat,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And turn you all your hatred now on me?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Did Yorks dread curse prevail so much with heaven?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: That Henrys death, my lovely Edwards death,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Their kingdoms loss, my woful banishment,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Could all but answer for that peevish brat?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Can curses pierce the clouds and enter heaven?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Why, then, give way, dull clouds, to my quick curses!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: If not by war, by surfeit die your king,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: As ours by murder, to make him a king!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Edward thy son, which now is Prince of Wales,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: For Edward my son, which was Prince of Wales,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Die in his youth by like untimely violence!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thyself a queen, for me that was a queen,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Outlive thy glory, like my wretched self!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Long mayst thou live to wail thy childrens loss;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And see another, as I see thee now,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Deckd in thy rights, as thou art stalld in mine!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Long die thy happy days before thy death;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And, after many lengthend hours of grief,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Die neither mother, wife, nor Englands queen!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Rivers and Dorset, you were standers by,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And so wast thou, Lord Hastings, when my son

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Was stabbd with bloody daggers: God, I pray him,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: That none of you may live your natural age,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: But by some unlookd accident cut off!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Have done thy charm, thou hateful witherd hag!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And leave out thee? stay, dog, for thou shalt hear me.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: If heaven have any grievous plague in store

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Exceeding those that I can wish upon thee,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O, let them keep it till thy sins be ripe,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And then hurl down their indignation

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: On thee, the troubler of the poor worlds peace!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: The worm of conscience still begnaw thy soul!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thy friends suspect for traitors while thou livest,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And take deep traitors for thy dearest friends!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: No sleep close up that deadly eye of thine,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Unless it be whilst some tormenting dream

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Affrights thee with a hell of ugly devils!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thou elvish-markd, abortive, rooting hog!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thou that wast seald in thy nativity

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: The slave of nature and the son of hell!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thou slander of thy mothers heavy womb!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thou loathed issue of thy fathers loins!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thou rag of honour! thou detested--

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Margaret.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Richard!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Ha!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: I call thee not.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I cry thee mercy then, for I had thought

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: That thou hadst calld me all these bitter names.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Why, so I did; but lookd for no reply.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O, let me make the period to my curse!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Tis done by me, and ends in Margaret.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Thus have you breathed your curse against yourself.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Poor painted queen, vain flourish of my fortune!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Why strewst thou sugar on that bottled spider,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Whose deadly web ensnareth thee about?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Fool, fool! thou whetst a knife to kill thyself.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: The time will come when thou shalt wish for me

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: To help thee curse that poisonous bunchbackd toad.

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: False-boding woman, end thy frantic curse,

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: Lest to thy harm thou move our patience.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Foul shame upon you! you have all moved mine.

speaker: RIVERS
text_entry: Were you well served, you would be taught your duty.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: To serve me well, you all should do me duty,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Teach me to be your queen, and you my subjects:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O, serve me well, and teach yourselves that duty!

speaker: DORSET
text_entry: Dispute not with her; she is lunatic.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Peace, master marquess, you are malapert:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Your fire-new stamp of honour is scarce current.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O, that your young nobility could judge

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: What twere to lose it, and be miserable!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: They that stand high have many blasts to shake them;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And if they fall, they dash themselves to pieces.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Good counsel, marry: learn it, learn it, marquess.

speaker: DORSET
text_entry: It toucheth you, my lord, as much as me.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Yea, and much more: but I was born so high,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Our aery buildeth in the cedars top,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And dallies with the wind and scorns the sun.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And turns the sun to shade; alas! alas!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Witness my son, now in the shade of death;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Whose bright out-shining beams thy cloudy wrath

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Hath in eternal darkness folded up.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Your aery buildeth in our aerys nest.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O God, that seest it, do not suffer it!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: As it was won with blood, lost be it so!

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Have done! for shame, if not for charity.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Urge neither charity nor shame to me:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Uncharitably with me have you dealt,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And shamefully by you my hopes are butcherd.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: My charity is outrage, life my shame

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And in that shame still live my sorrows rage.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Have done, have done.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O princely Buckingham Ill kiss thy hand,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: In sign of league and amity with thee:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Now fair befal thee and thy noble house!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Thy garments are not spotted with our blood,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Nor thou within the compass of my curse.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Nor no one here; for curses never pass

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The lips of those that breathe them in the air.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Ill not believe but they ascend the sky,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And there awake Gods gentle-sleeping peace.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O Buckingham, take heed of yonder dog!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Look, when he fawns, he bites; and when he bites,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: His venom tooth will rankle to the death:

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Have not to do with him, beware of him;

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Sin, death, and hell have set their marks on him,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And all their ministers attend on him.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: What doth she say, my Lord of Buckingham?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Nothing that I respect, my gracious lord.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: What, dost thou scorn me for my gentle counsel?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And soothe the devil that I warn thee from?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: O, but remember this another day,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: When he shall split thy very heart with sorrow,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And say poor Margaret was a prophetess!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Live each of you the subjects to his hate,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And he to yours, and all of you to Gods!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Exit

speaker: HASTINGS
text_entry: My hair doth stand on end to hear her curses.

speaker: RIVERS
text_entry: And so doth mine: I muse why shes at liberty.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I cannot blame her: by Gods holy mother,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: She hath had too much wrong; and I repent

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: My part thereof that I have done to her.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: I never did her any, to my knowledge.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But you have all the vantage of her wrong.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I was too hot to do somebody good,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: That is too cold in thinking of it now.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Marry, as for Clarence, he is well repaid,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: He is frankd up to fatting for his pains

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: God pardon them that are the cause of it!

speaker: RIVERS
text_entry: A virtuous and a Christian-like conclusion,

speaker: RIVERS
text_entry: To pray for them that have done scathe to us.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: So do I ever:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Aside

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: being well-advised.

text_entry: For had I cursed now, I had cursed myself.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Enter CATESBY

text_entry: Madam, his majesty doth call for you,

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: And for your grace; and you, my noble lords.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Catesby, we come. Lords, will you go with us?

text_entry: Madam, we will attend your grace.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I do the wrong, and first begin to brawl.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: The secret mischiefs that I set abroach

text_entry: I lay unto the grievous charge of others.

text_entry: Clarence, whom I, indeed, have laid in darkness,

text_entry: I do beweep to many simple gulls

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Namely, to Hastings, Derby, Buckingham;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And say it is the queen and her allies

text_entry: That stir the king against the duke my brother.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Now, they believe it; and withal whet me

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To be revenged on Rivers, Vaughan, Grey:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But then I sigh; and, with a piece of scripture,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Tell them that God bids us do good for evil:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And thus I clothe my naked villany

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: With old odd ends stolen out of holy writ;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And seem a saint, when most I play the devil.

speaker: GLOUCESTER

text_entry: But, soft! here come my executioners.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: How now, my hardy, stout resolved mates!

text_entry: Are you now going to dispatch this deed?

text_entry: We are, my lord; and come to have the warrant

speaker: First Murderer
text_entry: That we may be admitted where he is.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Well thought upon; I have it here about me.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Gives the warrant

text_entry: When you have done, repair to Crosby Place.

text_entry: But, sirs, be sudden in the execution,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Withal obdurate, do not hear him plead;

text_entry: For Clarence is well-spoken, and perhaps

text_entry: May move your hearts to pity if you mark him.

speaker: First Murderer
text_entry: Tush!

speaker: First Murderer
text_entry: Fear not, my lord, we will not stand to prate;

speaker: First Murderer
text_entry: Talkers are no good doers: be assured

text_entry: We come to use our hands and not our tongues.

text_entry: Your eyes drop millstones, when fools eyes drop tears:

text_entry: I like you, lads; about your business straight;

speaker: GLOUCESTER

text_entry: So full of ugly sights, of ghastly dreams,

text_entry: Who from my cabin tempted me to walk

text_entry: Upon the giddy footing of the hatches,

text_entry: What dreadful noise of waters in mine ears!

text_entry: Where eyes did once inhabit, there were crept,

text_entry: As twere in scorn of eyes, reflecting gems,

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: Which wood the slimy bottom of the deep,

text_entry: in the next room.

text_entry: Thy voice is thunder, but thy looks are humble.

text_entry: My voice is now the kings, my looks mine own.

text_entry: Offended us you have not, but the king.

text_entry: I shall be reconciled to him again.

text_entry: Are you calld forth from out a world of men

text_entry: Before I be convict by course of law,

text_entry: I charge you, as you hope to have redemption

text_entry: Spurn at his edict and fulfil a mans?

text_entry: To hurl upon their heads that break his law.

text_entry: And that same vengeance doth he hurl on thee,

text_entry: For false forswearing and for murder too:

text_entry: Thou didst receive the holy sacrament,

speaker: Second Murderer
text_entry: To fight in quarrel of the house of Lancaster.

text_entry: And, like a traitor to the name of God,

text_entry: Didst break that vow; and with thy treacherous blade

text_entry: Unripdst the bowels of thy sovereigns son.

speaker: Second Murderer
text_entry: Whom thou wert sworn to cherish and defend.

text_entry: How canst thou urge Gods dreadful law to us,

text_entry: When thou hast broke it in so dear degree?

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: For Edward, for my brother, for his sake: Why, sirs,

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: He sends ye not to murder me for this

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: For in this sin he is as deep as I.

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: If God will be revenged for this deed.

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: O, know you yet, he doth it publicly,

text_entry: Take not the quarrel from his powerful arm;

text_entry: He needs no indirect nor lawless course

speaker: CLARENCE
text_entry: To cut off those that have offended him.

text_entry: Who made thee, then, a bloody minister,

text_entry: When gallant-springing brave Plantagenet,

text_entry: That princely novice, was struck dead by thee?

text_entry: My brothers love, the devil, and my rage.

text_entry: Thy brothers love, our duty, and thy fault,

speaker: First Murderer
text_entry: Right,

text_entry: To his new kingdom of perpetual rest.

text_entry: Ah, so much interest have I in thy sorrow

text_entry: As I had title in thy noble husband!

text_entry: And lived by looking on his images:

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: To overgo thy plaints and drown thy cries!

text_entry: How can we aid you with our kindred tears?

speaker: Girl

text_entry: I am not barren to bring forth complaints

text_entry: All springs reduce their currents to mine eyes,

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: That I, being governd by the watery moon,

text_entry: What stays had I but they? and they are gone.

text_entry: Was never widow had so dear a loss!

speaker: Children
text_entry: Were never orphans had so dear a loss!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Was never mother had so dear a loss!

text_entry: Alas, I am the mother of these moans!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Their woes are parcelld, mine are general.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: She for an Edward weeps, and so do I;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: I for a Clarence weep, so doth not she:

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: These babes for Clarence weep and so do I;

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: I for an Edward weep, so do not they:

text_entry: Alas, you three, on me, threefold distressd,

text_entry: And I will pamper it with lamentations.

text_entry: I did not see your grace: humbly on my knee

text_entry: But lately splinterd, knit, and joind together,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Must gently be preserved, cherishd, and kept:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Me seemeth good, that, with some little train,

text_entry: By how much the estate is green and yet ungovernd:

text_entry: And may direct his course as please himself,

text_entry: As well the fear of harm, as harm apparent,

text_entry: I hope the king made peace with all of us

text_entry: And the compact is firm and true in me.

text_entry: For, by the way, Ill sort occasion,

text_entry: As index to the story we late talkd of,

text_entry: To part the queens proud kindred from the king.

text_entry: My other self, my counsels consistory,

text_entry: My oracle, my prophet! My dear cousin,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: SCENE III. London. A street.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Enter two Citizens meeting

text_entry: Neighbour, well met: whither away so fast?

text_entry: I promise you, I scarcely know myself:

text_entry: Hear you the news abroad?

text_entry: Bad news, byr lady; seldom comes the better:

text_entry: I fear, I fear twill prove a troublous world.

text_entry: Enter another Citizen

text_entry: Doth this news hold of good King Edwards death?

text_entry: In him there is a hope of government,

text_entry: That in his nonage council under him,

text_entry: And in his full and ripend years himself,

text_entry: For then this land was famously enrichd

speaker: Third Citizen

text_entry: Had virtuous uncles to protect his grace.

text_entry: Why, so hath this, both by the father and mother.

text_entry: Better it were they all came by the father,

text_entry: And the queens sons and brothers haught and proud:

text_entry: And were they to be ruled, and not to rule,

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: This sickly land might solace as before.

text_entry: Come, come, we fear the worst; all shall be well.

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: When clouds appear, wise men put on their cloaks;

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: When great leaves fall, the winter is at hand;

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: When the sun sets, who doth not look for night?

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: Untimely storms make men expect a dearth.

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: All may be well; but, if God sort it so,

speaker: Third Citizen
text_entry: Tis more than we deserve, or I expect.

text_entry: Truly, the souls of men are full of dread:

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: Ye cannot reason almost with a man

speaker: Second Citizen
text_entry: That looks not heavily and full of fear.

text_entry: Ensuing dangers; as by proof, we see

speaker: YORK

text_entry: To touch his growth nearer than he touchd mine.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK

text_entry: Aside

text_entry: As if the golden fee for which I plead

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Were for myself: and so, my lord, adieu.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: If you thrive well, bring them to Baynards Castle;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Where you shall find me well accompanied

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: With reverend fathers and well-learned bishops.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: I go: and towards three or four oclock

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Look for the news that the Guildhall affords.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Exit BUCKINGHAM

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Go, Lovel, with all speed to Doctor Shaw;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To CATESBY

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Go thou to Friar Penker; bid them both

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Meet me within this hour at Baynards Castle.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Exeunt all but GLOUCESTER

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Now will I in, to take some privy order,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To draw the brats of Clarence out of sight;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And to give notice, that no manner of person

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: At any time have recourse unto the princes.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Exit

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: SCENE VI. The same.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Enter a Scrivener, with a paper in his hand

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: This is the indictment of the good Lord Hastings;

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: Which in a set hand fairly is engrossd,

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: That it may be this day read over in Pauls.

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: And mark how well the sequel hangs together:

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: Eleven hours I spent to write it over,

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: For yesternight by Catesby was it brought me;

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: The precedent was full as long a-doing:

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: And yet within these five hours lived Lord Hastings,

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: Untainted, unexamined, free, at liberty

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: Heres a good world the while! Why whos so gross,

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: That seeth not this palpable device?

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: Yet whos so blind, but says he sees it not?

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: Bad is the world; and all will come to nought,

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: When such bad dealings must be seen in thought.

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: Exit

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: SCENE VII. Baynards Castle.

speaker: Scrivener
text_entry: Enter GLOUCESTER and BUCKINGHAM, at several doors

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: How now, my lord, what say the citizens?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Now, by the holy mother of our Lord,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The citizens are mum and speak not a word.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Touchd you the bastardy of Edwards children?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: I did; with his contract with Lady Lucy,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And his contract by deputy in France;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The insatiate greediness of his desires,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And his enforcement of the city wives;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: His tyranny for trifles; his own bastardy,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: As being got, your father then in France,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: His resemblance, being not like the duke;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Withal I did infer your lineaments,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Being the right idea of your father,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Both in your form and nobleness of mind;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Laid open all your victories in Scotland,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Your dicipline in war, wisdom in peace,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Your bounty, virtue, fair humility:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Indeed, left nothing fitting for the purpose

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Untouchd, or slightly handled, in discourse

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And when mine oratory grew to an end

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: I bid them that did love their countrys good

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Cry God save Richard, Englands royal king!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Ah! and did they so?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: No, so God help me, they spake not a word;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: But, like dumb statues or breathing stones,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Gazed each on other, and lookd deadly pale.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Which when I saw, I reprehended them;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And askd the mayor what meant this wilful silence:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: His answer was, the people were not wont

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: To be spoke to but by the recorder.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Then he was urged to tell my tale again,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Thus saith the duke, thus hath the duke inferrd;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: But nothing spake in warrant from himself.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: When he had done, some followers of mine own,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: At the lower end of the hall, hurld up their caps,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And some ten voices cried God save King Richard!

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And thus I took the vantage of those few,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Thanks, gentle citizens and friends, quoth I;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: This general applause and loving shout

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Argues your wisdoms and your love to Richard:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And even here brake off, and came away.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: What tongueless blocks were they! would not they speak?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: No, by my troth, my lord.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Will not the mayor then and his brethren come?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The mayor is here at hand: intend some fear;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Be not you spoke with, but by mighty suit:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And look you get a prayer-book in your hand,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And stand betwixt two churchmen, good my lord;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: For on that ground Ill build a holy descant:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And be not easily won to our request:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Play the maids part, still answer nay, and take it.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I go; and if you plead as well for them

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: As I can say nay to thee for myself,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: No doubt well bring it to a happy issue.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Go, go, up to the leads; the lord mayor knocks.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Exit GLOUCESTER

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Enter the Lord Mayor and Citizens

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Welcome my lord; I dance attendance here;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: I think the duke will not be spoke withal.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Enter CATESBY

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Here comes his servant: how now, Catesby,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: What says he?

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: My lord: he doth entreat your grace;

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: To visit him to-morrow or next day:

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: He is within, with two right reverend fathers,

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: Divinely bent to meditation;

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: And no worldly suit would he be moved,

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: To draw him from his holy exercise.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Return, good Catesby, to thy lord again;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Tell him, myself, the mayor and citizens,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: In deep designs and matters of great moment,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: No less importing than our general good,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Are come to have some conference with his grace.

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: Ill tell him what you say, my lord.

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: Exit

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Ah, ha, my lord, this prince is not an Edward!

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: He is not lolling on a lewd day-bed,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: But on his knees at meditation;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Not dallying with a brace of courtezans,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: But meditating with two deep divines;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Not sleeping, to engross his idle body,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: But praying, to enrich his watchful soul:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Happy were England, would this gracious prince

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Take on himself the sovereignty thereof:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: But, sure, I fear, we shall neer win him to it.

speaker: Lord Mayor
text_entry: Marry, God forbid his grace should say us nay!

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: I fear he will.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Re-enter CATESBY

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: How now, Catesby, what says your lord?

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: My lord,

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: He wonders to what end you have assembled

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: Such troops of citizens to speak with him,

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: His grace not being warnd thereof before:

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: My lord, he fears you mean no good to him.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Sorry I am my noble cousin should

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Suspect me, that I mean no good to him:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: By heaven, I come in perfect love to him;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And so once more return and tell his grace.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Exit CATESBY

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: When holy and devout religious men

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Are at their beads, tis hard to draw them thence,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: So sweet is zealous contemplation.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Enter GLOUCESTER aloft, between two Bishops. CATESBY returns

speaker: Lord Mayor
text_entry: See, where he stands between two clergymen!

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Two props of virtue for a Christian prince,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: To stay him from the fall of vanity:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And, see, a book of prayer in his hand,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: True ornaments to know a holy man.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Famous Plantagenet, most gracious prince,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Lend favourable ears to our request;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And pardon us the interruption

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Of thy devotion and right Christian zeal.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: My lord, there needs no such apology:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I rather do beseech you pardon me,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Who, earnest in the service of my God,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Neglect the visitation of my friends.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But, leaving this, what is your graces pleasure?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Even that, I hope, which pleaseth God above,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And all good men of this ungovernd isle.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I do suspect I have done some offence

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: That seems disgracious in the citys eyes,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And that you come to reprehend my ignorance.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: You have, my lord: would it might please your grace,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: At our entreaties, to amend that fault!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Else wherefore breathe I in a Christian land?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Then know, it is your fault that you resign

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The supreme seat, the throne majestical,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The scepterd office of your ancestors,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Your state of fortune and your due of birth,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The lineal glory of your royal house,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: To the corruption of a blemished stock:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Whilst, in the mildness of your sleepy thoughts,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Which here we waken to our countrys good,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: This noble isle doth want her proper limbs;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Her face defaced with scars of infamy,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Her royal stock graft with ignoble plants,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And almost shoulderd in the swallowing gulf

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Of blind forgetfulness and dark oblivion.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Which to recure, we heartily solicit

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Your gracious self to take on you the charge

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And kingly government of this your land,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Not as protector, steward, substitute,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Or lowly factor for anothers gain;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: But as successively from blood to blood,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Your right of birth, your empery, your own.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: For this, consorted with the citizens,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Your very worshipful and loving friends,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And by their vehement instigation,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: In this just suit come I to move your grace.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I know not whether to depart in silence,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Or bitterly to speak in your reproof.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Best fitteth my degree or your condition

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: If not to answer, you might haply think

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Tongue-tied ambition, not replying, yielded

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To bear the golden yoke of sovereignty,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Which fondly you would here impose on me;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: If to reprove you for this suit of yours,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: So seasond with your faithful love to me.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Then, on the other side, I chequed my friends.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Therefore, to speak, and to avoid the first,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And then, in speaking, not to incur the last,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Definitively thus I answer you.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Your love deserves my thanks; but my desert

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Unmeritable shuns your high request.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: First if all obstacles were cut away,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And that my path were even to the crown,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: As my ripe revenue and due by birth

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Yet so much is my poverty of spirit,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: So mighty and so many my defects,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: As I had rather hide me from my greatness,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Being a bark to brook no mighty sea,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Than in my greatness covet to be hid,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And in the vapour of my glory smotherd.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But, God be thankd, theres no need of me,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And much I need to help you, if need were;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: The royal tree hath left us royal fruit,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Which, mellowd by the stealing hours of time,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Will well become the seat of majesty,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: And make, no doubt, us happy by his reign.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: On him I lay what you would lay on me,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: The right and fortune of his happy stars;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Which God defend that I should wring from him!

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: My lord, this argues conscience in your grace;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: But the respects thereof are nice and trivial,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: All circumstances well considered.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: You say that Edward is your brothers son:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: So say we too, but not by Edwards wife;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: For first he was contract to Lady Lucy--

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Your mother lives a witness to that vow--

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And afterward by substitute betrothd

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: To Bona, sister to the King of France.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: These both put by a poor petitioner,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: A care-crazed mother of a many children,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: A beauty-waning and distressed widow,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Even in the afternoon of her best days,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Made prize and purchase of his lustful eye,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Seduced the pitch and height of all his thoughts

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: To base declension and loathed bigamy

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: By her, in his unlawful bed, he got

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: This Edward, whom our manners term the prince.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: More bitterly could I expostulate,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Save that, for reverence to some alive,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: I give a sparing limit to my tongue.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Then, good my lord, take to your royal self

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: This profferd benefit of dignity;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: If non to bless us and the land withal,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Yet to draw forth your noble ancestry

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: From the corruption of abusing times,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Unto a lineal true-derived course.

speaker: Lord Mayor
text_entry: Do, good my lord, your citizens entreat you.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Refuse not, mighty lord, this profferd love.

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: O, make them joyful, grant their lawful suit!

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Alas, why would you heap these cares on me?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I am unfit for state and majesty;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I do beseech you, take it not amiss;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I cannot nor I will not yield to you.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: If you refuse it,--as, in love and zeal,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Loath to depose the child, Your brothers son;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: As well we know your tenderness of heart

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And gentle, kind, effeminate remorse,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Which we have noted in you to your kin,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And egally indeed to all estates,--

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Yet whether you accept our suit or no,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Your brothers son shall never reign our king;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: But we will plant some other in the throne,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: To the disgrace and downfall of your house:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And in this resolution here we leave you.--

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Come, citizens: zounds! Ill entreat no more.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: O, do not swear, my lord of Buckingham.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Exit BUCKINGHAM with the Citizens

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: Call them again, my lord, and accept their suit.

speaker: ANOTHER
text_entry: Do, good my lord, lest all the land do rue it.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Would you enforce me to a world of care?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Well, call them again. I am not made of stone,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But penetrable to your. kind entreats,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Albeit against my conscience and my soul.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Re-enter BUCKINGHAM and the rest

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Cousin of Buckingham, and you sage, grave men,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Since you will buckle fortune on my back,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: To bear her burthen, whether I will or no,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: I must have patience to endure the load:

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: But if black scandal or foul-faced reproach

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Attend the sequel of your imposition,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Your mere enforcement shall acquittance me

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: From all the impure blots and stains thereof;

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: For God he knows, and you may partly see,

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: How far I am from the desire thereof.

speaker: Lord Mayor
text_entry: God bless your grace! we see it, and will say it.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: In saying so, you shall but say the truth.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Then I salute you with this kingly title:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Long live Richard, Englands royal king!

speaker: Citizens
text_entry: Amen.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: To-morrow will it please you to be crownd?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Even when you please, since you will have it so.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: To-morrow, then, we will attend your grace:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And so most joyfully we take our leave.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Come, let us to our holy task again.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Farewell, good cousin; farewell, gentle friends.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: GLOUCESTER

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: SCENE I. Before the Tower.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text_entry: Enter, on one side, QUEEN ELIZABETH, DUCHESS OF  YORK, and DORSET; on the other, ANNE, Duchess of  Gloucester, leading Lady Margaret Plantagenet, CLARENCEs young Daughter

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Who m eets us here?  my niece Plantagenet

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Led in the hand of her kind aunt of Gloucester?

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Now, for my life, shes wandering to the Tower,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: On pure hearts love to greet the tender princes.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Daughter, well met.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: God give your graces both

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: A happy and a joyful time of day!

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: As much to you, good sister! Whither away?

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: No farther than the Tower; and, as I guess,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Upon the like devotion as yourselves,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: To gratulate the gentle princes there.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Kind sister, thanks: well enter all together.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Enter BRAKENBURY

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: And, in good time, here the lieutenant comes.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Master lieutenant, pray you, by your leave,

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: How doth the prince, and my young son of York?

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: Right well, dear madam. By your patience,

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: I may not suffer you to visit them;

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: The king hath straitly charged the contrary.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: The king! why, whos that?

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: I cry you mercy: I mean the lord protector.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH

text_entry: And take thy office from thee, on my peril.

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: Exit

speaker: BRAKENBURY
text_entry: Enter LORD STANLEY

speaker: LORD STANLEY

speaker: LORD STANLEY
text_entry: To LADY ANNE

speaker: LORD STANLEY

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: With this dead-killing news!

speaker: LADY ANNE

speaker: DORSET

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: O Dorset, speak not to me, get thee hence!

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Death and destruction dog thee at the heels;

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Thy mothers name is ominous to children.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: If thou wilt outstrip death, go cross the seas,

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: And live with Richmond, from the reach of hell

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Go, hie thee, hie thee from this slaughter-house,

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Lest thou increase the number of the dead;

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: And make me die the thrall of Margarets curse,

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Nor mother, wife, nor Englands counted queen.

speaker: LORD STANLEY
text_entry: Full of wise care is this your counsel, madam.

speaker: LORD STANLEY
text_entry: Take all the swift advantage of the hours;

speaker: LORD STANLEY
text_entry: You shall have letters from me to my son

speaker: LORD STANLEY
text_entry: To meet you on the way, and welcome you.

speaker: LORD STANLEY
text_entry: Be not taen tardy by unwise delay.

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: O ill-dispersing wind of misery!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: O my accursed womb, the bed of death!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: A cockatrice hast thou hatchd to the world,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Whose unavoided eye is murderous.

speaker: LORD STANLEY
text_entry: Come, madam, come; I in all haste was sent.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: And I in all unwillingness will go.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: I would to God that the inclusive verge

text_entry: Of golden metal that must round my brow

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Were red-hot steel, to sear me to the brain!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Anointed let me be with deadly venom,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: And die, ere men can say, God save the queen!

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Go, go, poor soul, I envy not thy glory

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: To feed my humour, wish thyself no harm.

text_entry: No! why?  When he that is my husband now

text_entry: Came to me, as I followd Henrys corse,

text_entry: When scarce the blood was well washd from his hands

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: And that dead saint which then I weeping followd;

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: O, when, I say, I lookd on Richards face,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: This was my wish: Be thou, quoth I,  accursed,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: For making me, so young, so old a widow!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: And, when thou wedst, let sorrow haunt thy bed;

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: And be thy wife--if any be so mad--

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: As miserable by the life of thee

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: As thou hast made me by my dear lords death!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Lo, ere I can repeat this curse again,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Even in so short a space, my womans heart

text_entry: Grossly grew captive to his honey words

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: And proved the subject of my own souls curse,

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Which ever since hath kept my eyes from rest;

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: For never yet one hour in his bed

speaker: LADY ANNE

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: But have been waked by his timorous dreams.

speaker: LADY ANNE

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: And will, no doubt, shortly be rid of me.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Poor heart, adieu! I pity thy complaining.

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: No more than from my soul I mourn for yours.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Farewell, thou woful welcomer of glory!

speaker: LADY ANNE
text_entry: Adieu, poor soul, that takest thy leave of it!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: [To DORSET]

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Go thou to Richmond, and good fortune guide thee!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: To LADY ANNE

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Go thou to Richard, and good angels guard thee!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: To QUEEN ELIZABETH

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Go thou to sanctuary, and good thoughts possess thee!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: I to my grave, where peace and rest lie with me!

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: Eighty odd years of sorrow have I seen,

speaker: DUCHESS OF YORK
text_entry: And each hours joy wrecked with a week of teen.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Stay, yet look back with me unto the Tower.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Pity, you ancient stones, those tender babes

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Whom envy hath immured within your walls!

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Rough cradle for such little pretty ones!

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Rude ragged nurse, old sullen playfellow

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: For tender princes, use my babies well!

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: So foolish sorrow bids your stones farewell.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text_entry: SCENE II. London. The palace.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH

speaker: KING RICHARD III

text_entry: Give me thy hand.

text_entry: Here he ascendeth his throne

text_entry: Thus high, by thy advice

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: And thy assistance, is King Richard seated;

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: But shall we wear these honours for a day?

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Or shall they last, and we rejoice in them?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Still live they and for ever may they last!

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: O Buckingham, now do I play the touch,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: To try if thou be current gold indeed

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Young Edward lives: think now what I would say.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Say on, my loving lord.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Why, Buckingham, I say, I would be king,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Why, so you are, my thrice renowned liege.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Ha! am I king? tis so: but Edward lives.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: True, noble prince.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: O bitter consequence,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: That Edward still should live! True, noble prince!

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Cousin, thou wert not wont to be so dull:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Shall I be plain? I wish the bastards dead;

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: And I would have it suddenly performd.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: What sayest thou? speak suddenly; be brief.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Your grace may do your pleasure.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Tut, tut, thou art all ice, thy kindness freezeth:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Say, have I thy consent that they shall die?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Give me some breath, some little pause, my lord

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Before I positively herein:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: I will resolve your grace immediately.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Exit

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: [Aside to a stander by]

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: The king is angry: see, he bites the lip.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: I will converse with iron-witted fools

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: And unrespective boys: none are for me

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: That look into me with considerate eyes:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: High-reaching Buckingham grows circumspect.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Boy!

speaker: Page
text_entry: My lord?

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Knowst thou not any whom corrupting gold

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Would tempt unto a close exploit of death?

speaker: Page
text_entry: My lord, I know a discontented gentleman,

speaker: Page
text_entry: Whose humble means match not his haughty mind:

speaker: Page
text_entry: Gold were as good as twenty orators,

speaker: Page
text_entry: And will, no doubt, tempt him to any thing.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: What is his name?

speaker: Page
text_entry: His name, my lord, is Tyrrel.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: I partly know the man: go, call him hither.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Exit Page

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: The deep-revolving witty Buckingham

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: No more shall be the neighbour to my counsel:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Hath he so long held out with me untired,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: And stops he now for breath?

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Enter STANLEY

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: How now! what news with you?

speaker: STANLEY
text_entry: My lord, I hear the Marquis Dorsets fled

speaker: STANLEY
text_entry: To Richmond, in those parts beyond the sea

speaker: STANLEY
text_entry: Where he abides.

speaker: STANLEY
text_entry: Stands apart

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Catesby!

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: My lord?

text_entry: Rumour it abroad

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: That Anne, my wife, is sick and like to die:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: I will take order for her keeping close.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Inquire me out some mean-born gentleman,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Whom I will marry straight to Clarence daughter:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: The boy is foolish, and I fear not him.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Look, how thou dreamst! I say again, give out

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: That Anne my wife is sick and like to die:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: About it; for it stands me much upon,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: To stop all hopes whose growth may damage me.

speaker: KING RICHARD III

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: I must be married to my brothers daughter,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Murder her brothers, and then marry her!

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Uncertain way of gain! But I am in

speaker: KING RICHARD III

text_entry: Tear-falling pity dwells not in this eye.

text_entry: But I had rather kill two enemies.

text_entry: Foes to my rest and my sweet sleeps disturbers

text_entry: And soon Ill rid you from the fear of them.

text_entry: Thou singst sweet music. Hark, come hither, Tyrrel

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Whispers

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: There is no more but so: say it is done,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: And I will love thee, and prefer thee too.

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Tis done, my gracious lord.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Shall we hear from thee, Tyrrel, ere we sleep?

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Ye shall, my Lord.

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Exit

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Re-enter BUCKINGHAM

text_entry: My Lord, I have considerd in my mind

text_entry: The late demand that you did sound me in.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Well, let that pass. Dorset is fled to Richmond.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: I hear that news, my lord.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Stanley, he is your wifes son well, look to it.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: My lord, I claim your gift, my due by promise,

text_entry: For which your honour and your faith is pawnd;

text_entry: The earldom of Hereford and the moveables

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The which you promised I should possess.

text_entry: Stanley, look to your wife; if she convey

text_entry: Letters to Richmond, you shall answer it.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: What says your highness to my just demand?

text_entry: As I remember, Henry the Sixth

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Did prophesy that Richmond should be king,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: When Richmond was a little peevish boy.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: A king, perhaps, perhaps,--

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: My lord!

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: How chance the prophet could not at that time

text_entry: Have told me, I being by, that I should kill him?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: My lord, your promise for the earldom,--

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Richmond! When last I was at Exeter,

text_entry: The mayor in courtesy showd me the castle,

speaker: KING RICHARD III

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Because a bard of Ireland told me once

text_entry: I should not live long after I saw Richmond.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: My Lord!

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Ay, whats oclock?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: I am thus bold to put your grace in mind

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Of what you promised me.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Well, but whats oclock?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Upon the stroke of ten.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Well, let it strike.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Why let it strike?

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Because that, like a Jack, thou keepst the stroke

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Betwixt thy begging and my meditation.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: I am not in the giving vein to-day.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Why, then resolve me whether you will or no.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Tut, tut,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Thou troublest me; am not in the vein.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Exeunt all but BUCKINGHAM

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Is it even so? rewards he my true service

text_entry: With such deep contempt made I him king for this?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: O, let me think on Hastings, and be gone

speaker: BUCKINGHAM

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Exit

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: SCENE III. The same.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Enter TYRREL

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: The tyrannous and bloody deed is done.

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: The most arch of piteous massacre

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: That ever yet this land was guilty of.

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Dighton and Forrest, whom I did suborn

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: To do this ruthless piece of butchery,

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Although they were fleshd villains, bloody dogs,

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Melting with tenderness and kind compassion

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Wept like two children in their deaths sad stories.

text_entry: Lo, thus quoth Dighton, lay those tender babes:

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Thus, thus, quoth Forrest, girdling one another

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Within their innocent alabaster arms:

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Their lips were four red roses on a stalk,

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Which in their summer beauty kissd each other.

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: A book of prayers on their pillow lay;

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Which once, quoth Forrest, almost changed my mind;

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: But O! the devil--there the villain stoppd

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: Whilst Dighton thus told on: We smothered

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: The most replenished sweet work of nature,

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: That from the prime creation eer she framed.

text_entry: Thus both are gone with conscience and remorse;

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: They could not speak; and so I left them both,

speaker: TYRREL
text_entry: To bring this tidings to the bloody king.

speaker: TYRREL

text_entry: All hail, my sovereign liege!

speaker: TYRREL

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: And buried, gentle Tyrrel?

text_entry: But how or in what place I do not know.

text_entry: Come to me, Tyrrel, soon at after supper,

text_entry: And thou shalt tell the process of their death.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Meantime, but think how I may do thee good,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: And be inheritor of thy desire.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Farewell till soon.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Exit TYRREL

speaker: KING RICHARD III

text_entry: Than Buckingham and his rash-levied army.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Come, I have heard that fearful commenting

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Is leaden servitor to dull delay;

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Delay leads impotent and snail-paced beggary

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Then fiery expedition be my wing,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Joves Mercury, and herald for a king!

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Come, muster men: my counsel is my shield;

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: We must be brief when traitors brave the field.

speaker: KING RICHARD III

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: SCENE IV. Before the palace.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Enter QUEEN MARGARET

text_entry: So, now prosperity begins to mellow

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And drop into the rotten mouth of death.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Here in these confines slily have I lurkd,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: To watch the waning of mine adversaries.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: A dire induction am I witness to,

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: And will to France, hoping the consequence

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Will prove as bitter, black, and tragical.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text_entry: Withdraw thee, wretched Margaret: who comes here?
