speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: By the false faith of him I trusted most;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: This, this All-Souls day to my fearful soul

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Is the determined respite of my wrongs:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: That high All-Seer that I dallied with

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Hath turnd my feigned prayer on my head

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And given in earnest what I beggd in jest.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Thus doth he force the swords of wicked men

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: To turn their own points on their masters bosoms:

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Now Margarets curse is fallen upon my head;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: When he, quoth she, shall split thy heart with sorrow,

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Remember Margaret was a prophetess.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Come, sirs, convey me to the block of shame;

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Wrong hath but wrong, and blame the due of blame.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: SCENE II. The camp near Tamworth.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Enter RICHMOND, OXFORD, BLUNT, HERBERT, and others, with drum and colours

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Fellows in arms, and my most loving friends,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Bruised underneath the yoke of tyranny,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Thus far into the bowels of the land

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Have we marchd on without impediment;

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: And here receive we from our father Stanley

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Lines of fair comfort and encouragement.

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: The wretched, bloody, and usurping boar,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: That spoild your summer fields and fruitful vines,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Swills your warm blood like wash, and makes his trough

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: In your embowelld bosoms, this foul swine

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Lies now even in the centre of this isle,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Near to the town of Leicester, as we learn

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: From Tamworth thither is but one days march.

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: In Gods name, cheerly on, courageous friends,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: To reap the harvest of perpetual peace

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: By this one bloody trial of sharp war.

speaker: OXFORD
text_entry: Every mans conscience is a thousand swords,

speaker: OXFORD
text_entry: To fight against that bloody homicide.

speaker: HERBERT
text_entry: I doubt not but his friends will fly to us.

speaker: BLUNT
text_entry: He hath no friends but who are friends for fear.

speaker: BLUNT
text_entry: Which in his greatest need will shrink from him.

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: All for our vantage. Then, in Gods name, march:

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: True hope is swift, and flies with swallows wings:

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Kings it makes gods, and meaner creatures kings.

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: SCENE III. Bosworth Field.

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Enter KING RICHARD III in arms, with NORFOLK, SURREY, and others

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Here pitch our tents, even here in Bosworth field.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: My Lord of Surrey, why look you so sad?

speaker: SURREY
text_entry: My heart is ten times lighter than my looks.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: My Lord of Norfolk,--

speaker: NORFOLK
text_entry: Here, most gracious liege.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Norfolk, we must have knocks; ha! must we not?

speaker: NORFOLK
text_entry: We must both give and take, my gracious lord.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Up with my tent there! here will I lie tonight;

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: But where to-morrow?  Well, alls one for that.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Who hath descried the number of the foe?

speaker: NORFOLK
text_entry: Six or seven thousand is their utmost power.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Why, our battalion trebles that account:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Besides, the kings name is a tower of strength,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Which they upon the adverse party want.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Up with my tent there! Valiant gentlemen,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Let us survey the vantage of the field

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Call for some men of sound direction

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Lets want no discipline, make no delay,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: For, lords, to-morrow is a busy day.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Enter, on the other side of the field, RICHMOND,  Sir William Brandon, OXFORD, and others. Some of the Soldiers pitch RICHMONDs tent

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: The weary sun hath made a golden set,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: And by the bright track of his fiery car,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Gives signal, of a goodly day to-morrow.

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Sir William Brandon, you shall bear my standard.

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Give me some ink and paper in my tent

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Ill draw the form and model of our battle,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Limit each leader to his several charge,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: And part in just proportion our small strength.

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: My Lord of Oxford, you, Sir William Brandon,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: And you, Sir Walter Herbert, stay with me.

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: The Earl of Pembroke keeps his regiment:

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Good Captain Blunt, bear my good night to him

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: And by the second hour in the morning

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Desire the earl to see me in my tent:

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Yet one thing more, good Blunt, before thou gost,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Where is Lord Stanley quarterd, dost thou know?

speaker: BLUNT
text_entry: Unless I have mistaen his colours much,

speaker: BLUNT
text_entry: Which well I am assured I have not done,

speaker: BLUNT
text_entry: His regiment lies half a mile at least

speaker: BLUNT
text_entry: South from the mighty power of the king.

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: If without peril it be possible,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Good Captain Blunt, bear my good-night to him,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: And give him from me this most needful scroll.

speaker: BLUNT
text_entry: Upon my life, my lord, Ill under-take it;

speaker: BLUNT
text_entry: And so, God give you quiet rest to-night!

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Good night, good Captain Blunt. Come gentlemen,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Let us consult upon to-morrows business

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: In to our tent; the air is raw and cold.

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: They withdraw into the tent

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Enter, to his tent, KING RICHARD III, NORFOLK, RATCLIFF, CATESBY, and others

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: What ist oclock?

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: Its supper-time, my lord;

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: Its nine oclock.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: I will not sup to-night.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Give me some ink and paper.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: What, is my beaver easier than it was?

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: And all my armour laid into my tent?

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: If is, my liege; and all things are in readiness.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Good Norfolk, hie thee to thy charge;

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Use careful watch, choose trusty sentinels.

speaker: NORFOLK
text_entry: I go, my lord.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Stir with the lark to-morrow, gentle Norfolk.

speaker: NORFOLK
text_entry: I warrant you, my lord.

speaker: NORFOLK
text_entry: Exit

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Catesby!

speaker: CATESBY
text_entry: My lord?

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Send out a pursuivant at arms

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: To Stanleys regiment; bid him bring his power

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Before sunrising, lest his son George fall

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Into the blind cave of eternal night.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Exit CATESBY

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Fill me a bowl of wine. Give me a watch.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Saddle white Surrey for the field to-morrow.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Look that my staves be sound, and not too heavy.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Ratcliff!

speaker: RATCLIFF
text_entry: My lord?

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Sawst thou the melancholy Lord Northumberland?

speaker: RATCLIFF
text_entry: Thomas the Earl of Surrey, and himself,

speaker: RATCLIFF
text_entry: Much about cock-shut time, from troop to troop

speaker: RATCLIFF
text_entry: Went through the army, cheering up the soldiers.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: So, I am satisfied. Give me a bowl of wine:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: I have not that alacrity of spirit,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Nor cheer of mind, that I was wont to have.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Set it down. Is ink and paper ready?

speaker: RATCLIFF
text_entry: It is, my lord.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Bid my guard watch; leave me.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Ratcliff, about the mid of night come to my tent

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: And help to arm me. Leave me, I say.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Exeunt RATCLIFF and the other Attendants

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Enter DERBY to RICHMOND in his tent, Lords and others attending

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: Fortune and victory sit on thy helm!

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: All comfort that the dark night can afford

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Be to thy person, noble father-in-law!

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Tell me, how fares our loving mother?

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: I, by attorney, bless thee from thy mother

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: Who prays continually for Richmonds good:

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: So much for that. The silent hours steal on,

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: And flaky darkness breaks within the east.

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: In brief,--for so the season bids us be,--

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: Prepare thy battle early in the morning,

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: And put thy fortune to the arbitrement

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: Of bloody strokes and mortal-staring war.

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: I, as I may--that which I would I cannot,--

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: With best advantage will deceive the time,

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: And aid thee in this doubtful shock of arms:

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: But on thy side I may not be too forward

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: Lest, being seen, thy brother, tender George,

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: Be executed in his fathers sight.

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: Farewell: the leisure and the fearful time

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: Cuts off the ceremonious vows of love

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: And ample interchange of sweet discourse,

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: Which so long sunderd friends should dwell upon:

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: God give us leisure for these rites of love!

speaker: DERBY
text_entry: Once more, adieu: be valiant, and speed well!

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Good lords, conduct him to his regiment:

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Ill strive, with troubled thoughts, to take a nap,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Lest leaden slumber peise me down to-morrow,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: When I should mount with wings of victory:

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Once more, good night, kind lords and gentlemen.

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Exeunt all but RICHMOND

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: O Thou, whose captain I account myself,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Look on my forces with a gracious eye;

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Put in their hands thy bruising irons of wrath,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: That they may crush down with a heavy fall

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: The usurping helmets of our adversaries!

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Make us thy ministers of chastisement,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: That we may praise thee in the victory!

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: To thee I do commend my watchful soul,

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Ere I let fall the windows of mine eyes:

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Sleeping and waking, O, defend me still!

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Sleeps

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Enter the Ghost of Prince Edward, son to King Henry VI

speaker: RICHMOND
text_entry: Ghost

speaker: of Prince Edward
text_entry: [To KING RICHARD III]

speaker: of Prince Edward
text_entry: Let me sit heavy on thy soul to-morrow!

speaker: of Prince Edward
text_entry: Think, how thou stabdst me in my prime of youth

speaker: of Prince Edward
text_entry: At Tewksbury: despair, therefore, and die!

speaker: of Prince Edward
text_entry: To RICHMOND

speaker: of Prince Edward
text_entry: Be cheerful, Richmond; for the wronged souls

speaker: of Prince Edward
text_entry: Of butcherd princes fight in thy behalf

speaker: of Prince Edward
text_entry: King Henrys issue, Richmond, comforts thee.

speaker: of Prince Edward
text_entry: Enter the Ghost of King Henry VI

speaker: of Prince Edward
text_entry: Ghost

speaker: of King Henry VI
text_entry: [To KING RICHARD III]

speaker: of King Henry VI
text_entry: When I was mortal, my anointed body

speaker: of King Henry VI
text_entry: By thee was punched full of deadly holes

speaker: of King Henry VI
text_entry: Think on the Tower and me: despair, and die!

speaker: of King Henry VI
text_entry: Harry the Sixth bids thee despair, and die!

speaker: of King Henry VI
text_entry: To RICHMOND

speaker: of King Henry VI
text_entry: Virtuous and holy, be thou conqueror!

speaker: of King Henry VI
text_entry: Harry, that prophesied thou shouldst be king,

speaker: of King Henry VI
text_entry: Doth comfort thee in thy sleep: live, and flourish!

speaker: of King Henry VI
text_entry: Enter the Ghost of CLARENCE

speaker: Ghost of CLARENCE
text_entry: [To KING RICHARD III]

speaker: Ghost of CLARENCE
text_entry: Let me sit heavy on thy soul to-morrow!

speaker: Ghost of CLARENCE
text_entry: I, that was washd to death with fulsome wine,

speaker: Ghost of CLARENCE
text_entry: Poor Clarence, by thy guile betrayed to death!

speaker: Ghost of CLARENCE
text_entry: To-morrow in the battle think on me,

speaker: Ghost of CLARENCE
text_entry: And fall thy edgeless sword: despair, and die!--

speaker: Ghost of CLARENCE
text_entry: To RICHMOND

speaker: Ghost of CLARENCE
text_entry: Thou offspring of the house of Lancaster

speaker: Ghost of CLARENCE
text_entry: The wronged heirs of York do pray for thee

speaker: Ghost of CLARENCE
text_entry: Good angels guard thy battle! live, and flourish!

speaker: Ghost of CLARENCE
text_entry: Enter the Ghosts of RIVERS, GRAY, and VAUGHAN

speaker: Ghost of RIVERS
text_entry: [To KING RICHARD III]

speaker: Ghost of RIVERS
text_entry: Let me sit heavy on thy soul to-morrow,

speaker: Ghost of RIVERS
text_entry: Rivers. that died at Pomfret! despair, and die!

speaker: Ghost of GREY
text_entry: [To KING RICHARD III]

speaker: Ghost of GREY
text_entry: Think upon Grey, and let thy soul despair!

speaker: Ghost of VAUGHAN
text_entry: [To KING RICHARD III]

speaker: Ghost of VAUGHAN
text_entry: Think upon Vaughan, and, with guilty fear,

speaker: Ghost of VAUGHAN
text_entry: Let fall thy lance: despair, and die!

speaker: All
text_entry: [To RICHMOND]

speaker: All
text_entry: Awake, and think our wrongs in Richards bosom

speaker: All
text_entry: Will conquer him! awake, and win the day!

speaker: All
text_entry: Enter the Ghost of HASTINGS

speaker: Ghost of HASTINGS
text_entry: [To KING RICHARD III]

speaker: Ghost of HASTINGS
text_entry: Bloody and guilty, guiltily awake,

speaker: Ghost of HASTINGS
text_entry: And in a bloody battle end thy days!

speaker: Ghost of HASTINGS
text_entry: Think on Lord Hastings: despair, and die!

speaker: Ghost of HASTINGS
text_entry: To RICHMOND

speaker: Ghost of HASTINGS
text_entry: Quiet untroubled soul, awake, awake!

speaker: Ghost of HASTINGS
text_entry: Arm, fight, and conquer, for fair Englands sake!

speaker: Ghost of HASTINGS
text_entry: Enter the Ghosts of the two young Princes

speaker: Ghost of HASTINGS
text_entry: Ghosts

speaker: of young Princes
text_entry: [To KING RICHARD III]

speaker: of young Princes
text_entry: Dream on thy cousins smotherd in the Tower:

speaker: of young Princes
text_entry: Let us be led within thy bosom, Richard,

speaker: of young Princes
text_entry: And weigh thee down to ruin, shame, and death!

speaker: of young Princes
text_entry: Thy nephews souls bid thee despair and die!

speaker: of young Princes
text_entry: To RICHMOND

speaker: of young Princes
text_entry: Sleep, Richmond, sleep in peace, and wake in joy;

speaker: of young Princes
text_entry: Good angels guard thee from the boars annoy!

speaker: of young Princes
text_entry: Live, and beget a happy race of kings!

speaker: of young Princes
text_entry: Edwards unhappy sons do bid thee flourish.

speaker: of young Princes
text_entry: Enter the Ghost of LADY ANNE

speaker: Ghost of LADY ANNE
text_entry: [To KING RICHARD III]

speaker: Ghost of LADY ANNE
text_entry: Richard, thy wife, that wretched Anne thy wife,

speaker: Ghost of LADY ANNE
text_entry: That never slept a quiet hour with thee,

speaker: Ghost of LADY ANNE
text_entry: Now fills thy sleep with perturbations

speaker: Ghost of LADY ANNE
text_entry: To-morrow in the battle think on me,

speaker: Ghost of LADY ANNE
text_entry: And fall thy edgeless sword: despair, and die!

speaker: Ghost of LADY ANNE
text_entry: To RICHMOND

speaker: Ghost of LADY ANNE
text_entry: Thou quiet soul, sleep thou a quiet sleep

speaker: Ghost of LADY ANNE
text_entry: Dream of success and happy victory!

speaker: Ghost of LADY ANNE
text_entry: Thy adversarys wife doth pray for thee.

speaker: Ghost of LADY ANNE
text_entry: Enter the Ghost of BUCKINGHAM

speaker: Ghost of LADY ANNE
text_entry: Ghost

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: [To KING RICHARD III]

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The last was I that helped thee to the crown;

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The last was I that felt thy tyranny:

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: O, in the battle think on Buckingham,

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And die in terror of thy guiltiness!

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Dream on, dream on, of bloody deeds and death:

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: Fainting, despair; despairing, yield thy breath!

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: To RICHMOND

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: I died for hope ere I could lend thee aid:

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: But cheer thy heart, and be thou not dismayd:

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: God and good angel fight on Richmonds side;

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: And Richard falls in height of all his pride.

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: The Ghosts vanish

speaker: of BUCKINGHAM
text_entry: KING RICHARD III starts out of his dream

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Give me another horse: bind up my wounds.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Have mercy, Jesu!--Soft! I did but dream.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: O coward conscience, how dost thou afflict me!

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: The lights burn blue. It is now dead midnight.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Cold fearful drops stand on my trembling flesh.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: What do I fear?  myself?  theres none else by:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Richard loves Richard; that is, I am I.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Is there a murderer here?  No. Yes, I am:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Then fly. What, from myself?   Great reason why:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Lest I revenge. What, myself upon myself?

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Alack. I love myself. Wherefore?  for any good

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: That I myself have done unto myself?

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: O, no! alas, I rather hate myself

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: For hateful deeds committed by myself!

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: I am a villain: yet I lie. I am not.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Fool, of thyself speak well: fool, do not flatter.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: My conscience hath a thousand several tongues,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: And every tongue brings in a several tale,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: And every tale condemns me for a villain.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Perjury, perjury, in the highst degree

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Murder, stem murder, in the direst degree;

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: All several sins, all used in each degree,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Throng to the bar, crying all, Guilty! guilty!

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: I shall despair. There is no creature loves me;

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: And if I die, no soul shall pity me:

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Nay, wherefore should they, since that I myself

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Find in myself no pity to myself?

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Methought the souls of all that I had murderd

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Came to my tent; and every one did threat

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: To-morrows vengeance on the head of Richard.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Enter RATCLIFF

speaker: RATCLIFF
text_entry: My lord!

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Zounds! who is there?

speaker: RATCLIFF
text_entry: Ratcliff, my lord; tis I. The early village-cock

speaker: RATCLIFF
text_entry: Hath twice done salutation to the morn;

speaker: RATCLIFF
text_entry: Your friends are up, and buckle on their armour.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: O Ratcliff, I have dreamd a fearful dream!

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: What thinkest thou, will our friends prove all true?

speaker: RATCLIFF
text_entry: No doubt, my lord.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: O Ratcliff, I fear, I fear,--

speaker: RATCLIFF
text_entry: Nay, good my lord, be not afraid of shadows.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: By the apostle Paul, shadows to-night

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Have struck more terror to the soul of Richard

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Than can the substance of ten thousand soldiers

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Armed in proof, and led by shallow Richmond.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: It is not yet near day. Come, go with me;

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Under our tents Ill play the eaves-dropper,

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: To see if any mean to shrink from me.

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: KING RICHARD III
text_entry: Enter the Lords to RICHMOND, sitting in his tent

speaker: LORDS
text_entry: Good morrow, Richmond!

speaker: RICHMOND

text_entry: Cankerd with peace, to part your cankerd hate:

speaker: PRINCE
text_entry: If ever you disturb our streets again,

speaker: PRINCE
text_entry: Your lives shall pay the forfeit of the peace.

speaker: PRINCE
text_entry: For this time, all the rest depart away:

speaker: PRINCE
text_entry: You Capulet; shall go along with me:

speaker: PRINCE
text_entry: And, Montague, come you this afternoon,

speaker: PRINCE
text_entry: To know our further pleasure in this case,

speaker: PRINCE
text_entry: To old Free-town, our common judgment-place.

speaker: PRINCE
text_entry: Once more, on pain of death, all men depart.

speaker: PRINCE
text_entry: Exeunt all but MONTAGUE, LADY MONTAGUE, and BENVOLIO

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Who set this ancient quarrel new abroach?

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Speak, nephew, were you by when it began?

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Here were the servants of your adversary,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: And yours, close fighting ere I did approach:

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: I drew to part them: in the instant came

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: The fiery Tybalt, with his sword prepared,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Which, as he breathed defiance to my ears,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: He swung about his head and cut the winds,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Who nothing hurt withal hissd him in scorn:

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: While we were interchanging thrusts and blows,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Came more and more and fought on part and part,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Till the prince came, who parted either part.

speaker: LADY MONTAGUE
text_entry: O, where is Romeo? saw you him to-day?

speaker: LADY MONTAGUE
text_entry: Right glad I am he was not at this fray.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Madam, an hour before the worshippd sun

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Peerd forth the golden window of the east,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: A troubled mind drave me to walk abroad;

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Where, underneath the grove of sycamore

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: That westward rooteth from the citys side,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: So early walking did I see your son:

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Towards him I made, but he was ware of me

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: And stole into the covert of the wood:

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: I, measuring his affections by my own,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: That most are busied when theyre most alone,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Pursued my humour not pursuing his,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: And gladly shunnd who gladly fled from me.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Many a morning hath he there been seen,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: With tears augmenting the fresh morning dew.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Adding to clouds more clouds with his deep sighs;

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: But all so soon as the all-cheering sun

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Should in the furthest east begin to draw

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: The shady curtains from Auroras bed,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Away from the light steals home my heavy son,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: And private in his chamber pens himself,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Shuts up his windows, locks far daylight out

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: And makes himself an artificial night:

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Black and portentous must this humour prove,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Unless good counsel may the cause remove.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: My noble uncle, do you know the cause?

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: I neither know it nor can learn of him.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Have you importuned him by any means?

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Both by myself and many other friends:

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: But he, his own affections counsellor,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Is to himself--I will not say how true--

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: But to himself so secret and so close,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: So far from sounding and discovery,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: As is the bud bit with an envious worm,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Ere he can spread his sweet leaves to the air,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Or dedicate his beauty to the sun.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Could we but learn from whence his sorrows grow.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: We would as willingly give cure as know.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Enter ROMEO

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: See, where he comes: so please you, step aside;

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Ill know his grievance, or be much denied.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: I would thou wert so happy by thy stay,

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: To hear true shrift. Come, madam, lets away.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text_entry: Exeunt MONTAGUE and LADY MONTAGUE

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Good-morrow, cousin.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Is the day so young?

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: But new struck nine.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Ay me! sad hours seem long.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Was that my father that went hence so fast?

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: It was. What sadness lengthens Romeos hours?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Not having that, which, having, makes them short.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: In love?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Out--

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Of love?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Out of her favour, where I am in love.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Alas, that love, so gentle in his view,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Should be so tyrannous and rough in proof!

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Alas, that love, whose view is muffled still,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Should, without eyes, see pathways to his will!

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Where shall we dine? O me! What fray was here?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Yet tell me not, for I have heard it all.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Heres much to do with hate, but more with love.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Why, then, O brawling love! O loving hate!

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: O any thing, of nothing first create!

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: O heavy lightness! serious vanity!

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Mis-shapen chaos of well-seeming forms!

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Feather of lead, bright smoke, cold fire,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: sick health!

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Still-waking sleep, that is not what it is!

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: This love feel I, that feel no love in this.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Dost thou not laugh?

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: No, coz, I rather weep.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Good heart, at what?

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: At thy good hearts oppression.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Why, such is loves transgression.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Griefs of mine own lie heavy in my breast,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Which thou wilt propagate, to have it prest

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: With more of thine: this love that thou hast shown

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Doth add more grief to too much of mine own.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Love is a smoke raised with the fume of sighs;

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Being purged, a fire sparkling in lovers eyes;

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Being vexd a sea nourishd with lovers tears:

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: What is it else? a madness most discreet,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: A choking gall and a preserving sweet.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Farewell, my coz.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Soft! I will go along;

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: An if you leave me so, you do me wrong.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Tut, I have lost myself; I am not here;

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: This is not Romeo, hes some other where.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Tell me in sadness, who is that you love.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: What, shall I groan and tell thee?

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Groan! why, no.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: But sadly tell me who.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Bid a sick man in sadness make his will:

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Ah, word ill urged to one that is so ill!

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: In sadness, cousin, I do love a woman.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: I aimd so near, when I supposed you loved.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: A right good mark-man! And shes fair I love.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: A right fair mark, fair coz, is soonest hit.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Well, in that hit you miss: shell not be hit

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: With Cupids arrow; she hath Dians wit;

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: And, in strong proof of chastity well armd,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: From loves weak childish bow she lives unharmd.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: She will not stay the siege of loving terms,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Nor bide the encounter of assailing eyes,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Nor ope her lap to saint-seducing gold:

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: O, she is rich in beauty, only poor,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: That when she dies with beauty dies her store.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Then she hath sworn that she will still live chaste?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: She hath, and in that sparing makes huge waste,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: For beauty starved with her severity

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Cuts beauty off from all posterity.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: She is too fair, too wise, wisely too fair,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: To merit bliss by making me despair:

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: She hath forsworn to love, and in that vow

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Do I live dead that live to tell it now.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Be ruled by me, forget to think of her.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: O, teach me how I should forget to think.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: By giving liberty unto thine eyes;

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Examine other beauties.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Tis the way

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: To call hers exquisite, in question more:

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: These happy masks that kiss fair ladies brows

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Being black put us in mind they hide the fair;

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: He that is strucken blind cannot forget

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: The precious treasure of his eyesight lost:

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Show me a mistress that is passing fair,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: What doth her beauty serve, but as a note

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Where I may read who passd that passing fair?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Farewell: thou canst not teach me to forget.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Ill pay that doctrine, or else die in debt.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: SCENE II. A street.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Enter CAPULET, PARIS, and Servant

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: But Montague is bound as well as I,

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: In penalty alike; and tis not hard, I think,

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: For men so old as we to keep the peace.

speaker: PARIS
text_entry: Of honourable reckoning are you both;

speaker: PARIS
text_entry: And pity tis you lived at odds so long.

speaker: PARIS
text_entry: But now, my lord, what say you to my suit?

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: But saying oer what I have said before:

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: My child is yet a stranger in the world;

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: She hath not seen the change of fourteen years,

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Let two more summers wither in their pride,

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Ere we may think her ripe to be a bride.

speaker: PARIS
text_entry: Younger than she are happy mothers made.

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: And too soon marrd are those so early made.

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: The earth hath swallowd all my hopes but she,

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: She is the hopeful lady of my earth:

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: But woo her, gentle Paris, get her heart,

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: My will to her consent is but a part;

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: An she agree, within her scope of choice

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Lies my consent and fair according voice.

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: This night I hold an old accustomd feast,

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Whereto I have invited many a guest,

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Such as I love; and you, among the store,

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: One more, most welcome, makes my number more.

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: At my poor house look to behold this night

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Earth-treading stars that make dark heaven light:

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Such comfort as do lusty young men feel

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: When well-apparelld April on the heel

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Of limping winter treads, even such delight

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Among fresh female buds shall you this night

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Inherit at my house; hear all, all see,

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: And like her most whose merit most shall be:

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Which on more view, of many mine being one

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: May stand in number, though in reckoning none,

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Come, go with me.

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: To Servant, giving a paper

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Go, sirrah, trudge about

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Through fair Verona; find those persons out

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Whose names are written there, and to them say,

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: My house and welcome on their pleasure stay.

speaker: CAPULET
text_entry: Exeunt CAPULET and PARIS

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Find them out whose names are written here! It is

speaker: Servant
text_entry: written, that the shoemaker should meddle with his

speaker: Servant
text_entry: yard, and the tailor with his last, the fisher with

speaker: Servant
text_entry: his pencil, and the painter with his nets; but I am

speaker: Servant
text_entry: sent to find those persons whose names are here

speaker: Servant
text_entry: writ, and can never find what names the writing

speaker: Servant
text_entry: person hath here writ. I must to the learned.--In good time.

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Enter BENVOLIO and ROMEO

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Tut, man, one fire burns out anothers burning,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: One pain is lessend by anothers anguish;

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Turn giddy, and be holp by backward turning;

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: One desperate grief cures with anothers languish:

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Take thou some new infection to thy eye,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: And the rank poison of the old will die.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Your plaintain-leaf is excellent for that.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: For what, I pray thee?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: For your broken shin.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Why, Romeo, art thou mad?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Not mad, but bound more than a mad-man is;

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Shut up in prison, kept without my food,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Whippd and tormented and--God-den, good fellow.

speaker: Servant
text_entry: God gi god-den. I pray, sir, can you read?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Ay, mine own fortune in my misery.

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Perhaps you have learned it without book: but, I

speaker: Servant
text_entry: pray, can you read any thing you see?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Ay, if I know the letters and the language.

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Ye say honestly: rest you merry!

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Stay, fellow; I can read.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Reads

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Signior Martino and his wife and daughters;

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: County Anselme and his beauteous sisters; the lady

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: widow of Vitravio; Signior Placentio and his lovely

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: nieces; Mercutio and his brother Valentine; mine

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: uncle Capulet, his wife and daughters; my fair niece

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Rosaline; Livia; Signior Valentio and his cousin

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Tybalt, Lucio and the lively Helena. A fair

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: assembly: whither should they come?

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Up.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Whither?

speaker: Servant
text_entry: To supper; to our house.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Whose house?

speaker: Servant
text_entry: My masters.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Indeed, I should have askd you that before.

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Now Ill tell you without asking: my master is the

speaker: Servant
text_entry: great rich Capulet; and if you be not of the house

speaker: Servant
text_entry: of Montagues, I pray, come and crush a cup of wine.

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Rest you merry!

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Exit

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: At this same ancient feast of Capulets

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Sups the fair Rosaline whom thou so lovest,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: With all the admired beauties of Verona:

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Go thither; and, with unattainted eye,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Compare her face with some that I shall show,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: And I will make thee think thy swan a crow.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: When the devout religion of mine eye

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Maintains such falsehood, then turn tears to fires;

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: And these, who often drownd could never die,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Transparent heretics, be burnt for liars!

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: One fairer than my love! the all-seeing sun

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Neer saw her match since first the world begun.

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Tut, you saw her fair, none else being by,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Herself poised with herself in either eye:

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: But in that crystal scales let there be weighd

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: Your ladys love against some other maid

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: That I will show you shining at this feast,

speaker: BENVOLIO
text_entry: And she shall scant show well that now shows best.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Ill go along, no such sight to be shown,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: But to rejoice in splendor of mine own.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: SCENE III. A room in Capulets house.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Enter LADY CAPULET and Nurse

speaker: LADY CAPULET
text_entry: Nurse, wheres my daughter? call her forth to me.

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Now, by my maidenhead, at twelve year old,

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: I bade her come. What, lamb! what, ladybird!

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: God forbid! Wheres this girl? What, Juliet!

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Enter JULIET

text_entry: How now! who calls?

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Your mother.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Madam, I am here.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: What is your will?

speaker: LADY CAPULET
text_entry: This is the matter:--Nurse, give leave awhile,

speaker: LADY CAPULET
text_entry: We must talk in secret:--nurse, come back again;

speaker: LADY CAPULET
text_entry: I have rememberd me, thous hear our counsel.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
text_entry: Thou knowst my daughters of a pretty age.

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Faith, I can tell her age unto an hour.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
text_entry: Shes not fourteen.

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Ill lay fourteen of my teeth,--

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: And yet, to my teeth be it spoken, I have but four--

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: She is not fourteen. How long is it now

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: To Lammas-tide?

speaker: LADY CAPULET
text_entry: A fortnight and odd days.

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Even or odd, of all days in the year,

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Come Lammas-eve at night shall she be fourteen.

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Susan and she--God rest all Christian souls!--

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Were of an age: well, Susan is with God;

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: She was too good for me: but, as I said,

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: On Lammas-eve at night shall she be fourteen;

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: That shall she, marry; I remember it well.

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Tis since the earthquake now eleven years;

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: And she was weand,--I never shall forget it,--

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Of all the days of the year, upon that day:

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: For I had then laid wormwood to my dug,

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Sitting in the sun under the dove-house wall;

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: My lord and you were then at Mantua:--

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Nay, I do bear a brain:--but, as I said,

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: When it did taste the wormwood on the nipple

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Of my dug and felt it bitter, pretty fool,

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: To see it tetchy and fall out with the dug!

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Shake quoth the dove-house: twas no need, I trow,

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: To bid me trudge:

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: And since that time it is eleven years;

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: For then she could stand alone; nay, by the rood,

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: She could have run and waddled all about;

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: For even the day before, she broke her brow:

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: And then my husband--God be with his soul!

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: A was a merry man--took up the child:

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Yea, quoth he, dost thou fall upon thy face?

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Thou wilt fall backward when thou hast more wit;

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Wilt thou not, Jule? and, by my holidame,

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: The pretty wretch left crying and said Ay.

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: To see, now, how a jest shall come about!

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: I warrant, an I should live a thousand years,

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: I never should forget it: Wilt thou not, Jule? quoth he;

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: And, pretty fool, it stinted and said Ay.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
text_entry: Enough of this; I pray thee, hold thy peace.

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Yes, madam: yet I cannot choose but laugh,

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: To think it should leave crying and say Ay.

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: And yet, I warrant, it had upon its brow

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: A bump as big as a young cockerels stone;

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: A parlous knock; and it cried bitterly:

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Yea, quoth my husband,fallst upon thy face?

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Thou wilt fall backward when thou comest to age;

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Wilt thou not, Jule? it stinted and said Ay.

text_entry: And stint thou too, I pray thee, nurse, say I.

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Peace, I have done. God mark thee to his grace!

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Thou wast the prettiest babe that eer I nursed:

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: An I might live to see thee married once,

speaker: Nurse

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Unto the white-upturned wondering eyes

speaker: ROMEO

text_entry: Tis but thy name that is my enemy;

text_entry: Thou art thyself, though not a Montague.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Whats Montague? it is nor hand, nor foot,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Nor arm, nor face, nor any other part

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Belonging to a man. O, be some other name!

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Whats in a name? that which we call a rose

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: By any other name would smell as sweet;

speaker: JULIET

text_entry: Retain that dear perfection which he owes

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Without that title. Romeo, doff thy name,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: And for that name which is no part of thee

text_entry: Take all myself.

text_entry: Henceforth I never will be Romeo.

text_entry: What man art thou that thus bescreend in night

text_entry: By a name

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: My name, dear saint, is hateful to myself,

text_entry: Because it is an enemy to thee;

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Had I it written, I would tear the word.

text_entry: My ears have not yet drunk a hundred words

text_entry: The orchard walls are high and hard to climb,

text_entry: And the place death, considering who thou art,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: If any of my kinsmen find thee here.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: With loves light wings did I oer-perch these walls;

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: For stony limits cannot hold love out,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: And what love can do that dares love attempt;

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Therefore thy kinsmen are no let to me.

text_entry: If they do see thee, they will murder thee.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Alack, there lies more peril in thine eye

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Than twenty of their swords: look thou but sweet,

text_entry: And I am proof against their enmity.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: I would not for the world they saw thee here.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: I have nights cloak to hide me from their sight;

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: And but thou love me, let them find me here:

text_entry: My life were better ended by their hate,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Than death prorogued, wanting of thy love.

text_entry: By whose direction foundst thou out this place?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: He lent me counsel and I lent him eyes.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: I am no pilot; yet, wert thou as far

speaker: JULIET

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: And I will take thy word: yet if thou swearst,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Thou mayst prove false; at lovers perjuries

text_entry: Then say, Jove laughs. O gentle Romeo,

text_entry: Ill frown and be perverse an say thee nay,

text_entry: Than those that have more cunning to be strange.

text_entry: I should have been more strange, I must confess,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: But that thou overheardst, ere I was ware,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: My true loves passion: therefore pardon me,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: And not impute this yielding to light love,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Which the dark night hath so discovered.

text_entry: Lady, by yonder blessed moon I swear

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: That tips with silver all these fruit-tree tops--

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: O, swear not by the moon, the inconstant moon,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: That monthly changes in her circled orb,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Lest that thy love prove likewise variable.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: What shall I swear by?

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Do not swear at all;

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Or, if thou wilt, swear by thy gracious self,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Which is the god of my idolatry,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: And Ill believe thee.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: If my hearts dear love--

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Well, do not swear: although I joy in thee,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: I have no joy of this contract to-night:

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: It is too rash, too unadvised, too sudden;

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Too like the lightning, which doth cease to be

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Ere one can say It lightens. Sweet, good night!

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: This bud of love, by summers ripening breath,

text_entry: May prove a beauteous flower when next we meet.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Good night, good night! as sweet repose and rest

text_entry: O, wilt thou leave me so unsatisfied?

text_entry: What satisfaction canst thou have to-night?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: The exchange of thy loves faithful vow for mine.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: I gave thee mine before thou didst request it:

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: And yet I would it were to give again.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Wouldst thou withdraw it? for what purpose, love?

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: But to be frank, and give it thee again.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: And yet I wish but for the thing I have:

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: My bounty is as boundless as the sea,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: My love as deep; the more I give to thee,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: The more I have, for both are infinite.

speaker: JULIET

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Anon, good nurse! Sweet Montague, be true.

speaker: JULIET

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Exit, above

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: O blessed, blessed night! I am afeard.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Being in night, all this is but a dream,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Too flattering-sweet to be substantial.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Re-enter JULIET, above

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Three words, dear Romeo, and good night indeed.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: If that thy bent of love be honourable,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Thy purpose marriage, send me word to-morrow,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: By one that Ill procure to come to thee,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Where and what time thou wilt perform the rite;

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: And all my fortunes at thy foot Ill lay

text_entry: And follow thee my lord throughout the world.

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: [Within]  Madam!

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: I come, anon.--But if thou meanst not well,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: I do beseech thee--

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: [Within]  Madam!

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: By and by, I come:--

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: To cease thy suit, and leave me to my grief:

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: To-morrow will I send.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: So thrive my soul--

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: A thousand times good night!

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Exit, above

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: A thousand times the worse, to want thy light.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Love goes toward love, as schoolboys from

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: their books,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: But love from love, toward school with heavy looks.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Retiring

text_entry: Hist! Romeo, hist! O, for a falconers voice,

text_entry: To lure this tassel-gentle back again!

text_entry: Bondage is hoarse, and may not speak aloud;

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Else would I tear the cave where Echo lies,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: And make her airy tongue more hoarse than mine,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: With repetition of my Romeos name.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: It is my soul that calls upon my name:

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: How silver-sweet sound lovers tongues by night,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Like softest music to attending ears!

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Romeo!

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: My dear?

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: At what oclock to-morrow

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Shall I send to thee?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: At the hour of nine.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: I will not fail: tis twenty years till then.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: I have forgot why I did call thee back.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Let me stand here till thou remember it.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: I shall forget, to have thee still stand there,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Remembering how I love thy company.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: And Ill still stay, to have thee still forget,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Forgetting any other home but this.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Tis almost morning; I would have thee gone:

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: And yet no further than a wantons bird;

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Who lets it hop a little from her hand,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Like a poor prisoner in his twisted gyves,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: And with a silk thread plucks it back again,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: So loving-jealous of his liberty.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: I would I were thy bird.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Sweet, so would I:

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Yet I should kill thee with much cherishing.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Good night, good night! parting is such

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: sweet sorrow,

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: That I shall say good night till it be morrow.

speaker: JULIET
text_entry: Exit above

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Sleep dwell upon thine eyes, peace in thy breast!

speaker: ROMEO

speaker: ROMEO

text_entry: The day to cheer and nights dank dew to dry,

text_entry: We sucking on her natural bosom find,

text_entry: Many for many virtues excellent,

text_entry: None but for some and yet all different.

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: O, mickle is the powerful grace that lies

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: In herbs, plants, stones, and their true qualities:

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: For nought so vile that on the earth doth live

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Nor aught so good but straind from that fair use

text_entry: Revolts from true birth, stumbling on abuse:

text_entry: Virtue itself turns vice, being misapplied;

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: And vice sometimes by action dignified.

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Within the infant rind of this small flower

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Poison hath residence and medicine power:

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: For this, being smelt, with that part cheers each part;

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Being tasted, slays all senses with the heart.

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Two such opposed kings encamp them still

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: In man as well as herbs, grace and rude will;

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: And where the worser is predominant,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Full soon the canker death eats up that plant.

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Enter ROMEO

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Good morrow, father.

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Benedicite!

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: What early tongue so sweet saluteth me?

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Young son, it argues a distemperd head

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: So soon to bid good morrow to thy bed:

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Care keeps his watch in every old mans eye,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: And where care lodges, sleep will never lie;

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: But where unbruised youth with unstuffd brain

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE

speaker: ROMEO

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Too familiar

text_entry: Is my dear son with such sour company:

text_entry: I bring thee tidings of the princes doom.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: What less than dooms-day is the princes doom?

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: A gentler judgment vanishd from his lips,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Not bodys death, but bodys banishment.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Ha, banishment! be merciful, say death;

text_entry: For exile hath more terror in his look,

speaker: ROMEO

speaker: ROMEO

speaker: ROMEO

text_entry: And worlds exile is death: then banished,

text_entry: Thou cuttst my head off with a golden axe,

text_entry: And smilest upon the stroke that murders me.

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: O deadly sin! O rude unthankfulness!

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE

text_entry: And sayst thou yet that exile is not death?

text_entry: Hadst thou no poison mixd, no sharp-ground knife,

text_entry: No sudden mean of death, though neer so mean,

text_entry: But banished to kill me?--banished?

text_entry: O friar, the damned use that word in hell;

text_entry: Howlings attend it: how hast thou the heart,

text_entry: Being a divine, a ghostly confessor,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: A sin-absolver, and my friend professd,

text_entry: Thou fond mad man, hear me but speak a word.

speaker: ROMEO

text_entry: Adversitys sweet milk, philosophy,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Let me dispute with thee of thy estate.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Thou canst not speak of that thou dost not feel:

text_entry: Wert thou as young as I, Juliet thy love,

speaker: ROMEO

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Doting like me and like me banished,

speaker: ROMEO

text_entry: O holy friar, O, tell me, holy friar,

text_entry: For Juliets sake, for her sake, rise and stand;

text_entry: Why should you fall into so deep an O?

text_entry: Nurse!

text_entry: Spakest thou of Juliet? how is it with her?

text_entry: Doth she not think me an old murderer,

text_entry: With blood removed but little from her own?

text_entry: Where is she? and how doth she? and what says

text_entry: My conceald lady to our cancelld love?

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: As if that name,

text_entry: Shot from the deadly level of a gun,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Did murder her; as that names cursed hand

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Murderd her kinsman. O, tell me, friar, tell me,

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: In what vile part of this anatomy

text_entry: Doth my name lodge? tell me, that I may sack

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: The hateful mansion.

speaker: ROMEO
text_entry: Drawing his sword

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Hold thy desperate hand:

text_entry: Art thou a man? thy form cries out thou art:

text_entry: Thy tears are womanish; thy wild acts denote

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: The unreasonable fury of a beast:

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Unseemly woman in a seeming man!

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Or ill-beseeming beast in seeming both!

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Thou hast amazed me: by my holy order,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: I thought thy disposition better temperd.

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Hast thou slain Tybalt? wilt thou slay thyself?

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: And stay thy lady too that lives in thee,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: By doing damned hate upon thyself?

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Why railst thou on thy birth, the heaven, and earth?

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Since birth, and heaven, and earth, all three do meet

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: In thee at once; which thou at once wouldst lose.

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Fie, fie, thou shamest thy shape, thy love, thy wit;

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Which, like a usurer, aboundst in all,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: And usest none in that true use indeed

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Which should bedeck thy shape, thy love, thy wit:

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Thy noble shape is but a form of wax,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Digressing from the valour of a man;

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Thy dear love sworn but hollow perjury,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Killing that love which thou hast vowd to cherish;

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Thy wit, that ornament to shape and love,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Misshapen in the conduct of them both,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Like powder in a skitless soldiers flask,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: Is set afire by thine own ignorance,

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
text_entry: And thou dismemberd with thine own defence.

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE

speaker: FRIAR LAURENCE
