speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And say she uttereth piercing eloquence:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: If she do bid me pack, Ill give her thanks,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: As though she bid me stay by her a week:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: If she deny to wed, Ill crave the day

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: When I shall ask the banns and when be married.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: But here she comes; and now, Petruchio, speak.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Enter KATHARINA

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Good morrow, Kate; for thats your name, I hear.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Well have you heard, but something hard of hearing:

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: They call me Katharina that do talk of me.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: You lie, in faith; for you are calld plain Kate,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And bonny Kate and sometimes Kate the curst;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: But Kate, the prettiest Kate in Christendom

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Kate of Kate Hall, my super-dainty Kate,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: For dainties are all Kates, and therefore, Kate,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Take this of me, Kate of my consolation;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Hearing thy mildness praised in every town,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Thy virtues spoke of, and thy beauty sounded,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Yet not so deeply as to thee belongs,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Myself am moved to woo thee for my wife.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Moved! in good time: let him that moved you hither

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Remove you hence: I knew you at the first

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: You were a moveable.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Why, whats a moveable?

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: A joind-stool.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Thou hast hit it: come, sit on me.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Asses are made to bear, and so are you.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Women are made to bear, and so are you.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: No such jade as you, if me you mean.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Alas! good Kate, I will not burden thee;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: For, knowing thee to be but young and light--

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Too light for such a swain as you to catch;

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: And yet as heavy as my weight should be.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Should be! should--buzz!

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Well taen, and like a buzzard.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: O slow-wingd turtle! shall a buzzard take thee?

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Ay, for a turtle, as he takes a buzzard.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Come, come, you wasp; i faith, you are too angry.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: If I be waspish, best beware my sting.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: My remedy is then, to pluck it out.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Ay, if the fool could find it where it lies,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Who knows not where a wasp does

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: wear his sting? In his tail.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: In his tongue.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Whose tongue?

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Yours, if you talk of tails: and so farewell.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: What, with my tongue in your tail? nay, come again,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Good Kate; I am a gentleman.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: That Ill try.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: She strikes him

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: I swear Ill cuff you, if you strike again.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: So may you lose your arms:

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: If you strike me, you are no gentleman;

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: And if no gentleman, why then no arms.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: A herald, Kate? O, put me in thy books!

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: What is your crest? a coxcomb?

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: A combless cock, so Kate will be my hen.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: No cock of mine; you crow too like a craven.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Nay, come, Kate, come; you must not look so sour.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: It is my fashion, when I see a crab.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Why, heres no crab; and therefore look not sour.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: There is, there is.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Then show it me.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Had I a glass, I would.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: What, you mean my face?

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Well aimd of such a young one.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Now, by Saint George, I am too young for you.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Yet you are witherd.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Tis with cares.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: I care not.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Nay, hear you, Kate: in sooth you scape not so.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: I chafe you, if I tarry: let me go.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: No, not a whit: I find you passing gentle.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Twas told me you were rough and coy and sullen,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And now I find report a very liar;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: For thou are pleasant, gamesome, passing courteous,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: But slow in speech, yet sweet as spring-time flowers:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Thou canst not frown, thou canst not look askance,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Nor bite the lip, as angry wenches will,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Nor hast thou pleasure to be cross in talk,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: But thou with mildness entertainst thy wooers,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: With gentle conference, soft and affable.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Why does the world report that Kate doth limp?

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: O slanderous world! Kate like the hazel-twig

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Is straight and slender and as brown in hue

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: As hazel nuts and sweeter than the kernels.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: O, let me see thee walk: thou dost not halt.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Go, fool, and whom thou keepst command.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Did ever Dian so become a grove

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: As Kate this chamber with her princely gait?

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: O, be thou Dian, and let her be Kate;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And then let Kate be chaste and Dian sportful!

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Where did you study all this goodly speech?

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: It is extempore, from my mother-wit.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: A witty mother! witless else her son.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Am I not wise?

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Yes; keep you warm.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Marry, so I mean, sweet Katharina, in thy bed:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And therefore, setting all this chat aside,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Thus in plain terms: your father hath consented

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: That you shall be my wife; your dowry greed on;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And, Will you, nill you, I will marry you.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Now, Kate, I am a husband for your turn;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: For, by this light, whereby I see thy beauty,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Thy beauty, that doth make me like thee well,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Thou must be married to no man but me;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: For I am he am born to tame you Kate,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And bring you from a wild Kate to a Kate

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Conformable as other household Kates.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Here comes your father: never make denial;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: I must and will have Katharina to my wife.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Re-enter BAPTISTA, GREMIO, and TRANIO

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Now, Signior Petruchio, how speed you with my daughter?

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: How but well, sir? how but well?

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: It were impossible I should speed amiss.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Why, how now, daughter Katharina! in your dumps?

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Call you me daughter? now, I promise you

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: You have showd a tender fatherly regard,

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: To wish me wed to one half lunatic;

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: A mad-cup ruffian and a swearing Jack,

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: That thinks with oaths to face the matter out.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Father, tis thus: yourself and all the world,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: That talkd of her, have talkd amiss of her:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: If she be curst, it is for policy,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: For shes not froward, but modest as the dove;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: She is not hot, but temperate as the morn;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: For patience she will prove a second Grissel,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And Roman Lucrece for her chastity:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And to conclude, we have greed so well together,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: That upon Sunday is the wedding-day.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Ill see thee hangd on Sunday first.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Hark, Petruchio; she says shell see thee

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: hangd first.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Is this your speeding? nay, then, good night our part!

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Be patient, gentlemen; I choose her for myself:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: If she and I be pleased, whats that to you?

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Tis bargaind twixt us twain, being alone,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: That she shall still be curst in company.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: I tell you, tis incredible to believe

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: How much she loves me: O, the kindest Kate!

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: She hung about my neck; and kiss on kiss

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: She vied so fast, protesting oath on oath,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: That in a twink she won me to her love.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: O, you are novices! tis a world to see,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: How tame, when men and women are alone,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: A meacock wretch can make the curstest shrew.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Give me thy hand, Kate: I will unto Venice,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: To buy apparel gainst the wedding-day.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Provide the feast, father, and bid the guests;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: I will be sure my Katharina shall be fine.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: I know not what to say: but give me your hands;

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: God send you joy, Petruchio! tis a match.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Amen, say we: we will be witnesses.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Father, and wife, and gentlemen, adieu;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: I will to Venice; Sunday comes apace:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: We will have rings and things and fine array;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And kiss me, Kate, we will be married oSunday.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Exeunt PETRUCHIO and KATHARINA severally

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Was ever match clappd up so suddenly?

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Faith, gentlemen, now I play a merchants part,

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: And venture madly on a desperate mart.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Twas a commodity lay fretting by you:

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Twill bring you gain, or perish on the seas.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: The gain I seek is, quiet in the match.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: No doubt but he hath got a quiet catch.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: But now, Baptists, to your younger daughter:

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Now is the day we long have looked for:

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: I am your neighbour, and was suitor first.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: And I am one that love Bianca more

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Than words can witness, or your thoughts can guess.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Youngling, thou canst not love so dear as I.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Graybeard, thy love doth freeze.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: But thine doth fry.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Skipper, stand back: tis age that nourisheth.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: But youth in ladies eyes that flourisheth.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Content you, gentlemen: I will compound this strife:

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Tis deeds must win the prize; and he of both

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: That can assure my daughter greatest dower

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Shall have my Biancas love.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Say, Signior Gremio, What can you assure her?

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: First, as you know, my house within the city

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Is richly furnished with plate and gold;

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Basins and ewers to lave her dainty hands;

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: My hangings all of Tyrian tapestry;

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: In ivory coffers I have stuffd my crowns;

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: In cypress chests my arras counterpoints,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Costly apparel, tents, and canopies,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Fine linen, Turkey cushions bossd with pearl,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Valance of Venice gold in needlework,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Pewter and brass and all things that belong

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: To house or housekeeping: then, at my farm

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: I have a hundred milch-kine to the pail,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Sixscore fat oxen standing in my stalls,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: And all things answerable to this portion.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Myself am struck in years, I must confess;

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: And if I die to-morrow, this is hers,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: If whilst I live she will be only mine.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: That only came well in. Sir, list to me:

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: I am my fathers heir and only son:

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: If I may have your daughter to my wife,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Ill leave her houses three or four as good,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Within rich Pisa walls, as any one

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Old Signior Gremio has in Padua;

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Besides two thousand ducats by the year

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Of fruitful land, all which shall be her jointure.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: What, have I pinchd you, Signior Gremio?

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Two thousand ducats by the year of land!

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: My land amounts not to so much in all:

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: That she shall have; besides an argosy

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: That now is lying in Marseilles road.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: What, have I choked you with an argosy?

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Gremio, tis known my father hath no less

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Than three great argosies; besides two galliases,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: And twelve tight galleys: these I will assure her,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: And twice as much, whateer thou offerst next.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Nay, I have offerd all, I have no more;

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: And she can have no more than all I have:

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: If you like me, she shall have me and mine.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Why, then the maid is mine from all the world,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: By your firm promise: Gremio is out-vied.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: I must confess your offer is the best;

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: And, let your father make her the assurance,

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: She is your own; else, you must pardon me,

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: if you should die before him, wheres her dower?

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Thats but a cavil: he is old, I young.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: And may not young men die, as well as old?

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Well, gentlemen,

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: I am thus resolved: on Sunday next you know

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: My daughter Katharina is to be married:

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Now, on the Sunday following, shall Bianca

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Be bride to you, if you this assurance;

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: If not, Signior Gremio:

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: And so, I take my leave, and thank you both.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Adieu, good neighbour.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Exit BAPTISTA

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Now I fear thee not:

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Sirrah young gamester, your father were a fool

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: To give thee all, and in his waning age

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Set foot under thy table: tut, a toy!

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: An old Italian fox is not so kind, my boy.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Exit

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: A vengeance on your crafty witherd hide!

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Yet I have faced it with a card of ten.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Tis in my head to do my master good:

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: I see no reason but supposed Lucentio

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Must get a father, calld supposed Vincentio;

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: And thats a wonder: fathers commonly

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Do get their children; but in this case of wooing,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: A child shall get a sire, if I fail not of my cunning.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Exit

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: ACT III

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: SCENE I. Padua. BAPTISTAS house.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Enter LUCENTIO, HORTENSIO, and BIANCA

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Fiddler, forbear; you grow too forward, sir:

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Have you so soon forgot the entertainment

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Her sister Katharina welcomed you withal?

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: But, wrangling pedant, this is

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: The patroness of heavenly harmony:

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Then give me leave to have prerogative;

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: And when in music we have spent an hour,

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Your lecture shall have leisure for as much.

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Preposterous ass, that never read so far

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: To know the cause why music was ordaind!

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Was it not to refresh the mind of man

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: After his studies or his usual pain?

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Then give me leave to read philosophy,

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: And while I pause, serve in your harmony.

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Sirrah, I will not bear these braves of thine.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Why, gentlemen, you do me double wrong,

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: To strive for that which resteth in my choice:

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: I am no breeching scholar in the schools;

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Ill not be tied to hours nor pointed times,

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: But learn my lessons as I please myself.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: And, to cut off all strife, here sit we down:

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Take you your instrument, play you the whiles;

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: His lecture will be done ere you have tuned.

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Youll leave his lecture when I am in tune?

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: That will be never: tune your instrument.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Where left we last?

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Here, madam:

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Hic ibat Simois; hic est Sigeia tellus;

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Hic steterat Priami regia celsa senis.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Construe them.

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Hic ibat, as I told you before, Simois, I am

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Lucentio, hic est, son unto Vincentio of Pisa,

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Sigeia tellus, disguised thus to get your love;

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Hic steterat, and that Lucentio that comes

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: a-wooing, Priami, is my man Tranio, regia,

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: bearing my port, celsa senis, that we might

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: beguile the old pantaloon.

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Madam, my instruments in tune.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Lets hear. O fie! the treble jars.

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Spit in the hole, man, and tune again.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Now let me see if I can construe it: Hic ibat

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Simois, I know you not, hic est Sigeia tellus, I

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: trust you not; Hic steterat Priami, take heed

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: he hear us not, regia, presume not, celsa senis,

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: despair not.

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Madam, tis now in tune.

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: All but the base.

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: The base is right; tis the base knave that jars.

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Aside

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: How fiery and forward our pedant is!

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Now, for my life, the knave doth court my love:

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Pedascule, Ill watch you better yet.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: In time I may believe, yet I mistrust.

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Mistrust it not: for, sure, AEacides

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Was Ajax, calld so from his grandfather.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: I must believe my master; else, I promise you,

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: I should be arguing still upon that doubt:

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: But let it rest. Now, Licio, to you:

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Good masters, take it not unkindly, pray,

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: That I have been thus pleasant with you both.

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: You may go walk, and give me leave a while:

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: My lessons make no music in three parts.

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Are you so formal, sir? well, I must wait,

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Aside

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: And watch withal; for, but I be deceived,

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Our fine musician groweth amorous.

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Madam, before you touch the instrument,

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: To learn the order of my fingering,

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: I must begin with rudiments of art;

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: To teach you gamut in a briefer sort,

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: More pleasant, pithy and effectual,

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Than hath been taught by any of my trade:

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: And there it is in writing, fairly drawn.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Why, I am past my gamut long ago.

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Yet read the gamut of Hortensio.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: [Reads]  Gamut I am, the ground of all accord,

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: A re, to Plead Hortensios passion;

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: B mi, Bianca, take him for thy lord,

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: C fa ut, that loves with all affection:

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: D sol re, one clef, two notes have I:

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: E la mi, show pity, or I die.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Call you this gamut? tut, I like it not:

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Old fashions please me best; I am not so nice,

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: To change true rules for old inventions.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Enter a Servant

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Mistress, your father prays you leave your books

speaker: Servant
text_entry: And help to dress your sisters chamber up:

speaker: Servant
text_entry: You know to-morrow is the wedding-day.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Farewell, sweet masters both; I must be gone.

speaker: BIANCA
text_entry: Exeunt BIANCA and Servant

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Faith, mistress, then I have no cause to stay.

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Exit

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: But I have cause to pry into this pedant:

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Methinks he looks as though he were in love:

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Yet if thy thoughts, Bianca, be so humble

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: To cast thy wandering eyes on every stale,

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Seize thee that list: if once I find thee ranging,

speaker: HORTENSIO

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Exit

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: SCENE II. Padua. Before BAPTISTAS house.

speaker: HORTENSIO
text_entry: Enter BAPTISTA, GREMIO, TRANIO, KATHARINA, BIANCA, LUCENTIO, and others, attendants

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: [To TRANIO]  Signior Lucentio, this is the

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: pointed day.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: That Katharina and Petruchio should be married,

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: And yet we hear not of our son-in-law.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: What will be said? what mockery will it be,

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: To want the bridegroom when the priest attends

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: To speak the ceremonial rites of marriage!

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: What says Lucentio to this shame of ours?

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: No shame but mine: I must, forsooth, be forced

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: To give my hand opposed against my heart

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Unto a mad-brain rudesby full of spleen;

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Who wood in haste and means to wed at leisure.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: I told you, I, he was a frantic fool,

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Hiding his bitter jests in blunt behavior:

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: And, to be noted for a merry man,

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Hell woo a thousand, point the day of marriage,

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Make feasts, invite friends, and proclaim the banns;

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Yet never means to wed where he hath wood.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Now must the world point at poor Katharina,

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: And say, Lo, there is mad Petruchios wife,

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: If it would please him come and marry her!

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Patience, good Katharina, and Baptista too.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Upon my life, Petruchio means but well,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Whatever fortune stays him from his word:

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Though he be blunt, I know him passing wise;

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Though he be merry, yet withal hes honest.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Would Katharina had never seen him though!

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Exit weeping, followed by BIANCA and others

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Go, girl; I cannot blame thee now to weep;

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: For such an injury would vex a very saint,

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Much more a shrew of thy impatient humour.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Enter BIONDELLO

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: Master, master! news, old news, and such news as

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: you never heard of!

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Is it new and old too? how may that be?

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: Why, is it not news, to hear of Petruchios coming?

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Is he come?

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: Why, no, sir.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: What then?

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: He is coming.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: When will he be here?

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: When he stands where I am and sees you there.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: But say, what to thine old news?

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: Why, Petruchio is coming in a new hat and an old

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: jerkin, a pair of old breeches thrice turned, a pair

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: of boots that have been candle-cases, one buckled,

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: another laced, an old rusty sword taen out of the

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: town-armory, with a broken hilt, and chapeless;

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: with two broken points: his horse hipped with an

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: old mothy saddle and stirrups of no kindred;

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: besides, possessed with the glanders and like to mose

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: in the chine; troubled with the lampass, infected

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: with the fashions, full of wingdalls, sped with

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: spavins, rayed with yellows, past cure of the fives,

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: stark spoiled with the staggers, begnawn with the

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: bots, swayed in the back and shoulder-shotten;

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: near-legged before and with, a half-chequed bit

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: and a head-stall of sheeps leather which, being

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: restrained to keep him from stumbling, hath been

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: often burst and now repaired with knots; one girth

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: six time pieced and a womans crupper of velure,

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: which hath two letters for her name fairly set down

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: in studs, and here and there pieced with packthread.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Who comes with him?

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: O, sir, his lackey, for all the world caparisoned

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: like the horse; with a linen stock on one leg and a

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: kersey boot-hose on the other, gartered with a red

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: and blue list; an old hat and the humour of forty

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: fancies pricked int for a feather: a monster, a

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: very monster in apparel, and not like a Christian

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: footboy or a gentlemans lackey.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Tis some odd humour pricks him to this fashion;

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Yet oftentimes he goes but mean-apparelld.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: I am glad hes come, howsoeer he comes.

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: Why, sir, he comes not.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Didst thou not say he comes?

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: Who? that Petruchio came?

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Ay, that Petruchio came.

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: No, sir, I say his horse comes, with him on his back.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Why, thats all one.

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: Nay, by Saint Jamy,

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: I hold you a penny,

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: A horse and a man

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: Is more than one,

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: And yet not many.

speaker: BIONDELLO
text_entry: Enter PETRUCHIO and GRUMIO

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Come, where be these gallants? whos at home?

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: You are welcome, sir.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And yet I come not well.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: And yet you halt not.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Not so well apparelld

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: As I wish you were.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Were it better, I should rush in thus.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: But where is Kate? where is my lovely bride?

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: How does my father? Gentles, methinks you frown:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And wherefore gaze this goodly company,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: As if they saw some wondrous monument,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Some comet or unusual prodigy?

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Why, sir, you know this is your wedding-day:

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: First were we sad, fearing you would not come;

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Now sadder, that you come so unprovided.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Fie, doff this habit, shame to your estate,

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: An eye-sore to our solemn festival!

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: And tells us, what occasion of import

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Hath all so long detaind you from your wife,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: And sent you hither so unlike yourself?

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Tedious it were to tell, and harsh to hear:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Sufficeth I am come to keep my word,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Though in some part enforced to digress;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Which, at more leisure, I will so excuse

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: As you shall well be satisfied withal.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: But where is Kate? I stay too long from her:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: The morning wears, tis time we were at church.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: See not your bride in these unreverent robes:

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Go to my chamber; Put on clothes of mine.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Not I, believe me: thus Ill visit her.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: But thus, I trust, you will not marry her.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Good sooth, even thus; therefore ha done with words:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: To me shes married, not unto my clothes:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Could I repair what she will wear in me,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: As I can change these poor accoutrements,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Twere well for Kate and better for myself.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: But what a fool am I to chat with you,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: When I should bid good morrow to my bride,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And seal the title with a lovely kiss!

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Exeunt PETRUCHIO and GRUMIO

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: He hath some meaning in his mad attire:

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: We will persuade him, be it possible,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: To put on better ere he go to church.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Ill after him, and see the event of this.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Exeunt BAPTISTA, GREMIO, and attendants

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: But to her love concerneth us to add

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Her fathers liking: which to bring to pass,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: As I before unparted to your worship,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: I am to get a man,--whateer he be,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: It skills not much. well fit him to our turn,--

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: And he shall be Vincentio of Pisa;

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: And make assurance here in Padua

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Of greater sums than I have promised.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: So shall you quietly enjoy your hope,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: And marry sweet Bianca with consent.

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Were it not that my fellow-school-master

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Doth watch Biancas steps so narrowly,

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Twere good, methinks, to steal our marriage;

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Which once performd, let all the world say no,

speaker: LUCENTIO
text_entry: Ill keep mine own, despite of all the world.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: That by degrees we mean to look into,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: And watch our vantage in this business:

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Well over-reach the greybeard, Gremio,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: The narrow-prying father, Minola,

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: The quaint musician, amorous Licio;

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: All for my masters sake, Lucentio.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Re-enter GREMIO

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Signior Gremio, came you from the church?

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: As willingly as eer I came from school.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: And is the bride and bridegroom coming home?

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: A bridegroom say you? tis a groom indeed,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: A grumbling groom, and that the girl shall find.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Curster than she? why, tis impossible.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Why hes a devil, a devil, a very fiend.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Why, shes a devil, a devil, the devils dam.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Tut, shes a lamb, a dove, a fool to him!

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Ill tell you, Sir Lucentio: when the priest

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Should ask, if Katharina should be his wife,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Ay, by gogs-wouns, quoth he; and swore so loud,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: That, all-amazed, the priest let fall the book;

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: And, as he stoopd again to take it up,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: The mad-braind bridegroom took him such a cuff

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: That down fell priest and book and book and priest:

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Now take them up, quoth he, if any list.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: What said the wench when he rose again?

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Trembled and shook; for why, he stampd and swore,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: As if the vicar meant to cozen him.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: But after many ceremonies done,

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: He calls for wine: A health! quoth he, as if

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: He had been aboard, carousing to his mates

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: After a storm; quaffd off the muscadel

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: And threw the sops all in the sextons face;

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Having no other reason

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: But that his beard grew thin and hungerly

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: And seemd to ask him sops as he was drinking.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: This done, he took the bride about the neck

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: And kissd her lips with such a clamorous smack

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: That at the parting all the church did echo:

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: And I seeing this came thence for very shame;

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: And after me, I know, the rout is coming.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Such a mad marriage never was before:

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Hark, hark! I hear the minstrels play.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Music

speaker: GREMIO

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Gentlemen and friends, I thank you for your pains:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: I know you think to dine with me to-day,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And have prepared great store of wedding cheer;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: But so it is, my haste doth call me hence,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And therefore here I mean to take my leave.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Ist possible you will away to-night?

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: I must away to-day, before night come:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Make it no wonder; if you knew my business,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: You would entreat me rather go than stay.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: And, honest company, I thank you all,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: That have beheld me give away myself

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: To this most patient, sweet and virtuous wife:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Dine with my father, drink a health to me;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: For I must hence; and farewell to you all.

speaker: TRANIO
text_entry: Let us entreat you stay till after dinner.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: It may not be.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Let me entreat you.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: It cannot be.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Let me entreat you.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: I am content.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Are you content to stay?

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: I am content you shall entreat me stay;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: But yet not stay, entreat me how you can.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Now, if you love me, stay.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Grumio, my horse.

speaker: GRUMIO
text_entry: Ay, sir, they be ready: the oats have eaten the horses.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Nay, then,

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Do what thou canst, I will not go to-day;

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: No, nor to-morrow, not till I please myself.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: The door is open, sir; there lies your way;

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: You may be jogging whiles your boots are green;

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: For me, Ill not be gone till I please myself:

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Tis like youll prove a jolly surly groom,

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: That take it on you at the first so roundly.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: O Kate, content thee; prithee, be not angry.

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: I will be angry: what hast thou to do?

speaker: KATHARINA
text_entry: Father, be quiet; he shall stay my leisure.

speaker: GREMIO
text_entry: Ay, marry, sir, now it begins to work.

speaker: KATARINA
text_entry: Gentlemen, forward to the bridal dinner:

speaker: KATARINA
text_entry: I see a woman may be made a fool,

speaker: KATARINA
text_entry: If she had not a spirit to resist.

text_entry: Obey the bride, you that attend on her;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Go to the feast, revel and domineer,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Carouse full measure to her maidenhead,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Be mad and merry, or go hang yourselves:

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: But for my bonny Kate, she must with me.

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Nay, look not big, nor stamp, nor stare, nor fret;

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: She is my goods, my chattels; she is my house,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: My household stuff, my field, my barn,

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: My horse, my ox, my ass, my any thing;

speaker: PETRUCHIO

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Ill bring mine action on the proudest he

speaker: PETRUCHIO

speaker: PETRUCHIO
text_entry: Fear not, sweet wench, they shall not touch

speaker: PETRUCHIO

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: SCENE I. PETRUCHIOS country house.

speaker: BAPTISTA
text_entry: Enter GRUMIO

speaker: GRUMIO
text_entry: Fie, fie on all tired jades, on all mad masters, and

text_entry: all foul ways! Was ever man so beaten? was ever

text_entry: man so rayed? was ever man so weary? I am sent

speaker: GRUMIO

text_entry: Who is that calls so coldly?

text_entry: from my shoulder to my heel with no greater a run
