text_entry: SCENE III. A lonely part of the forest.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Enter AARON, with a bag of gold

speaker: AARON
text_entry: He that had wit would think that I had none,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: To bury so much gold under a tree,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: And never after to inherit it.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Let him that thinks of me so abjectly

text_entry: Know that this gold must coin a stratagem,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Which, cunningly effected, will beget

speaker: AARON
text_entry: A very excellent piece of villany:

speaker: AARON
text_entry: And so repose, sweet gold, for their unrest

text_entry: Hides the gold

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Enter TAMORA

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: My lovely Aaron, wherefore lookst thou sad,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: When every thing doth make a gleeful boast?

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: The birds chant melody on every bush,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: The snake lies rolled in the cheerful sun,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: The green leaves quiver with the cooling wind

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: And make a chequerd shadow on the ground:

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Under their sweet shade, Aaron, let us sit,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: And, whilst the babbling echo mocks the hounds,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Replying shrilly to the well-tuned horns,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: As if a double hunt were heard at once,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Let us sit down and mark their yelping noise;

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: And, after conflict such as was supposed

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: The wandering prince and Dido once enjoyd,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: When with a happy storm they were surprised

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: And curtaind with a counsel-keeping cave,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: We may, each wreathed in the others arms,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Our pastimes done, possess a golden slumber;

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Whiles hounds and horns and sweet melodious birds

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Be unto us as is a nurses song

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Of lullaby to bring her babe asleep.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Madam, though Venus govern your desires,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Saturn is dominator over mine:

speaker: AARON
text_entry: What signifies my deadly-standing eye,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: My silence and my cloudy melancholy,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: My fleece of woolly hair that now uncurls

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Even as an adder when she doth unroll

speaker: AARON
text_entry: To do some fatal execution?

speaker: AARON
text_entry: No, madam, these are no venereal signs:

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Vengeance is in my heart, death in my hand,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Blood and revenge are hammering in my head.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Hark Tamora, the empress of my soul,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Which never hopes more heaven than rests in thee,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: This is the day of doom for Bassianus:

speaker: AARON
text_entry: His Philomel must lose her tongue to-day,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Thy sons make pillage of her chastity

speaker: AARON
text_entry: And wash their hands in Bassianus blood.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Seest thou this letter? take it up, I pray thee,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: And give the king this fatal plotted scroll.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Now question me no more; we are espied;

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Here comes a parcel of our hopeful booty,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Which dreads not yet their lives destruction.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Ah, my sweet Moor, sweeter to me than life!

speaker: AARON
text_entry: No more, great empress; Bassianus comes:

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Be cross with him; and Ill go fetch thy sons

speaker: AARON
text_entry: To back thy quarrels, whatsoeer they be.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Exit

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Enter BASSIANUS and LAVINIA

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: Who have we here? Romes royal empress,

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: Unfurnishd of her well-beseeming troop?

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: Or is it Dian, habited like her,

text_entry: Who hath abandoned her holy groves

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: To see the general hunting in this forest?

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Saucy controller of our private steps!

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Had I the power that some say Dian had,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Thy temples should be planted presently

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: With horns, as was Actaeons; and the hounds

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Should drive upon thy new-transformed limbs,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Unmannerly intruder as thou art!

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Under your patience, gentle empress,

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Tis thought you have a goodly gift in horning;

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: And to be doubted that your Moor and you

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Are singled forth to try experiments:

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Jove shield your husband from his hounds to-day!

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Tis pity they should take him for a stag.

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: Believe me, queen, your swarth Cimmerian

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: Doth make your honour of his bodys hue,

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: Spotted, detested, and abominable.

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: Why are you sequesterd from all your train,

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: Dismounted from your snow-white goodly steed.

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: And wanderd hither to an obscure plot,

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: Accompanied but with a barbarous Moor,

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: If foul desire had not conducted you?

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: And, being intercepted in your sport,

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Great reason that my noble lord be rated

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: For sauciness. I pray you, let us hence,

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: And let her joy her raven-colourd love;

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: This valley fits the purpose passing well.

speaker: BASSIANUS
text_entry: The king my brother shall have note of this.

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Ay, for these slips have made him noted long:

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Good king, to be so mightily abused!

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Why have I patience to endure all this?

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Enter DEMETRIUS and CHIRON

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: How now, dear sovereign, and our gracious mother!

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Why doth your highness look so pale and wan?

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Have I not reason, think you, to look pale?

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: These two have ticed me hither to this place:

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: A barren detested vale, you see it is;

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: The trees, though summer, yet forlorn and lean,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Oercome with moss and baleful mistletoe:

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Here never shines the sun; here nothing breeds,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Unless the nightly owl or fatal raven:

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: And when they showd me this abhorred pit,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: They told me, here, at dead time of the night,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: A thousand fiends, a thousand hissing snakes,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Ten thousand swelling toads, as many urchins,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Would make such fearful and confused cries

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: As any mortal body hearing it

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Should straight fall mad, or else die suddenly.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: No sooner had they told this hellish tale,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: But straight they told me they would bind me here

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Unto the body of a dismal yew,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: And leave me to this miserable death:

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: And then they calld me foul adulteress,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Lascivious Goth, and all the bitterest terms

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: That ever ear did hear to such effect:

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: And, had you not by wondrous fortune come,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: This vengeance on me had they executed.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Revenge it, as you love your mothers life,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Or be ye not henceforth calld my children.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: This is a witness that I am thy son.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Stabs BASSIANUS

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: And this for me, struck home to show my strength.

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: Also stabs BASSIANUS, who dies

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Ay, come, Semiramis, nay, barbarous Tamora,

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: For no name fits thy nature but thy own!

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Give me thy poniard; you shall know, my boys

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Your mothers hand shall right your mothers wrong.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Stay, madam; here is more belongs to her;

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: First thrash the corn, then after burn the straw:

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: This minion stood upon her chastity,

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Upon her nuptial vow, her loyalty,

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: And with that painted hope braves your mightiness:

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: And shall she carry this unto her grave?

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: An if she do, I would I were an eunuch.

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: Drag hence her husband to some secret hole,

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: And make his dead trunk pillow to our lust.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: But when ye have the honey ye desire,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Let not this wasp outlive, us both to sting.

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: I warrant you, madam, we wil l make that sure.

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: Come, mistress, now perforce we will enjoy

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: That nice-preserved honesty of yours.

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: O Tamora! thou bearst a womans face,--

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: I will not hear her speak; away with her!

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Sweet lords, entreat her hear me but a word.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Listen, fair madam: let it be your glory

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: To see her tears; but be your heart to them

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: As unrelenting flint to drops of rain.

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: When did the tigers young ones teach the dam?

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: O, do not learn her wrath; she taught it thee;

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: The milk thou suckdst from her did turn to marble;

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Even at thy teat thou hadst thy tyranny.

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Yet every mother breeds not sons alike:

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: To CHIRON

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Do thou entreat her show a woman pity.

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: What, wouldst thou have me prove myself a bastard?

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Tis true; the raven doth not hatch a lark:

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Yet have I heard,--O, could I find it now!--

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: The lion moved with pity did endure

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: To have his princely paws pared all away:

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Some say that ravens foster forlorn children,

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: The whilst their own birds famish in their nests:

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: O, be to me, though thy hard heart say no,

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Nothing so kind, but something pitiful!

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: I know not what it means; away with her!

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: O, let me teach thee! for my fathers sake,

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: That gave thee life, when well he might have

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: slain thee,

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Be not obdurate, open thy deaf ears.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Hadst thou in person neer offended me,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Even for his sake am I pitiless.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Remember, boys, I pourd forth tears in vain,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: To save your brother from the sacrifice;

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: But fierce Andronicus would not relent;

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Therefore, away with her, and use her as you will,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: The worse to her, the better loved of me.

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: O Tamora, be calld a gentle queen,

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: And with thine own hands kill me in this place!

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: For tis not life that I have beggd so long;

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Poor I was slain when Bassianus died.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: What beggst thou, then? fond woman, let me go.

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Tis present death I beg; and one thing more

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: That womanhood denies my tongue to tell:

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: O, keep me from their worse than killing lust,

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: And tumble me into some loathsome pit,

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Where never mans eye may behold my body:

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Do this, and be a charitable murderer.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: So should I rob my sweet sons of their fee:

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: No, let them satisfy their lust on thee.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Away! for thou hast stayd us here too long.

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: No grace? no womanhood? Ah, beastly creature!

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: The blot and enemy to our general name!

speaker: LAVINIA
text_entry: Confusion fall--

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: Nay, then Ill stop your mouth. Bring thou her husband:

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: This is the hole where Aaron bid us hide him.

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: DEMETRIUS throws the body of BASSIANUS into the  pit; then exeunt DEMETRIUS and CHIRON, dragging off LAVINIA

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Farewell, my sons: see that you make her sure.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Neer let my heart know merry cheer indeed,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Till all the Andronici be made away.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Now will I hence to seek my lovely Moor,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: And let my spleenful sons this trull deflowr.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Exit

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Re-enter AARON, with QUINTUS and MARTIUS

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Come on, my lords, the better foot before:

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Straight will I bring you to the loathsome pit

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Where I espied the panther fast asleep.

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: My sight is very dull, whateer it bodes.

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: And mine, I promise you; weret not for shame,

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: Well could I leave our sport to sleep awhile.

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: Falls into the pit

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: What art thou falln? What subtle hole is this,

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Whose mouth is coverd with rude-growing briers,

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Upon whose leaves are drops of new-shed blood

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: As fresh as morning dew distilld on flowers?

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: A very fatal place it seems to me.

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Speak, brother, hast thou hurt thee with the fall?

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: O brother, with the dismallst object hurt

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: That ever eye with sight made heart lament!

speaker: AARON
text_entry: [Aside]  Now will I fetch the king to find them here,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: That he thereby may give a likely guess

speaker: AARON
text_entry: How these were they that made away his brother.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Exit

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: Why dost not comfort me, and help me out

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: From this unhallowed and blood-stained hole?

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: I am surprised with an uncouth fear;

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: A chilling sweat oer-runs my trembling joints:

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: My heart suspects more than mine eye can see.

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: To prove thou hast a true-divining heart,

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: Aaron and thou look down into this den,

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: And see a fearful sight of blood and death.

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Aaron is gone; and my compassionate heart

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Will not permit mine eyes once to behold

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: The thing whereat it trembles by surmise;

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: O, tell me how it is; for neer till now

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Was I a child to fear I know not what.

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: Lord Bassianus lies embrewed here,

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: All on a heap, like to a slaughterd lamb,

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: In this detested, dark, blood-drinking pit.

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: If it be dark, how dost thou know tis he?

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: Upon his bloody finger he doth wear

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: A precious ring, that lightens all the hole,

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: Which, like a taper in some monument,

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: Doth shine upon the dead mans earthy cheeks,

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: And shows the ragged entrails of the pit:

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: So pale did shine the moon on Pyramus

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: When he by night lay bathed in maiden blood.

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: O brother, help me with thy fainting hand--

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: If fear hath made thee faint, as me it hath--

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: Out of this fell devouring receptacle,

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: As hateful as Cocytus misty mouth.

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Reach me thy hand, that I may help thee out;

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Or, wanting strength to do thee so much good,

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: I may be pluckd into the swallowing womb

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Of this deep pit, poor Bassianus grave.

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: I have no strength to pluck thee to the brink.

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: Nor I no strength to climb without thy help.

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Thy hand once more; I will not loose again,

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Till thou art here aloft, or I below:

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Thou canst not come to me: I come to thee.

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Falls in

speaker: QUINTUS
text_entry: Enter SATURNINUS with AARON

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Along with me: Ill see what hole is here,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: And what he is that now is leapd into it.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Say who art thou that lately didst descend

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Into this gaping hollow of the earth?

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: The unhappy son of old Andronicus:

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: Brought hither in a most unlucky hour,

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: To find thy brother Bassianus dead.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: My brother dead! I know thou dost but jest:

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: He and his lady both are at the lodge

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Upon the north side of this pleasant chase;

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Tis not an hour since I left him there.

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: We know not where you left him all alive;

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: But, out, alas! here have we found him dead.

speaker: MARTIUS
text_entry: Re-enter TAMORA, with Attendants; TITUS ANDRONICUS, and Lucius

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Where is my lord the king?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Here, Tamora, though grieved with killing grief.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Where is thy brother Bassianus?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Now to the bottom dost thou search my wound:

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Poor Bassianus here lies murdered.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Then all too late I bring this fatal writ,

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: The complot of this timeless tragedy;

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: And wonder greatly that mans face can fold

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: In pleasing smiles such murderous tyranny.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: She giveth SATURNINUS a letter

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: [Reads]  An if we miss to meet him handsomely--

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Sweet huntsman, Bassianus tis we mean--

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Do thou so much as dig the grave for him:

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Thou knowst our meaning. Look for thy reward

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Among the nettles at the elder-tree

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Which overshades the mouth of that same pit

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Where we decreed to bury Bassianus.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Do this, and purchase us thy lasting friends.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: O Tamora! was ever heard the like?

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: This is the pit, and this the elder-tree.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Look, sirs, if you can find the huntsman out

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: That should have murdered Bassianus here.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: My gracious lord, here is the bag of gold.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: [To TITUS]  Two of thy whelps, fell curs of

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: bloody kind,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Have here bereft my brother of his life.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Sirs, drag them from the pit unto the prison:

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: There let them bide until we have devised

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Some never-heard-of torturing pain for them.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: What, are they in this pit? O wondrous thing!

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: How easily murder is discovered!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: High emperor, upon my feeble knee

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: I beg this boon, with tears not lightly shed,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That this fell fault of my accursed sons,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Accursed if the fault be proved in them,--

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: If it be proved! you see it is apparent.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Who found this letter? Tamora, was it you?

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Andronicus himself did take it up.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: I did, my lord: yet let me be their bail;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For, by my fathers reverend tomb, I vow

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: They shall be ready at your highness will

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: To answer their suspicion with their lives.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Thou shalt not bail them: see thou follow me.

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Some bring the murderd body, some the murderers:

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: Let them not speak a word; the guilt is plain;

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: For, by my soul, were there worse end than death,

speaker: SATURNINUS
text_entry: That end upon them should be executed.

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Andronicus, I will entreat the king;

speaker: TAMORA
text_entry: Fear not thy sons; they shall do well enough.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Come, Lucius, come; stay not to talk with them.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: SCENE IV. Another part of the forest.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Enter DEMETRIUS and CHIRON with LAVINIA, ravished; her hands cut off, and her tongue cut out

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: So, now go tell, an if thy tongue can speak,

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Who twas that cut thy tongue and ravishd thee.

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: Write down thy mind, bewray thy meaning so,

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: An if thy stumps will let thee play the scribe.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: See, how with signs and tokens she can scrowl.

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: Go home, call for sweet water, wash thy hands.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: She hath no tongue to call, nor hands to wash;

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: And so lets leave her to her silent walks.

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: An twere my case, I should go hang myself.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: If thou hadst hands to help thee knit the cord.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Exeunt DEMETRIUS and CHIRON

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Enter MARCUS

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Who is this? my niece, that flies away so fast!

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Cousin, a word; where is your husband?

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: If I do dream, would all my wealth would wake me!

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: If I do wake, some planet strike me down,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: That I may slumber in eternal sleep!

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Speak, gentle niece, what stern ungentle hands

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Have loppd and hewd and made thy body bare

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Of her two branches, those sweet ornaments,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Whose circling shadows kings have sought to sleep in,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: And might not gain so great a happiness

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: As have thy love? Why dost not speak to me?

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Alas, a crimson river of warm blood,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Like to a bubbling fountain stirrd with wind,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Doth rise and fall between thy rosed lips,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Coming and going with thy honey breath.

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: But, sure, some Tereus hath deflowered thee,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: And, lest thou shouldst detect him, cut thy tongue.

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Ah, now thou turnst away thy face for shame!

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: And, notwithstanding all this loss of blood,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: As from a conduit with three issuing spouts,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Yet do thy cheeks look red as Titans face

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Blushing to be encountered with a cloud.

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Shall I speak for thee? shall I say tis so?

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: O, that I knew thy heart; and knew the beast,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: That I might rail at him, to ease my mind!

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Sorrow concealed, like an oven stoppd,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Doth burn the heart to cinders where it is.

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Fair Philomela, she but lost her tongue,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: And in a tedious sampler sewd her mind:

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: But, lovely niece, that mean is cut from thee;

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: A craftier Tereus, cousin, hast thou met,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: And he hath cut those pretty fingers off,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: That could have better sewd than Philomel.

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: O, had the monster seen those lily hands

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Tremble, like aspen-leaves, upon a lute,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: And make the silken strings delight to kiss them,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: He would not then have touchd them for his life!

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Or, had he heard the heavenly harmony

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Which that sweet tongue hath made,

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: He would have droppd his knife, and fell asleep

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: As Cerberus at the Thracian poets feet.

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Come, let us go, and make thy father blind;

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: For such a sight will blind a fathers eye:

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: One hours storm will drown the fragrant meads;

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: What will whole months of tears thy fathers eyes?

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Do not draw back, for we will mourn with thee

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: O, could our mourning ease thy misery!

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: ACT III

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: SCENE I. Rome. A street.

speaker: MARCUS
text_entry: Enter Judges, Senators and Tribunes, with MARTIUS  and QUINTUS, bound, passing on to the place of execution; TITUS going before, pleading

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Hear me, grave fathers! noble tribunes, stay!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For pity of mine age, whose youth was spent

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: In dangerous wars, whilst you securely slept;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For all my blood in Romes great quarrel shed;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For all the frosty nights that I have watchd;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And for these bitter tears, which now you see

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Filling the aged wrinkles in my cheeks;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Be pitiful to my condemned sons,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Whose souls are not corrupted as tis thought.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For two and twenty sons I never wept,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Because they died in honours lofty bed.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Lieth down; the Judges,  and c., pass by him, and Exeunt

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For these, these, tribunes, in the dust I write

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: My hearts deep languor and my souls sad tears:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Let my tears stanch the earths dry appetite;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: My sons sweet blood will make it shame and blush.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O earth, I will befriend thee more with rain,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That shall distil from these two ancient urns,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Than youthful April shall with all his showers:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: In summers drought Ill drop upon thee still;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: In winter with warm tears Ill melt the snow

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And keep eternal spring-time on thy face,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: So thou refuse to drink my dear sons blood.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Enter LUCIUS, with his sword drawn

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O reverend tribunes! O gentle, aged men!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Unbind my sons, reverse the doom of death;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And let me say, that never wept before,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: My tears are now prevailing orators.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: O noble father, you lament in vain:

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: The tribunes hear you not; no man is by;

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: And you recount your sorrows to a stone.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Ah, Lucius, for thy brothers let me plead.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Grave tribunes, once more I entreat of you,--

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: My gracious lord, no tribune hears you speak.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Why, tis no matter, man; if they did hear,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: They would not mark me, or if they did mark,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: They would not pity me, yet plead I must;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Therefore I tell my sorrows to the stones;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Who, though they cannot answer my distress,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Yet in some sort they are better than the tribunes,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For that they will not intercept my tale:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: When I do weep, they humbly at my feet

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Receive my tears and seem to weep with me;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And, were they but attired in grave weeds,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Rome could afford no tribune like to these.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: A stone is soft as wax,--tribunes more hard than stones;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: A stone is silent, and offendeth not,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And tribunes with their tongues doom men to death.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Rises

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But wherefore standst thou with thy weapon drawn?

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: To rescue my two brothers from their death:

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: For which attempt the judges have pronounced

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: My everlasting doom of banishment.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O happy man! they have befriended thee.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Why, foolish Lucius, dost thou not perceive

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That Rome is but a wilderness of tigers?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Tigers must prey, and Rome affords no prey

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But me and mine: how happy art thou, then,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: From these devourers to be banished!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But who comes with our brother Marcus here?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Enter MARCUS and LAVINIA

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Titus, prepare thy aged eyes to weep;

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Or, if not so, thy noble heart to break:

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: I bring consuming sorrow to thine age.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Will it consume me? let me see it, then.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: This was thy daughter.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Why, Marcus, so she is.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Ay me, this object kills me!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Faint-hearted boy, arise, and look upon her.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Speak, Lavinia, what accursed hand

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Hath made thee handless in thy fathers sight?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: What fool hath added water to the sea,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Or brought a faggot to bright-burning Troy?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: My grief was at the height before thou camest,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And now like Nilus, it disdaineth bounds.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Give me a sword, Ill chop off my hands too;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For they have fought for Rome, and all in vain;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And they have nursed this woe, in feeding life;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: In bootless prayer have they been held up,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And they have served me to effectless use:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Now all the service I require of them

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Is that the one will help to cut the other.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Tis well, Lavinia, that thou hast no hands;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For hands, to do Rome service, are but vain.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Speak, gentle sister, who hath martyrd thee?

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O, that delightful engine of her thoughts

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That blabbd them with such pleasing eloquence,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Is torn from forth that pretty hollow cage,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Where, like a sweet melodious bird, it sung

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Sweet varied notes, enchanting every ear!

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: O, say thou for her, who hath done this deed?

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O, thus I found her, straying in the park,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Seeking to hide herself, as doth the deer

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That hath received some unrecuring wound.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: It was my deer; and he that wounded her

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Hath hurt me more than had he killed me dead:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For now I stand as one upon a rock

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Environed with a wilderness of sea,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Who marks the waxing tide grow wave by wave,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Expecting ever when some envious surge

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Will in his brinish bowels swallow him.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: This way to death my wretched sons are gone;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Here stands my other son, a banished man,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And here my brother, weeping at my woes.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But that which gives my soul the greatest spurn,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Is dear Lavinia, dearer than my soul.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Had I but seen thy picture in this plight,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: It would have madded me: what shall I do

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Now I behold thy lively body so?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Thou hast no hands, to wipe away thy tears:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Nor tongue, to tell me who hath martyrd thee:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Thy husband he is dead: and for his death

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Thy brothers are condemnd, and dead by this.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Look, Marcus! ah, son Lucius, look on her!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: When I did name her brothers, then fresh tears

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Stood on her cheeks, as doth the honey-dew

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Upon a gatherd lily almost witherd.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Perchance she weeps because they killd her husband;

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Perchance because she knows them innocent.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: If they did kill thy husband, then be joyful

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Because the law hath taen revenge on them.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: No, no, they would not do so foul a deed;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Witness the sorrow that their sister makes.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Gentle Lavinia, let me kiss thy lips.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Or make some sign how I may do thee ease:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Shall thy good uncle, and thy brother Lucius,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And thou, and I, sit round about some fountain,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Looking all downwards to behold our cheeks

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: How they are staind, as meadows, yet not dry,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: With miry slime left on them by a flood?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And in the fountain shall we gaze so long

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Till the fresh taste be taken from that clearness,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And made a brine-pit with our bitter tears?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Or shall we cut away our hands, like thine?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Or shall we bite our tongues, and in dumb shows

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Pass the remainder of our hateful days?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: What shall we do? let us, that have our tongues,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Plot some deuce of further misery,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: To make us wonderd at in time to come.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Sweet father, cease your tears; for, at your grief,

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: See how my wretched sister sobs and weeps.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Patience, dear niece. Good Titus, dry thine eyes.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Ah, Marcus, Marcus! brother, well I wot

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Thy napkin cannot drink a tear of mine,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For thou, poor man, hast drownd it with thine own.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Ah, my Lavinia, I will wipe thy cheeks.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Mark, Marcus, mark! I understand her signs:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Had she a tongue to speak, now would she say

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That to her brother which I said to thee:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: His napkin, with his true tears all bewet,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Can do no service on her sorrowful cheeks.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O, what a sympathy of woe is this,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: As far from help as Limbo is from bliss!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Enter AARON

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Titus Andronicus, my lord the emperor

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Sends thee this word,--that, if thou love thy sons,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Let Marcus, Lucius, or thyself, old Titus,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Or any one of you, chop off your hand,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: And send it to the king: he for the same

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Will send thee hither both thy sons alive;

speaker: AARON
text_entry: And that shall be the ransom for their fault.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O gracious emperor! O gentle Aaron!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Did ever raven sing so like a lark,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That gives sweet tidings of the suns uprise?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: With all my heart, Ill send the emperor My hand:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Good Aaron, wilt thou help to chop it off?

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Stay, father! for that noble hand of thine,

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: That hath thrown down so many enemies,

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Shall not be sent: my hand will serve the turn:

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: My youth can better spare my blood than you;

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: And therefore mine shall save my brothers lives.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Which of your hands hath not defended Rome,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And reard aloft the bloody battle-axe,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Writing destruction on the enemys castle?

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O, none of both but are of high desert:

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: My hand hath been but idle; let it serve

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: To ransom my two nephews from their death;

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Then have I kept it to a worthy end.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Nay, come, agree whose hand shall go along,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: For fear they die before their pardon come.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: My hand shall go.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: By heaven, it shall not go!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Sirs, strive no more: such witherd herbs as these

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Are meet for plucking up, and therefore mine.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Sweet father, if I shall be thought thy son,

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Let me redeem my brothers both from death.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And, for our fathers sake and mothers care,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Now let me show a brothers love to thee.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Agree between you; I will spare my hand.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Then Ill go fetch an axe.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But I will use the axe.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Exeunt LUCIUS and MARCUS

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Come hither, Aaron; Ill deceive them both:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Lend me thy hand, and I will give thee mine.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: [Aside]  If that be calld deceit, I will be honest,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: And never, whilst I live, deceive men so:

speaker: AARON
text_entry: But Ill deceive you in another sort,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: And that youll say, ere half an hour pass.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Cuts off TITUSs hand

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Re-enter LUCIUS and MARCUS

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Now stay your strife: what shall be is dispatchd.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Good Aaron, give his majesty my hand:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Tell him it was a hand that warded him

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: From thousand dangers; bid him bury it

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: More hath it merited; that let it have.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: As for my sons, say I account of them

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: As jewels purchased at an easy price;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And yet dear too, because I bought mine own.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: I go, Andronicus: and for thy hand

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Look by and by to have thy sons with thee.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Aside

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Their heads, I mean. O, how this villany

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Doth fat me with the very thoughts of it!

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Let fools do good, and fair men call for grace.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Aaron will have his soul black like his face.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Exit

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O, here I lift this one hand up to heaven,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And bow this feeble ruin to the earth:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: If any power pities wretched tears,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: To that I call!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: To LAVINIA

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: What, wilt thou kneel with me?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Do, then, dear heart; for heaven shall hear our prayers;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Or with our sighs well breathe the welkin dim,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And stain the sun with fog, as sometime clouds

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: When they do hug him in their melting bosoms.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O brother, speak with possibilities,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And do not break into these deep extremes.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Is not my sorrow deep, having no bottom?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Then be my passions bottomless with them.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But yet let reason govern thy lament.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: If there were reason for these miseries,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Then into limits could I bind my woes:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: When heaven doth weep, doth not the earth oerflow?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: If the winds rage, doth not the sea wax mad,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Threatening the welkin with his big-swoln face?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And wilt thou have a reason for this coil?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: I am the sea; hark, how her sighs do blow!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: She is the weeping welkin, I the earth:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Then must my sea be moved with her sighs;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Then must my earth with her continual tears

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Become a deluge, overflowd and drownd;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For why my bowels cannot hide her woes,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But like a drunkard must I vomit them.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Then give me leave, for losers will have leave

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: To ease their stomachs with their bitter tongues.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Enter a Messenger, with two heads and a hand

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Worthy Andronicus, ill art thou repaid

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: For that good hand thou sentst the emperor.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Here are the heads of thy two noble sons;

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: And heres thy hand, in scorn to thee sent back;

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Thy griefs their sports, thy resolution mockd;

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: That woe is me to think upon thy woes

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: More than remembrance of my fathers death.

speaker: Messenger
text_entry: Exit

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Now let hot AEtna cool in Sicily,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And be my heart an ever-burning hell!

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: These miseries are more than may be borne.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: To weep with them that weep doth ease some deal;

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But sorrow flouted at is double death.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Ah, that this sight should make so deep a wound,

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: And yet detested life not shrink thereat!

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: That ever death should let life bear his name,

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Where life hath no more interest but to breathe!

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: LAVINIA kisses TITUS

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Alas, poor heart, that kiss is comfortless

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: As frozen water to a starved snake.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: When will this fearful slumber have an end?

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Now, farewell, flattery: die, Andronicus;

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Thou dost not slumber: see, thy two sons heads,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Thy warlike hand, thy mangled daughter here:

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Thy other banishd son, with this dear sight

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Struck pale and bloodless; and thy brother, I,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Even like a stony image, cold and numb.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Ah, now no more will I control thy griefs:

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Rend off thy silver hair, thy other hand

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Gnawing with thy teeth; and be this dismal sight

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: The closing up of our most wretched eyes;

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Now is a time to storm; why art thou still?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Ha, ha, ha!

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Why dost thou laugh? it fits not with this hour.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Why, I have not another tear to shed:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Besides, this sorrow is an enemy,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And would usurp upon my watery eyes

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And make them blind with tributary tears:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Then which way shall I find Revenges cave?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For these two heads do seem to speak to me,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And threat me I shall never come to bliss

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Till all these mischiefs be returnd again

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Even in their throats that have committed them.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Come, let me see what task I have to do.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: You heavy people, circle me about,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That I may turn me to each one of you,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And swear unto my soul to right your wrongs.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: The vow is made. Come, brother, take a head;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And in this hand the other I will bear.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Lavinia, thou shalt be employd: these arms!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Bear thou my hand, sweet wench, between thy teeth.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: As for thee, boy, go get thee from my sight;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Thou art an exile, and thou must not stay:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Hie to the Goths, and raise an army there:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And, if you love me, as I think you do,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Lets kiss and part, for we have much to do.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Exeunt TITUS, MARCUS, and LAVINIA

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Farewell Andronicus, my noble father,

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: The wofullst man that ever lived in Rome:

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Farewell, proud Rome; till Lucius come again,

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: He leaves his pledges dearer than his life:

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Farewell, Lavinia, my noble sister;

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: O, would thou wert as thou tofore hast been!

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: But now nor Lucius nor Lavinia lives

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: But in oblivion and hateful griefs.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: If Lucius live, he will requite your wrongs;

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: And make proud Saturnine and his empress

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Beg at the gates, like Tarquin and his queen.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Now will I to the Goths, and raise a power,

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: To be revenged on Rome and Saturnine.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: SCENE II. A room in Tituss house. A banquet set out.

speaker: LUCIUS
text_entry: Enter TITUS, MARCUS, LAVINIA and Young LUCIUS, a boy

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: So, so; now sit: and look you eat no more

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Than will preserve just so much strength in us

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: As will revenge these bitter woes of ours.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Marcus, unknit that sorrow-wreathen knot:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Thy niece and I, poor creatures, want our hands,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And cannot passionate our tenfold grief

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: With folded arms. This poor right hand of mine

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Is left to tyrannize upon my breast;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Who, when my heart, all mad with misery,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Beats in this hollow prison of my flesh,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Then thus I thump it down.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: To LAVINIA

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Thou map of woe, that thus dost talk in signs!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: When thy poor heart beats with outrageous beating,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Thou canst not strike it thus to make it still.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Wound it with sighing, girl, kill it with groans;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Or get some little knife between thy teeth,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And just against thy heart make thou a hole;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That all the tears that thy poor eyes let fall

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: May run into that sink, and soaking in

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Drown the lamenting fool in sea-salt tears.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Fie, brother, fie! teach her not thus to lay

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Such violent hands upon her tender life.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: How now! has sorrow made thee dote already?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Why, Marcus, no man should be mad but I.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: What violent hands can she lay on her life?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Ah, wherefore dost thou urge the name of hands;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: To bid AEneas tell the tale twice oer,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: How Troy was burnt and he made miserable?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O, handle not the theme, to talk of hands,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Lest we remember still that we have none.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Fie, fie, how franticly I square my talk,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: As if we should forget we had no hands,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: If Marcus did not name the word of hands!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Come, lets fall to; and, gentle girl, eat this:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Here is no drink! Hark, Marcus, what she says;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: I can interpret all her martyrd signs;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: She says she drinks no other drink but tears,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Brewd with her sorrow, meshd upon her cheeks:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Speechless complainer, I will learn thy thought;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: In thy dumb action will I be as perfect

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: As begging hermits in their holy prayers:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Thou shalt not sigh, nor hold thy stumps to heaven,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Nor wink, nor nod, nor kneel, nor make a sign,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But I of these will wrest an alphabet

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And by still practise learn to know thy meaning.

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Good grandsire, leave these bitter deep laments:

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Make my aunt merry with some pleasing tale.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Alas, the tender boy, in passion moved,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Doth weep to see his grandsires heaviness.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Peace, tender sapling; thou art made of tears,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And tears will quickly melt thy life away.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: MARCUS strikes the dish with a knife

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: What dost thou strike at, Marcus, with thy knife?

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: At that that I have killd, my lord; a fly.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Out on thee, murderer! thou killst my heart;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Mine eyes are cloyd with view of tyranny:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: A deed of death done on the innocent

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Becomes not Titus brother: get thee gone:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: I see thou art not for my company.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Alas, my lord, I have but killd a fly.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But how, if that fly had a father and mother?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: How would he hang his slender gilded wings,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And buzz lamenting doings in the air!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Poor harmless fly,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That, with his pretty buzzing melody,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Came here to make us merry! and thou hast

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: killd him.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Pardon me, sir; it was a black ill-favord fly,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Like to the empress Moor; therefore I killd him.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O, O, O,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Then pardon me for reprehending thee,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For thou hast done a charitable deed.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Give me thy knife, I will insult on him;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Flattering myself, as if it were the Moor

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Come hither purposely to poison me.--

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Theres for thyself, and thats for Tamora.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Ah, sirrah!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Yet, I think, we are not brought so low,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But that between us we can kill a fly

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That comes in likeness of a coal-black Moor.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Alas, poor man! grief has so wrought on him,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: He takes false shadows for true substances.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Come, take away. Lavinia, go with me:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Ill to thy closet; and go read with thee

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Sad stories chanced in the times of old.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Come, boy, and go with me: thy sight is young,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And thou shalt read when mine begin to dazzle.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: ACT IV

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: SCENE I. Rome. Tituss garden.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Enter young LUCIUS, and LAVINIA running after him,  and the boy flies from her, with books under his arm. Then enter TITUS and MARCUS

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Help, grandsire, help! my aunt Lavinia

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Follows me every where, I know not why:

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Good uncle Marcus, see how swift she comes.

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Alas, sweet aunt, I know not what you mean.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Stand by me, Lucius; do not fear thine aunt.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: She loves thee, boy, too well to do thee harm.

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Ay, when my father was in Rome she did.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: What means my niece Lavinia by these signs?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Fear her not, Lucius: somewhat doth she mean:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: See, Lucius, see how much she makes of thee:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Somewhither would she have thee go with her.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Ah, boy, Cornelia never with more care

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Read to her sons than she hath read to thee

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Sweet poetry and Tullys Orator.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Canst thou not guess wherefore she plies thee thus?

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: My lord, I know not, I, nor can I guess,

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Unless some fit or frenzy do possess her:

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: For I have heard my grandsire say full oft,

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Extremity of griefs would make men mad;

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: And I have read that Hecuba of Troy

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Ran mad through sorrow: that made me to fear;

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Although, my lord, I know my noble aunt

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Loves me as dear as eer my mother did,

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: And would not, but in fury, fright my youth:

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Which made me down to throw my books, and fly--

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Causeless, perhaps. But pardon me, sweet aunt:

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: And, madam, if my uncle Marcus go,

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: I will most willingly attend your ladyship.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Lucius, I will.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: LAVINIA turns over with her stumps the books which LUCIUS has let fall

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: How now, Lavinia! Marcus, what means this?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Some book there is that she desires to see.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Which is it, girl, of these? Open them, boy.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But thou art deeper read, and better skilld

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Come, and take choice of all my library,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And so beguile thy sorrow, till the heavens

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Reveal the damnd contriver of this deed.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Why lifts she up her arms in sequence thus?

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: I think she means that there was more than one

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Confederate in the fact: ay, more there was;

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Or else to heaven she heaves them for revenge.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Lucius, what book is that she tosseth so?

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Grandsire, tis Ovids Metamorphoses;

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: My mother gave it me.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For love of her thats gone,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Perhaps she culld it from among the rest.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Soft! see how busily she turns the leaves!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Helping her

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: What would she find? Lavinia, shall I read?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: This is the tragic tale of Philomel,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And treats of Tereus treason and his rape:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And rape, I fear, was root of thine annoy.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: See, brother, see; note how she quotes the leaves.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Lavinia, wert thou thus surprised, sweet girl,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Ravishd and wrongd, as Philomela was,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Forced in the ruthless, vast, and gloomy woods? See, see!

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Ay, such a place there is, where we did hunt--

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O, had we never, never hunted there!--

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Patternd by that the poet here describes,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: By nature made for murders and for rapes.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O, why should nature build so foul a den,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Unless the gods delight in tragedies?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Give signs, sweet girl, for here are none

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: but friends,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: What Roman lord it was durst do the deed:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Or slunk not Saturnine, as Tarquin erst,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That left the camp to sin in Lucrece bed?

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Sit down, sweet niece: brother, sit down by me.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Apollo, Pallas, Jove, or Mercury,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Inspire me, that I may this treason find!

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: My lord, look here: look here, Lavinia:

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: This sandy plot is plain; guide, if thou canst

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: This after me, when I have writ my name

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Without the help of any hand at all.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: He writes his name with his staff, and guides it with feet and mouth

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Cursed be that heart that forced us to this shift!

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Write thou good niece; and here display, at last,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: What God will have discoverd for revenge;

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Heaven guide thy pen to print thy sorrows plain,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That we may know the traitors and the truth!

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: She takes the staff in her mouth, and guides it with her stumps, and writes

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O, do ye read, my lord, what she hath writ?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Stuprum. Chiron. Demetrius.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: What, what! the lustful sons of Tamora

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Performers of this heinous, bloody deed?

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Magni Dominator poli,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Tam lentus audis scelera? tam lentus vides?

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O, calm thee, gentle lord; although I know

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: There is enough written upon this earth

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: To stir a mutiny in the mildest thoughts

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And arm the minds of infants to exclaims.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: My lord, kneel down with me; Lavinia, kneel;

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And kneel, sweet boy, the Roman Hectors hope;

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And swear with me, as, with the woful fere

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And father of that chaste dishonourd dame,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Lord Junius Brutus sware for Lucrece rape,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That we will prosecute by good advice

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Mortal revenge upon these traitorous Goths,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And see their blood, or die with this reproach.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Tis sure enough, an you knew how.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But if you hunt these bear-whelps, then beware:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: The dam will wake; and, if she wind you once,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Shes with the lion deeply still in league,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And lulls him whilst she playeth on her back,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And when he sleeps will she do what she list.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: You are a young huntsman, Marcus; let it alone;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And, come, I will go get a leaf of brass,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And with a gad of steel will write these words,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And lay it by: the angry northern wind

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Will blow these sands, like Sibyls leaves, abroad,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And wheres your lesson, then? Boy, what say you?

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: I say, my lord, that if I were a man,

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Their mothers bed-chamber should not be safe

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: For these bad bondmen to the yoke of Rome.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Ay, thats my boy! thy father hath full oft

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: For his ungrateful country done the like.

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: And, uncle, so will I, an if I live.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Come, go with me into mine armoury;

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Lucius, Ill fit thee; and withal, my boy,

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Shalt carry from me to the empress sons

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Presents that I intend to send them both:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Come, come; thoult do thy message, wilt thou not?

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Ay, with my dagger in their bosoms, grandsire.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: No, boy, not so; Ill teach thee another course.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Lavinia, come. Marcus, look to my house:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Lucius and Ill go brave it at the court:

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Ay, marry, will we, sir; and well be waited on.

speaker: TITUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Exeunt TITUS, LAVINIA, and Young LUCIUS

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: O heavens, can you hear a good man groan,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: And not relent, or not compassion him?

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Marcus, attend him in his ecstasy,

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: That hath more scars of sorrow in his heart

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Than foemens marks upon his batterd shield;

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: But yet so just that he will not revenge.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Revenge, ye heavens, for old Andronicus!

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: SCENE II. The same. A room in the palace.

speaker: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
text_entry: Enter, from one side, AARON, DEMETRIUS, and  CHIRON; from the other side, Young LUCIUS, and an  Attendant, with a bundle of weapons, and verses writ upon them

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: Demetrius, heres the son of Lucius;

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: He hath some message to deliver us.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Ay, some mad message from his mad grandfather.

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: My lords, with all the humbleness I may,

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: I greet your honours from Andronicus.

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Aside

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: And pray the Roman gods confound you both!

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Gramercy, lovely Lucius: whats the news?

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: [Aside]  That you are both decipherd, thats the news,

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: For villains markd with rape.--May it please you,

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: My grandsire, well advised, hath sent by me

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: The goodliest weapons of his armoury

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: To gratify your honourable youth,

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: The hope of Rome; for so he bade me say;

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: And so I do, and with his gifts present

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Your lordships, that, whenever you have need,

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: You may be armed and appointed well:

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: And so I leave you both:

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Aside

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: like bloody villains.

speaker: Young LUCIUS
text_entry: Exeunt Young LUCIUS, and Attendant

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Whats here? A scroll; and written round about?

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Lets see;

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Reads

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Integer vitae, scelerisque purus,

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Non eget Mauri jaculis, nec arcu.

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: O, tis a verse in Horace; I know it well:

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: I read it in the grammar long ago.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Ay, just; a verse in Horace; right, you have it.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Aside

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Now, what a thing it is to be an ass!

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Heres no sound jest! the old man hath found their guilt;

speaker: AARON
text_entry: And sends them weapons wrapped about with lines,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: That wound, beyond their feeling, to the quick.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: But were our witty empress well afoot,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: She would applaud Andronicus conceit:

speaker: AARON
text_entry: But let her rest in her unrest awhile.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: And now, young lords, wast not a happy star

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Led us to Rome, strangers, and more than so,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Captives, to be advanced to this height?

speaker: AARON
text_entry: It did me good, before the palace gate

speaker: AARON
text_entry: To brave the tribune in his brothers hearing.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: But me more good, to see so great a lord

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Basely insinuate and send us gifts.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Had he not reason, Lord Demetrius?

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Did you not use his daughter very friendly?

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: I would we had a thousand Roman dames

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: At such a bay, by turn to serve our lust.

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: A charitable wish and full of love.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Here lacks but your mother for to say amen.

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: And that would she for twenty thousand more.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Come, let us go; and pray to all the gods

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: For our beloved mother in her pains.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: [Aside]  Pray to the devils; the gods have given us over.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Trumpets sound within

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Why do the emperors trumpets flourish thus?

speaker: CHIRON
text_entry: Belike, for joy the emperor hath a son.

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Soft! who comes here?

speaker: DEMETRIUS
text_entry: Enter a Nurse, with a blackamoor Child in her arms

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Good morr ow, lords:

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: O, tell me, did you see Aaron the Moor?

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Well, more or less, or neer a whit at all,

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Here Aaron is; and what with Aaron now?

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: O gentle Aaron, we are all undone!

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Now help, or woe betide thee evermore!

speaker: AARON
text_entry: Why, what a caterwauling dost thou keep!

speaker: AARON
text_entry: What dost thou wrap and fumble in thine arms?

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: O, that which I would hide from heavens eye,

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: Our empress shame, and stately Romes disgrace!

speaker: Nurse
text_entry: She is deliverd, lords; she is deliverd.

speaker: AARON
text_entry: To whom?
