speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: May worthy Troilus be half attachd

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: With that which here his passion doth express?

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Ay, Greek; and that shall be divulged well

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: In characters as red as Mars his heart

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Inflamed with Venus: never did young man fancy

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: With so eternal and so fixd a soul.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Hark, Greek: as much as I do Cressid love,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: So much by weight hate I her Diomed:

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: That sleeve is mine that hell bear on his helm;

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Were it a casque composed by Vulcans skill,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: My sword should bite it: not the dreadful spout

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Which shipmen do the hurricano call,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Constringed in mass by the almighty sun,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Shall dizzy with more clamour Neptunes ear

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: In his descent than shall my prompted sword

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Falling on Diomed.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Hell tickle it for his concupy.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: O Cressid! O false Cressid! false, false, false!

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Let all untruths stand by thy stained name,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: And theyll seem glorious.

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: O, contain yourself

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: Your passion draws ears hither.

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: Enter AENEAS

speaker: AENEAS
text_entry: I have been seeking you this hour, my lord:

speaker: AENEAS
text_entry: Hector, by this, is arming him in Troy;

speaker: AENEAS
text_entry: Ajax, your guard, stays to conduct you home.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Have with you, prince. My courteous lord, adieu.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Farewell, revolted fair! and, Diomed,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Stand fast, and wear a castle on thy head!

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: Ill bring you to the gates.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Accept distracted thanks.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Exeunt TROILUS, AENEAS, and ULYSSES

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Would I could meet that rogue Diomed! I would

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: croak like a raven; I would bode, I would bode.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Patroclus will give me any thing for the

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: intelligence of this whore: the parrot will not

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: do more for an almond than he for a commodious drab.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Lechery, lechery; still, wars and lechery; nothing

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: else holds fashion: a burning devil take them!

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Exit

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: SCENE III. Troy. Before Priams palace.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Enter HECTOR and ANDROMACHE

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: When was my lord so much ungently temperd,

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: To stop his ears against admonishment?

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: Unarm, unarm, and do not fight to-day.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: You train me to offend you; get you in:

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: By all the everlasting gods, Ill go!

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: My dreams will, sure, prove ominous to the day.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: No more, I say.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Enter CASSANDRA

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Where is my brother Hector?

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: Here, sister; armd, and bloody in intent.

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: Consort with me in loud and dear petition,

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: Pursue we him on knees; for I have dreamd

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: Of bloody turbulence, and this whole night

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: Hath nothing been but shapes and forms of slaughter.

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: O, tis true.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Ho! bid my trumpet sound!

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: No notes of sally, for the heavens, sweet brother.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Be gone, I say: the gods have heard me swear.

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: The gods are deaf to hot and peevish vows:

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: They are polluted offerings, more abhorrd

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Than spotted livers in the sacrifice.

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: O, be persuaded! do not count it holy

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: To hurt by being just: it is as lawful,

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: For we would give much, to use violent thefts,

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: And rob in the behalf of charity.

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: It is the purpose that makes strong the vow;

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: But vows to every purpose must not hold:

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Unarm, sweet Hector.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Hold you still, I say;

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Mine honour keeps the weather of my fate:

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Lie every man holds dear; but the brave man

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Holds honour far more precious-dear than life.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Enter TROILUS

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: How now, young man! meanst thou to fight to-day?

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: Cassandra, call my father to persuade.

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: Exit CASSANDRA

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: No, faith, young Troilus; doff thy harness, youth;

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: I am to-day i the vein of chivalry:

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Let grow thy sinews till their knots be strong,

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: And tempt not yet the brushes of the war.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Unarm thee, go, and doubt thou not, brave boy,

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Ill stand to-day for thee and me and Troy.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Brother, you have a vice of mercy in you,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Which better fits a lion than a man.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: What vice is that, good Troilus? chide me for it.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: When many times the captive Grecian falls,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Even in the fan and wind of your fair sword,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: You bid them rise, and live.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: O,tis fair play.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Fools play, by heaven, Hector.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: How now! how now!

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: For the love of all the gods,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Lets leave the hermit pity with our mothers,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: And when we have our armours buckled on,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: The venomd vengeance ride upon our swords,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Spur them to ruthful work, rein them from ruth.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Fie, savage, fie!

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Hector, then tis wars.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Troilus, I would not have you fight to-day.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Who should withhold me?

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Not fate, obedience, nor the hand of Mars

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Beckoning with fiery truncheon my retire;

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Not Priamus and Hecuba on knees,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Their eyes oergalled with recourse of tears;

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Not you, my brother, with your true sword drawn,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Opposed to  hinder me, should stop my way,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: But by my ruin.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Re-enter CASSANDRA, with PRIAM

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Lay hold upon him, Priam, hold him fast:

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: He is thy crutch; now if thou lose thy stay,

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Thou on him leaning, and all Troy on thee,

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Fall all together.

speaker: PRIAM
text_entry: Come, Hector, come, go back:

speaker: PRIAM
text_entry: Thy wife hath dreamd; thy mother hath had visions;

speaker: PRIAM
text_entry: Cassandra doth foresee; and I myself

speaker: PRIAM
text_entry: Am like a prophet suddenly enrapt

speaker: PRIAM
text_entry: To tell thee that this day is ominous:

speaker: PRIAM
text_entry: Therefore, come back.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: AEneas is a-field;

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: And I do stand engaged to many Greeks,

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Even in the faith of valour, to appear

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: This morning to them.

speaker: PRIAM
text_entry: Ay, but thou shalt not go.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: I must not break my faith.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: You know me dutiful; therefore, dear sir,

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Let me not shame respect; but give me leave

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: To take that course by your consent and voice,

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Which you do here forbid me, royal Priam.

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: O Priam, yield not to him!

speaker: ANDROMACHE
text_entry: Do not, dear father.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Andromache, I am offended with you:

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Upon the love you bear me, get you in.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Exit ANDROMACHE

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: This foolish, dreaming, superstitious girl

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Makes all these bodements.

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: O, farewell, dear Hector!

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Look, how thou diest! look, how thy eye turns pale!

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Look, how thy wounds do bleed at many vents!

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Hark, how Troy roars! how Hecuba cries out!

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: How poor Andromache shrills her dolours forth!

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Behold, distraction, frenzy and amazement,

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Like witless antics, one another meet,

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: And all cry, Hector! Hectors dead! O Hector!

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Away! away!

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Farewell: yet, soft! Hector! take my leave:

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Thou dost thyself and all our Troy deceive.

speaker: CASSANDRA
text_entry: Exit

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: You are amazed, my liege, at her exclaim:

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Go in and cheer the town: well forth and fight,

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Do deeds worth praise and tell you them at night.

speaker: PRIAM
text_entry: Farewell: the gods with safety stand about thee!

speaker: PRIAM
text_entry: Exeunt severally PRIAM and HECTOR. Alarums

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: They are at it, hark! Proud Diomed, believe,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: I come to lose my arm, or win my sleeve.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Enter PANDARUS

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Do you hear, my lord? do you hear?

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: What now?

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Heres a letter come from yond poor girl.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Let me read.

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: A whoreson tisick, a whoreson rascally tisick so

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: troubles me, and the foolish fortune of this girl;

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: and what one thing, what another, that I shall

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: leave you one o these days: and I have a rheum

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: in mine eyes too, and such an ache in my bones

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: that, unless a man were cursed, I cannot tell what

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: to think ont. What says she there?

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Words, words, mere words, no matter from the heart:

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: The effect doth operate another way.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Tearing the letter

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Go, wind, to wind, there turn and change together.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: My love with words and errors still she feeds;

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: But edifies another with her deeds.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Exeunt severally

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: SCENE IV. Plains between Troy and the Grecian camp.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Alarums: excursions. Enter THERSITES

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Now they are clapper-clawing one another; Ill go

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: look on. That dissembling abominable varlets Diomed,

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: has got that same scurvy doting foolish young knaves

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: sleeve of Troy there in his helm: I would fain see

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: them meet; that that same young Trojan ass, that

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: loves the whore there, might send that Greekish

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: whore-masterly villain, with the sleeve, back to the

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: dissembling luxurious drab, of a sleeveless errand.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: O the tother side, the policy of those crafty

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: swearing rascals, that stale old mouse-eaten dry

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: cheese, Nestor, and that same dog-fox, Ulysses, is

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: not proved worthy a blackberry: they set me up, in

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: policy, that mongrel cur, Ajax, against that dog of

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: as bad a kind, Achilles: and now is the cur Ajax

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: prouder than the cur Achilles, and will not arm

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: to-day; whereupon the Grecians begin to proclaim

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: barbarism, and policy grows into an ill opinion.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Soft! here comes sleeve, and tother.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Enter DIOMEDES, TROILUS following

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Fly not; for shouldst thou take the river Styx,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: I would swim after.

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: Thou dost miscall retire:

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: I do not fly, but advantageous care

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: Withdrew me from the odds of multitude:

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: Have at thee!

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Hold thy whore, Grecian!--now for thy whore,

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Trojan!--now the sleeve, now the sleeve!

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Exeunt TROILUS and DIOMEDES, fighting

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Enter HECTOR

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: What art thou, Greek? art thou for Hectors match?

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Art thou of blood and honour?

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: No, no, I am a rascal; a scurvy railing knave:

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: a very filthy rogue.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: I do believe thee: live.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Exit

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: God-a-mercy, that thou wilt believe me; but a

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: plague break thy neck for frightening me! Whats

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: become of the wenching rogues? I think they have

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: swallowed one another: I would laugh at that

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: miracle: yet, in a sort, lechery eats itself.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Ill seek them.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Exit

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: SCENE V. Another part of the plains.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Enter DIOMEDES and a Servant

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: Go, go, my servant, take thou Troilus horse;

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: Present the fair steed to my lady Cressid:

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: Fellow, commend my service to her beauty;

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: Tell her I have chastised the amorous Trojan,

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: And am her knight by proof.

speaker: Servant
text_entry: I go, my lord.

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Exit

speaker: Servant
text_entry: Enter AGAMEMNON

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Renew, renew! The fierce Polydamas

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Hath beat down Menon: bastard Margarelon

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Hath Doreus prisoner,

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: And stands colossus-wise, waving his beam,

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Upon the pashed corses of the kings

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Epistrophus and Cedius: Polyxenes is slain,

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Amphimachus and Thoas deadly hurt,

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Patroclus taen or slain, and Palamedes

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Sore hurt and bruised: the dreadful Sagittary

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Appals our numbers: haste we, Diomed,

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: To reinforcement, or we perish all.

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Enter NESTOR

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: Go, bear Patroclus body to Achilles;

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: And bid the snail-paced Ajax arm for shame.

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: There is a thousand Hectors in the field:

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: Now here he fights on Galathe his horse,

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: And there lacks work; anon hes there afoot,

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: And there they fly or die, like scaled sculls

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: Before the belching whale; then is he yonder,

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: And there the strawy Greeks, ripe for his edge,

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: Fall down before him, like the mowers swath:

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: Here, there, and every where, he leaves and takes,

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: Dexterity so obeying appetite

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: That what he will he does, and does so much

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: That proof is calld impossibility.

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: Enter ULYSSES

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: O, courage, courage, princes! great Achilles

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: Is arming, weeping, cursing, vowing vengeance:

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: Patroclus wounds have roused his drowsy blood,

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: Together with his mangled Myrmidons,

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: That noseless, handless, hackd and chippd, come to him,

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: Crying on Hector. Ajax hath lost a friend

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: And foams at mouth, and he is armd and at it,

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: Roaring for Troilus, who hath done to-day

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: Mad and fantastic execution,

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: Engaging and redeeming of himself

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: With such a careless force and forceless care

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: As if that luck, in very spite of cunning,

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: Bade him win all.

speaker: ULYSSES
text_entry: Enter AJAX

speaker: AJAX
text_entry: Troilus! thou coward Troilus!

speaker: AJAX
text_entry: Exit

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: Ay, there, there.

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: So, so, we draw together.

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: Enter ACHILLES

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Where is this Hector?

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Come, come, thou boy-queller, show thy face;

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Know what it is to meet Achilles angry:

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Hector? wheres Hector? I will none but Hector.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: SCENE VI. Another part of the plains.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Enter AJAX

speaker: AJAX
text_entry: Troilus, thou coward Troilus, show thy head!

speaker: AJAX
text_entry: Enter DIOMEDES

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: Troilus, I say! wheres Troilus?

speaker: AJAX
text_entry: What wouldst thou?

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: I would correct him.

speaker: AJAX
text_entry: Were I the general, thou shouldst have my office

speaker: AJAX
text_entry: Ere that correction. Troilus, I say! what, Troilus!

speaker: AJAX
text_entry: Enter TROILUS

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: O traitor Diomed! turn thy false face, thou traitor,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: And pay thy life thou owest me for my horse!

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: Ha, art thou there?

speaker: AJAX
text_entry: Ill fight with him alone: stand, Diomed.

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: He is my prize; I will not look upon.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Come, both you cogging Greeks; have at you both!

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Exeunt, fighting

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Enter HECTOR

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Yea, Troilus? O, well fought, my youngest brother!

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Enter ACHILLES

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Now do I see thee, ha! have at thee, Hector!

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Pause, if thou wilt.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: I do disdain thy courtesy, proud Trojan:

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Be happy that my arms are out of use:

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: My rest and negligence befriends thee now,

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: But thou anon shalt hear of me again;

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Till when, go seek thy fortune.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Exit

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Fare thee well:

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: I would have been much more a fresher man,

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Had I expected thee. How now, my brother!

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Re-enter TROILUS

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Ajax hath taen AEneas: shall it be?

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: No, by the flame of yonder glorious heaven,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: He shall not carry him: Ill be taen too,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Or bring him off: fate, hear me what I say!

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: I reck not though I end my life to-day.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Enter one in sumptuous armour

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Stand, stand, thou Greek; thou art a goodly mark:

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: No? wilt thou not? I like thy armour well;

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Ill frush it and unlock the rivets all,

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: But Ill be master of it: wilt thou not,

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: beast, abide?

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Why, then fly on, Ill hunt thee for thy hide.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: SCENE VII. Another part of the plains.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Enter ACHILLES, with Myrmidons

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Come here about me, you my Myrmidons;

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Mark what I say. Attend me where I wheel:

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Strike not a stroke, but keep yourselves in breath:

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: And when I have the bloody Hector found,

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Empale him with your weapons round about;

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: In fellest manner execute your aims.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Follow me, sirs, and my proceedings eye:

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: It is decreed Hector the great must die.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Enter MENELAUS and PARIS, fighting: then THERSITES

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: The cuckold and the cuckold-maker are at it. Now,

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: bull! now, dog! Loo, Paris, loo! now my double-

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: henned sparrow! loo, Paris, loo! The bull has the

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: game: ware horns, ho!

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Exeunt PARIS and MENELAUS

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Enter MARGARELON

speaker: MARGARELON
text_entry: Turn, slave, and fight.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: What art thou?

speaker: MARGARELON
text_entry: A bastard son of Priams.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: I am a bastard too; I love bastards: I am a bastard

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: begot, bastard instructed, bastard in mind, bastard

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: in valour, in every thing illegitimate. One bear will

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: not bite another, and wherefore should one bastard?

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Take heed, the quarrels most ominous to us: if the

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: son of a whore fight for a whore, he tempts judgment:

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: farewell, bastard.

speaker: THERSITES
text_entry: Exit

speaker: MARGARELON
text_entry: The devil take thee, coward!

speaker: MARGARELON
text_entry: Exit

speaker: MARGARELON
text_entry: SCENE VIII. Another part of the plains.

speaker: MARGARELON
text_entry: Enter HECTOR

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Most putrefied core, so fair without,

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Thy goodly armour thus hath cost thy life.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Now is my days work done; Ill take good breath:

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Rest, sword; thou hast thy fill of blood and death.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Puts off his helmet and hangs his shield behind him

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: Enter ACHILLES and Myrmidons

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Look, Hector, how the sun begins to set;

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: How ugly night comes breathing at his heels:

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Even with the vail and darking of the sun,

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: To close the day up, Hectors life is done.

speaker: HECTOR
text_entry: I am unarmd; forego this vantage, Greek.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Strike, fellows, strike; this is the man I seek.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: HECTOR falls

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: So, Ilion, fall thou next! now, Troy, sink down!

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Here lies thy heart, thy sinews, and thy bone.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: On, Myrmidons, and cry you all amain,

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Achilles hath the mighty Hector slain.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: A retreat sounded

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Hark! a retire upon our Grecian part.

speaker: MYRMIDONS
text_entry: The Trojan trumpets sound the like, my lord.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: The dragon wing of night oerspreads the earth,

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: And, stickler-like, the armies separates.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: My half-suppd sword, that frankly would have fed,

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Pleased with this dainty bait, thus goes to bed.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Sheathes his sword

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Come, tie his body to my horses tail;

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Along the field I will the Trojan trail.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: SCENE IX. Another part of the plains.

speaker: ACHILLES
text_entry: Enter AGAMEMNON, AJAX, MENELAUS, NESTOR, DIOMEDES, and others, marching. Shouts within

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Hark! hark! what shout is that?

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: Peace, drums!

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: Within

speaker: NESTOR
text_entry: Achilles! Achilles! Hectors slain! Achilles.

speaker: DIOMEDES
text_entry: The bruit is, Hectors slain, and by Achilles.

speaker: AJAX
text_entry: If it be so, yet bragless let it be;

speaker: AJAX
text_entry: Great Hector was a man as good as he.

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: March patiently along: let one be sent

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: To pray Achilles see us at our tent.

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: If in his death the gods have us befriended,

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Great Troy is ours, and our sharp wars are ended.

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Exeunt, marching

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: SCENE X. Another part of the plains.

speaker: AGAMEMNON
text_entry: Enter AENEAS and Trojans

speaker: AENEAS
text_entry: Stand, ho! yet are we masters of the field:

speaker: AENEAS
text_entry: Never go home; here starve we out the night.

speaker: AENEAS
text_entry: Enter TROILUS

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Hector is slain.

speaker: ALL
text_entry: Hector! the gods forbid!

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Hes dead; and at the murderers horses tail,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: In beastly sort, draggd through the shameful field.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Frown on, you heavens, effect your rage with speed!

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Sit, gods, upon your thrones, and smile at Troy!

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: I say, at once let your brief plagues be mercy,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: And linger not our sure destructions on!

speaker: AENEAS
text_entry: My lord, you do discomfort all the host!

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: You understand me not that tell me so:

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: I do not speak of flight, of fear, of death,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: But dare all imminence that gods and men

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Address their dangers in. Hector is gone:

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Who shall tell Priam so, or Hecuba?

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Let him that will a screech-owl aye be calld,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Go in to Troy, and say there, Hectors dead:

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: There is a word will Priam turn to stone;

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Make wells and Niobes of the maids and wives,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Cold statues of the youth, and, in a word,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Scare Troy out of itself. But, march away:

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Hector is dead; there is no more to say.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Stay yet. You vile abominable tents,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Thus proudly pight upon our Phrygian plains,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Let Titan rise as early as he dare,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Ill through and through you! and, thou great-sized coward,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: No space of earth shall sunder our two hates:

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Ill haunt thee like a wicked conscience still,

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: That mouldeth goblins swift as frenzys thoughts.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Strike a free march to Troy! with comfort go:

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Hope of revenge shall hide our inward woe.

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Exeunt AENEAS and Trojans

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: As TROILUS is going out, enter, from the other side, PANDARUS

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: But hear you, hear you!

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Hence, broker-lackey! ignomy and shame

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Pursue thy life, and live aye with thy name!

speaker: TROILUS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: A goodly medicine for my aching bones! O world!

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: world! world! thus is the poor agent despised!

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: O traitors and bawds, how earnestly are you set

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: a-work, and how ill requited! why should our

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: endeavour be so loved and the performance so loathed?

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: what verse for it? what instance for it? Let me see:

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Full merrily the humble-bee doth sing,

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Till he hath lost his honey and his sting;

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: And being once subdued in armed tail,

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Sweet honey and sweet notes together fail.

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Good traders in the flesh, set this in your

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: painted cloths.

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: As many as be here of panders hall,

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Your eyes, half out, weep out at Pandars fall;

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Or if you cannot weep, yet give some groans,

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Though not for me, yet for your aching bones.

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Brethren and sisters of the hold-door trade,

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Some two months hence my will shall here be made:

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: It should be now, but that my fear is this,

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Some galled goose of Winchester would hiss:

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Till then Ill sweat and seek about for eases,

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: And at that time bequeathe you my diseases.

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Exit

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: ACT I

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: SCENE I. DUKE ORSINOs palace.

speaker: PANDARUS
text_entry: Enter DUKE ORSINO, CURIO, and other Lords; Musicians attending

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: If music be the food of love, play on;

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Give me excess of it, that, surfeiting,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: The appetite may sicken, and so die.

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: That strain again! it had a dying fall:

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: O, it came oer my ear like the sweet sound,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: That breathes upon a bank of violets,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Stealing and giving odour! Enough; no more:

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Tis not so sweet now as it was before.

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: O spirit of love! how quick and fresh art thou,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: That, notwithstanding thy capacity

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Receiveth as the sea, nought enters there,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Of what validity and pitch soeer,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: But falls into abatement and low price,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Even in a minute: so full of shapes is fancy

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: That it alone is high fantastical.

speaker: CURIO
text_entry: Will you go hunt, my lord?

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: What, Curio?

speaker: CURIO
text_entry: The hart.

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Why, so I do, the noblest that I have:

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: O, when mine eyes did see Olivia first,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Methought she purged the air of pestilence!

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: That instant was I turnd into a hart;

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: And my desires, like fell and cruel hounds,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Eer since pursue me.

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Enter VALENTINE

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: How now! what news from her?

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: So please my lord, I might not be admitted;

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: But from her handmaid do return this answer:

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: The element itself, till seven years heat,

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: Shall not behold her face at ample view;

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: But, like a cloistress, she will veiled walk

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: And water once a day her chamber round

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: With eye-offending brine: all this to season

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: A brothers dead love, which she would keep fresh

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: And lasting in her sad remembrance.

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: O, she that hath a heart of that fine frame

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: To pay this debt of love but to a brother,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: How will she love, when the rich golden shaft

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Hath killd the flock of all affections else

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: That live in her; when liver, brain and heart,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: These sovereign thrones, are all supplied, and filld

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Her sweet perfections with one self king!

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Away before me to sweet beds of flowers:

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Love-thoughts lie rich when canopied with bowers.

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: SCENE II. The sea-coast.

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Enter VIOLA, a Captain, and Sailors

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: What country, friends, is this?

speaker: Captain
text_entry: This is Illyria, lady.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: And what should I do in Illyria?

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: My brother he is in Elysium.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Perchance he is not drownd: what think you, sailors?

speaker: Captain
text_entry: It is perchance that you yourself were saved.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: O my poor brother! and so perchance may he be.

speaker: Captain
text_entry: True, madam: and, to comfort you with chance,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Assure yourself, after our ship did split,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: When you and those poor number saved with you

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Hung on our driving boat, I saw your brother,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Most provident in peril, bind himself,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Courage and hope both teaching him the practise,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: To a strong mast that lived upon the sea;

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Where, like Arion on the dolphins back,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: I saw him hold acquaintance with the waves

speaker: Captain
text_entry: So long as I could see.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: For saying so, theres gold:

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Mine own escape unfoldeth to my hope,

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Whereto thy speech serves for authority,

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: The like of him. Knowst thou this country?

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Ay, madam, well; for I was bred and born

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Not three hours travel from this very place.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Who governs here?

speaker: Captain
text_entry: A noble duke, in nature as in name.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: What is the name?

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Orsino.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Orsino! I have heard my father name him:

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: He was a bachelor then.

speaker: Captain
text_entry: And so is now, or was so very late;

speaker: Captain
text_entry: For but a month ago I went from hence,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: And then twas fresh in murmur,--as, you know,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: What great ones do the less will prattle of,--

speaker: Captain
text_entry: That he did seek the love of fair Olivia.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Whats she?

speaker: Captain
text_entry: A virtuous maid, the daughter of a count

speaker: Captain
text_entry: That died some twelvemonth since, then leaving her

speaker: Captain
text_entry: In the protection of his son, her brother,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Who shortly also died: for whose dear love,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: They say, she hath abjured the company

speaker: Captain
text_entry: And sight of men.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: O that I served that lady

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: And might not be delivered to the world,

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Till I had made mine own occasion mellow,

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: What my estate is!

speaker: Captain
text_entry: That were hard to compass;

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Because she will admit no kind of suit,

speaker: Captain
text_entry: No, not the dukes.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: There is a fair behavior in thee, captain;

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: And though that nature with a beauteous wall

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Doth oft close in pollution, yet of thee

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: I will believe thou hast a mind that suits

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: With this thy fair and outward character.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: I prithee, and Ill pay thee bounteously,

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Conceal me what I am, and be my aid

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: For such disguise as haply shall become

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: The form of my intent. Ill serve this duke:

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Thou shall present me as an eunuch to him:

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: It may be worth thy pains; for I can sing

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: And speak to him in many sorts of music

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: That will allow me very worth his service.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: What else may hap to time I will commit;

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Only shape thou thy silence to my wit.

speaker: Captain
text_entry: Be you his eunuch, and your mute Ill be:

speaker: Captain
text_entry: When my tongue blabs, then let mine eyes not see.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: I thank thee: lead me on.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: SCENE III. OLIVIAS house.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Enter SIR TOBY BELCH and MARIA

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: What a plague means my niece, to take the death of

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: her brother thus? I am sure cares an enemy to life.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: By my troth, Sir Toby, you must come in earlier o

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: nights: your cousin, my lady, takes great

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: exceptions to your ill hours.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Why, let her except, before excepted.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Ay, but you must confine yourself within the modest

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: limits of order.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Confine! Ill confine myself no finer than I am:

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: these clothes are good enough to drink in; and so be

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: these boots too: an they be not, let them hang

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: themselves in their own straps.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: That quaffing and drinking will undo you: I heard

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: my lady talk of it yesterday; and of a foolish

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: knight that you brought in one night here to be her wooer.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Who, Sir Andrew Aguecheek?

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Ay, he.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Hes as tall a man as anys in Illyria.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Whats that to the purpose?

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Why, he has three thousand ducats a year.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Ay, but hell have but a year in all these ducats:

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: hes a very fool and a prodigal.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Fie, that youll say so! he plays o the

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: viol-de-gamboys, and speaks three or four languages

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: word for word without book, and hath all the good

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: gifts of nature.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: He hath indeed, almost natural: for besides that

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: hes a fool, hes a great quarreller: and but that

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: he hath the gift of a coward to allay the gust he

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: hath in quarrelling, tis thought among the prudent

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: he would quickly have the gift of a grave.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: By this hand, they are scoundrels and subtractors

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: that say so of him. Who are they?

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: They that add, moreover, hes drunk nightly in your company.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: With drinking healths to my niece: Ill drink to

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: her as long as there is a passage in my throat and

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: drink in Illyria: hes a coward and a coystrill

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: that will not drink to my niece till his brains turn

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: o the toe like a parish-top. What, wench!

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Castiliano vulgo! for here comes Sir Andrew Agueface.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Enter SIR ANDREW

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Sir Toby Belch! how now, Sir Toby Belch!

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Sweet Sir Andrew!

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Bless you, fair shrew.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: And you too, sir.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Accost, Sir Andrew, accost.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Whats that?

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: My nieces chambermaid.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Good Mistress Accost, I desire better acquaintance.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: My name is Mary, sir.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Good Mistress Mary Accost,--

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: You mistake, knight; accost is front her, board

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: her, woo her, assail her.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: By my troth, I would not undertake her in this

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: company. Is that the meaning of accost?

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Fare you well, gentlemen.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: An thou let part so, Sir Andrew, would thou mightst

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: never draw sword again.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: An you part so, mistress, I would I might never

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: draw sword again. Fair lady, do you think you have

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: fools in hand?

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Sir, I have not you by the hand.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Marry, but you shall have; and heres my hand.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Now, sir, thought is free: I pray you, bring

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: your hand to the buttery-bar and let it drink.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Wherefore, sweet-heart? whats your metaphor?

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Its dry, sir.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Why, I think so: I am not such an ass but I can

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: keep my hand dry. But whats your jest?

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: A dry jest, sir.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Are you full of them?

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Ay, sir, I have them at my fingers ends: marry,

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: now I let go your hand, I am barren.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Exit

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: O knight thou lackest a cup of canary: when did I

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: see thee so put down?

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Never in your life, I think; unless you see canary

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: put me down. Methinks sometimes I have no more wit

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: than a Christian or an ordinary man has: but I am a

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: great eater of beef and I believe that does harm to my wit.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: No question.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: An I thought that, Ild forswear it. Ill ride home

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: to-morrow, Sir Toby.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Pourquoi, my dear knight?

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: What is Pourquoi? do or not do? I would I had

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: bestowed that time in the tongues that I have in

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: fencing, dancing and bear-baiting: O, had I but

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: followed the arts!

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Then hadst thou had an excellent head of hair.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Why, would that have mended my hair?

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Past question; for thou seest it will not curl by nature.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: But it becomes me well enough, doest not?

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Excellent; it hangs like flax on a distaff; and I

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: hope to see a housewife take thee between her legs

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: and spin it off.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Faith, Ill home to-morrow, Sir Toby: your niece

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: will not be seen; or if she be, its four to one

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: shell none of me: the count himself here hard by woos her.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Shell none o the count: shell not match above

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: her degree, neither in estate, years, nor wit; I

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: have heard her sweart. Tut, theres life int,

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: man.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Ill stay a month longer. I am a fellow o the

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: strangest mind i the world; I delight in masques

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: and revels sometimes altogether.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Art thou good at these kickshawses, knight?

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: As any man in Illyria, whatsoever he be, under the

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: degree of my betters; and yet I will not compare

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: with an old man.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: What is thy excellence in a galliard, knight?

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Faith, I can cut a caper.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: And I can cut the mutton tot.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: And I think I have the back-trick simply as strong

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: as any man in Illyria.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Wherefore are these things hid? wherefore have

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: these gifts a curtain before em? are they like to

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: take dust, like Mistress Malls picture? why dost

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: thou not go to church in a galliard and come home in

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: a coranto? My very walk should be a jig; I would not

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: so much as make water but in a sink-a-pace. What

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: dost thou mean? Is it a world to hide virtues in?

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: I did think, by the excellent constitution of thy

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: leg, it was formed under the star of a galliard.

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Ay, tis strong, and it does indifferent well in a

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: flame-coloured stock. Shall we set about some revels?

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: What shall we do else? were we not born under Taurus?

speaker: SIR ANDREW
text_entry: Taurus! Thats sides and heart.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: No, sir; it is legs and thighs. Let me see the

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: caper; ha! higher: ha, ha! excellent!

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: SCENE IV. DUKE ORSINOs palace.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Enter VALENTINE and VIOLA in mans attire

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: If the duke continue these favours towards you,

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: Cesario, you are like to be much advanced: he hath

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: known you but three days, and already you are no stranger.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: You either fear his humour or my negligence, that

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: you call in question the continuance of his love:

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: is he inconstant, sir, in his favours?

speaker: VALENTINE
text_entry: No, believe me.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: I thank you. Here comes the count.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Enter DUKE ORSINO, CURIO, and Attendants

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Who saw Cesario, ho?

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: On your attendance, my lord; here.

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Stand you a while aloof, Cesario,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Thou knowst no less but all; I have unclaspd

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: To thee the book even of my secret soul:

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Therefore, good youth, address thy gait unto her;

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Be not denied access, stand at her doors,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: And tell them, there thy fixed foot shall grow

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Till thou have audience.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Sure, my noble lord,

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: If she be so abandond to her sorrow

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: As it is spoke, she never will admit me.

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Be clamorous and leap all civil bounds

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Rather than make unprofited return.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Say I do speak with her, my lord, what then?

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: O, then unfold the passion of my love,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Surprise her with discourse of my dear faith:

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: It shall become thee well to act my woes;

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: She will attend it better in thy youth

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Than in a nuncios of more grave aspect.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: I think not so, my lord.

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Dear lad, believe it;

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: For they shall yet belie thy happy years,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: That say thou art a man: Dianas lip

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Is not more smooth and rubious; thy small pipe

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: Is as the maidens organ, shrill and sound,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: And all is semblative a womans part.

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: I know thy constellation is right apt

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: For this affair. Some four or five attend him;

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: All, if you will; for I myself am best

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: When least in company. Prosper well in this,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: And thou shalt live as freely as thy lord,

speaker: DUKE ORSINO
text_entry: To call his fortunes thine.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Ill do my best

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: To woo your lady:

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Aside

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: yet, a barful strife!

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Whoeer I woo, myself would be his wife.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Exeunt

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: SCENE V. OLIVIAS house.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Enter MARIA and Clown

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Nay, either tell me where thou hast been, or I will

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: not open my lips so wide as a bristle may enter in

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: way of thy excuse: my lady will hang thee for thy absence.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Let her hang me: he that is well hanged in this

speaker: Clown
text_entry: world needs to fear no colours.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Make that good.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: He shall see none to fear.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: A good lenten answer: I can tell thee where that

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: saying was born, of I fear no colours.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Where, good Mistress Mary?

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: In the wars; and that may you be bold to say in your foolery.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Well, God give them wisdom that have it; and those

speaker: Clown
text_entry: that are fools, let them use their talents.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Yet you will be hanged for being so long absent; or,

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: to be turned away, is not that as good as a hanging to you?

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Many a good hanging prevents a bad marriage; and,

speaker: Clown
text_entry: for turning away, let summer bear it out.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: You are resolute, then?

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Not so, neither; but I am resolved on two points.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: That if one break, the other will hold; or, if both

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: break, your gaskins fall.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Apt, in good faith; very apt. Well, go thy way; if

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Sir Toby would leave drinking, thou wert as witty a

speaker: Clown
text_entry: piece of Eves flesh as any in Illyria.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Peace, you rogue, no more o that. Here comes my

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: lady: make your excuse wisely, you were best.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Exit

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Wit, ant be thy will, put me into good fooling!

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Those wits, that think they have thee, do very oft

speaker: Clown
text_entry: prove fools; and I, that am sure I lack thee, may

speaker: Clown
text_entry: pass for a wise man: for what says Quinapalus?

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Better a witty fool, than a foolish wit.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Enter OLIVIA with MALVOLIO

speaker: Clown
text_entry: God bless thee, lady!

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Take the fool away.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Do you not hear, fellows? Take away the lady.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Go to, youre a dry fool; Ill no more of you:

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: besides, you grow dishonest.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Two faults, madonna, that drink and good counsel

speaker: Clown
text_entry: will amend: for give the dry fool drink, then is

speaker: Clown
text_entry: the fool not dry: bid the dishonest man mend

speaker: Clown
text_entry: himself; if he mend, he is no longer dishonest; if

speaker: Clown
text_entry: he cannot, let the botcher mend him. Any thing

speaker: Clown
text_entry: thats mended is but patched: virtue that

speaker: Clown
text_entry: transgresses is but patched with sin; and sin that

speaker: Clown
text_entry: amends is but patched with virtue. If that this

speaker: Clown
text_entry: simple syllogism will serve, so; if it will not,

speaker: Clown
text_entry: what remedy? As there is no true cuckold but

speaker: Clown
text_entry: calamity, so beautys a flower. The lady bade take

speaker: Clown
text_entry: away the fool; therefore, I say again, take her away.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Sir, I bade them take away you.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Misprision in the highest degree! Lady, cucullus non

speaker: Clown
text_entry: facit monachum; thats as much to say as I wear not

speaker: Clown
text_entry: motley in my brain. Good madonna, give me leave to

speaker: Clown
text_entry: prove you a fool.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Can you do it?

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Dexterously, good madonna.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Make your proof.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: I must catechise you for it, madonna: good my mouse

speaker: Clown
text_entry: of virtue, answer me.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Well, sir, for want of other idleness, Ill bide your proof.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Good madonna, why mournest thou?

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Good fool, for my brothers death.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: I think his soul is in hell, madonna.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: I know his soul is in heaven, fool.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: The more fool, madonna, to mourn for your brothers

speaker: Clown
text_entry: soul being in heaven. Take away the fool, gentlemen.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: What think you of this fool, Malvolio? doth he not mend?

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: Yes, and shall do till the pangs of death shake him:

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: infirmity, that decays the wise, doth ever make the

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: better fool.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: God send you, sir, a speedy infirmity, for the

speaker: Clown
text_entry: better increasing your folly! Sir Toby will be

speaker: Clown
text_entry: sworn that I am no fox; but he will not pass his

speaker: Clown
text_entry: word for two pence that you are no fool.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: How say you to that, Malvolio?

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: I marvel your ladyship takes delight in such a

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: barren rascal: I saw him put down the other day

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: with an ordinary fool that has no more brain

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: than a stone. Look you now, hes out of his guard

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: already; unless you laugh and minister occasion to

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: him, he is gagged. I protest, I take these wise men,

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: that crow so at these set kind of fools, no better

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: than the fools zanies.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Oh, you are sick of self-love, Malvolio, and taste

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: with a distempered appetite. To be generous,

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: guiltless and of free disposition, is to take those

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: things for bird-bolts that you deem cannon-bullets:

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: there is no slander in an allowed fool, though he do

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: nothing but rail; nor no railing in a known discreet

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: man, though he do nothing but reprove.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Now Mercury endue thee with leasing, for thou

speaker: Clown
text_entry: speakest well of fools!

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Re-enter MARIA

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Madam, there is at the gate a young gentleman much

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: desires to speak with you.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: From the Count Orsino, is it?

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: I know not, madam: tis a fair young man, and well attended.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Who of my people hold him in delay?

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Sir Toby, madam, your kinsman.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Fetch him off, I pray you; he speaks nothing but

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: madman: fie on him!

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Exit MARIA

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Go you, Malvolio: if it be a suit from the count, I

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: am sick, or not at home; what you will, to dismiss it.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Exit MALVOLIO

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Now you see, sir, how your fooling grows old, and

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: people dislike it.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Thou hast spoke for us, madonna, as if thy eldest

speaker: Clown
text_entry: son should be a fool; whose skull Jove cram with

speaker: Clown
text_entry: brains! for,--here he comes,--one of thy kin has a

speaker: Clown
text_entry: most weak pia mater.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Enter SIR TOBY BELCH

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: By mine honour, half drunk. What is he at the gate, cousin?

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: A gentleman.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: A gentleman! what gentleman?

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Tis a gentle man here--a plague o these

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: pickle-herring! How now, sot!

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Good Sir Toby!

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Cousin, cousin, how have you come so early by this lethargy?

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Lechery! I defy lechery. Theres one at the gate.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Ay, marry, what is he?

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Let him be the devil, an he will, I care not: give

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: me faith, say I. Well, its all one.

speaker: SIR TOBY BELCH
text_entry: Exit

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Whats a drunken man like, fool?

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Like a drowned man, a fool and a mad man: one

speaker: Clown
text_entry: draught above heat makes him a fool; the second mads

speaker: Clown
text_entry: him; and a third drowns him.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Go thou and seek the crowner, and let him sit o my

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: coz; for hes in the third degree of drink, hes

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: drowned: go, look after him.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: He is but mad yet, madonna; and the fool shall look

speaker: Clown
text_entry: to the madman.

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Exit

speaker: Clown
text_entry: Re-enter MALVOLIO

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: Madam, yond young fellow swears he will speak with

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: you. I told him you were sick; he takes on him to

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: understand so much, and therefore comes to speak

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: with you. I told him you were asleep; he seems to

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: have a foreknowledge of that too, and therefore

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: comes to speak with you. What is to be said to him,

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: lady? hes fortified against any denial.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Tell him he shall not speak with me.

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: Has been told so; and he says, hell stand at your

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: door like a sheriffs post, and be the supporter to

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: a bench, but hell speak with you.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: What kind o man is he?

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: Why, of mankind.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: What manner of man?

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: Of very ill manner; hell speak with you, will you or no.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Of what personage and years is he?

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: Not yet old enough for a man, nor young enough for

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: a boy; as a squash is before tis a peascod, or a

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: cooling when tis almost an apple: tis with him

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: in standing water, between boy and man. He is very

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: well-favoured and he speaks very shrewishly; one

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: would think his mothers milk were scarce out of him.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Let him approach: call in my gentlewoman.

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: Gentlewoman, my lady calls.

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: Exit

speaker: MALVOLIO
text_entry: Re-enter MARIA

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Give me my veil: come, throw it oer my face.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Well once more hear Orsinos embassy.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Enter VIOLA, and Attendants

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: The honourable lady of the house, which is she?

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Speak to me; I shall answer for her.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Your will?

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Most radiant, exquisite and unmatchable beauty,--I

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: pray you, tell me if this be the lady of the house,

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: for I never saw her: I would be loath to cast away

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: my speech, for besides that it is excellently well

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: penned, I have taken great pains to con it. Good

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: beauties, let me sustain no scorn; I am very

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: comptible, even to the least sinister usage.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Whence came you, sir?

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: I can say little more than I have studied, and that

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: questions out of my part. Good gentle one, give me

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: modest assurance if you be the lady of the house,

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: that I may proceed in my speech.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Are you a comedian?

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: No, my profound heart: and yet, by the very fangs

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: of malice I swear, I am not that I play. Are you

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: the lady of the house?

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: If I do not usurp myself, I am.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Most certain, if you are she, you do usurp

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: yourself; for what is yours to bestow is not yours

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: to reserve. But this is from my commission: I will

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: on with my speech in your praise, and then show you

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: the heart of my message.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Come to what is important int: I forgive you the praise.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Alas, I took great pains to study it, and tis poetical.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: It is the more like to be feigned: I pray you,

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: keep it in. I heard you were saucy at my gates,

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: and allowed your approach rather to wonder at you

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: than to hear you. If you be not mad, be gone; if

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: you have reason, be brief: tis not that time of

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: moon with me to make one in so skipping a dialogue.

speaker: MARIA
text_entry: Will you hoist sail, sir? here lies your way.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: No, good swabber; I am to hull here a little

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: longer. Some mollification for your giant, sweet

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: lady. Tell me your mind: I am a messenger.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Sure, you have some hideous matter to deliver, when

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: the courtesy of it is so fearful. Speak your office.

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: It alone concerns your ear. I bring no overture of

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: war, no taxation of homage: I hold the olive in my

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: hand; my words are as fun of peace as matter.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Yet you began rudely. What are you? what would you?

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: The rudeness that hath appeared in me have I

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: learned from my entertainment. What I am, and what I

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: would, are as secret as maidenhead; to your ears,

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: divinity, to any others, profanation.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Give us the place alone: we will hear this divinity.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Exeunt MARIA and Attendants

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Now, sir, what is your text?

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: Most sweet lady,--

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: A comfortable doctrine, and much may be said of it.

speaker: OLIVIA
text_entry: Where lies your text?

speaker: VIOLA
text_entry: In Orsinos bosom.

speaker: OLIVIA
